[COMMENTARY TAKEN OVER FROM
GAUDIYA GRANTHA MANDIRA:
This is an interesting text. There appear to be many original verses sprinkled
throughout the text, many of which are incomplete. Some of the verses don't follow
any regular meter and some work is needed to edit this text. Some verses are likely
quotes, but I haven't been able to trace them.

children.translated_text: I have used Haridas Shastri's edition, and have not had access to another. It would be worth finding other manuscripts in order to produce a true critical edition.]
<s>Śrī Sādhanā-dīpikā</s> (The Lamp of Spiritual Practice)
First Level
Within the temple of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, abundantly,
upon a wonderful pavement of fine gold and jeweled necklaces,
seated together with His beloved, His equal,
I take refuge in <s>Govinda</s>, the directly manifest Lord. ||1||
All those who have fallen into the well of <s>saṃsāra</s> (worldly existence),
desiring to uplift the people of the age of <s>Kali</s>,
He who appeared indeed in the land of <s>Gauḍa</s> (Bengal) —
I surrender to that <s>Caitanya-candra</s> (moon-like <s>Caitanya</s>). ||2||
The most beloved of <s>Śrī Caitanya</s>, the glorious <s>Rādhā-Gadādhara</s>,
the worship of <s>Śrī Govinda</s> who is of the form of His entourage,
the worthy recipient of the true <s>prema</s> (divine love) of those two, <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, an ocean of compassion —

children.text: tat-pāda-kamala-dvandve ratir me syād vraje sadā ||3||
children.translated_text: may my attachment to the pair of his lotus feet be ever [present] in <s>Vraja</s>. ||3||
The chief steward of his service, the noble-minded one,
the sole abode of all auspicious qualities,
the ornament of the lineage of <s>Vārendra</s> brāhmaṇas, my <s>guru</s> —
I constantly worship him who is named <s>Śrī Haridāsa</s>. ||4||
By whose service the glorious <s>Govinda</s>, the son of <s>Nanda</s>, is brought under control,
that ocean of compassion asks for <s>bhakta</s> (devotion) mixed with milk. ||5||

children.text:
kiṃ cāsmin kadācid vasanta-vāsarāvasare rātrau rāsa-maṇḍale bhramati sati
saṃcāriṇyāḥ śrī-vṛṣabhānu-sutāyā āścaryaṃ rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā tamālasya mūle
mūrcchitavān iti mahatī prasiddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Moreover, once on a spring evening, at night, when the <s>rāsa-maṇḍala</s> (circle of the <s>rāsa</s> dance) was revolving, having seen the astonishing beauty of the wandering daughter of <s>Śrī Vṛṣabhānu</s>, He fainted at the root of a <s>tamāla</s> tree — this is the great well-known [event].
Her own attendant of the beloved,

children.text: tayoś ca dāsaḥ kila ko'pi nāmnā |
children.translated_text: and the servant of those two, indeed a certain one by name,
for his own people, in the servitude of those [divine couple],
he strives to introduce [their] minds. ||6||
The daily pastimes (<s>carita</s>) of the beloved of <s>Śrīmatī Rādhā</s>'s very life,
were mercifully manifested by <s>Śrīmat Kṛṣṇa Kavīndra</s>. ||7||
By the command of <s>Śrīla Rūpa</s>, by that most trusted of those [devotees],

children.text: kṛtaṃ tasmin mayā bhāṣye teṣāṃ vākya-pramāṇataḥ ||8||
children.translated_text: a commentary on that was composed by me, on the authority of their words. ||8||
Now, separately from that, of <s>Hari</s> who is the directly manifest Lord,
the worship consisting of <s>mantras</s>, in brief, is herein written. ||9||

children.text:
tat-tat-prasaṅga-saṅgatyā siddhānto'pi ca likhyate |
tasya madhye na likhito grantha-vistāra-bhītitaḥ |

children.translated_text: this work, complete in ten levels, will come to be. ||10||
The <s>siddhānta</s> (established doctrine) too is written in connection with the respective topics. What is not written therein, out of fear of extending the text —
In the first level, the revelation of the glorious worship (<s>sevā</s>);
in the second, the account of <s>Śrīla Govinda</s>, the directly manifest Lord. ||11||
In the third, the determination of the excellence of <s>rasa</s> in middle adolescence;
in the fourth, the meaning of the eighteen-syllabled <s>mantra</s> is written. ||12||
In the fifth, the greatness of this land of <s>Vraja</s> is proclaimed;
in the sixth, the auspicious account of the manifestation of the daughter of <s>Śrībhānu</s>. ||13||
Of <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s> and of his assembly of devotees,
the account pertaining to their essential nature is told, on the authority of the respective texts. ||14||

children.text: saptame tv aṣṭame proktā punaḥ śrī-rūpa-sat-kathā |
children.translated_text: In the seventh and eighth, the sacred account of <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> is again told,
[along with] the determination of <s>rāgātmikā</s> (spontaneous) and <s>rāgānugā</s> (following spontaneous) <s>bhakti</s> (devotion). ||15||

children.text: kakṣāyā navame lekhyaṃ daśame likhyate punaḥ |
children.translated_text: What is to be written in the ninth level; in the tenth is again written
the description of the essential nature of <s>bhakti</s> and the like of the blessed Lord. ||16||

children.text:
atha śrīmad-rūpa-sanātanābhyāṃ śrīla-paṇḍita-gosvāmi-śiṣya-śrī-paramānanda-
gosvāminā ca śrīmad-vṛndāvana-yoga-pīṭhādiṣu sarvaṃ svarūpa-rāja-svayaṃ-
bhagavataḥ śrīmad-govinda-devasya śrīman-madana-gopāla-gopīnāthayoś ca sevā
śrīmad-īśvarecchayā sva-sva-sthāne sva-sva-sevāḥ prakāśitāḥ | prakāśas tu na
bhedeṣu gaṇyate sa hi na pṛthak [Laghubhāg. 1.18] iti |
children.translated_text: Now, by <s>Śrīmad Rūpa</s> and <s>Sanātana</s>, and by <s>Śrī Paramānanda Gosvāmin</s> who was a disciple of <s>Śrīla Paṇḍita Gosvāmin</s>, in the <s>Yoga-pīṭha</s> and other [places] in <s>Śrīmad Vṛndāvana</s>, all the worship of <s>Śrīmad Govinda-deva</s>, who is the <s>svarūpa-rāja</s> (king of [divine] forms) and <s>svayaṃ-bhagavat</s> (the Lord Himself), and of <s>Śrīman Madana-Gopāla</s> and <s>Gopīnātha</s>, was revealed by the will of the Lord, each worship in its own place. 'A manifestation is not counted among the divisions, for it is not separate' [<s>Laghubhāgavatāmṛta</s> 1.18].
Of <s>Svayaṃ Bhagavat</s> (the Lord Himself), <s>Śrīmad Govinda</s>, the most blissful,
in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, at the <s>Yoga-pīṭha</s>, the worship was revealed,
accomplished in the form of <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, who is the embodiment of <s>Śrī Caitanya</s>'s grace. ||17||
The auspicious worship of <s>Śrī Gopāla-deva</s>, which bestows supreme bliss,
was revealed there itself in the form of <s>Śrī Sanātana</s>. ||18||
At [the place of] <s>Paramānanda-deva</s>, at the foot of the glorious <s>nīpa</s> (kadamba) tree,
fashioned as if by the cool fire united with the waters of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā), ||19||
A student of <s>Rādhā-Gadādhara</s>, named <s>Paramānanda</s>,
by whom was quickly manifested <s>Gopīnātha</s>, an ocean of mercy,
on the bank of the <s>Vaṃśī-vaṭa</s> (the banyan tree of the flute), on the beautiful bank of the glorious <s>Yamunā</s>. ||20||

children.text:
tataḥ sarvasva-rūpaṃ jānatā śrīla-rūpeṇa śrī-sanātanena ca mūla-svarūpa-śakti-śrī-
rādhā-gadādhara-parivāre śrīman-mahāprabhor ājñānusāreṇa sva-sva-sthāne sva-
sva-sevā samarpitā | tatrāpi śrī-paṇḍita-gosvāmi-śiṣyaḥ premi-kṛṣṇa-dāsa-
gosvāmine samarpitā śrī-rūpeṇa | tathā hi,

children.translated_text: The essential form and original characteristics of <s>Śrīmad Gadādhara</s>,
being known by <s>Śrīla Rūpa</s>, the worship was entrusted to him. ||21||

Then, by <s>Śrīla Rūpa</s> and <s>Śrī Sanātana</s>, who knew the <s>sarvasva-rūpa</s> (all-encompassing form), in accordance with the command of <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s>, each worship was offered in its own place to the <s>mūla-svarūpa-śakti</s> (original inherent energy) <s>Śrī Rādhā-Gadādhara</s> entourage. Moreover, the worship was offered by <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> to <s>Premī Kṛṣṇadāsa Gosvāmin</s>, a disciple of <s>Śrī Paṇḍita Gosvāmin</s>. Thus indeed,

children.text:
śrīla-sanātana-gosvāminā svasyātīvāntaraṅgāya śrī-kṛṣṇa-dāsa-brahmacāriṇe
śrī-madana-gopāla-devasya seva samarpitā | evaṃ śrīmad-rūpādvaita-rūpeṇa
śrīmad-raghunāthena śrī=yuta-kuṇḍa-yugala-paricaryā tat-parisara-bhūmiś ca śrī-
govindāya samarpitā | evaṃ śrī-gopīnāthasya sevā śrī-paramānanda-gosvāminā
śrīmadhu-paṇḍita-gosvāmine samarpitā | kiṃ ca trayāṇāṃ śrī-vigrahāṇāṃ preyasī
kila śrī-hari-dāsa-gosvāmi-śrī-kṛṣṇa-dāsa-brahmacāri-gosvāmi-śrī-madhu-
paṇḍita-gosvāmibhiś ca prakāśitā ||
children.translated_text: By <s>Śrīla Sanātana Gosvāmin</s>, the worship of <s>Śrī Madana-Gopāla-deva</s> was entrusted to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa Brahmacārin</s>, who was his most intimate [associate]. Similarly, in the form of <s>Śrīmad Rūpa</s>'s non-duality, by <s>Śrīmad Raghunātha</s>, the service of the glorious pair of <s>Kuṇḍas</s> (sacred ponds) and their surrounding land was entrusted to <s>Śrī Govinda</s>. Similarly, the worship of <s>Śrī Gopīnātha</s> was entrusted by <s>Śrī Paramānanda Gosvāmin</s> to <s>Śrī Madhu Paṇḍita Gosvāmin</s>. Moreover, the beloveds of the three sacred images (<s>vigrahas</s>) were manifested by <s>Śrī Haridāsa Gosvāmin</s>, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa Brahmacārin Gosvāmin</s>, and <s>Śrī Madhu Paṇḍita Gosvāmin</s> respectively.
Thus [ends] the first level.
(2) Second Level

children.text:
atha śrī-vṛndāvanottamāṅga-yoga-pīṭhāṣṭa-dala-kamala-karṇikā-rāja-siṃhāsana-
virājamānaḥ sarvasva-rūpa-rājaḥ sarva-prakāśa-mūla-bhūtaḥ svayaṃ bhagavat-śrī-
vrajendra-nandano madhya-kaiśorāvasthitaḥ śrī-govinda-deva eva śrī-
vṛndāvanādhirājaḥ | yathā bahūnāṃ rāja-putrāṇāṃ rāja-putratve sāmye tathāpy
eko rāja-siṃhāsanārho rājā bhavati śruti-smṛti-purāṇādāv asyaiva prādhānyāt,
yathā vraje mahā-rāse dhāmno'bhede'pi parikara-bhedena sarveṣu yūtheṣu
pūrṇatama-prakāśena sthitaḥ san śrī-rādhikāyāḥ pārśve svayam eva virājate, tathā
| ataeva mauna-mudrādikaṃ prakāśya vigrahaval-līlā-kāle sarveṣāṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa-
prakāśānāṃ tatraivānyatra sthitaḥ san śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-mahāprabhos tat
pārṣadānāṃ ca niratiśaya-kṛpā prakāśa-rūpa-śrī-rūpa-sevām aṅgīkṛtya śrī-
govinda-devaḥ svayam eva virājate | tathā hlādinī-śakti-sārāṃśa-mahābhāva-
svarūpayā śruti-smṛti-purāṇādiṣu vṛndāvanādhīśātvena prasiddhayā śrī-rādhayā
saha virājamānatvenāsyaiva prasiddheḥ, yathā brahma-saṃhitāyām (5.37)-
children.translated_text: Now, seated upon the royal lion-throne on the pericarp of the eight-petaled lotus of the <s>Yoga-pīṭha</s>, the foremost [place] of <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>, the <s>sarvasva-rūpa-rāja</s> (king of the all-encompassing form), the root source of all manifestations, <s>Svayaṃ Bhagavat</s> (the Lord Himself) <s>Śrī Vrajendra-nandana</s> (the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>), situated in the stage of middle adolescence, <s>Śrī Govinda-deva</s> Himself is the supreme Lord of <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>. Just as among many princes, though equal in princehood, one alone is worthy of the royal throne and becomes king — because of His primacy in <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s>, and the like — just as in <s>Vraja</s> during the great <s>rāsa</s> [dance], though there is no difference in the abode (<s>dhāman</s>), by the difference of entourage, being present in all groups (<s>yūthas</s>) in the most complete manifestation, He Himself shines forth beside <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> — so too [here]. For this very reason, having manifested the seal of silence (<s>mauna-mudrā</s>) and the like during the pastimes of the manifested sacred images, while all the manifestations of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> are present there and elsewhere, having accepted the worship in the form of <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> — [which is] the manifestation of the unsurpassable grace of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu</s> and His associates — <s>Śrī Govinda-deva</s> Himself shines forth. And because of His well-known [presence] as shining forth together with <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> — who, being the essence of the <s>hlādinī-śakti</s> (bliss-potency), is the embodiment of <s>mahābhāva</s> (the highest state of ecstatic love), and who is celebrated in <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇa</s>, and the like as the sovereign of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. As in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (5.37) —
Imbued with the flavors (<s>rasas</s>) of blissful spiritual consciousness,
with those [energies], who are indeed His own forms as arts (<s>kalās</s>),
He dwells in <s>Goloka</s> alone, being the Self of all —
I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Person.
As in the <s>Harivaṃśa</s> —

children.text: ahaṃ kilendro devānāṃ tvaṃ gavām indratāṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'I am indeed <s>Indra</s> of the <s>devas</s>; You have attained the lordship of cows.',

children.text: govinda iti lokās tvāṃ stoṣyanti bhuvi śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: 'The people shall eternally praise You on earth as <s>Govinda</s>.'
And in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> (10.21.23) —
<s>Indra</s>, urged by the divine sages together with the mothers of the <s>devas</s>,
anointed the <s>Dāśārha</s> (descendant of <s>Daśārha</s>) and called Him '<s>Govinda</s>.'

children.text:
ṭīkā ca-deva-mātṛbhir iti | gāḥ paśūn gāṃ svargaṃ vā indratvena vindatīti kṛtvā
ca govinda ity abhyadhāt nāma kṛtavān |
children.translated_text: And the commentary — 'by the mothers of the <s>devas</s>' — means: because He finds (<s>vindati</s>) cows (<s>gāḥ</s>), cattle, or heaven (<s>gām</s>) as their lord (<s>indra</s>), therefore He called [Him] '<s>Govinda</s>' — [that is,] He gave [Him] the name.
Again, in the same tenth canto (10.27.28) —
Having thus anointed the lord of the cows and the <s>gokula</s>, <s>Govinda</s>,

children.text: anujñāto yayau śakro vṛto devādibhir divam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakra</s> (<s>Indra</s>), having received permission, departed to heaven accompanied by the <s>devas</s> and others.
In the <s>Padyāvalī</s> [*ENDNOTE #1] —
His lotus feet gleaming at the foot of a wish-fulfilling tree on the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā),
His flute melodiously sounded by gently swaying fingers, rejoicing in soft song,
immersed in savoring the sweet nectar of the gentle smile on the moon-face of <s>Rādhā</s>,
may the glorious Lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa-candra</s>, bring you prosperity.
In the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>, <s>Mathurā-khaṇḍa</s>, in the words of <s>Nārada</s> —
'In that <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is the sacred abode of <s>Govinda</s>,
filled with His servants — there I remain.'
'On earth, the <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> of <s>Govinda</s> is in that <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, O King,
where <s>Vṛndā</s> and other servants, eager for <s>Govinda</s>, abide.'
'Those supreme souls who have beheld the great abode
of <s>Govinda</s> in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, O King, have fulfilled their purpose on earth.'

children.text:
tathā hi śrī-kṛṣṇa-sandarbhe śrī-bhāgavata-ṣaṣṭha-skandhe (6.8.20)-māṃ keśvavo
gadayā prātar avyād govinda āsaṅgavam ātta-veṇuḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Thus indeed, in the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha</s>, from the sixth canto of the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> (6.8.20) — 'May <s>Keśava</s> protect me with His mace in the morning; may <s>Govinda</s>, who has taken up the flute, [protect me] until dusk.'

children.text:
ṭīkā ca-tau hi śrī-mathurā-vṛndāvanayoḥ suprasiddha-mahā-yogapīṭhayos tat-tan-
nāmnaiva sahitau prasiddhau tau ca tatra tatra prāpañcika-loka-dṛṣṭyā śrīmat-
pratimākāreṇa bhātaḥ | svajana-dṛṣṭyā sākṣād-bhūtau ca | tatrottara-rūpaṃ
brahma-saṃhitā-govinda-stavādau prasiddham | ataevātrāpi sākṣād-rūpa-vṛnda-
prakaraṇa evaitau paṭhitau ity ādi-sandarbha-ṭīkety arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: And the commentary — 'For those two [names] are well-known together with their respective names at the supremely famous great <s>Yoga-pīṭhas</s> of <s>Śrī Mathurā</s> and <s>Vṛndāvana</s>; and there, in the eyes of worldly people, they appear in the form of sacred images (<s>pratimā</s>). In the eyes of their own devotees, they are directly manifest. The latter form is well-known in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s>, the <s>Govinda-stava</s>, and the like. Therefore, here too, these two are read in the section on the directly manifest group' — thus is the meaning of the <s>Sandarbha</s> commentary.

children.text:
tathā hi-sākṣād bhagavataḥ śrīmad-govindasya sukhādhikā | tathā hi śrī-caitanya-
caritāmṛte (1.8.50-51)-
children.translated_text: Thus indeed — 'Of <s>Svayaṃ Bhagavat</s>, <s>Śrīmad Govinda</s>, the most blissful' — thus indeed, in the <s>Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s> (1.8.50-51) —

children.text:
vṛndāvane kalpa-vṛkṣa suvarṇa-sadana
mahā-yoga-pīṭha tāṅhā ratna-siṃhāsana
tāte basi āchena sākṣāt vrajendra-nandana
śrī-govinda nāma sākṣāt manmatha-madana
children.translated_text: 'In <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, under the wish-fulfilling trees, in a golden mansion, upon the great <s>Yoga-pīṭha</s>, on a jeweled throne, there sits directly the son of <s>Vrajendra</s> — named <s>Śrī Govinda</s>, directly <s>Manmatha-Madana</s> (the enchanter of Cupid himself).'

children.text:
nau sarvatra deśe yathā śrī-kṛṣṇa-prakāśādīnāṃ navīna-prācīnā-dhātu-śīlādy-
ākārāḥ kvacid bhakta-vatsalatayā calac-chakti-prakāśikā arcāyamānāḥ kvacit
sāmānyākārāś ca śrī-nanda-nandana-prakāśā dṛśyante | tathāsau svayaṃ bhagavān
śrī-govinda-devo'pi (iti cet) ? na, kiṃ tv asau tathātve dṛśyamāno'py arcāyamāna-
viśeṣaḥ svayaṃ prakāśaḥ sākṣād vrajendra-nandana eva |
atra yukti-sudṛṣṭāntāṃ prācīna-paurāṇikāṃ kathām āha-prema-nagarāpara-
paryāye pratiṣṭhāna-pure ko'pi rājāsīt | sa ca pañca-putraḥ | vārdhaka-daśāyāṃ
manasi evaṃ vicāritavān-mat-putreṣu yo rājyādi-pālanen samartho mayi premavāṃś
ca bhavet | tasmin rājyādi samarpayiṣyāmi | iti manasi kṛtvā bahir jaḍavad
ācaritavān | taṃ dṛṣṭvā sarve janā manasi duḥkhitā abhavan | putrāṇāṃ madhye
tu ye duṣṭācārās te manasi hṛṣṭā rājyādikaṃ netuṃ viṣaya-sukhaṃ ca kartuṃ
pravṛttā abhavan | teṣu ko'pi paṇḍito jñānavān pūrvato'pi pitroḥ prītiṃ kṛtvā
sevāyāṃ pravṛttaḥ | rājā tu tasya bhaktiṃ dṛṣṭvā tasmin rājyādi-bhāraṃ
samarpitavān | anye putrās tu tac chrutvā tad-upari daṇḍādikaṃ kṛtavantaḥ | tān
dṛṣṭvāmātyāḥ sarve tad-vṛttāntaṃ rājñi niveditavantaḥ |
children.translated_text:
Everywhere in the land, the forms of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s manifestations and others — of new and ancient material, character, and the like — are seen: in some places, due to His tenderness toward devotees, manifesting moving power, they are worshipped; in some places, of ordinary form, the manifestations of <s>Śrī Nanda-nandana</s> are seen. Likewise, is that self-same <s>Bhagavān Śrī Govinda-deva</s> also [merely such]? No — although appearing thus, He is a special [form] among worshipped [images], a self-manifest (<s>svayaṃ prakāśa</s>) form, directly <s>Vrajendra-nandana</s> Himself.
Here he tells an ancient <s>Paurāṇika</s> story with apt reasoning and example — In the city of <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s>, also known as <s>Premanagara</s>, there was a certain king. He had five sons. In his old age, he deliberated in his mind thus: 'Whichever among my sons is capable of ruling the kingdom and the like, and is also loving toward me — to him I shall entrust the kingdom and the rest.' Having decided this in his mind, he outwardly conducted himself as if he were an imbecile. Seeing him thus, all people became sorrowful in their hearts. But among the sons, those of wicked conduct were secretly delighted and set about to seize the kingdom and enjoy sensual pleasures. Among them, one who was learned and wise, having shown affection to his parents even beforehand, engaged himself in service. The king, seeing his devotion, entrusted the burden of the kingdom and the rest to him. But the other sons, hearing of this, inflicted punishment and the like upon him. Seeing this, all the ministers reported the entire affair to the king.

children.text:
rājā tu tac chrutvā kṛtrima-jaḍa-svabhāvādikaṃ tyaktvā tān putrān nirasya tasmin
putre svacchandam abhiṣekaṃ kṛtavān | tathāyaṃ śrī-govinda-devaḥ sākṣād
vrajendra-kumāro'py ādhunika-bhaktānāṃ prema-tāratamyaṃ kartuṃ mauna-
mudrādikam aṅgīkṛtya rādhikayā saha virājate | atrāpi śruti-smṛti-purāṇādi-

children.translated_text: the authoritative sources are many. There, in the <s>Śrī Gopāla-tāpanī</s> (1.9-10) —

The king, hearing of this, abandoned his feigned imbecility and the like, expelled those sons, and freely performed the consecration of that [devoted] son. Likewise, this <s>Śrī Govinda-deva</s>, though directly the prince of <s>Vraja</s>, in order to test the gradation of love (<s>prema</s>) among modern devotees, having adopted the posture of silence (<s>mauna-mudrā</s>) and the like, presides together with <s>Rādhikā</s>. Here too there are many authoritative sources (<s>pramāṇa</s>) from <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, <s>Purāṇas</s>, and the like. Among them, in the <s>Śrī Gopāla-tāpanī</s> (1.9-10) —
With eyes like pure lotuses, dark as a cloud, with garments [brilliant] like lightning,
two-armed, adorned with the <s>jñāna-mudrā</s> (gesture of knowledge), wearing a forest garland, the Lord — (9)
surrounded by cowherds, cowherd women, and cows, seated beneath a celestial wish-fulfilling tree — and so on.

children.text: tam ekaṃ govindaṃ sac-cid-ānanda-vigraham ity ādi |
children.translated_text: 'That one <s>Govinda</s>, whose form is being-consciousness-bliss (<s>sac-cid-ānanda</s>)' — and so on.
Obeisance, obeisance to <s>Gopāla</s>, to the lifter of <s>Govardhana</s>, to the beloved of the cowherd women!
And thus in the <s>Ūrdhvāmnāya</s> —
<s>Gopāla</s> Himself is <s>Govinda</s>, ever manifest and unmanifest,

children.text: vṛndāvane yoga-pīṭhe sa eva satataṃ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He eternally abides in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, on the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> (mystic seat).
Even throughout the four <s>yugas</s>, He is the Lord of glorious <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
worshipped by <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd and others, and also greatly worshipped by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [Himself].
The stealer of the garments of the women of <s>Vraja</s>, the fulfiller of their vow —
of the form of a stone of consciousness and bliss, pervading the realm of <s>Vraja</s>.

Therein —
Unassailable by <s>Candrāvalī</s>, the abode of the good fortune of <s>Rādhā</s>.

children.text:
tathā hi atharva-vede-gokulāraṇye mathurā-maṇḍale vṛndāvana-madhye sahasra-
dala-padme ṣoḍaśa-dala-madhye'ṣṭa-dala-keśare govindo'pi śyāmaḥ pītāmbaro
dvibhujo mayūra-puccha-śiro veṇu-vetra-hasto nirguṇaḥ sa-guṇo nirākāraḥ sākāro
nirīhaḥ sa-ceṣṭo virājate iti |
  dve pārśve candrāvalī rādhā ca ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
And thus in the <s>Atharva Veda</s> — In the forest of <s>Gokula</s>, in the <s>Mathurā</s> region, in the midst of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, on a thousand-petaled lotus, in the center of sixteen petals, on the filaments of eight petals, <s>Govinda</s> — dark-complexioned, clad in yellow garments, two-armed, with a peacock feather on His head, holding a flute and a stick in His hands — without qualities (<s>nirguṇa</s>), with qualities (<s>saguṇa</s>), without form (<s>nirākāra</s>), with form (<s>sākāra</s>), without desire (<s>nirīha</s>), with activity (<s>saceṣṭa</s>) — presides.
On the two sides are <s>Candrāvalī</s> and <s>Rādhā</s> — and so on.
And thus the statement of the <s>Saṃmohana Tantra</s> —
I perpetually bow to <s>Rādhā</s>, the mistress of the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>,
who is accompanied by <s>Govinda</s>, devoted to abundant amorous gestures and sentiments.
And thus in the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa] —
<s>Acyuta</s>, in the form of an <s>arcā</s> (worshippable image), dwells [there] under the name <s>Govinda-svāmī</s>,

children.text: gandarvair apsarobhiś ca krīḍamānaḥ sa modate ||
children.translated_text: playing with <s>Gandharvas</s> and <s>Apsarases</s>, He delights.
And thus in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (5.1) —
The supreme Lord is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose form is being-consciousness-bliss (<s>sac-cid-ānanda</s>),
without beginning, the origin, <s>Govinda</s>, the cause of all causes.

children.text: atra śloke kṛṣṇoḥ viśeṣyaḥ | anyatrāpi govindasya viśeṣyatvam | yathā-
children.translated_text: In this verse, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the principal subject. Elsewhere too, <s>Govinda</s> is the principal subject. As follows —

children.text: vraje govinda-nāmā yaḥ paśūnām indratāṃ gataḥ |
children.translated_text: He who in <s>Vraja</s>, named <s>Govinda</s>, attained lordship over the cattle —
He Himself becomes <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, because of attracting the mind, eyes, and the like.
And in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (5.39) —
Abiding in the forms of <s>Rāma</s> and others by a fixed measure of potencies (<s>kalā</s>),
He made various descents (<s>avatāra</s>) in the worlds; but

children.text: kṛṣṇaḥ svayaṃ samabhavat paramaḥ pumān yo
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is the supreme person (<s>puruṣa</s>), Himself appeared —
I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primordial person.

children.text:
ṭīkā ca-yo govindo rāmādi-mūrtiṣu kalā-niyamena tiṣṭhan san nānāvatāram
akarot, sa devaḥ svayaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ samabhavan taṃ bhajāmīti |
children.translated_text: And the commentary: '<s>Govinda</s>, who, abiding in the forms of <s>Rāma</s> and others by a fixed measure of potencies, made various descents — that deity Himself became <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; Him I worship.' Thus.

children.text:
śrī-gopāla-tāpanyāṃ (1.35, 39-42, 45)-
kṛṣṇāya gopīnāthāya govindāya namo namaṃ ||
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Śrī Gopāla-tāpanī</s> (1.35, 39-42, 45) —
Obeisance, obeisance to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to the Lord of the cowherd women, to <s>Govinda</s>!
And thus —
To Him who delights in playing the flute, the cowherd, the crusher of the serpent,
who sports on the banks of the <s>Kālindī</s>, who wears swinging earrings,
who is garlanded with the lotus-faces of the cowherd women, skilled in dancing —
obeisance to the protector of those who bow down, obeisance, obeisance to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>!
Obeisance to the destroyer of sins, to the lifter of <s>Govardhana</s>,
to the ender of <s>Pūtanā</s>'s life, to the stealer of <s>Tṛṇāvarta</s>'s breath!
To the partless one, the deluder, the pure one, the enemy of the impure,
to the non-dual, the great one — obeisance, obeisance to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>!

children.text:
keśava kleśa-haraṇa nārāyaṇa janārdana |
govinda paramānanda māṃ samuddhara mādhava || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
O <s>Keśava</s>, remover of affliction! O <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>!
O <s>Govinda</s>, supreme bliss! O <s>Mādhava</s>, deliver me! — and so on.

children.text:
tatra ūrdhvāmnāye-
śrīman-madana-gopālo'py atraiva supratiṣṭhitaḥ | iti |
children.translated_text:
There, in the <s>Ūrdhvāmnāya</s> —
'Glorious <s>Madana-gopāla</s> too is well-established here alone.' Thus.

children.text:
śrī-daśame (10.19.16)-
gopīnāṃ paramānanda āsīd govinda-darśane || iti |
children.translated_text:
In the glorious tenth [canto] (10.19.16) —
'The cowherd women experienced supreme bliss upon seeing <s>Govinda</s>.' Thus.

children.text:
tathā hi (10.21.10)-
vṛndāvane sakhi bhuvo vitanoti kīrtiṃ
yad devakī-suta-padāmbuja-labdha-lakṣmi |
govinda-veṇum anu matta-mayūra-nṛtyaṃ
prekṣādri-sānv-aparatānya-samasta-sattvam || iti |
children.translated_text:
And thus (10.21.10) —
'O friend, [<s>Vṛndāvana</s>] spreads the fame of the earth,
for it has gained the splendor of the lotus-feet of the son of <s>Devakī</s>.
Following the flute of <s>Govinda</s>, the intoxicated peacocks dance,
and all creatures on the mountain-peaks watch, oblivious to everything else.' Thus.
And thus in the <s>Śrī Govinda-līlāmṛta</s> (21.28) —
This pure bank called <s>Śrī Govinda-sthala</s>, the seat of union with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
the crown of <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s>, bowing down in sequence all around, resembling a tortoise-seat,
rich with rows of bowers and foliage, with a beautiful whorl of jeweled pavilions, with golden plantain-trees
as filaments — she beheld [it as] equal to a lotus of a thousand petals.
<s>Pārvatī</s> said:
What is the wonder of <s>Govinda</s>, whose form embodies beauty?

children.text: tad ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi kathayasva dayā-nidhe ||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear about that — please tell me, O treasury of compassion!
In the <s>Śrī Padma Purāṇa</s> (5.69.79-85) —
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
In the midst of delightful <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, adorned with charming anklets,
decorated with the branches and foliage of excellent trees within a <s>yojana</s> —
in its midst, in a lovely pavilion, the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> (mystic seat) blazes forth,
octagonal in construction, enchanting with manifold radiance.
Upon it, an auspicious throne of rubies and gems,
on that, a blooming lotus whose whorl (<s>karṇikā</s>) is the abode of bliss.

children.text: govindasya paraṃ sthānaṃ kim asya mahimocyate |
children.translated_text: The supreme abode of <s>Govinda</s> — what can be said of its glory?
It is served by the assembly of cowherd women dwelling in the sacred mantra of <s>Govinda</s>,
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, of divine form and youthfulness befitting <s>Vraja</s>, the Lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
the Lord of <s>Vraja</s>, of eternal sovereignty, the sole beloved of the children of <s>Vraja</s>,
in budding adolescence blossoming into youth, of a form wondrous in age.
And in the <s>Varāha-saṃhitā</s> —

children.text: vṛndāvane tu govindaṃ ye paśyanti vasundhare |
children.translated_text: Those who behold <s>Govinda</s> in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, O Earth,

children.text: na te yama-puraṃ yānti yānti puṇya-kṛtāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: do not go to the city of <s>Yama</s> — they go to the destination of the meritorious.

children.text:
asya ṭīkā ca-atha sarvāsām arcānāṃ darśana-māhātmyaṃ vadan upary upari
sphūrtyā śrīmad-arcā-viśeṣāyamāṇasya sākṣād-bhagavataḥ śrī-govinda-devasya
darśana-māhātmyam āha vṛndāvana iti |
children.translated_text: And its commentary — Now, while describing the glory of beholding all <s>arcā</s> images, rising higher and higher in manifestation, the glory of beholding the directly present <s>Bhagavān Śrī Govinda-deva</s> is stated as the supreme — 'in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>' and so on.
<s>Śrī Varāha</s> said:

children.text: karṇikā tan mahad dhāma govinda-sthānam avyayam |
children.translated_text: The whorl (<s>karṇikā</s>) is that great abode, the imperishable seat of <s>Govinda</s>,
above it, upon a golden seat, adorned with a jeweled pavilion.
And thus in the <s>Varāha Tantra</s>, in the fifth chapter, as follows —
And thus —
In the whorl, the great <s>līlā</s> (divine play), the essence of that play, upon that mountain,
where <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> would be the Lord of the eternal <s>Vṛndā</s>-forest.

children.text: kṛṣṇo govindatāṃ prāptaḥ kim anyair bahu-bhāṣitaiḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has attained the status of <s>Govinda</s> — what need of many words about others?
The third petal, beautiful, supremely excellent above all —
And thus —
The beloved abode of <s>Govinda</s> — what can be said of its glory?
<s>Govinda</s> abiding there, the beloved of the assembly of cowherd women,
of divine form and youthfulness befitting <s>Vraja</s>, the increaser of the cowherd women's love,
the Lord of <s>Vraja</s>, of regulated sovereignty, the sole beloved of the children of <s>Vraja</s>.
The Earth said:
The supreme cause, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, called <s>Govinda</s>, the highest of the high,
the Lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, eternal, the sole cause of the unqualified (<s>nirguṇa</s>).
And thus —
<s>Varāha</s> said:
<s>Govinda</s> together with <s>Rādhā</s>, seated on a golden throne,
of the beauty and loveliness described before, divinely ornamented, supremely beautiful,
gracefully bent in a triple curve (<s>tribhaṅga</s>), charmingly tender, the star of the eyes of the cowherd women.
There, upon the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>, surrounded by a golden throne,
the principal beloved companions of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, full of passionate ardor in every limb,
<s>Lalitā</s> and the others are the <s>prakṛtis</s> (potencies); <s>Rādhikā</s> is the original <s>Prakṛti</s> (<s>mūla-prakṛti</s>).

children.text: saṃmukhe lalitā devī śyāmalāpi ca vāyave |
children.translated_text: In front is the goddess <s>Lalitā</s>, and <s>Śyāmalā</s> [is positioned] in the direction of <s>Vāyu</s> (northwest),
on the other [side is] glorious <s>Madhumatī</s>; in the northeast, <s>Dhanyā</s>, beloved of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: viśākhā ca tathā pūrve śaivyā cāgnau tataḥ param |
children.translated_text: and <s>Viśākhā</s> in the east, <s>Śaivyā</s> in the direction of <s>Agni</s> (southeast), then

children.text: padmā ca dakṣiṇe bhadrā nairṛte kramaśaḥ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Padmā</s> in the south, <s>Bhadrā</s> in the southwest — stationed in order.
At the corner of the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>, the lovely beloved <s>Candrāvalī</s>,

children.text: prakṛty aṣṭau tad anyāś ca pradhānāḥ kṛṣṇa-vallabhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: these eight <s>prakṛtis</s>, and others too, are the principal beloved companions of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
The foremost and original <s>prakṛti</s> is <s>Rādhikā</s>, supreme in every way.

children.text: citrarekhā ca vṛndā ca candrā madana-sundarī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Citrarekhā</s> and <s>Vṛndā</s> and <s>Candrā</s> and <s>Madana-sundarī</s>,
<s>Supriyā</s> and <s>Madhumatī</s>, <s>Śaśīrekhā</s>, <s>Haripriyā</s>,

children.text: saṃmukhādi-krame dikṣu vidikṣu ca tathā sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: stationed in the cardinal and intermediate directions in the order of [the position] facing [<s>Govinda</s>] and so on.
The sixteen supreme <s>prakṛtis</s>, the principal beloved companions of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: vṛndāvaneśvarī rādhā tavad tu lalitā priyā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, the queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — and then <s>Lalitā</s>, the beloved [of <s>Govinda</s>].
In the <s>Gautamīya Tantra</s> —
Set upon a jeweled throne attached to a mountain of gems,
situated in a golden pavilion amidst wish-fulfilling trees.

children.text:
ity anena govindasyaiva viśeṣaṇam iti vivecanīyam | tāpanī ca- tam ekaṃ govindaṃ
sac-cid-ānanda-vigraham iti |
children.translated_text: By this, it is to be discerned that [these descriptions] are qualifications of <s>Govinda</s> Himself. And the <s>Tāpanī</s> [says]: 'That one <s>Govinda</s>, whose form is being-consciousness-bliss.'
And by the venerable feet of <s>Śrī Jayadeva</s> (<s>Gītagovinda</s> 2.19) —
'I behold <s>Govinda</s> surrounded by the assembly of beautiful women of <s>Vraja</s>, and I rejoice.'
In the <s>Śrī Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</s> (2.1.43) —
<s>Līlā</s> (divine play), love (<s>prema</s>), the excellence of the beloved, the sweetness of flute and form —
these four are declared to be the unique [attributes] of <s>Govinda</s>.
In the same work (1.2.239) —
Smiling, familiar with the triple curve, casting a wide sidelong glance,
with a fresh sprout-like lip resting on the flute, radiant with a peacock feather —
do not look upon this form of <s>Hari</s> called <s>Govinda</s>, near <s>Keśī-tīrtha</s>,

children.text: mā prekṣiṣṭhās tava yadi sakhe bandhu-sange'sti raṅgaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O friend, if you still have attachment to the company of kinsmen!
In the <s>Śrī Dāna-keli-kaumudī</s> —

children.text:
arjunaḥ: bisāhe | idaṃ bi thoa ccea | tā suṇāhi | so kira assuda-ara-sāhammo
sammohaṇa-māhurā-bhara-ṇabbo sabbobari virehanto pia-baassassa saala-goula-
baittaṇeṇa goindāhisea-mahūsabo kassa bā gabbaṃ ṇa kkhu khabbedi ?
|[*ENDNOTE #2]
children.translated_text: <s>Arjuna</s>: O merchant woman! This too is just so! Then listen! That one — who is of unprecedented, terrible prowess (<s>dharma</s>), overflowing with the weight of enchanting sweetness, shining supremely above all, renowned as <s>Govinda</s> by the lordship of the entire <s>Gokula</s>-community of the dear one [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] — whose heart does he not agitate?

children.text:
ity evambhūtasya mauna-mudrādikaṃ prakāśya vigrahavat sthitasya śrī-govinda-
devasya prakaṭa-līlā-kāle mauna-mudrādikam ācchāditam abhavat | tathā ca-
prakaṭa-līlā-kāle bhaktānāṃ bhakti-sadarśanārthaṃ prakaṭitam eva | tatra śrī-
gopāla-tāpanyādi-prasiddhaṃ-kadācit prakaṭībhūya (1.10) dvibhujaṃ mauna-
mudrāḍhyaṃ iti ca |
children.translated_text: Having thus revealed the <s>mauna-mudrā</s> (gesture of silence) and the like of one who is of this nature, during the time of the manifest <s>līlā</s> (divine play) of Śrī <s>Govindadeva</s>, who was standing in the form of an image (<s>vigraha</s>), the <s>mauna-mudrā</s> and the like were concealed. And thus — during the time of the manifest <s>līlā</s>, it was revealed for the purpose of showing devotion to the devotees. In that regard, what is well-known from the <s>Gopāla-tāpanī</s> and the like — 'having sometimes become manifest' (1.10) — 'two-armed, adorned with the <s>mauna-mudrā</s>' — and so on.
Moreover, in the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha</s> (153) —

children.text:
tad evaṃ tatra śrī-kṛṣṇa-līlā dvividhā aprakaṭa-rūpā prakaṭa-rūpā ca |
prāpañcika-lokāprakaṭatvāt tat-prakaṭatvāc ca | tatrāprakaṭā -
children.translated_text: Thus, in that [context], the <s>līlā</s> of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is twofold: in unmanifest form (<s>aprakaṭa-rūpā</s>) and in manifest form (<s>prakaṭa-rūpā</s>) — because of being unmanifest to the people of the material world, and because of being manifest to them [respectively]. Among these, the unmanifest [is described as follows] —

children.text: yatrāsau saṃsthitaḥ kṛṣṇas tribhiḥ śaktyā samāhitaḥ |

children.translated_text: the all-pervading Lord (<s>Vibhu</s>), together with <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Pradyumna</s>, and <s>Rukmiṇī</s>. [GTU 2.36]
Where <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is situated, endowed with three powers (<s>śakti</s>),

children.text:
mathurā-tattva-pratipādaka-śrī-gopāla-tāpany-ādau - cintāmaṇi-prakara-sadmasu-
kalpa-vṛkṣa [BhP 5.40] ity ādi vṛndāvana-tattva-pratipādaka-brahma-saṃhitādau ca
prakaṭa-līlātaḥ kiñcid vilakṣaṇatvena dṛṣṭā, prāpañcika-lokais tad-vastubhiś
cāmiśrā, kālavad-ādi-madhyāvasāna-pariccheda-rahita-sva-pravāhā, yādavendratva-
vraja-yuvarājatvādy-ucitāharahar-mahā-sabhopaveśa-gocāraṇa-vinodādi-lakṣaṇā
| prakaṭa-rūpā tu śrī-vigrahavat kālādibhir aparicchedyaiva satī bhagavad-
icchātmaka-svarūpa-śaktyaiva labdhārambha-samāpanā prāpañcikāprāpañcika-loka-
vastu-saṃvalitā tadīya-janmādi-lakṣaṇā |
children.translated_text: In the <s>Gopāla-tāpanī</s> and the like, which establish the reality of <s>Mathurā</s>, and in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> and the like, which establish the reality of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — '<s>cintāmaṇi</s>-jeweled abodes, <s>kalpa-vṛkṣa</s> [wish-fulfilling trees]' [BhP 5.40] — [the unmanifest <s>līlā</s>] is seen as somewhat different from the manifest <s>līlā</s>: unmixed with the worldly people and worldly objects; its own stream without the divisions of beginning, middle, and end like time; characterized by daily great assembly-sitting, cow-herding pastimes, and the like befitting [his being] the lord of the <s>Yādavas</s> and the young prince of <s>Vraja</s>. The manifest form, however — like the divine image (<s>vigraha</s>), though it cannot be delimited by time and the like — has its commencement and conclusion brought about by the Lord's own intrinsic power (<s>svarūpa-śakti</s>) which is of the nature of his will; it is intertwined with both worldly and non-worldly beings and objects, and is characterized by his birth and the like.

children.text:
tatrāprakaṭā dvividhā | mantropāsanāmayī svārasikī ca | prathamā yathā tat-tad-
ekatara-sthānādi-niyata-sthitikā tat-tan-mantra-dhyāna-mayī | yathā bṛhad-dhyāna-
ratnābhiṣekādi-prastāvaḥ krama-dīpikāyām | yathā vā --
children.translated_text: The unmanifest [<s>līlā</s>] is further twofold: that consisting in <s>mantra</s>-worship (<s>mantropāsanāmayī</s>) and the spontaneous (<s>svārasikī</s>). The first is as follows: situated with a fixed location at one or another [sacred] place, consisting in meditation on this or that <s>mantra</s> — as in the context of the great <s>dhyāna-ratnābhiṣeka</s> and the like in the <s>Krama-dīpikā</s>. Or as —

children.text:
atha dhyānaṃ pravakṣyāmi sarva-pāpa-praṇāśanam |
pītāmbara-dharaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ puṇḍarīka-nibhekṣaṇam || ity ādi gautamīya-tantre |
children.translated_text: 'Now I shall declare the meditation that destroys all sins: upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> wearing a yellow garment, with eyes like lotus petals' — and so on, in the <s>Gautamīya-tantra</s>.
Or as —
Playing the flute, with eyes wide like lotus petals,
with a peacock-feather crest, with a beautiful body like a dark cloud,
with the special splendor beautiful as ten million <s>Kandarpa</s>s (Cupids),
that primeval person <s>Govinda</s> — him I worship.

children.text:
ālola-candraka-lasad-vanamālya-vaṃśī-
ratnāṅgadaṃ praṇaya-keli-kalā-vilāsam |
śyāmaṃ tri-bhaṅga-lalitaṃ niyata-prakāśaṃ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi || iti brahma-saṃhitāyām [5.39-40] |
children.translated_text: that primeval person <s>Govinda</s> — him I worship. Thus in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> [5.39-40].
With a swaying garland of forest flowers, a flute, jeweled armlets, and the playful arts of amorous <s>līlā</s>; dark-complexioned, gracefully bent in three places, of eternally manifest [beauty],

children.text: homas tu pūrvavat kāryo govinda-prītaye tataḥ ity-ādy-anantaraṃ -
children.translated_text: The <s>homa</s> (fire-offering) should be performed as before, for the pleasure of <s>Govinda</s> — and immediately after this [it is stated] —

children.text: govindaṃ manasā dhyāyet gavāṃ madhye sthitaṃ śubham |
children.translated_text: One should meditate with the mind upon <s>Govinda</s>, standing amidst the cows, auspicious,
adorned with a peacock-feather crest, devoted to playing the flute,

children.text:
gopī-janaiḥ parivṛtaṃ vanya-puṣpāvataṃsakam || iti bodhāyana-karma-vipāka-
prāyaścitta-smṛtau |
children.translated_text: surrounded by the <s>gopī</s>-folk, wearing a garland of forest flowers. Thus in the <s>Bodhāyana-karma-vipāka-prāyaścitta-smṛti</s>.

children.text:
tad u hovāca hairaṇyo gopa-veśam abhrābhaṃ taruṇaṃ kalpa-drumāśritam | tadiha
ślokā bhavanti --
children.translated_text: The golden one [<s>Hiraṇya</s>] then said: 'In the attire of a cowherd, dark as a cloud, youthful, taking shelter of a wish-fulfilling tree.' Therein the verses are as follows —
With eyes like noble lotus-blossoms, dark as a cloud, with garments [bright] as lightning,
two-armed, adorned with the <s>mauna-mudrā</s> (gesture of silence), the lord wearing a forest-garland,
surrounded by cowherds, <s>gopīs</s>, and cows, taking shelter at the foot of a divine tree,
endowed with divine ornaments, seated in the midst of red lotuses,
served by breezes mingling with the waves of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) river —

children.text: cintayaṃś cetasā kṛṣṇaṃ mukto bhavati saṃsṛteḥ ||
children.translated_text: one who meditates on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with the mind is liberated from the cycle of rebirth.

children.text:
iti śrī-gopāla-tāpanyām [1.11-15] - govindaṃ gokulānandaṃ sac-cid-ānanda-vigraham
[GTU 1.37] ity ādi ca |
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Gopāla-tāpanī</s> [1.11-15] — '<s>Govinda</s>, the bliss of <s>Gokula</s>, whose form is being, consciousness, and bliss (<s>sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha</s>)' [GTU 1.37] — and so on.

children.text: atha svārasikī ca yathodāhṛtam eva skānde --
children.translated_text: Now the spontaneous (<s>svārasikī</s>) [unmanifest <s>līlā</s>] is as cited, for instance, in the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa] —

children.text:
vatsair vatsatarībhiś ca sadā krīḍati mādhavaḥ |
vṛndāvanāntaragataḥ sa-rāmo bālakaiḥ saha || ity ādi |
children.translated_text: '<s>Mādhava</s> (Kṛṣṇa) always plays with calves and young cows, within <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, together with <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma) and the cowherd boys.' And so on.

children.text:
tatra ca-kārāt śrī-gopendrādayo gṛhyante | rāma-śabdena rohiṇy api | tathā tenaiva
krīḍatīty ādinā vrajāgamana-śayanādi-līlāpi | krīḍā-śabdasya vihārārthatvād
vihārasya nānā-sthānānusāraṇa-rūpatvād eka-sthāna-niṣṭhāyā
mantropāsanāmayyā bhidyate'sau | yathāvasara-vividha-svecchāmayī svārasikī |
evaṃ brahma-saṃhitāyām --
children.translated_text: By the word 'ca' (and) therein, Śrī <s>Gopendra</s> (Nanda) and others are included. By the word '<s>Rāma</s>', <s>Rohiṇī</s> too [is included]. Similarly, by 'plays with him' and the like, the <s>līlā</s> of arriving at <s>Vraja</s>, going to sleep, and the like [is included]. Because the word '<s>krīḍā</s>' (play) has the meaning of 'pastime' (<s>vihāra</s>), and because a pastime has the nature of moving to various places, it differs from the <s>mantra</s>-worship type that is fixed at a single place. The spontaneous [type] consists in various activities according to [the Lord's] own will at the appropriate occasions. Similarly, in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> —

children.text:
cintāmaṇi-prakara-sadmasu kalpa-vṛkṣa-
lakṣāvṛteṣu surabhir abhipālayantam
lakṣmī-sahasra-śata-sambhrama-sevyamānaṃ
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi || [BrahmaS 5.28] iti |
children.translated_text: served with great reverence by hundreds of thousands of <s>Lakṣmīs</s> — that primeval person <s>Govinda</s>, him I worship. [<s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> 5.28]
In the abodes made of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> jewels, surrounded by millions of wish-fulfilling trees, tending the cows (<s>surabhī</s>),

children.text:
atra kathā gānaṃ nātyaṃ gamanam api vaṃśī [BrahmaS 5.52] ity atrānusandheyam
| tatra nānā-līlā-pravāha-rūpatayā svārasikī gaṅgeva |
children.translated_text: Here, what should be further investigated is [the verse] 'there [are] stories, songs, drama, going about, and the flute' [<s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> 5.52]. Among these, by virtue of being in the form of a stream of various <s>līlās</s>, the spontaneous [type] is like the <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Now, regarding the unmanifest [<s>līlā</s>], he speaks of the one consisting in <s>mantra</s>-worship —
[may] <s>Govinda</s> [protect me] during the forenoon, holding his flute. [BhP 6.8.2]
May <s>Keśava</s> protect me in the morning with his mace,

children.text:
ātta-veṇur iti viśeṣeṇa govindaḥ śrī-vṛndāvana-mathurā-prasiddha-mahā-yoga-
pīṭhayos tan-nāmnaiva sahitau prasiddhau | tau ca tatra tatra prāpañcika-loka-
dṛṣṭyāṃ śrīmat-pratimākāreṇābhātaḥ svajana-dṛṣṭyāṃ sākṣād-rūpa-vṛnda-
prakaraṇa eva etau paṭhitau | tataś ca nārāyaṇa-varmākhya-mantropāsya-
devatātvena (śrī-gopāla-tāpanyādi-prasiddha-svatantra-mantrāntaropāsya-
devatātvena) ca mantropāsanā-mayyām idam udāhṛtam ||
children.translated_text: 'Holding his flute' — by this specification, <s>Govinda</s> [is identified with] the great <s>yoga-pīṭhas</s> (sacred seats of power) well-known in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> and <s>Mathurā</s>, which are famous by that very name together [with him]. And those two [<s>Govinda</s> forms], in those respective places, appear to the vision of worldly people in the form of a sacred image (<s>pratimā</s>), [but] to the vision of his own people, [they appear] directly as a multitude of forms. These two are cited in [the context of] <s>mantra</s>-worship, because of their being the presiding deity of the <s>mantra</s> known as the <s>Nārāyaṇa-varma</s> and because of being the presiding deity of an independent <s>mantra</s> well-known from the <s>Gopāla-tāpanī</s> and the like.
Similarly, in the <s>Lalita-mādhava</s> (7.33f) —

children.text:
rādhikā (śrī-kṛṣṇa-mukhendum avalokya): hanta ! hanta ! ṇibbha-rūkkaṇḍidā e
mama muddhattaṇaṃ, jaṃ goindassa paḍimaṃ jebba goindaṃ maṇṇemi |
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhikā</s> (seeing the moon-like face of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>): 'Alas! Alas! My foolishness is thoroughly exposed — that I mistake the image of <s>Govinda</s> for <s>Govinda</s> himself!' [in Prakrit]
Similarly, <s>Rādhikā</s> (7.35) —

children.text: puro dhinvan ghrāṇaṃ parimilati so'yaṃ parimalo
children.translated_text: 'This fragrance, wafting before [me], overpowers [my] sense of smell;
this expanse of deep-dark radiance captivates [my] eyes;

children.text: svaraḥ so'yaṃ dhīras taralayati karṇau mama balād
children.translated_text: this deep, steady tone forcibly agitates my ears —
ah, this image has attained the very nature of <s>Govinda</s>!'
In the <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇa] —
'Having seen <s>Govinda</s> being swung on a swing, <s>Madhusūdana</s> standing on a platform,

children.text: rathe ca vāmanaṃ dṛṣṭvā punar janma na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Vāmana</s> on a chariot — one is not born again.'

children.text:
dvārakāyāṃ śrī-puruṣottame ca | etat-padya-dvaye govinda-śabdas tu sarva-
prakāśa-mūla-bhūtasya śrī-vṛndāvana-nāthasya govindasya prakāśāpekṣayā | sa
ca prakāśas tu na bhedeṣu gaṇyate sa hi na pṛthak iti (LBhāg 1.1.20) |
children.translated_text: In <s>Dvārakā</s> and at Śrī <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Jagannātha Purī). In these two verses, the word '<s>Govinda</s>' is used with reference to the manifestation of <s>Govinda</s>, the Lord of Śrī <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, who is the root of all manifestations. And that manifestation 'is not counted among differences; for it is not separate' (LBhāg 1.1.20).

children.text:
dakṣiṇābhimukhaṃ devaṃ dolārūḍhaṃ sureśvaram |
sakṛd dṛṣṭvā tu govindaṃ mucyate brahma-hatyāyāḥ |
vartamānaṃ ca yat pāpaṃ yad bhūtaṃ yad bhaviṣyati |
children.translated_text: one is freed from the sin of killing a <s>Brāhmaṇa</s>. Whatever sin exists in the present, whatever existed in the past, whatever will exist in the future —
all of it is quickly burnt away by the chanting of the fire [that is the name] of <s>Govinda</s>.

children.text: govindeti yathā proktaṃ bhaktyā vā bhakti-varjitam |
children.translated_text: However the [name] '<s>Govinda</s>' is uttered — with devotion or without devotion —
it burns all sins, like the fire at the end of an age, risen up.'
'Having seen just once <s>Govinda</s>, the Lord facing south, mounted on a swing, the lord of the gods —

children.text: govinda-nāmā yaḥ kaścin naro bhavati bhūtale |
children.translated_text: Whoever on this earth bears the name <s>Govinda</s> —

children.text: tan nāsti karmajaṃ loke vāṅ-mānasam eva vā |
children.translated_text: there is no sin born of action in this world, whether of speech or mind,

children.text: yan na kṣapayate pāpaṃ kalau govinda-kīrtanam ||
children.translated_text: that the chanting of <s>Govinda</s> does not destroy in the <s>Kali</s> age.
What need is there of the elaboration of <s>Vedas</s>, <s>Āgamas</s>, and <s>Śāstras</s>?
What purpose is served by numerous <s>tīrthas</s> (pilgrimage sites)?
If you desire the cause of liberation,
cry out clearly: '<s>Govinda</s>, <s>Govinda</s>!'
In the <s>Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s> (1.8.50-51) —
In <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, in the wish-fulfilling trees, in the golden abodes,
at the great <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>, on the jeweled throne —
there sits the very son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s> (<s>Vrajendranandana</s>),
named Śrī <s>Govinda</s>, who is directly the enchanter of Cupid.

children.text:
(1.5.221, 225-6)
yāṅra dhyāna nija-loke kare padmāsana
aṣṭādaśākṣara-mantre kare upāsana
sākṣāt vrajendra-suta ithe nāhi āna
yebā ajñe kare tāṅre pratimā-hena jñāna
sei aparādhe tāra nāhika nistāra
ghora narakete paḍe ki baliba āra
children.translated_text: (1.5.221, 225-6) 'He upon whom <s>Padmāsana</s> (<s>Brahmā</s>) meditates in his own world, whom he worships with the eighteen-syllable <s>mantra</s> — he is directly the son of the lord of <s>Vraja</s>, there is no other. Whoever out of ignorance considers him to be [merely] an image — by that offense, there is no deliverance for him; into terrible hell he falls — what more can be said?'
In the <s>Brahma-vaivarta</s> [Purāṇa] —
'Having obtained human birth, which is rarer than rare and desired by the gods,

children.text: yair āśrito na govindas tair ātmā vañcitaś ciram ||
children.translated_text: those who have not taken shelter of <s>Govinda</s> have cheated themselves for a long time.'

children.text: draṣṭuṃ na yogyā vaktuṃ vā triṣu lokeṣu te'dhamāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Not worthy of being seen or spoken of in the three worlds are those lowest [of beings]
who are averse to the two lotus feet of Śrī <s>Govinda</s>.'

children.text:
asau rasika-śekharo govinda-devaḥ kadācid ṛtu-bhedena sva-sevā-kāle yathocita-
bhojanādi-nimittāya svādhikāra-niyuktena kenāpi saha-gopa-kiśora-rūpeṇa rātrau
svapna-sphūrtyā sākṣād rūpeṇa vā kathopakathanaṃ kurute | etac ca loka-
paramparayā śrūyate | kintu atīva-rahasyatvāt ācārya-vacanādy-anurodhāc ca
prakāśya na likhyate ity ādi |
children.translated_text: This <s>Govindadeva</s>, the crest-jewel of connoisseurs (<s>rasika-śekhara</s>), sometimes, according to the season, during his time of service (<s>sevā</s>), for the purpose of appropriate meals and the like, together with some [companion] in the form of a cowherd youth appointed to his domain, converses at night — either through the revelation in a dream or in his direct form. And this is heard through the tradition of the people. But because of its extreme secrecy and in accordance with the words of the <s>ācāryas</s>, it is not revealed in writing — and so on.
Śrī <s>Pārvatī</s> said —

children.text: ko'sau govinda-devo'sti yas tvayā sūcitaḥ purā |
children.translated_text: 'Who is this <s>Govindadeva</s> whom you previously indicated?

children.text: kīdṛśaṃ tasya māhātmyaṃ kiṃ svarūpaṃ ca śaṅkara ||
children.translated_text: What is his greatness? And what is his essential nature, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>?'
Now he cites passages from the <s>Ūrdhvāmnāya-tantra</s> —
Śrī <s>Mahādeva</s> said —
'<s>Gopāla</s> himself is <s>Govinda</s>, always manifest and unmanifest,

children.text: vṛndāvane yoga-pīṭhe sa eva satataṃ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: situated eternally at the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.
Through all four ages (<s>yugas</s>), [he is] the lord of Śrīmat <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
worshipped by <s>Nanda Gopa</s> and others, and supremely worshipped by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself.
The stealer of the garments of the <s>Vraja</s> women, the fulfiller of their vows,
of the form of a divine consciousness-bliss stone (<s>cid-ānanda-śilā</s>), pervading the <s>Vraja-maṇḍala</s>.
Commencing from adolescence, existing day by day,
with mouth filled with betel, the life-deity of <s>Rādhikā</s>.
A pond named <s>Brahma-kuṇḍa</s>, with four banks set with jewels, full of swans and lotuses,
[lies] to the south of him.
A jeweled pavilion shines, surrounded by <s>mandāra</s> trees;
in its midst [is] the supreme sovereignty-seat called <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>.
Delighted by the abundant sovereign <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic rapture) of the queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>),
here <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is conquered by <s>Rādhā</s> of the confident smile.

children.text: tasyāṃ go śrīḥ sadā vṛndā vīrā cākhila-sādhanā |
children.translated_text: In her [service]: <s>Go</s> [is] <s>Śrī</s> (fortune), eternally; <s>Vṛndā</s>; <s>Vīrā</s>; and [she who is] the accomplisher of all <s>sādhanas</s>.
To the east of the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>, there stands [the deity] named <s>Līlāvatī</s>;
to the south stands <s>Śyāmā</s>, delighting in the amorous pastimes of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text: paścime saṃsthitā devī bhoginī nāma sarvadā |
children.translated_text: To the west stands the goddess named <s>Bhoginī</s>, always;

children.text: uttaratra sthitā nityaṃ siddheśī nāma devatā |
children.translated_text: to the north stands eternally the deity named <s>Siddheśī</s>.

children.text: pañca-vaktraḥ sthitaḥ pūrve daśa-vaktraś ca dakṣiṇe ||
children.translated_text: Five-headed [<s>Śiva</s>] stands to the east; ten-headed [<s>Rāvaṇa</s> / another guardian] to the south;
four-headed [<s>Brahmā</s>] to the west; thousand-headed [<s>Ananta</s>] to the north.
And [a female attendant] with a golden staff in hand stands everywhere in [the role of] governance,
[named] <s>Madanonmodinī</s>, a dear companion (<s>sakhī</s>) of <s>Rādhikā</s>;
she casts <s>Govinda</s>, overwhelmed by [<s>Rādhā</s>'s] sulky pride (<s>māna</s>), at [<s>Rādhā</s>'s] feet.
Even to the mind of the lord of <s>Rati</s> (Cupid), who is himself the giver of pride,
here, in the abode of the form of the divine couple, the pavilion of desire,
with the sweetnesses of fresh sapphires [dark as] <s>Hari</s>'s jewel,
at every step, the palace of Cupid is piled high.
After the two [names of] Cupid, [comes] the auspicious word 'Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>';
then '<s>Govindāya</s>'; after that '<s>Svāhā</s>' — this is the twelve-syllable [<s>mantra</s>].
The great <s>mantra</s> of <s>Govinda</s>, which in the [proper] time bears the [mood of] <s>pūrvānurāga</s> (initial passionate love).
Hereafter I shall declare <s>Govinda</s> in the form of the divine couple (<s>yugalātmaka</s>).
'<s>Lakṣmī-Manmatha-Rādhā</s>' — then '<s>Govindābhyāṃ namaḥ</s>' — [this is] the word-formula.
By the mere knowledge of this [<s>mantra</s>], <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> are pleased.

children.text: anayos tu ṛṣiḥ kāmo virāṭ chanda udāhṛtaḥ |
children.translated_text: Of these two [<s>mantras</s>], the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) is <s>Kāma</s> (Cupid); the <s>chandas</s> (meter) is declared to be <s>Virāṭ</s>;
the presiding deity is eternal <s>Govinda</s> — indeed <s>Rādhā-Govinda</s>.
The <s>Śakti</s> who is the sovereign of the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>, with the six-limbed [mantra] and <s>kāma-bījas</s>,
One should meditate on <s>Govinda Deva</s>, sweet as a fresh rain-cloud, dancing in divine <s>līlā</s>,
with his sparkling wrestler's girdle, and supported by the jewel-staffed flute in both hands,
charming with the unfastened bright yellow garment (<s>pītāmbara</s>) with its broad hem-tassels in pairs,
the full-glorious king of enchantment (<s>Mohanendra</s>), whose right foot-stalk is trodden by his other foot.
Having thus meditated, one should chant the <s>mantra</s> up to four hundred thousand [times];
at the end of the <s>homa</s> with sesame and ghee, one should worship the Lord and Lady of the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>.
With <s>campaka</s>, <s>aśoka</s>, <s>tulasī</s>, and <s>kahlāra</s> [lilies], and with lotuses,
one directly sees with one's own eyes the divine couple <s>Rādhā</s>-<s>Govinda</s>.
<s>Śrīman Madana-Gopāla</s> too is well-established right here.
<s>Gopāla</s> has a youthful (<s>kaiśora</s>) form; <s>Govinda</s> has a mature form.
Between the two, by gradation, <s>Gopīnātha</s> is supremely beautiful.
<s>Gopāla</s> is of the <s>dhīroddhata</s> (haughty-heroic) type, while [<s>Gopīnātha</s>] is called the <s>dhīrodātta</s> (noble-heroic) type;
<s>Govinda</s>, the Lord of the <s>gopīs</s>, is of the <s>dhīra-lalita</s> (gallant-heroic) form.
<s>Gopāla</s> has a lion-waist and a gracefully three-bent (<s>tribhaṅga-lalita</s>) form;
<s>Govinda</s>, the Lord of the <s>gopīs</s>, has a broad chest and is a <s>viṭa</s> (libertine).

children.text: trisandhyam anyad anyad dhi mādhuryaṃ govidāṃ patau |
children.translated_text: At each of the three junctions of the day, a different, different sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>) [manifests] in the Lord of the cows;
adorned with the minerals, sprouts, and the like of the caves of <s>Govardhana</s>,
having surpassed childhood and passed beyond adolescence,
<s>Śrī Govinda</s>, entering the state of <s>Kandarpa</s> (the god of love), shines resplendent.
In this <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>, [there are] various jewel-enchanting [features];
for the innate power of this [place] is such that it bestows satisfaction without delay.
The perfection (<s>siddhi</s>) that [takes] many years at other perfected seats (<s>siddha-pīṭhas</s>),
at the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, that is born in a single day.
In the morning, [it has] the appearance of the rising sun; in the forenoon, an auspicious hue;
at midday, [it shines] like the young sun; in the afternoon, like a lotus petal.
In the evening, [it has] the appearance of a mass of vermillion; at night, pure as the moon;
in the dark fortnights, [it has] a dark-blue lustre like the rays of an indranīla sapphire.
In the rainy season, it always shines with the lustre of green emerald grass;
in autumn, [it is] like the orb of the bright moon; in the cold season, like a ruby.
In the dewy season, [it has] the brilliance of diamond; in spring, the red of new sprouts;
in summer, [it has] the appearance of a flood of nectar — thus the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> shines resplendent.
Always covered with sweetnesses (<s>mādhurī</s>), honored by <s>Aśoka</s> and <s>Lalitā</s> [<s>sakhīs</s>],
above and around, surrounded by rays of great jewels,
unapproachable by <s>Candrāvalī</s>, [it is] the abode of <s>Rādhā</s>'s good fortune.
It is called <s>Śrī-Ratna-Maṇḍapa</s> (Jewel Pavilion) and also <s>Śṛṅgāra-Maṇḍapa</s> (Adornment Pavilion),
<s>Saubhāgya-Maṇḍapa</s> (Good-Fortune Pavilion), <s>Mahā-Mādhurya-Maṇḍapa</s> (Great-Sweetness Pavilion),
<s>Sāmrājya-Maṇḍapa</s> (Sovereignty Pavilion), and also <s>Kandarpa-Maṇḍapa</s> (Love-God Pavilion),
<s>Ānanda-Maṇḍapa</s> (Bliss Pavilion), and also <s>Surata-Maṇḍapa</s> (Love-Play Pavilion) —

children.text: ity aṣṭau yoga-pīṭhasya nāmāni śṛṇu pārvati ||
children.translated_text: these are the eight names of the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> — hear them, O <s>Pārvatī</s>.
One who recites these eight names at dawn
of the most exalted <s>Śrī Yoga-Pīṭha</s>,
brings <s>Govinda Deva</s> under [devotional] control thereby,
and attains the <s>prema</s> (divine love) of the Supreme Person.

children.text:
atha mantra-mayyāṃ sad-ācāra-vidhir likhyate | mantra-mayī dvidhā | tatra śrī-
bhāgavatādi-varṇita-janma-karma-go-cāraṇādi-līlā eka-vidhā | sā tu smaraṇa-
maṅgala-śrī-govinda-līlāmṛtādy-anusāreṇa kartavyā | dvitīyā tu arcāyamāna-
viśeṣa-mauna-mudrāḍhya-śrī-vigraha-viśeṣa-sevā | sā ca sarva-smṛti-saṃmatā śrī-
hari-bhakti-vilāse likhitāsti | tad-anusāreṇa prema-yuktayā bhaktyā kartavyā |
tasmāt kiñcit prakāśya likhyate |
children.translated_text: Now, the rules of righteous conduct (<s>sad-ācāra-vidhi</s>) pertaining to the <s>mantra-mayī</s> [devotion] are written. The <s>mantra-mayī</s> is of two kinds. Of these, one kind is the <s>līlā</s> of birth, activities, cow-herding, and so on as described in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> and other [texts]. That should be performed following the <s>Smaraṇa-Maṅgala-Śrī-Govinda-Līlāmṛta</s> and similar [works]. The second is the special service of the sacred image (<s>śrī-vigraha</s>) endowed with special silent gestures (<s>mauna-mudrā</s>) and worship. And that, approved by all <s>smṛti</s> texts, is written in the <s>Śrī Hari-Bhakti-Vilāsa</s>. It should be performed in accordance with that, with devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) imbued with <s>prema</s>. Therefore, a brief account is written here.

children.text:
brāhma-muhūrtād utthāya pūjakādayaḥ sarve pārṣadāḥ sevānāmāparādha-rahitā
bhagavat-paricaryāṃ vinā prasādānnam apy asvīkurvantaḥ | kiṃ punar bhagavad-
dravyaṃ svecchayā balātkāreṇa vā | vidhivat gurvādi-praṇāma-danta-dhāvana-
yathocita-snānādi-vidhiṃ kṛtvā sva-sevāyāṃ sāvadhānāḥ śrī-mandire praviśanti |
pūjakas tu vidhivat ghaṇṭādi-vādyaṃ kṛtvā prabhoḥ śrīmad-īśvaryāś ca
prabodhanaṃ kārayet | grīṣma-śīta-varṣādy-anusāreṇa devādi-durlabha-sevāṃ
[Additional text? yathā sādhakaḥ siddha-rūpeṇa mānasīṃ līlāṃ daṇḍātmikāṃ
bhāvayet tathā tenaiva guru-paramparayā rāgānugā-matena mauna-mudrāḍhyaḥ
| daṇḍātmikā-līlā-sevā caikā nāmnā bhedaḥ pṛthag bhavet | atas tayor aikya-
sevanaṃ ca |]
children.translated_text: Rising from the <s>brāhma-muhūrta</s>, the worshiper and all attendants (<s>pārṣadas</s>), free from offenses in service, do not accept even <s>prasāda</s>-food without attending to the service of the Lord — what to speak of taking the Lord's property by one's own will or by force. Having properly performed obeisance to the <s>guru</s> and others, tooth-cleaning, bathing as appropriate, and so forth, they enter the sacred temple attentively for their own service. The worshiper, having properly sounded the bell and other instruments, should cause the awakening of the Lord and <s>Śrīmad Īśvarī</s> (the divine Goddess). According to the summer, cold, rainy, and other seasons, one should perform the service that is rare even for the gods. [Additional text: Just as the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>) should contemplate in his perfected form (<s>siddha-rūpa</s>) the mental (<s>mānasī</s>) <s>līlā</s> in the form of the daily round, so too, by the same <s>guru-paramparā</s>, in the mood of <s>rāgānugā</s> devotion, endowed with silent gestures. The daily-round <s>līlā</s> service is one [kind]; distinct by name. Therefore their unified practice [is described].]
Then the washing of the sacred face (<s>śrī-mukha-prakṣālana</s>) and so on, as in the <s>Śrī Govinda-Līlāmṛta</s> (1.24?):
Raising both fists upward,
stretching, His limbs languid with drowsiness,
with nets of teeth-rays spreading from yawns,
<s>tamāla</s>-dark, He arose from His bed.
Having risen from the excellent bed, seated on a fine seat,
bathed with water poured from golden shower-pipes,
with an excellent betel-roll fashioned from fragrant fallen leaves,
He polished His divine teeth.
Namely thus —
Similarly for <s>Śrīmad Īśvarī</s> (from <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇāhnika-Kaumudī</s> 2.49, 52):
Having risen from the bed-surface, seated on a golden seat,
the regular arrangement loosening at the close of sleep,
She, with Her lotus feet placed on the footstool,
shone then, greeted with joy by Her attendants.
Having wiped with a fine white cloth Her lovely [teeth],
She, with a piece of tooth-stick, scrubbed Her teeth,
and with a tongue-cleaner, She scraped Her tongue,
which was charming, devoted to the taste of betel, and a connoisseur of flavors.

children.text: tataḥ susvādu-miṣṭa-dadhi-samarpaṇam | tato maṅgalārātrikam | tatra dhyānam-
children.translated_text: Then the offering of delicious, sweet yogurt. Then the <s>maṅgala-āratrika</s>. The meditation therein:
Wearing a beautiful garment that shames rows of camphor upon His hips,
bearing a lovely red turban upon His excellent head, with eyes mixed with sleep,
accepting the auspicious āratrika that is wish-fulfilling and joy-giving,

children.text: govindaḥ kuśalaṃ karoti bhavato rātry-anta-kāle sadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s> bestows welfare upon you always at the close of night.
Then in winter, the wearing of the <s>phalgulā</s> (quilted winter garment):
The one called <s>phalgulā</s>, made of silk cloth,
a frost-protector obtainable at great cost,
embroidered with golden designs on every part,
resplendent from the crown of the head to both feet.

children.text:
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ vraja-rāja-putraṃ
paśyantam agnim amalaṃ bhagavantam īḍe |
children.translated_text:
I praise <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Person, the prince of <s>Vraja</s>,
who gazes upon the pure fire, the blessed Lord.
Of matchless reddish complexion,
wearing the <s>phalgulā</s> decorated with many varied gems,
wearing <s>Govinda</s>,
with a smiling face — when shall I behold [Him]?
Now, in summer, the wearing of the <s>taniyā</s> (thin summer garment):
Made of fine cloth, cut in three-part form,
adorned with gold thread and pearls on all border regions,
resplendent in the middle portion of Lord <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
I take refuge in the cooling garment that dispels the heat of summer.
The wearing of the closed jacket (<s>mukulita-kañcuka</s>):
Bearing a red turban and a robe,
and wearing upon it a variegated [garment],
bound with a closed jacket,
may <s>Śrī Govinda</s> flash forth in my heart.

children.text: tataḥ sarve militvā ārātrika-darśanam | evaṃ deva-munīndrādayo'pi gītāvādya-

children.translated_text: <s>kīrtana</s>, and so on. As in the <s>Padyāvalī</s> (22):
Then, all having gathered, the beholding of the <s>āratrika</s>. Thus even the gods, great sages, and others perform singing, instrumental music,
Cleansing the mirror of the heart, extinguishing the great forest-fire of material existence,
spreading the moonbeams of the white lotus of supreme good, the life of the bride of knowledge,
increasing the ocean of bliss, at every step [giving] the taste of full nectar,
bathing the entire self — may the <s>saṅkīrtana</s> of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> be supremely victorious!
Now, the fruit of the <s>darśana</s>:
The auspicious beholding of the <s>maṅgala-āratrika</s> grants all desires,
bestows <s>prema-bhakti</s>, and removes all bad dreams and the like.

children.text:
evaṃ pācakādayaḥ sarve sva-sva-sevāyāṃ parama-bhaktyā ca sāvadhānā vartiṣyante
| sevāyāṃ mukho'dhikārī tu sva-pratinidhiṃ karma-cāriṇam uddiśya tasmin sva-
sarva-karma samarpya sevāyāṃ sāvadhānaḥ svayaṃ kariṣyati abhāve pūjakādi-dvārā
ca | evaṃ śrīmad-īśvaryā dadhi-bhojanaṃ maṅgala-nīrājanaṃ ca kartavyam |
children.translated_text: Thus the cooks and all others should be attentive with supreme devotion in their respective services. The chief officer of service, designating his representative as the executor of actions, having entrusted all his duties to him, will himself be attentive in service — or through the worshiper and others in [his] absence. Similarly, the yogurt-offering and <s>maṅgala-nīrājana</s> for <s>Śrīmad Īśvarī</s> should be performed.

children.text:
atha śṛṅgārārātri-vidhir likhyate | tataḥ sugandha-tailādibhir mardanon-
mārjanādikaṃ hima-grīṣma-varṣādi-kālocitam uṣṇa-śītala-jalādibhiḥ snānaṃ ca,
sūkṣma-vastreṇa śrīmad-aṅga-saṃmārjanaṃ, yathā śrī-govinda-līlāmṛte (4.8-12)-
children.translated_text: Now the procedure of the <s>Śṛṅgāra-āratrika</s> (adornment āratrika) is written. Then, rubbing and cleansing with fragrant oil and the like — appropriate for the cold, hot, rainy, and other seasons — bathing with warm, cool, or other water, and wiping the sacred limbs with a fine cloth, as in the <s>Śrī Govinda-Līlāmṛta</s> (4.8–12):
When He came to the bathing platform,
His servant removed the ornaments from His body,
and the one named <s>Sāraṅga</s>, a fine newly-imported Chinese cloth,
lightly wrapped around [Him]. //8//
Having anointed [Him] with applications of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>-oil,
preceded by various soft bindings on each limb,
the one named <s>Subandha</s>, the barber's son,
with love, extended the body-massage. //9//
With joyful rubbing, the one called <s>Sugandha</s>,
always cool, with a cool, yellow [paste],
the gentle one, with a ball of fresh butter,
slowly rubbed down those limbs. //10//
With a paste moist with <s>dhātrī</s> (gooseberry) fruit, cool and fragrant,
the affectionate one, <s>Karpūra</s>, with affection, prepared
his affectionate, sleek hair. //11//
Then the servants,
with waters gathered from rows of gently heated, scented pots,
released from golden pitchers,

children.text:
iti śrī-govinda-devasya sākṣād vrajendra-nandanatvena pūjakādibhir bhāva-yuktena
manasā snānādikaṃ kartavyam | tataḥ pītāruṇādi-nānā-vidha-svarṇa-citra-vastrādi
| evaṃ svarṇa-rūpya-mauktika-ratna-jaṭita-nānālaṅkāra-guñjā-mālādi-vidagdha-
pūjakena paridhāpanīyam | kadācit sevāvasare lokottara-camatkāra-svāda-
pakvānnādikaṃ prema-yuktena manasā tat-sevā-sukha-parādhīno'rpayet |
children.translated_text:
joyfully bathed their Lord. //12//

Thus, the bathing and other [services] of <s>Śrī Govinda Deva</s>, who is directly the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, should be performed by the worshipers and others with a mind imbued with devotional feeling (<s>bhāva</s>). Then [comes the dressing with] various yellow, red, and other gold-embroidered garments. Similarly, the skilled worshiper should dress [the Lord] with various ornaments studded with gold, silver, pearls, and gems, and with <s>guñjā</s> garlands and the like. Sometimes, during the service, one should offer extraordinary, wondrous, well-cooked food and the like with a mind imbued with <s>prema</s>, absorbed in the happiness of that service.
Therein, the wearing of the jacket (<s>kañcuka</s>) and the like, as in (<s>BRS</s> 2.1.351):
With a smiling face, graced with the splendor of a pink garment worn [upon Him],
His body covered with a golden-lustrous, large jacket,

children.text: uṣṇīṣaṃ dadhad aruṇaṃ dhaṭīṃ ca citrāḥ
children.translated_text: wearing a red turban and a variegated robe,
the enemy of <s>Kaṃsa</s> bears delight for us at the great festival.
And sometimes in the costume of a chief dancer (<s>naṭa-vara</s>), as in (<s>BRS</s> 2.1.353):
With unbroken and divided cloths — white, tawny, blue, and red —
brilliant with a prominently arranged display fitted as appropriate,
this one, radiant as a young elephant-king, richly adorned for the theatrical stage,

children.text: karoti karabhoru me ghana-rucir mudaṃ mādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O beautiful-thighed one, <s>Mādhava</s>, cloud-lustrous, produces delight in me.
In the <s>Ūrdhvāmnāya</s> —
One should meditate on <s>Govinda Deva</s>, sweet as a fresh rain-cloud, dancing in divine <s>līlā</s>,
with his sparkling wrestler's girdle, and supported by the jewel-staffed flute in both hands,
charming with the unfastened bright yellow garment with its broad hem-tassels in pairs,
the full-glorious king of enchantment, whose right foot-stalk is trodden by his other foot.
Having thus meditated, one should chant the <s>mantra</s> up to four hundred thousand [times];
at the end of the <s>homa</s> with sesame and ghee, one should worship the Lord and Lady of the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>.
With <s>campaka</s>, <s>aśoka</s>, <s>tulasī</s>, and <s>kahlāra</s> [lilies], and with lotuses,
one directly sees with one's own eyes the divine couple <s>Rādhā</s>-<s>Govinda</s>.
<s>Śrīman Madana-Gopāla</s> too is well-established right here.
Similarly, in the <s>Śrī Tāpanī</s> [<s>Upaniṣad</s>]:
Obeisance, obeisance to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to <s>Gopīnātha</s>, to <s>Govinda</s>.
Therein, the full ornamentation (<s>ākalpa</s>) (from <s>BRS</s> 2.1.354):
Hair-binding, anointing-paste, garlands, and special decorative designs —
Betel-nut play, lotus, and the like are declared as the [items of] adornment. ||
As [stated] (2.1.358) —
With betel reddening His glowing moon-face, beautifying His spotless locks,
graceful with the splendor of well-rubbed saffron-paste glistening in stripes of devotion,
with a tawny garland on His high chest, leaf-designs glittering on His forehead, fingers [adorned],

children.text: śyāmāṅga-dyutir adya me sakhi dṛśor dugdhe mudaṃ mādhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His dark-limbed radiance — today, O friend, <s>Mādhava</s> milks delight for my eyes. ||
Now, adornment (2.1.359-360) —
Crown, ear-rings, necklace, a four-stringed [ornament], bracelets encrusted with jewels,
armlets, anklets, and the like are called jewel-adornment. ||

children.text: kāñcī citrā mukuṭam atulaṃ kuṇḍale hāri-hīre
children.translated_text: A marvelous girdle, a matchless crown, ear-rings of charming diamonds,

children.text: hāras tāro valayam amalaṃ candrā-cāruś catuṣkī |
children.translated_text: a resplendent necklace, spotless bracelets, a beautiful moon-like four-stringed [ornament],

children.text: ramyā cormir madhurima-pūre nūpure cety aghārer
children.translated_text: lovely armlets, sweet-sounding anklets — thus from the limbs of the destroyer of <s>Agha</s>,
the array of ornaments, being adorned [by His limbs], milks forth beauty. ||
As —
As in the <s>Stavāvalī</s>, in the <s>Mukundāṣṭaka</s> (3) —
Golden, gladdening with the splendor of heaps of gold, a yellow [garment] on the hips,
upon that, a fresh reddish cloth — thus wearing [them],
a golden turban placed upon the head,
the ever-new youthful prince of <s>Vraja</s> — may He bring you happiness! ||

children.text:
etad-upalakṣaṇaṃ samaya-krame ṛtu-krame nānāveśa-bhūṣādi-mukulita-bandha-
kañcukādikaṃ jñeyam, yathā-
children.translated_text: This is illustrative — according to the order of occasions and the order of seasons, various costumes, ornaments, bud-like fastenings, jackets, and the like should be known. As —
Wearing a red turban, a variegated lower garment,
and bearing [another cloth] upon it,
with a bud-like jacket fastening,
<s>Śrī Govinda</s> — may He shine forth in [my] heart! ||

children.text: puṣpaiś cūḍāṃ mukuṭam atulaṃ kuṇḍale cāru-hīre
children.translated_text: With flowers on the crest, a matchless crown, charming diamond ear-rings,
placing upon the chest various beautiful flower-garlands and wearing a forest garland,
another [consort] placing upon the knees a bee-attracting [garland], and He bearing,

children.text: nāmnā tāṃ vaijayantīṃ nija-priyatamayā paśya govinda-devam ||
children.translated_text: the one called <s>Vaijayantī</s> by name — with His own dearest beloved, behold <s>Govinda-deva</s>! ||
As —
<s>Govinda</s>! Between the pair of ear-rings on both ears,
at the throat, between the finger-joints of the pair of hands,
above the lotus-feet, upon the toes — those radiant
diamonds the meritorious ones contemplate in their hearts. ||
The pearl-and-gold-studded turban — on the right side and above the principal [jewel],
O beautiful one, my mind is attached to the king of diamonds resting on the heart of <s>Hari</s>. ||
In the <s>Śrī Govinda-līlāmṛta</s> (4.14) —
Wearing devotion-striped saffron-paste of sandal and <s>ghusṛṇa</s>, bearing mineral-painted [marks],

children.text: bhūyiṣṭhaṃ navya-vāsaḥ śikhi-dala-mukuṭaṃ mudrikāḥ kuṇḍale dve |
children.translated_text: abundantly new garments, a peacock-feather crown, finger-rings, two ear-rings,

children.text: guñjāhāraṃ suratna-srajam api taralaṃ kaustubhaṃ vaijayantīṃ
children.translated_text: a necklace of <s>guñjā</s>-berries, a jeweled garland, the sparkling <s>Kaustubha</s> gem, the <s>Vaijayantī</s> garland,

children.text: keyūre kaṅkaṇe śrī-yuta-padaka-kaṭakau nūpurau śṛṅkhalāṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: armlets, bracelets, auspicious foot-ornaments, anklets, and a chain. ||
In the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇāhnika-kaumudī</s> (3.18) —
With a charming moon-touching crest, with <s>guñjā</s>-berry vine resplendent at the ears,
<s>punnāga</s>-blossom clusters, clove-vine, beautiful <s>kuṇḍalas</s> (ear-ornaments) on the full [earlobes],
on the glorious chest a released pearl-vine, a glorious <s>guñjā</s>-berry lake,
His mind eager for the sport of going to the pleasure-garden — He, wearing yellow garments, shone forth. ||
Now, the vision of the divine couple on the full-moon day and the like —
With bodies [like] lightning and cloud, with garments [like] cloud and lightning,
with beautiful faces of naturally gentle smiles,
their hearts pierced by the arrows of mutual side-glances —
I bow joyfully to those two, <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mukunda</s>! ||

children.text:
evaṃ śrīmad-īśvaryā dvādaśābharaṇa-ṣoḍaśa-śṛṅgārādikaṃ kartavyam | tad yathā
(UN 4.9-10)-
children.translated_text: Thus, for the glorious <s>Īśvarī</s> (the Divine Mistress), the twelve ornaments and the sixteen <s>śṛṅgāras</s> (adornments) and the like should be performed. As follows (UN 4.9-10) —
Bathed, with a jewel gleaming at the tip of the nose, wearing a fine cloth, garlanded, with braided hair,
with a flower-ornament [above the ear], body anointed with paste, flowers in the hair, garlanded, lotus in hand,
betel in the mouth, a dot on the broad chin decorated with <s>stavaka</s>-blossoms, eyes adorned with <s>kajjala</s>, beautifully painted,
<s>Rādhā</s>, with feet radiant with <s>alakta</s> (lac-dye), shines forth with a <s>tilaka</s>-mark — this is the sixteen-fold adornment. ||
The twelve ornaments are as follows —
A divine chief among crest-jewels, gold-fashioned twin ear-rings, girdle,
pendants, a pair of hairpins, bangles formed in pairs, throat-ornaments, and finger-rings,
star-imitating necklaces, arm-bangles, jewel-set tip-ornaments,

children.text: tuṅgā pādāṅgurīya-cchavir iti ravibhir bhūṣaṇair bhāti rādhā ||
children.translated_text: lofty toe-rings — with twelve ornaments, <s>Rādhā</s> shines forth! ||
As —
Concealing the array of bodily ornaments, a red-painted inner garment,

children.text: śroṇau celaṃ tad-upari varaṃ daṇḍikākhyaṃ ca nīlam |
children.translated_text: on the hips a cloth, and upon that an excellent one called <s>daṇḍikā</s>, blue in color,

children.text: sarvāṅgānāvarayitum aye devi kiṃ te prayojyaṃ
children.translated_text: to cover all limbs — O Goddess, what is Your purpose?
For upon seeing [You], the Lord's heart bursts into joy! ||
(In the <s>Vilāpa-kusumāñjalī</s>, 28) —

children.text: yā te kañculir atra sundari mayā vakṣojayor arpitā
children.translated_text: This bodice, O beautiful one, was placed by me upon Your breasts,
with the desire of covering the dark [Lord] — but know that it does not remain.

children.text: kintu svāmini kṛṣṇa eva sahasā tat tām avāpya svayaṃ
children.translated_text: Rather, O Mistress, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself, having suddenly obtained it,
