children.text: prāṇebhyo'py adhikaṃ svakaṃ nidhi-yugaṃ saṃgopayaty eva hi ||
children.translated_text: conceals His own treasure-pair, dearer than life itself! ||
(In the <s>Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</s>, 3.5.8) —
With a glance that steals the beauty of a <s>cakorī</s>-bird startled by intoxication,
Her face vanquishing the beauty of the beloved of the full-moon <s>Rohiṇī</s>,
with the glory of being the foremost in the cascade of perfect art,
a vessel of the honey of sweetness — behold, <s>Rādhā</s> reigns supreme! ||

children.text:
evaṃ samayānurūpa-vastrādi-paridhāpanaṃ kartavyaṃ, tathā svarṇa-raupya-
mauktika-ratna-jaṭita-nānālaṅkārādikaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Thus, the dressing in garments and the like appropriate to the occasion should be done; also, various ornaments studded with gold, silver, pearls, and jewels.
Now, for the purpose of viewing the <s>tilaka</s> and the like, the showing of a mirror — as in the <s>Śrī Govinda-līlāmṛta</s> (2.104-105), for the glorious <s>Īśvarī</s> —
Then, <s>Sugandhā</s>, the barber's daughter, who knew the proper time,
showed before [Her] a mirror with a jewel-encrusted handle. ||
She, beholding in the mirror Her own form reflected —
a figure and attire fit for the delight of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s eyes —
trembled with eagerness for the proximity of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. For the special attire of noble women
has as its fruit the sight of the Beloved. ||
Now, for the glorious Lord, in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> (10.35.10) —
He whose <s>tilaka</s> is worth beholding, with a forest garland,
the divine fragrance of <s>Tulasī</s> attracting
swarms of bees who sing deeply the beloved [melody] —
they honored Him when He had joined the flute [to His lips]. ||
Now, the offering of <s>Tulasī</s> in accordance with the method of worship following <s>rāgānuga</s> — as (10.30.1) —
O <s>Tulasī</s>! O auspicious one! Dear to the feet of <s>Govinda</s>!

children.text:
tad yathā-
mātas tulasi govinda-hṛdayānanda-kāriṇī ity ādi |
children.translated_text: As follows: 'O Mother <s>Tulasī</s>, You who delight the heart of <s>Govinda</s>' — and so forth.
Then, the offering of incense, lamp, and the like —
That incense-and-lamp [service] — the glorious lotus-face of <s>Govinda</s>,

children.text: śṛṅgāre ye tu paśyati te yānti paramaṃ padam |
children.translated_text: those who behold it in its adornment — they attain the supreme abode;

children.text: tenāpi saha divyanti tal-loke śāśvatīḥ samāḥ ||
children.translated_text: with Him too they sport in His realm for eternal years. ||

Then the offering of cooked food. Then the offering of betel prepared with camphor and the like. Then the offering of various kinds of food — cooked rice, savory dishes, pastries, cakes, sweet rice, fruit preparations, <s>rasālā</s> (sweet yogurt), and the like.

children.text:
atraiva śrī-govindaḥ priya-pūjāri-gosvāminaṃ prati dadhi-kaḍamānnaṃ svayaṃ
yācitavān | yathā-
children.translated_text: Here itself, <s>Śrī Govinda</s> personally asked the dear worshiper <s>Gosvāmin</s> for yogurt-rice. As —
The sweet yogurt-rice — <s>Govinda</s>, the dear [Lord] of His worshiper,

children.text: yācitvā yena nītaṃ taṃ vande svayaṃ bhagavantam ||
children.translated_text: having asked for it, by whom it was brought — I bow to that Lord Himself. ||

children.text: tata ārātrikaṃ, sarve militvā tad-darśanam | athārātrika-darśana-phalaṃ-
children.translated_text: Then the <s>āratrika</s> (waving of lights). All gather together to behold it. Now, the fruit of beholding the <s>āratrika</s> —
The <s>śṛṅgāra-āratrika</s> (adornment-lamp-offering), which brings happiness to <s>Govinda</s>,
which bestows <s>prema-bhakti</s> (loving devotion), and which destroys sins by its mere beholding. ||

children.text:
atha rājabhoga-vidhir likhyate | vastra-bhūṣādikaṃ samarpya tathaiva mandira-
sevakas tu tata āgatya mandira-dhautādikaṃ kṛtvā tato dhūpa-dīpaṃ ca nivedayet
| tat tu saṅgopanam | tataḥ pācakāḥ parama-rasikāḥ parama-sāvadhānā
niyatendriyā nānā-prakāra-śākādy-anna-vyañjana-roṭikā-pūpa-pāyasa-piṣṭakādi-
śikhariṇī-rasālādikaṃ lehya-coṣya-peya-carvya-ṣaḍ-rasa-nirmitaṃ suvarṇa-pātrādiṣu
pariveṣayanti | sva-sva-rtu-bhavaṃ phalādikaṃ ca | evam ekādaśyādi-vrata-dināni,
sad-ācārānusāreṇa śrī-prabhoḥ śrīmad-īśvaryā nitya-niyamita-pāka-racanādi
kartavyam | pūjako niyatendriyaḥ sāvadhānaḥ san bhojana-sāmagrīṃ vidhivad
rāgānugīya-matena daśa-ghaṭikāntaḥ samaprya samayān nivarti nivaset | pūjakasya
tu naivedya-samarpaṇe vijñaptir, yathā śrī-rūpa-gosvāmi-pādaiḥ śrī-padyāvalyāṃ
(118)-
children.translated_text: Now the procedure of the <s>rājabhoga</s> (royal feast) is written. Having offered garments, ornaments, and the like in the same manner, the temple servant then comes and, having cleaned the temple and the like, should offer incense and lamp. That [service] is the concealment [of the Lord for rest]. Then the cooks, who are supremely relishing, supremely careful, and with controlled senses, serve in golden vessels and the like the various kinds of vegetables, cooked rice, savory dishes, <s>roṭikā</s> (flatbreads), cakes, sweet rice, pastries, <s>śikhariṇī</s> (a sweet preparation), <s>rasālā</s> (sweet yogurt), and the like — prepared in the six flavors as foods to be licked, sucked, drunk, and chewed — as well as fruits of the respective season. Thus, on <s>ekādaśī</s> and other observance-days, in accordance with righteous custom, the eternally prescribed cooking arrangements for the Lord and the glorious <s>Īśvarī</s> should be made. The worshiper, with controlled senses and being careful, should offer the food provisions methodically according to the <s>rāgānuga</s> method, completing the offering within ten <s>ghaṭikās</s> (approximately four hours), and then retire from the occasion. The worshiper's prayer at the offering of <s>naivedya</s> (food), as [composed] by <s>Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmipāda</s> in the <s>Śrī Padyāvalī</s> (118) —
When milk has been offered by the dark-complexioned one (<s>Śyāmalā</s>), when sugar has been bestowed by <s>Kamalā</s>,

children.text: datte laḍḍūni bhadrayā madhurase sobhābhayā lambhite |
children.translated_text: when <s>laḍḍūs</s> have been given by <s>Bhadrā</s>, when sweet juices have been obtained by <s>Śobhā-Abhayā</s> —

children.text: tuṣṭiryā bhavatas tataḥ śataguṇāṃ rādhā-nideśān mayā
children.translated_text: the satisfaction that is Yours from those is a hundred-fold [multiplied]. By the command of <s>Rādhā</s>, by me,

children.text: naste'smin puratas tvam arpaya hare ramyopahāre ratim ||
children.translated_text: in this lovely offering placed before You — bestow Your delight, O <s>Hari</s>! ||
In the <s>Āhnika-kaumudī</s> (3.9-10) —
Vegetables and the like, in order, by the force of [His] satisfaction, all the excellent savory dishes,

children.text: ādaṃ mātṛ-mude bhaved api yathā paktrī-mano-rañjanā |
children.translated_text: He eats, that the joy of [His] mother may also be to the cook's heart's delight.

children.text: tān sarvān saha-bhojinaḥ sarasayā vācā sahan hāsayan
children.translated_text: Making all those co-diners laugh with sweet words and [Himself] laughing,

children.text: bhuñjadhvaṃ na parityajan kim apīty ekāntam āhlādayan ||
children.translated_text: 'Eat! Do not leave anything!' — thus He gladdens [them] in solitude. ||

children.text: annaṃ vyañjanavat kiyat kiyad adaṃś cakre'nnavad vyañjanaṃ
children.translated_text: How much rice with savory dishes did He eat! How much savory dishes like rice He made!

children.text: paryāptaṃ na tathāpi lālasatayā vābhūd anuvyañjanam |
children.translated_text: Yet not enough — from eagerness there was again a side-dish.

children.text: pratyekaṃ ca tad iṣṭa-piṣṭaka-kulaṃ tāṃ gorasānāṃ bhidām
children.translated_text: And each of those desired groups of pastries, and those varieties of milk-products —

children.text: ekaikāṃ ca kṛtābhinandanam adan saṃpipriye sarvadā ||
children.translated_text: eating each one with appreciation, He was pleased always. ||

children.text:
pūjakas tu śītala-jalādi samarpya mandirān nirgatya niyama-japādi kuryāt | japa-
niyamānte ca vidhivad ghaṇṭādi-vādyaṃ kṛtvā śrī-mandire praviśya tato jala-
sevakena datta-pāṭalādi-parivāsitayamunā-jalenācamanaṃ dattvā sukṣma-vastreṇa
mukha-mārjanādikaṃ kuryāt | tato mahā-prasādānayanaṃ tato mandira-sevakena
mandiramārjanaṃ | tatas tāmbūlādi-samarpaṇaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: The worshiper, having offered cool water and the like, should exit the temple and perform his regulated chanting and the like. At the end of the chanting and regulations, having properly sounded the bell and other instruments, he should enter the sacred temple and, with water from the <s>Yamunā</s> perfumed with <s>pāṭalā</s> and other [fragrances] given by the water-servant, offer rinsing of the mouth, and with a fine cloth perform the wiping of the face and the like. Then the bringing of the <s>mahā-prasāda</s> (great consecrated food). Then the cleaning of the temple by the temple servant. Then the offering of betel and the like — as:
With betel-nut powder filled with cardamom and cloves,
with heaps of powder perfumed with the abundance of camphor,
with leaves cut at the sides by a fine cutter —
that <s>vīṭikā</s> (betel preparation) of excellent betel-vine — He enjoyed it. ||

children.text:
tato grīṣmārtau nānā-vidha-suvāsita-jala-nānā-vidha-jala-yantrādinā secanam |
evaṃ mantramaya-nānā-vījanādikaṃ ca | evaṃ sugandha-dravyādi purato dhāraṇam
| evaṃ sugandha-puṣpādibhir mālā-kuñja-kuṭīra-racanam | evaṃ varṣādiṣu yathā-
yogyaṃ jñeyam | tata ārātrikasya sarve militvā darśanam | tato darśana-phalaṃ,
yathā-
children.translated_text: Then, in the summer season, sprinkling with various kinds of fragrant water and various water-devices. Also, fanning with various <s>mantra</s>-[consecrated] fans and the like. Also, placing fragrant substances and the like before [the Lord]. Also, making garland-bowers and small cottages with fragrant flowers and the like. In the rainy season and the like, [arrangements] should be known as appropriate. Then, all gather together for the beholding of the <s>āratrika</s>. Then, the fruit of the beholding — as:
Of the Lord Himself, glorious <s>Govinda</s>, the ocean of mercy,
the <s>āratrika</s> called <s>mahārāja-upacāra</s> (royal-service) — unsurpassed.

children.text: ya idaṃ śraddhayā devi paśyen mantrī subhaktimān |
children.translated_text: Whoever beholds this with faith, O Goddess, [being] an initiated devotee full of devotion —

children.text: sa sarva-kāmān labhate bhaktiṃ tat-pādayoḥ parām ||
children.translated_text: he obtains all desires and supreme devotion at His feet. ||

children.text: evaṃ śrīmad-īśvaryā bhojanācamana-tāmbūlādi-samarpaṇaṃ ca | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: Thus, the offering of food, mouth-rinsing, betel, and the like for the glorious <s>Īśvarī</s> as well. As follows —
<s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s>, through <s>Tulasī</s>, served food to them,
with affection — just as <s>Mohinī</s> [served] nectar to the <s>devas</s> in order. ||

children.text:
tato ratna-khaṭṭopari śayyādi-racanaṃ tatra bhāva-yuktena manasā śayanaṃ kārayet
|
children.translated_text: Then, the arrangement of a bed and the like upon a jeweled couch — there, with a mind endowed with devotional sentiment, one should arrange the sleeping.

children.text:
tataḥ sevāyāṃ mukhyo'dhikārī pūjaka-pācakādi-sarvāṃs tathākiñcanān vaiṣṇavān
ānīya tair militvā mahā-prasādasya mahad-bhaktyā ca-
children.translated_text: Then the chief authorized person of the service — having brought together the worshiper, cooks, and all such [servants], as well as the renunciant <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> — together with them, with great devotion toward the <s>mahā-prasāda</s> —

children.text: anādi purato nyastaṃ cakṣuṣā gṛhyate mayā |
children.translated_text: What is placed before [me] since beginningless [time], I grasp with my eyes;
The taste — on the tongue of a servant — I eat, O <s>Kamalādbhava</s> (Lotus-born)! ||
which turns [one] away from <s>saṃsāra</s>, which again leads to the pair of feet of <s>Hari</s> —
What has been eaten — which destroys all clusters of sin, which delights all the senses,

children.text: śrī-govindas tat prasādaś caraṇāmṛtam eva ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Govinda</s>, His grace (<s>prasāda</s>), the nectar of His feet (<s>caraṇāmṛta</s>),
garments, sandalwood paste, flower garlands, and the like, and <s>tulasī</s> — all these are of one form.

children.text:
sa ca punar madhyamādhikāri-guṇam āśritya teṣu vaiṣṇava-vargeṣu yathocita-
maryādā-mārga-rakṣaṇāya kṛpāpekṣā ity ādi-diśā tatra bhagavad-bhaktāya ca
vastrādi-vārṣikaṃ dattvā sneha-yuktena śrī-śrī-sevāyāṃ sāvadhānaṃ kṛtavān |
tataḥ sarve pūjakādayaḥ sva-sva-dehādi-vyāpāraṃ kṛtvā śrī-bhagavat-kathā-
śravaṇaṃ kuryuḥ | tataḥ sarve snānādikaṃ kṛtvā sva-sva-sevāyāṃ sāvadhānā
bhavanti |
children.translated_text: And he, again relying on the qualities of a devotee of middle qualification (<s>madhyamādhikārin</s>), for the sake of protecting the proper path of conduct among those groups of <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, with the intention of [seeking] grace and the like — having given the annual [allotment of] garments and the like to the devotees of the Lord, he attended carefully to the glorious worship (<s>sevā</s>) with affection. Then all the worshipers and others, having attended to the activities of their own bodies and the like, should listen to the narration of the Lord (<s>bhagavat-kathā</s>). Then all, having bathed and the like, become attentive in their respective services.

children.text:
tato'parāhne vidhivad dvārodghāṭanaṃ kṛtvā śrī-bhagavat-prabodhanaṃ tataḥ śrī-
mukha-prakṣālanādikaṃ tasmāt pakvānna-bhojanaṃ tasmād elā-lavaṅga-karpūrādi-
saṃskṛta-tāmbūlādi-samarpaṇam | tato dhūpa-dīpādi-samarpaṇaṃ ca tad-darśana-
phalaṃ ca -
children.translated_text: Then, in the afternoon, having opened the doors according to the prescribed method, the awakening of the Lord; then the washing of His holy face and the like; then the offering of cooked food; then the offering of betel and the like prepared with cardamom, cloves, camphor, and the like. Then the offering of incense, lamp, and the like — and the fruit of beholding that —

children.text: utthāpane dhūpa-dīpaṃ ye paśyanti narā bhuvi |
children.translated_text: Those people on earth who behold the incense and lamp at the time of awakening,

children.text: te yānti paramaṃ viṣṇoḥ padaṃ śāśvatam avyayam ||
children.translated_text: they attain the supreme, eternal, and imperishable abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: kanaka-nivaha-śobhā ity ādi | evaṃ śrīmad-īśvaryāś ca |
children.translated_text: 'The splendor of heaps of gold' — and so on. Similarly for <s>Śrīmad Īśvarī</s> (the divine Goddess) as well.

children.text:
atha sandhyāratrika-vidhir likhyate | sandhyāyāṃ pakvānna-nivedanaṃ, tataḥ śītala-
jala-susaṃskṛta-tāmbūlādikaṃ ca | tato nīrājanaṃ mahā-maṅgalaṃ ca | tataḥ
paśyatāṃ deva-munīndra-manuṣyādīnāṃ gīta-vādyaiḥ saha jaya-jaya-śabdaḥ |
tathā hi ānanda-vṛndāvana-campvāṃ (13.141)-
children.translated_text: Now the procedure for the evening <s>āratrika</s> (lamp ceremony) is written. At twilight, the offering of cooked food; then cool water, well-prepared betel, and the like. Then the waving of lights (<s>nīrājana</s>) and the great auspicious ceremony (<s>mahā-maṅgala</s>). Then, before the watching <s>devas</s>, great sages, humans, and others, the exclamation of 'jaya jaya' (victory, victory) accompanied by song and instrumental music. Thus indeed, in the <s>Ānanda-Vṛndāvana-campū</s> (13.141) —
His beautiful curly locks dusted with cow-dust, His turban bound aslant,
wearing a peacock feather — a fresh cluster of swaying <s>kiṅkarāta</s> blossoms,
the beauty of earrings [visible] from childhood, the blue lotus of His ear being overtaken by the rays of the sun [i.e., the earring's luster],
the beauty at the edges of His softly perspiring cheeks sprinkled with lines of emerging pollen filaments.
In the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> (10.35.15) —
At every <s>savana</s> (pressing of soma), hearing that [music],
the lords of the <s>devas</s>, led by <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), <s>Śarva</s> (Śiva), and <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> (Brahmā),
the poets, with bowed heads and minds,
became bewildered, unable to ascertain its true nature.
Then the greatness of beholding [the Lord] —
Those people who behold the face of <s>Kṛṣṇa-deva</s> during the evening <s>āratrika</s>,

children.text: ye paśyanti tu te yānti tad-dhāma param avyayam ||
children.translated_text: they indeed attain His supreme, imperishable abode.
Similarly for <s>Śrīmad Īśvarī</s> (the divine Goddess) as well.

children.text:
tataḥ śayanārātrika-vidhir likhyate | tataḥ pūjakaḥ śṛṅgāra-maṇi-maṇḍanādikam
uttārya yathā-rahaḥ yugma-vastrādi-paridhāpanam | evaṃ mālya-lepanādeś ca |
tataḥ kiyat-kṣaṇaṃ darśanārthaṃ virāmaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Then the procedure for the bedtime <s>āratrika</s> is written. Then the worshiper, having removed the ornamental jewelry and gem-decorations, puts on night garments and the like as appropriate for the intimate [setting]. Similarly with garlands, ointments, and the like. Then a brief pause for <s>darśana</s> (beholding) and rest.
Wearing a beautiful garment that surpasses rows of camphor [in whiteness] on His hips,
bearing on His noble head a lovely, reddish turban, His eyes mingled with drowsiness,
accepting the wish-fulfilling, bliss-giving auspicious <s>āratrika</s>,

children.text: govindaḥ kuśalaṃ karoti bhavato rātry-anta-kāle sadā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Govinda</s> always brings you well-being at the close of night.

children.text:
tato bhojana-saṃskaraṇaṃ sumiṣṭa-susvādu-durdarśanīya-loka-praśaṃsya-svātma-
rocaka-bhagavad-rocaka-nānā-prakārānna-vyañjana-pakvānna-dugdhānna-
piṣṭakādi-samarpaṇam tatra gopanīya-dhūpa-dīpam | tato bhojana-nimittaṃ
samayāpekṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: Then the preparation of the meal — the offering of various kinds of food, cooked dishes, milk-preparations, pastries, and the like that are exquisitely sweet, delightfully tasty, wonderful to behold, praised by all, pleasing to oneself and pleasing to the Lord. There, incense and lamp [are offered] privately. Then one waits for the appropriate time for the meal.

children.text:
yat-sevayā vaśaḥ śrīmad-govindo nanda-nandanaḥ |
payasā saṃyutaṃ bhaktaṃ yācate karuṇāmbudhiḥ || iti pūrvaṃ darśitavān |
children.translated_text: 'By whose service the glorious <s>Govinda</s>, the son of <s>Nanda</s>, is brought under control — that ocean of compassion asks for <s>bhakta</s> (food offering) mixed with milk' — this was shown previously.

children.text:
tasmād ācamanaṃ mukha-mārjanārthaṃ vastra-samarpaṇaṃ | tato mahā-
prasādānayanaṃ, tato mandira-sevakena bhojana-sthala-mārjanaṃ | tasmād elā-
lavaṅga-jātiphala-karpūrādi-saṃskṛta-tāmbūlādi-samarpaṇam |
children.translated_text: After that, <s>ācamana</s> (sipping of water), offering a cloth for wiping the face. Then bringing forth the <s>mahā-prasāda</s> (great sanctified food). Then the temple servant cleans the dining area. After that, the offering of betel and the like prepared with cardamom, cloves, nutmeg, camphor, and the like.
Then, in winter, the wearing of the <s>phalgulā</s> (winter wrap) —
Named <s>phalgulā</s>, fashioned from silk garments,
a guard against frost, obtainable at great cost,
adorned with golden embroidery throughout,
resplendent from the crown of the head to the pair of feet.

children.text:
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ vraja-rāja-putraṃ
paśyantam agnim amalaṃ bhagavantam īḍe |
children.translated_text: I praise <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Person, the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, the immaculate Lord who gazes at the [sacred] fire.
Of incomparable reddish hue,
wearing a <s>phalgulā</s> beautifully variegated with many gems,
bearing <s>Govinda</s>,
when shall I behold [Him] with a laughing face?
Now, in summer, the wearing of the <s>taniyā</s> (thin cloth) —
Made of fine cloth, cut into a three-part form,
adorned with gold thread and pearls along all its edges,
resplendent and beautifying the middle part of <s>Kṛṣṇa-deva</s>'s [body],
I take refuge in this cool garment that dispels the heat of summer.
The wearing of a buttoned jacket (<s>mukulita-kañcuka</s>) —
Wearing a reddish turban and a variegated <s>dhaṭī</s> (upper garment),
and bearing [another garment] over that,
with a buttoned jacket fastened,
may <s>Śrī Govinda</s> shine forth in [my] heart.

children.text:
evaṃ karpūra-parivāsita-śītala-jalaṃ yamunāyā nānā-vidha-sugandha-dravyaṃ
vījanādikaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Similarly, cool water scented with camphor, various fragrant substances from the <s>Yamunā</s>, fanning, and the like.
Then the <s>āratrika</s> at the interval of ten <s>ghaṭikās</s> (approximately four hours) — the fruit of beholding that —

children.text: ye paśyanti janāḥ śreṣṭhaṃ śayanārātrikaṃ hareḥ |
children.translated_text: Those people who behold the excellent bedtime <s>āratrika</s> of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: te tu govinda-devasya kṛpā-pūrṇā na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are indeed filled with the grace of <s>Govinda-deva</s>, without doubt.

children.text:
tatra ratna-khaṭṭopari śayyādi-nirmāṇam | tatra khaṭṭādho rātri-sevanārthaṃ
suvāsita-śītala-jala-pakvānna-tāmbūlādi-sthāpanam | tato mandirān niṣkṛṣya
bhāva-yuktena manasā śayana-samayāpekṣaṇam | evaṃ śrīmad-īśvaryāś ca |
grantha-vistāra-bhiyā vistārya na likhyate | evaṃ pañca-vidhārātrika-darśana-
phalam-
children.translated_text: There, the preparation of the bed and the like on a jeweled cot. There, beneath the cot, the placing of fragrant cool water, cooked food, betel, and the like for night service. Then, leading [the Lord] out of the temple, with a heart full of devotion, one waits for the time of sleep. Similarly for <s>Śrīmad Īśvarī</s> (the divine Goddess) as well. Out of fear of extending the text, [this] is not written at length. Thus, the fruit of beholding the five types of <s>āratrika</s> —
Beginning from the auspicious morning <s>āratrika</s> up to the final bedtime [<s>āratrika</s>],

children.text: evam ārātrikaṃ pañca ye paśyanti janā bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: thus, those people on earth who behold the five <s>āratikas</s>,

children.text: te sarve vāñchitaṃ prāpya putraṃ pautraṃ dhanaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: they all, having obtained their desires — sons, grandsons, and wealth —
at the end, by the grace of <s>Govinda-deva</s>, attain His abode.
<s>Śrī Vijaya-Govinda</s> — as follows:
The <s>tamāla</s> tree of the <s>mādhavikā</s> creeper of <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>,
the spring breeze for the creeper-rows of her <s>sakhīs</s> (female companions),
the sun (<s>saroja-bandhu</s>, friend of the lotus) for the lotus-garland of <s>Rādhā</s> —
I praise <s>Govinda</s>, whose [name] begins with the syllable of victory (<s>vijaya</s>).
His victory over <s>Kaṃsa</s> and others, who had taken birth from the womb, is 'jaya' (triumph);
His victory over <s>Kāma</s> (desire), who is born from the mind, is proclaimed as '<s>vijaya</s>' (supreme triumph).

children.text: tvaṃ gavām indra ity āder govinda iti kathyate |
children.translated_text: 'You are the <s>Indra</s> of cows' and so on — therefore He is called <s>Govinda</s>.

children.text: tasmād vijaya-govindaṃ budhā evaṃ vadanti hi ||
children.translated_text: Therefore, the wise call Him '<s>Vijaya-Govinda</s>.'

children.text: athavā yasya bhajanāt kāmādy-ari-jayāt tu tam |
children.translated_text: Alternatively, because by His worship one conquers enemies such as desire (<s>kāma</s>) and the like,
the wise declare Him to be '<s>Vijaya-Govinda</s>.'
I bow to <s>Vijaya-Govinda</s>, the non-dual form (<s>vigraha</s>) of <s>Govinda</s>,

children.text: mano lagati govinde yasya sandarśanād dhruvam ||
children.translated_text: by whose <s>darśana</s> (beholding), the mind is surely attached to <s>Govinda</s>.
Now, the ancient account of <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s>'s arrival at <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s> —
I bow to <s>Śrīmat Kāśīśvara</s>, out of love for whom
<s>Caitanya-deva</s> Himself, out of grace, came to the western region.

children.text:
atha śrī-mahāprabhu-pārṣada-śrīmukha-śruta-kathā-ekadā śrī-mahāprabhuḥ
śrī-kāśīśvaraṃ kathitavān - bhavān śrī-vṛndāvanaṃ gatvā śrīla-rūpa-sanātanayor
antikaṃ nivasatu iti | sa tu tac chrutvā harṣa-vismito'bhūt | sarvajña-śiromaṇis tad-
dhṛdayaṃ jñātvā punaḥ kathitavān - śrī-jagannātha-pārśva-vartinaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa-
vigraham ānīya kathitavān svayaṃ bhagavatānena mamābhedaṃ jānīhi | ata enaṃ
sevasva | tac chrutvā sa tūṣṇīṃ babhūva | tato vigrahasya gaura-vapuṣā śrī-kṛṣṇena
mahā-prabhunā ca ekatra bhojanaṃ kṛtam | tataḥ śrī-kāśīśvaro daṇḍavat praṇamya
gaura-govinda-vigrahaṃ śrī-vṛndāvnaaṃ prāpitavān | so'yaṃ śrī-govinda-pārśvarti-
śrī-mahāprabhuḥ | ato yathā śrī-govindasya sevā-vidhiḥ śrī-mahāprabhor api
tathā grantha-vistāra-bhiyā vistārya na likhyate |
children.translated_text: Now, the account heard from the holy mouth of an associate of <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s>: Once, <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s> said to <s>Śrī Kāśīśvara</s> — 'You should go to <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s> and reside near <s>Śrīla Rūpa</s> and <s>Sanātana</s>.' And he, hearing that, was filled with joy and wonder. The omniscient crest-jewel, knowing his heart, said again — having brought the sacred image of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> that stood beside <s>Śrī Jagannātha</s>, He said: 'Know this one to be non-different from Me, <s>Svayaṃ Bhagavat</s> (the Lord Himself). Therefore, worship Him.' Hearing that, he became silent. Then, the golden-bodied <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> [image], together with the sacred image, dined together with <s>Mahāprabhu</s> in one place. Then <s>Śrī Kāśīśvara</s>, prostrating fully, brought the <s>Gaura-Govinda</s> image to <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>. That is this <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s> who stands beside <s>Śrī Govinda</s>. Therefore, just as is the method of worship for <s>Śrī Govinda</s>, so also for <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s> — but out of fear of extending the text, [this] is not written at length.
He whose foot-luster conquers <s>Madana</s> (Cupid),
whose face-luster humbles the pride of the lotus-gem,
whose feet are sheltered by <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> —
may <s>Gaura-Govinda</s> be gracious to me.

children.text:
evaṃ śrī-mahāprabhor janma-yātrādi kartavyam | tathā śrī-mahāprabhoḥ
pārṣadānāṃ sevā | mukhyādhikāriṇām aprakaṭa-tithi-pālanaṃ ca kartavyam |
children.translated_text: Similarly, the birth-anniversary festival (<s>janma-yātrā</s>) and the like of <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s> should be performed. Similarly, the worship of <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s>'s associates. The observance of the disappearance dates (<s>aprakaṭa-tithi</s>) of the principal qualified [devotees] should also be performed.
Now, the greatness of <s>Śrī Vṛndā-devī</s> —
<s>Vṛndā</s>, whose feet are venerated, in the forest of <s>Vṛndā</s> and the like, by <s>Netra</s> and others;

children.text: yad vācā vṛkṣa-latāḥ kāle'kāle puṣpitāḥ syuḥ ||
children.translated_text: by whose word, the trees and creepers blossom in season and out of season.
On her head she wears a beautiful gem-and-jewel crown with precious stones,

children.text: karṇa-dvandvaṃ ca dīpte puraṭa-viracite kuṇḍale hāri-hīre |
children.translated_text: on her pair of ears, bright golden earrings with captivating diamonds,

children.text: niṣkaṃ kāñcīṃ suhārān bhuja-kaṭaka-tulākoṭikādīṃś ca vande
children.translated_text: a pendant, a girdle, fine necklaces, armlets, bracelets, and anklets — I bow to
<s>Vṛndā</s>, in beautiful garments, within <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, beside <s>Śrīla Govinda</s>.
The lotus feet of <s>Śrī Vṛndā</s>, worthy of worship by all the worlds,
being served with devotion, [they] remove the impurities of the age of <s>Kali</s> and grant all desires.

children.text: vaktavyaṃ cātra kiṃ vā yad anubhajanato durlabhe deva-lokaiḥ
children.translated_text: And what more is there to say? For one who devotedly serves [her], [obtaining what is] unobtainable even by the <s>devas</s>,
a person dwells in that [place] called <s>Śrīmad Vṛndāvana</s>, freed from all sorrows.

children.text:
asyāḥ sva-prājñā likhyate - ekadā rātrau suptaṃ śrīmat-prabhuṃ śrī-haridāsa-
gosvāminaṃ prati vṛndayādideśe - aye śrīmad-rādhā-govinda-sevādhikārin ! mat-
prabhoḥ śrīmahā-prasādānnaṃ dātum arhasi | evaṃ sevā-vastra-bhūṣādikaṃ
śrīmad-īśvaryāś ca |
children.translated_text: Her own intelligence is now described: Once at night, <s>Vṛndā</s> instructed <s>Śrīmat Prabhu Śrī Haridāsa Gosvāmin</s> who was sleeping — 'O overseer of the worship of <s>Śrīmad Rādhā-Govinda</s>! You should give the <s>mahā-prasāda</s> food of my Lord.' Similarly, garments, ornaments, and the like for the worship of <s>Śrīmad Īśvarī</s> (the divine Goddess) as well.
Now the procedure for the annual festivals (<s>vārṣikā-yātrā</s>) is written.

children.text: bhaktānāṃ vyadadhan mahotsavam ayaṃ netrārbudānāṃ param
svīkurvan prathamaṃ sumaṅgalataraṃ snānaṃ ca pañcāmṛtaiḥ ||[*ENDNOTE #5]
children.translated_text: first accepting the most auspicious bathing with <s>pañcāmṛta</s> (the five nectars). [*ENDNOTE #5]
He who bestows a great festival upon the devotees, supreme for multitudes of eyes,
Placing yogurt, honey, sugar, ghee, and the like upon the Lord's head —
is it as if a hundred streams of the <s>Jāhnavī</s> (Ganges) flow upon a sapphire mountain? [*ENDNOTE #6]

children.text:
pañcamyāṃ prathame vasanta-samaye govinda-devo hariḥ |
yaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhava-padma-japa-prabhṛtayaḥ sadyaḥ kṛtārthaṃ gatāḥ
||[*ENDNOTE #7]
children.translated_text: On the fifth [day of the bright fortnight], in the first spring season, <s>Govinda-deva Hari</s>, seeing whom, <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva), <s>Padmaja</s> (Brahmā), and others instantly attained fulfillment. [*ENDNOTE #7]
<s>Brahmā</s> and other <s>devas</s>, out of greed from drinking the nectar of His feet, sneaking in,
disguised in human form, beg from the associate-devotees. [*ENDNOTE #8]

children.text: pītaṃ kañcukam atulaṃ coṣṇīṣaṃ citra-dhaṭīṃ dhṛtaṃ devam |
children.translated_text: A golden jacket, incomparable, and a turban, and a variegated <s>dhaṭī</s> (upper garment) worn by the Lord,
playing with His beloved — O friend, behold <s>Śrī Govinda</s>!

children.text:
yadyapi māgha-śrī-pañcamītaḥ phālgunī-paurṇamāsī-paryantaṃ vasantotsavaḥ
pravartate | tathā hi, phālguna-śukla-daśamītaḥ caitra-kṛṣṇa-pratipat-paryantaṃ
mukhyo vidhiḥ | teṣu pañca-dineṣu prabhuḥ priyayā sahitaḥ sadā virājate |
children.translated_text: Although the spring festival (<s>vasantotsava</s>) commences from the <s>Śrī Pañcamī</s> (fifth) of <s>Māgha</s> and continues until the full moon of <s>Phālgunī</s>, the main observance is from the tenth of <s>Phālguna-śukla</s> until the first day of <s>Caitra-kṛṣṇa</s>. During those five days, the Lord, accompanied by His beloved, always shines forth.
All the <s>devas</s> beginning with <s>Brahmā</s>, filled with supreme bliss,
having assembled with <s>Indra</s> and others, dwell here in the region of <s>Vraja</s>.

children.text:
sarva-vraja-maṇḍala-mukhyatve śrī-govinda-sthalaṃ jñeyam | vasanta-vastrādikaṃ
ca paridadhāti |
children.translated_text: The place of <s>Śrī Govinda</s> should be known as the foremost of all the <s>Vraja-maṇḍala</s>. He is dressed in spring garments and the like.
A crown studded with divine gems, earrings, a beautiful necklace,

children.text: niṣkaṃ kāñcīṃ supada-kaṭakāv aṅgade kaṅkaṇe ca |
children.translated_text: a pendant, a girdle, fine ankle-bracelets, armlets, and bangles,

children.text: pītaṃ vāsaś catuṣkaṃ maṇi-gaṇa-ghaṭitā mudrikāś cāṅguliṣu
children.translated_text: a yellow fourfold garment, rings set with clusters of gems on the fingers,

children.text: bibhrāṇaṃ vāma-pārśve nija-priyatamayā sevitaṃ devam īḍe ||
children.translated_text: bearing [all these], served on His left side by His most beloved — I praise that Lord.
A supremely divine crest-jewel, a crown of gems, earrings, star-necklaces,

children.text: niṣkaṃ kāñcī-śalākā yuga-valaya-ghaṭā nūpurān mudrikāś ca |
children.translated_text: a gold necklace, a girdle-clasp, a pair of bangles, anklets, and rings;

children.text: śroṇau raktaṃ dukūlaṃ tad-uparama-tulaṃ cāru-nīlaṃ dadhānāṃ
children.translated_text: wearing a red silken garment on her hips, and upon its hem, a beautiful blue [garment] —
I take refuge in <s>Rādhikā</s>, shining at the left side [of <s>Govinda</s>], the moon of the lotus-like <s>Vraja</s>.
And also —
Now the <s>Vasantotsava</s> (Spring Festival) —
Throwing heaps of garments of various kinds,
balls made of flowers and the like, and soft water-sprinklers,
with fragrant waters released from water-devices, with love,
<s>Śrī Pūjaka</s> and others drenched their Lord.
With fragrant powders of various colors, fully filled,

children.text: ādau bhūr dyau vyānaśe dik vidik ca |
children.translated_text: first the earth, sky, directions, and intermediate directions vanished;
then, with the roots cut off by showers of fragrant waters,
afterwards [the scene] obtained the appearance of a variegated canopy.
Now <s>Śrī Rāma-navamī</s> —

children.text: uccasthe graha-pañcake suraguro sendau navamyāṃ tithau
children.translated_text: When the five planets were in exaltation, with <s>Jupiter</s> and the moon, on the ninth <s>tithi</s>,

children.text: lagne karkaṭake punar vasu-yute meṣaṃ gate pūṣaṇi |
children.translated_text: with <s>Cancer</s> as the ascendant, conjoined with the <s>Puṣya</s> [asterism], with the sun entered into <s>Aries</s>,
all the <s>palāśa</s>-wood sticks went forth from the sacred [altar] in <s>Ayodhyā</s> —

children.text: āvirbhūtam abhūd apūrva-vibhavaṃ yat kiñcid ekaṃ mahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: there appeared a certain singular, unprecedented, glorious radiance!
We bow to the great Lord, the breaker of <s>Hara</s>'s bow,
the sandalwood of bliss for the heart of <s>Jānakī</s>, the joy of the <s>Raghu</s> dynasty.
Now the <s>Dolotsava</s> (Swing Festival) —
At the root of a wish-fulfilling tree in glorious <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s>,
in the midst of a divine swing [decorated] with various flowers,
glorious <s>Rādhā</s> and glorious <s>Govinda-deva</s>,
served by the rows of devotees — them I remember.

children.text: puṣpaiś cūḍāṃ mukuṭam atulaṃ kuṇḍale cāru-hīre
children.translated_text: A crown of flowers, a matchless diadem, beautiful diamond earrings,
upon His chest, [she who is] placing garlands of diverse lovely flowers, [and He] wearing a forest garland,
she who places upon His knee a bee-attracting [garland], and He who bears another

children.text: nāmnā tāṃ vaijayantīṃ nija-priyatamayā paśya govinda-devam ||
children.translated_text: by the name <s>Vaijayantī</s>, with His most beloved — behold <s>Govinda-deva</s>!
Arrangements of bower-rows with flowers, a floral canopy,
a swing fashioned of various flowers, and a flute [adorned] with clusters of flowers,
a garden of flowers shines all around — artificial, yet as if created by the gods —
thus on the swing, the God of gods is served by His dear attendants.

children.text: agrataḥ pṛṣṭhataḥ pārśve govindaṃ priyayā yutam |
children.translated_text: In front, behind, and on the sides, <s>Govinda</s> together with His beloved —
the servitors joyfully swung [them] on the swing.
On the wildly swaying swing, that beloved, trembling with [playful] fear,

children.text: kāntam āliṅgya hṛṣṭā taiḥ prema-bhaktais tadojjvalaiḥ |
children.translated_text: embracing her lover, was delighted; and those brilliant loving devotees [sang]:
'Victory to the Lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>! Victory to the Queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>!
Victory to the bulb of bliss of <s>Nanda</s>, the bestower of all bliss!'

children.text: iti brahmādayo devā gāyanto divi harṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods, singing in heaven with delight,
showered flowers, each devoted to their own service.
<s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, <s>Cāraṇas</s>, and others,
the hosts of great sages and lords of the gods, all attentive,
eager to swing that little swing,
having attained their eligibility, remained stationed there.

children.text: ye mānavā bhāgya-bhājo divi devās tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: Those human beings who are blessed by fortune, and likewise the gods in heaven —

children.text: tair dṛṣṭaḥ priyayā yukto govindo dolanotsave ||
children.translated_text: by them was <s>Govinda</s> seen, together with His beloved, at the swing festival.
Now the <s>Candanotsava</s> (Sandalwood-paste Festival) (in <s>āryā</s> meter) —

children.text: mama kurute mudam atulaṃ vaiśākhī śukla-tṛtīyā śubhadā |
children.translated_text: The auspicious third day of the bright half of <s>Vaiśākha</s> brings me incomparable joy,
on which <s>Śrī Govinda</s> is served by devotees with pastes of sandalwood.
I bow to <s>Śrī Gaura-Govinda</s>, anointed on all limbs
with divine sandalwood pastes mixed with saffron and camphor.
Upon the top of the head, upon the turban, upon the bodice covering all limbs,
He is anointed with a paste of camphor, musk, and saffron mixed with liquid sandalwood;
attended all around by the host of devotees, with auspicious songs and instrumental music,
may this golden-hued <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> bring you auspiciousness!
As follows —
Beginning from <s>Vaiśākha</s> through <s>Āśvina</s>, with care,

children.text: suvījanaṃ tu kartavyaṃ bhaktair yantrādinā hareḥ ||
children.translated_text: devotees should fan <s>Hari</s> with good fans, instruments, and the like.
With waters mixed with fragrance and sandalwood, extremely cool,
sprinkling before the Lord with streams released from water-devices.
Now <s>Śrī Nṛsiṃha Caturdaśī</s> —
The auspicious fourteenth of <s>Jyaiṣṭhī</s> [the bright half of <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>] of <s>Śrī Nṛsiṃha</s> approaches;
may it remove my inner [darkness] through the arrangement of a great festival!
Since the seed of all incarnations, the self-same <s>Bhagavān Hari</s>,
is non-different from <s>Śrīmad Govinda-deva</s> and <s>Nṛsiṃha</s> and the others,
on the respective birth-days of each,
a festival is performed by the devotees in proper ritual form, with songs and instrumental music.
Beginning from the fourteenth, divine food [is prepared] with great care,
called <s>paryuṣita</s> (overnight food), combined with yogurt and the like.
Now, the procedure for mounting the chariot in <s>Āṣāḍha</s> —
The second day of the bright half of <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, bestower of auspiciousness,
creates excitement — the preparation of the Lord's chariot-mounting.

children.text:
atra bhojana-sāmagrī dviguṇīkṛtya kartavyā | bhūṣāveśādikaṃ sarvaṃ mahārāja-
kumāratvena kartavyam |
children.translated_text: Here the food preparations should be doubled. All the ornaments, dress, and the like should be done as for a great prince.

children.text: āyātā sakhi rādhe tava sukhadā śrāvaṇa-tṛtīyeyam |
children.translated_text: O friend <s>Rādhā</s>, this third day of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> has come, bringing you happiness!
Arrange an incomparable swing adorned with many jewels and begin [the festival]!

children.text:
ato vraja-maṇḍala-prasiddhāyāṃ śrāvaṇa-śukla-tṛtīyāyāṃ śrī-vṛṣabhānu-
nandinyāḥ śrīmad-īśvaryā dolārūḍha-mahotsavo yatnataḥ kartavyaḥ | evaṃ pavitrā
dvādaśī saubhāgya-paurṇamāsī ca |
children.translated_text: Therefore, on the third day of the bright half of <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, which is famous in the <s>Vraja</s> region, the great swing-mounted festival of the daughter of <s>Śrī Vṛṣabhānu</s>, the glorious mistress [<s>Rādhā</s>], should be performed with care. Likewise the <s>Pavitrā Dvādaśī</s> and the <s>Saubhāgya Paurṇamāsī</s> [should be observed].
Now, <s>Śrī Janmāṣṭamī</s> in <s>Bhādra</s> —

children.text: yasmin dine prasūyeta devakī tvāṃ janārdana |
children.translated_text: O <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, tell [us] on which day <s>Devakī</s> gave birth to you, O <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: tad dinaṃ brūhi vaikuṇṭha kurmas te tatra cotsavam ||[*ENDNOTE #9]
children.translated_text: [so that] we may celebrate a festival for you on that day!

children.text: sphurati kathaṃ mama satataṃ vāma-netraṃ vicāraya sakhi tvam |
children.translated_text: Why does my left eye constantly flutter? Consider this, O friend!
I understand — this birthday of <s>Kṛṣṇa-candra</s> (moon-like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) is approaching!

children.text: bhadre tu bhadradā ceyaṃ śrī-harer janmanas tithiḥ |
children.translated_text: In <s>Bhadra</s>, this auspicious <s>tithi</s> of the birth of <s>Śrī Hari</s> bestows blessings;

children.text: lokato vidhitas tatra cotsavaḥ kriyate budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: the wise celebrate a festival there, according to both popular custom and scriptural injunction.
The devotees, roaring in the mud of yogurt and ghee,

children.text: kūrdantaḥ punar api tat kṣipanta ārāt |
children.translated_text: leaping again and again, throwing it far away,
on each other's heads, faces, and backs —
submerged in the ocean of the nectar of bliss, they smear [one another].
Knowing the birthday of the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>,
all the residents of <s>Vraja</s> have come from the <s>Vraja</s> region.
And from various directions and lands, the beloved servants of <s>Govinda</s>,
wearing divine garlands and garments, accompanied by sons and wives.

children.text: vandino gāyakāś caiva nartakā vādakāś ca ye |
children.translated_text: Bards, singers, dancers, and musicians —

children.text: divya-veśa-dharās te tu nanṛtuḥ papaṭhur jaguḥ ||
children.translated_text: wearing divine costumes, they danced, recited, and sang.

children.text: gāyanto mṛdu-madhuraṃ vandi-gaṇāḥ paṭhanti bhṛśam uccaiḥ |
children.translated_text: The bards sing softly and sweetly, the panegyrists recite loudly and eagerly;

children.text: vṛttiṃ vināpi te te yācante pāritoṣikaṃ tebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: even without [regular] livelihood, they request gifts from those [assembled].
Thus, when the moment of birth arrived, with the five nectars (<s>pañcāmṛta</s>), joyfully,
uttering cries of 'Victory!', they bathe their own Lord.
Granting to the devotees a great festival that is supreme [even] for billions of eyes,

children.text: svīkurvan prathamaṃ sumaṅgalataraṃ snānaṃ ca pañcāmṛtaiḥ |
children.translated_text: first accepting the most auspicious bathing with the five nectars,
on the eighth <s>tithi</s>, the auspicious day, at midnight, <s>Govinda-deva Hari</s> —

children.text: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhava-padmaja-prabhṛtayaḥ sadyaḥ kṛtārthaṃ gatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing whom, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Padmaja</s> (the Lotus-born), and others instantly became fulfilled.
Wandering about, <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods, out of greed for drinking the foot-nectar [of the Lord],
having assumed human forms and disguises, beg from the attendant-devotees.

children.text: iti brahmādayo devā gāyanto divi harṣataḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Brahmā</s> and the other gods, singing in heaven with delight,
shower flowers, each devoted to their own service.

children.text: divi deva-gaṇāḥ sarve āgatās tad-dine śubhe |
children.translated_text: All the hosts of gods in heaven, obedient to the Lord's command,

children.text: tad ye paśyanti tad-rātrau te kṛtārthās tu bhūtale ||
children.translated_text: come on that auspicious day. Those who behold that night are fulfilled on earth.

children.text: cakṣuṣmantas tu te proktāḥ prabhoḥ pārśvaṃ vrajanti ca ||
children.translated_text: They are said to be the truly seeing ones, and they go to the side of the Lord.
In the <s>Ānanda-vṛndāvana-campū</s>, in the second cluster (17-19) —

children.text:
evaṃ paripūrṇa-maṅgala-guṇatayā dūṣaṇa-dvāparānte dvāparānte nirantarāla-
bhādrapade bhādrapade māsi māsite pakṣe'pakṣepa-rahite hite rasamaye guṇa-gaṇa-
rohiṇīṃ rohiṇīṃ sarati sudhākare sudhākare yoge yogeśvareśvaro madhye
kṣaṇadāyāḥ kṣaṇadāyāḥ pūrṇānandatayā jīvavaj-jananī-jaṭhara-
saṃbandhābhāvād bandhābhāvāc ca kevalaṃ vilasat-karuṇayāruṇayā tathāvidha-
līlālī-lāsikayā kayācana purandara-dig-aṅganotsaṅga iva rajanīkaraḥ sva-
prakāśatayā prādurbhāvam eva bhāvayan agre pūrva-pūrvajani janita-tapaḥ
saubhāgya-phalenopalabdhi-pitṛ-mātṛ-bhāvayoḥ śrī-vasudeva-devakyor vāsudeva-
svarūpeṇāvirbhāvaṃ bhāvayitvā stanandhayatvābhimānam eva kṣaṇaṃ tayoḥ
prakaṭayya paścān nitya-siddha-pitṛ-mātṛ-bhāvayoḥ śrī-nanda-yaśodayor api śrī-
govinda-priya-ramaṇī-gaṇeṣu mukhyā rādheyaṃ trijagati rājate svayaṃ śrīḥ priyāli-
premonnā janimāpa jananyāḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, by virtue of being full of auspicious qualities, at the end of <s>Dvāpara</s> [age], in the uninterrupted month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>, in the [dark] fortnight free from reproach, auspicious, full of <s>rasa</s>, when the nectar-rayed [moon] moves into the asterism <s>Rohiṇī</s>, in the conjunction of the Lord of <s>Yoga</s>, at midnight — with perfect bliss, since there was no connection with a mother's womb as in the case of [ordinary] living beings, and since there was no bondage — solely through His shining compassion and through a certain [divine] playful-dancing of such a <s>līlā</s>, like the moon [arising] from the lap of the lady of the eastern quarter, through His self-luminosity, manifesting [His] appearance — first, for <s>Śrī Vasudeva</s> and <s>Devakī</s>, who had attained the status of father and mother as the fruit of austerities performed in previous births, taking the form of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, He manifested [His] appearance, displaying the pretense of being a suckling infant to them for a moment; then, for <s>Śrī Nanda</s> and <s>Yaśodā</s>, who have the eternally perfected status of father and mother — and also among the beloved women of <s>Śrī Govinda</s>, the chief is <s>Rādhā</s>, who shines as <s>Śrī</s> Herself in all three worlds; elevated by the love of her dear companions, she obtained birth from [her] mother.
Now <s>Śrī Vāmana-abhiṣeka</s> and the like.
Now, on the full-moon night of autumn (<s>Śarat-paurṇamāsī</s>), as follows —
Rich in deep love, with faces [bright] like the gentle autumn moon,
wearing diadems and crowns, clad in blue and yellow garments,
in the pleasure-giving autumnal forest, on the seat of the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> of <s>rasa</s>,
behold before you the urbane <s>Mādhava</s> and sweet <s>Rādhikā</s>!
On the autumn moonlit night, the glorious son of <s>Nanda</s>,
wearied from the <s>rāsa</s> dance, together with His beloved and the groups of <s>sakhīs</s>,
wearing divine garlands and garments, in a costume befitting a dancer, <s>Hari</s> —
one should meditate [upon Him] in beautiful <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, in the forest on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>.
Cooling drinks (<s>prapānaka</s>) and cold foods, combined with various cooked dishes —
the practitioner (<s>sādhaka</s>), having offered food to Him — [who is] accompanied by the groups of <s>sakhīs</s> — being satisfied,
should then respectfully accept the remnants (<s>śeṣānna</s>) together with the <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>.
Now, the offering of lamps on the new-moon day (<s>Amāvāsyā</s>), as follows —
The new-moon day of <s>Kārttika</s> is especially auspicious;
by offering lamps on it, <s>Keśava</s> is pleased.

children.text: cala cala naya naya bho bho govinde copaḍhaukanam |
children.translated_text: 'Come, come! Bring, bring! O, O! An offering to <s>Govinda</s>!

children.text: divyaṃ paśyāmo mukha-padmaṃ dāsyāmo dīpa-mālikās tatra ||
children.translated_text: Let us behold [His] divine lotus-face! Let us offer garlands of lamps there!'

children.text: iti kṛtvā pragāyanti pralapanti punaḥ punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus they sing and speak again and again —
all the townspeople, and especially the residents of <s>Vraja</s>.
In front, behind, on the sides, on the rooftops, in the houses —
they will offer garlands of lamps that give pleasure to <s>Govinda</s>.

children.text: yamunāyās taṭe kecit tīrthe kecij jale tathā |
children.translated_text: Some on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>, some at the sacred bathing spot (<s>tīrtha</s>), some in the water —
in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> they celebrate the great festival of lamp-garlands.
All the hosts of gods in heaven, devoted to the Lord's command,
will grant the desires of those who perform [the offering of] lamp-garlands.
I bow to glorious <s>Govinda</s>, whose form is grace toward the devotees,
whose eyes are blissfully pleased upon seeing the garlands of lamps.
Now the <s>Anna-kūṭa</s> (Mountain of Food) —
Knowing that the <s>Anna-kūṭa</s>, the supreme festival of <s>Kārttika</s>, is approaching,
all the beloved attendants of <s>Govinda</s> become eager
to prepare food provisions that bestow supreme bliss
for <s>Śrīmad Govinda-deva</s>, the lifter of <s>Govardhana</s>.
Various rice dishes and curries, cakes and sweetmeats prepared in many ways,
by skilled cooks and others, according to the different types of ingredients.

children.text: tair anna-kūṭaṃ saṃsthāpya yathā govardhano giriḥ |
children.translated_text: Having arranged the <s>Anna-kūṭa</s> (food-mountain) like Mount <s>Govardhana</s> itself,

children.text: tasya pārśve dhṛtaṃ sarvaṃ vyañjanādikam uttamam ||
children.translated_text: on its sides, all the excellent curries and accompaniments are placed.
And other cooked dishes too, prepared with great effort,
and many kinds of milk-products (<s>go-rasa</s>), differentiated as <s>rasālā</s> and the like.
That food-mountain, carefully prepared, [is placed] before the glorious <s>Bhagavān</s>;

children.text: yad anna-kūṭaṃ saṃvīkṣya santuṣṭo bhavati prabhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: upon seeing that <s>Anna-kūṭa</s>, the Lord is pleased.
With a greatly delighted mind, He eats, generating joy among the gods.

children.text: prabhor agre tu tat kūṭaṃ ye paśyanti narā bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: Those humans on earth who behold that food-mountain before the Lord —

children.text: bhāgya-bhājas tu te loke triṣu lokeṣu durlabhāḥ |
children.translated_text: they are blessed by fortune in this world, rare [to find] in all three worlds.
with yogurt and other food-offerings and cakes, [forming] a great, auspicious food-mountain (<s>anna-kūṭa</s>).
Having performed circumambulation (<s>parikramaṇa</s>), then together with kinsmen and friends,

children.text: mahad-ārātrikaṃ nāma ye paśyanti janā bhuvi ||
children.translated_text: those people on earth who behold the great <s>āratrika</s>,

children.text: teṣāṃ bhāgyaṃ na vaktavyaṃ sahasra-vadanair api |
children.translated_text: their fortune cannot be told even by one with a thousand mouths.
Endowed with wealth, grains, and the like, accompanied by sons and wife,

children.text: mahad-bhogaṃ bhuri kṛtvā cānte vaikuṇṭham āpnuyuḥ |
children.translated_text: having greatly enjoyed abundant pleasures, at the end they attain <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>.

children.text: prasādam anna-kūṭasya ye janāḥ param ādarāt |
children.translated_text: Those people who, with supreme reverence, [receive] the <s>prasāda</s> of the food-mountain,
feeding <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> and partaking [themselves], devoted to <s>bhakti</s>,
for them, O Goddess, the fruit of the observance becomes multiplied millions of times.

children.text: svalaṅkṛtānāṃ tu gavāṃ pūjā kāryā tataḥ śubhā ||
children.translated_text: Then the auspicious worship of well-adorned cows should be performed.
Now, the <s>darśana</s> of <s>Gopāṣṭamī</s>, as [in the <s>Bhāgavata</s>] (10.21.5):
Wearing a peacock-feather crest, with the form of the best of dancers, with <s>karṇikāra</s> flowers at His ears,
wearing a garment golden-brown, and a <s>Vaijayantī</s> garland,
filling the holes of the flute with the nectar of His lips, accompanied by the multitude of cowherds,
He entered <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> (the forest of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>), made beautiful by His own footsteps, His glories being sung.
The fruit of that <s>darśana</s>:

children.text: gopāṣṭmyāṃ tu devasya ye paśyanti harer mukham |
children.translated_text: Those who behold the face of Lord <s>Hari</s> on <s>Gopāṣṭamī</s>,

children.text: dūrān naśyanti pāpāni tasmin bhaktiś ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: their sins perish from afar, and devotion to Him is born [in them].

children.text:
dhyāyed govinda-devaṃ nava-ghana-madhuraṃ divya-līlāṃ naṭantam ity ādi
pūrvavat |
children.translated_text: One should meditate on <s>Govinda Deva</s>, sweet as a fresh rain-cloud, dancing in divine <s>līlā</s> — and so forth, as before.
On the <s>Prabodhanyā</s> [<s>Ekādaśī</s>], the <s>darśana</s> of the divine couple, as follows:

children.text: prabodhanyās tu govindaṃ ye paśyanti priyāyutam |
children.translated_text: Those who behold <s>Govinda</s> united with His beloved on <s>Prabodhanyā</s>,
for such people whose sins are diminished, unwavering devotion to Him arises.
As [stated] (in <s>Premendu</s> 12):
The <s>Prabodhinī</s> [<s>Ekādaśī</s>], which reveals the greatness of the nocturnal dance,
moving in moonlight, purifying all [who partake of] the <s>gāndharva</s> and <s>bakula</s> [celebrations].

children.text:
dvādaśyāṃ kārttikādi-vrata-mahotsavaḥ kartavyaḥ | mārga-śīrṣe pauṣe
khecaḍānnaṃ, yathā-
children.translated_text: On the <s>dvādaśī</s> (twelfth day), the great festival of the <s>Kārttika</s> observance and the like should be performed. In <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s> and <s>Pauṣa</s>, the <s>khecaḍānna</s> (a rice-and-lentil dish), as follows:
In <s>Pauṣa</s>, in this fierce frost, by the connoisseurs who are <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s attendants,
having carefully prepared there the <s>khecaḍānna</s>, dear to the Lord,
with excellent fragrant, supreme grain-rice and mung beans (<s>mudga</s>),

children.text: samabhāgaṃ tu kiñcid vā viṣamaṃ parikalpitam ||
children.translated_text: in equal portions, or somewhat unequal as prepared,
prepared appropriately for the cold season, according to popular and scriptural injunctions,

children.text: hiṅguṃ trijātaṃ maricaṃ lavaṇaṃ cādrakaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: with <s>hiṅgu</s> (asafoetida), the three spices (<s>trijāta</s>), pepper, salt, and fresh ginger,
and whatever else is well-known among the people, and especially pure cow's ghee,
by skillful workers and expert cooks,

children.text: yathāyogyaṃ tu tair dravyaiḥ pacyate bahu-yatnataḥ |
children.translated_text: it is prepared with great care using those ingredients as appropriate,
pleasing to behold, delightful, appetizing, and nourishing.
Very sweet, with yogurt dishes, and other condiments and side-dishes,
offered lovingly in the manner of the world, with great affection, to <s>Hari</s>,
prepared with cloves, cardamom, camphor, pepper, and quantities of sugar,
and with various fruits and grains from various lands,
excellent <s>laḍḍus</s> are carefully made with an abundance of love,

children.text: yad dṛṣṭvā bhojanāt kṛṣṇo jāyate hy atiharṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: seeing and eating which, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> becomes exceedingly delighted.

children.text: prabhor harṣāt tu bhaktānām atiharṣaiḥ prajāyate |
children.translated_text: From the Lord's delight, the devotees' delight arises.
Performing that daily which gives pleasure to <s>Govinda</s>,
along with matching inner garments and the like, and also fire-attendance.
I bow to <s>Śrīla Govinda</s>, the eternal form, [worshiped] at the three junctions of the day,

children.text: bhajanād yasya nityatvaṃ nityatve tasya kā kathā ||
children.translated_text: by whose worship eternality [is attained] — what need to speak of His own eternality?

children.text: draṣṭuṃ na yogyā vaktuṃ vā triṣu lokeṣu te'dhamāḥ |
children.translated_text: Unfit to behold or even to speak of in the three worlds are those lowest ones
who are averse to the twin lotus feet of <s>Śrī Govinda</s>.
I bow to the attendants (<s>pārṣadas</s>) of <s>Govinda</s>, likewise established in the three times,
by the mere remembrance of whom one obtains all desired fruits.
For those whose daily and annual
service of <s>Govinda Deva</s>, in summary the principal [forms], has been described here by me.
Moreover (from <s>BRS</s> 2.1.49):

children.text: rāgaḥ saptasu hanta ṣaṭsv api śiśor aṅgeṣv alaṃ tuṅgatā
children.translated_text: Redness in seven [parts], and in six [parts] of the child, ample prominence,

children.text: vistāras triṣu kharvatā triṣu punar gambhīratā ca triṣu |
children.translated_text: breadth in three, shortness in three, and again depth in three,

children.text: dairghyaṃ pañcasu kiṃ ca pañcasu sakhe saṃprekṣyate sūkṣmatā
children.translated_text: length in five, and in five, O friend, fineness is observed —
how can He of thirty-two excellent marks be reckoned among the cowherds?

children.text:
rāga iti vrajeśvaraṃ prati kvacit tat-sama-vayaso gopasya vākyam idam | saptasu
netrānta-pādaka-rata-latālpa-dharoṣṭha-jihvā-nakheṣu | ṣaṭsu vakṣaḥ skandha-
nakha-nāsikā-kaṭi-mukheṣu | pañcasu nāsā-bhuja-netra-hanū-jānuṣu | punaḥ
pañcasu tvak-keśāṅguli-dantāṅguli-parvasu | tathaiva mahā-puruṣa-lakṣaṇaṃ
sāmudraka-prasiddheḥ | dvātriṃśad varāṇi tal-lakṣaṇebhyo'nyebhyo'pi śreṣṭhāni
lakṣaṇāni yasya saḥ | gopeṣu katham iti bhagavad-avatārādiṣu
etādṛśīatvāśravaṇād iti bhāvaḥ |

children.translated_text: On His hands, a lotus and also a discus (<s>rathāṅga</s>),
in the form of clear lines — behold [them on] your son, [O <s>Yaśodā</s>]!
And on the tender feet, O chief of the cowherds,
[the marks of] flag, thunderbolt, goad, fish, and lotus. (from <s>BRS</s> 2.1.51)

'Redness' — this is the statement of some cowherd of the same age, addressed to the king of <s>Vraja</s>. In seven: the corners of the eyes, soles of the feet, palate, tongue, lips, palate, and nails. In six: the chest, shoulders, nails, nose, waist, and face. In five: the nose, arms, eyes, chin, and knees. Again in five: the skin, hair, finger-tips, teeth, and finger-joints. Likewise, the marks of a <s>mahāpuruṣa</s> (great person) are well-known from the <s>Sāmudraka</s> [science of physiognomy]. 'Thirty-two excellent marks' means marks superior even to those [standard] identifying features. 'How among the cowherds?' — the sense is that such [marks] have not been heard of even in the incarnations of the Lord.

children.text:
karayor iti kasyāścid vṛddha-gopyā vacanam | upalakṣaṇāny evaitāni cihnāni
padma-purāṇādi-dṛṣṭyānyāny apy asādhāraṇāni jñeyāni | tāni yathā padma-
purāṇe-
children.translated_text: 'On His hands' — this is the statement of some elderly <s>gopī</s>. These are merely indicative marks; other uncommon ones too should be known from the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> and other [sources]. They are as follows, from the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:
Listen, O <s>Nārada</s>, I shall tell the characteristics of the marks on the feet
of the blessed <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-form, who is the sole bliss of delight.

children.text: avatārā hy asaṅkhyātāḥ kathitā me tavāgrataḥ |
children.translated_text: His incarnations are innumerable — [they] have been told to you before.

children.text: paraṃ samyak pravakṣyāmi kṛṣṇas tu bhagavān svayam ||
children.translated_text: But I shall now properly declare that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is indeed the Supreme Lord Himself.

children.text: devānāṃ kārya-siddhy-artham ṛṣīṇāṃ ca tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: For the accomplishment of the gods' purposes, and likewise of the sages',
the Lord appeared, out of desire to please His own devotees.

children.text: yair eva jñāyate devo bhagavān bhakta-vatsalaḥ |
children.translated_text: Those [marks] by which the Lord, the blessed one, who is affectionate toward His devotees, is known —

children.text: tāny ahaṃ veda nānyo'pi satyam etan mayoditam ||
children.translated_text: those I [alone] know, and no one else — this truth has been declared by me.

children.text: ṣoḍaśaiva tu cihnāni mayā dṛṣṭāni tat-pade |
children.translated_text: Sixteen marks have been seen by me on His feet:
eight marks on the right [foot], and seven on the other.

children.text: dhvajāḥ padmaṃ tathā vajram aṅkuśo yava eva ca |
children.translated_text: A flag, a lotus, a thunderbolt, a goad, and a barley-grain,

children.text: svastikaṃ cordhva-rekhā ca aṣṭa-koṇas tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: a <s>svastika</s>, a vertical line, and an eight-pointed [figure].
I shall now tell the other seven, O best of <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>:
<s>Indra</s>'s bow (rainbow), a triangle, a water-pot, and a half-moon,

children.text: ambaraṃ matsya-cihnaṃ ca goṣpadaṃ saptamaṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: the sky [mark], a fish-mark, and a cow's hoof-print is remembered as the seventh.

children.text: aṅkāny etāni bho vidvan dṛśyante tu yadā kadā ||
children.translated_text: These marks, O learned one, whenever they are seen,

children.text: kṛṣṇākhyaṃ tu paraṃ brahma bhuvi jātaṃ na saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: [indicate that] the Supreme <s>Brahman</s> named <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> has been born on earth — there is no doubt.

children.text: dvayaṃ vātha trayaṃ vātha catvāraḥ pañca eva vā ||
children.translated_text: Two, or three, or four, or five [of these marks]
are seen, O best of <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>, in some incarnation or another.

children.text: ṣoḍaśaṃ tu tathā cihnaṃ śṛṇu devarṣi-saptam |
children.translated_text: And the sixteenth mark — hear [of it], O seventh among the divine sages:
resembling a <s>jambū</s> (rose-apple) fruit, it is seen here and there.
In other <s>śāstras</s>, conch, discus, and umbrella [marks] should also be known.
Now, the meditation on the hands:
With conch, half-moon, barley, goad, mace of the enemy, umbrella, flag, <s>svastika</s>,
sacrificial post, lotus, lion, bow, plough, [the mark of] <s>Śrī</s>, tree, fish, and arrows,
and with clusters of <s>nandāvarta</s> [spirals], and with these, one's own marks on the fingers,
O brother, know [Him] by these line-marked signs that indicate His being the Supreme Person (<s>Puruṣottama</s>).
Now, the gentle smile (from <s>Kṛṣṇa-Karṇāmṛta</s> 99):
By unbroken streams of the nectar of ultimate bliss (<s>nirvāṇa-rasa</s>),
shattering all other <s>rasas</s> (sentiments),
spontaneously overflowing with oceans of nectar,
Your cool smiles are victorious!
The charming fragrance of divine lotuses and other [flowers],
sipped by the bee-like eyes of the cowherd women (<s>gopāṅganās</s>),
the sweetness bestowed by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s flute-song upon
the honey of the smile of His lotus-face — that I remember.
(From the <s>Brahma-Saṃhitā</s>, 5.31):
With a swaying <s>candraka</s> ornament, a resplendent forest garland, flute,
jeweled armlet, the arts and sports of loving play,
dark-complexioned, gracefully three-bent, of eternal manifestation —
I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Person.
In the <s>Śrī Hari-Bhakti-Vilāsa</s> (18.31–37):
Thus, having examined the <s>Purāṇas</s>, <s>Tantras</s>, and the like, this is written here.
From the forehead to the chin, the sacred face should be twelve finger-breadths.
Therein, the face [proper] is one portion, therein itself four finger-breadths.

children.text: lalāṭaṃ nāsikā tadvad gulpham ardhāṅgulaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: The forehead and the nose likewise; the ankle should be half a finger-breadth.
The upper lip is half a finger-breadth; the lower is considered one finger-breadth.

children.text: dvy-aṅgulaṃ cibukaṃ cātha grīvā syāt caturaṅgulā ||
children.translated_text: The chin is two finger-breadths; then the neck should be four finger-breadths.

children.text: vakṣo-bhogo bhaved anyas tasmān nābhy-avadhiḥ paraḥ |
children.translated_text: The chest is another portion; from that, the navel-region is another.
From that, another [portion extends to] the end of the genitals; from that, the two thigh-portions.
Likewise, the two shanks are of two portions each; the two knees are four finger-breadths.

children.text: pādau ca tat-samāv itthaṃ dairghya-bhāgā navoditāḥ ||
children.translated_text: And the two feet are equal to those — thus the nine length-portions are stated.
In some [recensions], the head above the forehead [measures] three finger-breadths.

children.text: tadvad grīvā jānu-pādās tathāpi syur navaiva te ||
children.translated_text: Likewise the neck, knees, and feet — even so, they are just nine.
Thus, in total length, [the image should be] one hundred and eight finger-breadths.

children.text:
tad yathā idam eva rahasyam-yadyapi tiryaṅ-narādiṣu bhagavato janma, tathāpi
svecchayā gauḍa-deśe tad-deśīyān brāhmaṇān sarva-śreṣṭhān vijñāya teṣāṃ kule
śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-nityānandādvaitādayo janma svīkurvantaḥ | ato
mahāprabhuṇāṅgīkṛteṣu gauḍotkala-dākṣiṇātya-pāścātyeṣu gauḍa-deśa-nivāsina
eva bahavaḥ pārṣadāḥ | te khalu mahat-kula-prasūtās teṣāṃ bhojanādi-vyavahāraḥ
sat-kula-prasūtān gauḍīyān brāhmaṇān vinā na sambhavati | tathā hi-nijatve
gauḍīyān iti jñātvā sarvajña-śiromaṇir mahāprabhuḥ śrī-rūpa-sanātanau
nijāntaraṅgau vijñāpya tayoḥ sarva-śaktiṃ saṃcārya paścima-deśe svīya-vitaraṇa-
bhakta-bhūpatvena sthāpitavān | tad-dvārā nija-prakaṭana-hetu-bhūtaṃ vāñchā-
traya-samullasita-paramāntaraṅga-rūpasyātula-bhajana-ratnasya lupta-tīrthādeś ca
prakaṭanāt, svayaṃ prakāśa-śrī-govindādi-svarūpa-rāja-sevā prakāśāc ca |
children.translated_text: Namely thus — this is the secret: although the Lord takes birth among animals, humans, and the like, still, by His own will, recognizing the <s>brāhmaṇas</s> of the <s>Gauḍa</s> region as the best of all, He accepted birth in their families as <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, <s>Nityānanda</s>, <s>Advaita</s>, and others. Therefore, among those accepted by <s>Mahāprabhu</s> — from <s>Gauḍa</s>, <s>Utkala</s>, the South, and the West — the many attendants (<s>pārṣadas</s>) are indeed residents of the <s>Gauḍa</s> region. They are indeed born of great families; their food and other dealings are not possible without <s>Gauḍīya brāhmaṇas</s> born of good families. Thus — knowing the <s>Gauḍīyas</s> as His own, the all-knowing crest-jewel <s>Mahāprabhu</s>, having informed <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> and <s>Sanātana</s> as His most intimate [associates] and having transmitted all power to them, established them in the western region as the sovereignty of His devotees for the purpose of His own distribution [of <s>prema</s>]. Through them, the incomparable jewel of worship of His supremely intimate <s>Rūpa</s> — illuminating his three wishes — and the revelation of the lost sacred sites, and the revelation of the original self-manifest <s>Śrī Govinda</s> and other forms and their royal service [were accomplished].

children.text:
tābhyāṃ ca punaḥ śrī-vṛndāvanaṃ gatvā śrī-śrī-sevādikaṃ parivāre tat samarpitam
| na tu nija-pārśva-vartiṣu śrī-gopāla-bhaṭṭa-śrī-raghunātha-dāsādiṣu svato
bhagavan-mantra-gṛhīta-sva-bhrātuṣputra-śrī-jīva-gosvāmiṣu ca | aho parama-
bhāgavatānāṃ maryādā-rakṣaṇa-svabhāvaḥ svayaṃ caite sevā-samaye mandire na
praviśanti ca | kim utānyat | etat tu śrī-caitanya-caritāmṛtādau prasiddhaṃ vartate
|
children.translated_text: And having gone again to <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>, they entrusted the service and the like to those in their retinue — but not to those at their own side, <s>Śrī Gopāla Bhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Śrī Raghunātha Dāsa</s>, and others, nor to <s>Śrī Jīva Gosvāmī</s>, his own brother's grandson who had taken the divine <s>mantra</s> from him. Ah, the nature of the supremely devout is to protect propriety (<s>maryādā</s>)! They themselves did not enter the temple at the time of service. What to speak of others? This is well-known in the <s>Śrī Caitanya-Caritāmṛta</s> and other [works].

(3)
Third Section (<s>Kakṣā</s>)
Now, regarding the <s>dhīra-lalita</s> (gallant-heroic) <s>Śrīmad Govinda Deva</s> (from <s>BRS</s> 2.1.63):
Although His age varies, [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] as the substrate of all devotional <s>rasas</s>,
the defined subject (<s>dharmī</s>) here is precisely the adolescent (<s>kiśora</s>), eternally sporting in various ways.

children.text:
tad yathā (BRS 2.1.308-312)-
vayaḥ kaumāra-paugaṇḍa-kaiśoram iti tat tridhā ||
children.translated_text:
Namely thus (from <s>BRS</s> 2.1.308–312):
Age is threefold: <s>kaumāra</s> (childhood), <s>paugaṇḍa</s> (boyhood), and <s>kaiśora</s> (adolescence).
<s>Kaumāra</s> extends to the end of the fifth year; <s>paugaṇḍa</s> up to the tenth.

children.text: ā-ṣoḍaśāc ca kaiśoraṃ yauvanaṃ syāt tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kaiśora</s> extends up to the sixteenth [year]; <s>yauvana</s> (youth) would be thereafter.

children.text: aucityāt tatra kaumāraṃ vaktavyaṃ vatsale rase |
children.translated_text: By propriety, <s>kaumāra</s> is to be spoken of in the <s>vātsalya rasa</s> (parental affection);
<s>paugaṇḍa</s> [is spoken of] in <s>preyas</s> (friendship), by virtue of its connection with various sports and the like.

children.text: śraiṣṭhyam ujjvala evāsya kaiśorasya tathāpy adaḥ |
children.translated_text: The supremacy of this <s>kaiśora</s> [age] is indeed in the <s>ujjvala</s> (amorous) [<s>rasa</s>]; and yet,
because of its suitability for nearly all <s>rasas</s>, it is cited here in sequence.

children.text: ādyaṃ madhyaṃ tathā śeṣaṃ kaiśoraṃ trividhaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Adolescence (<s>kaiśora</s>) is threefold: early, middle, and final.
Among these, the middle [adolescence] is as follows (BRS 2.1.320-324):

children.text: ūru-dvayasya bāhvoś ca kāpi śrīr urasas tathā |
children.translated_text: A certain beauty of the thighs, arms, and chest;

children.text: mūrter mādhurimādyaṃ ca kaiśore sati madhyame ||
children.translated_text: the first [signs of] sweetness of form — [these are seen] in the middle [stage of] adolescence.
The pair of thighs aspires to rival the trunk of an elephant;
the chest desires the companionship of the sapphire door-panel;
the pair of arms too wishes to put to shame the array of door-bolts —
[all this happens] at the onset of <s>Keśava</s>'s fresh youth.
For instance —
The face rich with the play of smiles; the eyes with the uppermost flutter of coquetry;

children.text: tri-jagan-mohanaṃ gītam ity ādir iha mādhurī ||
children.translated_text: the singing that enchants the three worlds — this, to begin with, is the sweetness here.
The eyes, cresting with waves of skill in the strategies of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Cupid);
the lotus-face with its charmingly upturned, playfully smiling lips;
the singing that mocks the vows of steadfast family women —

children.text: hares taruṇimāṅkure sphurati mādhurī kāpy abhūt ||
children.translated_text: in the budding youth of <s>Hari</s>, an indescribable sweetness manifested.
For instance —
The full extent of the essence of cleverness (<s>vaidagdhī</s>); the great festival of <s>kuñja</s>-pastimes (<s>kuñja-keli</s>);
the commencement of the <s>rāsa-līlā</s> and the like — here, [there is] the beauty of activities and the like.
'sameness. Here, in the middle [age], the beauty of activities and the like' — for instance (BRS 2.1.325):
Somewhere with footprints clearly marked with <s>alaktaka</s> (lac-dye), somewhere with scattered peacock-feather crests,
somewhere with couches from which girdle-bells have slipped off — she, strewn with clusters of <s>kuñjas</s> (bowers),
with sandy banks shining with the auspicious splendor of circular dance-formations (<s>maṇḍala-bandha-tāṇḍava</s>),
the <s>Vṛndā</s> forest proclaims abundantly the cluster of pastimes of <s>Govinda</s>.
The commentary of the venerable Śrī <s>Jīva Gosvāmī</s> [states]: 'In the middle and final ages, there is mostly',
The characteristics of the <s>dhīra-lalita</s> [hero] (BRS 2.1.230-2) —
Clever (<s>vidagdha</s>), of fresh youth, expert in jest,
carefree — the <s>dhīra-lalita</s> is mostly under the sway of his beloveds.
With words hinting at the boldness of the amorous arts of the previous night, making <s>Rādhikā</s>
lower her eyes with bashfulness, in front of her companions,
having reached the far shore of expertise in the wondrous play of [painting] <s>makarī</s> (fish-designs) on her breasts —

children.text: kaiśoraṃ saphalī-karoti kalayan kuñje vihāraṃ hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hari</s> makes adolescence fruitful, arranging pastimes in the bower.
For instance —
In <s>Govinda</s>, the <s>dhīra-lalita</s> nature is openly displayed;
those who know drama (<s>nāṭya-jña</s>) generally cite the banner-of-Cupid (<s>makara-dhvaja</s>) here.
Therefore, in Śrī <s>Govindadeva</s>, who has the permanent mood (<s>sthāyibhāva</s>) characterized as <s>dhīra-lalita</s>, the middle adolescence is clearly seen.

children.text: antaḥpuras tu devasya madhye pūryā manoharam |
children.translated_text: The inner apartments of the Lord, in the center of the city, beautiful,
enclosed by jeweled walls, adorned with splendid arched gateways,

children.text: vimānair gṛhamukhyaiś ca prāsādair bahubhir vṛtam |
children.translated_text: surrounded by aerial mansions, chief residences, and many palaces,
everywhere adorned by divine <s>Apsaras</s> women.

children.text: madhye tu maṇḍapaṃ divyaṃ rājasthānaṃ mahotsavam |
children.translated_text: In the center, a divine pavilion — the royal hall, [the site of] great festivals,
graced by a thousand ruby pillars, made of jewels, auspicious,
filled with eternally liberated souls, beautified by the singing of <s>Sāma</s> [Veda hymns].
In the center, a charming throne, constituted of all the <s>Vedas</s>, auspicious,
surrounded by the eternal deities of <s>Dharma</s> and the like, whose nature is the <s>Vedas</s>,
by <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), great sovereignty (<s>Mahaiśvarya</s>), and <s>Vairāgya</s> (dispassion), in embodied forms;
in the middle there dwell Fire, Sun, and Moon,

children.text: kūrmaś ca nāgarājaś ca vainateyas trayīśvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and Tortoise, the King of Serpents, <s>Vainateya</s> (Garuḍa), and the lord of the three [<s>Vedas</s>];
all meters and all <s>mantras</s> have assumed the form of the seat (<s>pīṭha</s>);
this divine [seat], composed of all syllables, is known as the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>.
In its center, an eight-petaled lotus with the radiance of the rising sun;
in the center of that, on the pericarp, in <s>Sāvitrī</s>, of auspicious appearance —

children.text: īśvaryā saha deveśas tatrāsīnaḥ paraḥ pumān |
children.translated_text: there, together with <s>Īśvarī</s> (the Goddess), the supreme Person, the Lord of gods, is seated,
dark as the petal of a blue lotus, with the radiance of ten million suns.
Thus the third enclosure. ||3||
(4) The fourth enclosure.
Now, the greatness of the <s>mantra</s> of Śrī <s>Gopāladeva</s>:

children.text: mantrās tu kṛṣṇa-devasya sākṣād bhagavato hareḥ |
children.translated_text: The <s>mantras</s> of <s>Kṛṣṇadeva</s>, the directly manifest <s>Bhagavān Hari</s>,
the seed of all <s>avatāras</s>, are the most powerful of all.
Similarly, in the <s>Bṛhad-gautamīya</s>, [in the section] called <s>Śrī Govinda-Vṛndāvana</s> —
Among all the best of <s>mantras</s>, the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> [<s>mantra</s>] is declared supreme;
especially the <s>Kṛṣṇa-mantras</s>, which are the sole means to both enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: yasya yasya ca mantrasya yo yo devas tathā punaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>mantra</s> belongs to whatever deity,

children.text: abhedāt tan-manūnāṃ ca devatā saiva bhāṣyate ||
children.translated_text: because of the non-difference of those <s>mantras</s>, the deity [of each] is declared to be the same [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>].
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone is the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, whose form is being, consciousness, and bliss (<s>sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha</s>);
by merely remembering those [<s>mantras</s>], he bestows the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
Moreover, among those [<s>mantras</s>], the supreme ones are those of him who manifests his own divinity through cowherd pastimes (<s>gopa-līlā</s>);

children.text: tasya śreṣṭhatamā mantrās teṣv apy aṣṭādaśākṣaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and among those, the eighteen-syllable [<s>mantra</s>] is the most excellent.
Now, the greatness of the eighteen-syllable [<s>mantra</s>] in the <s>Tāpanī Śrutis</s>:

children.text:
oṃ munayo ha vai brahmāṇam ūcuḥ | kaḥ paramo devaḥ | kuto mṛtyur bibheti |
kasya jñānenākhilaṃ jñātaṃ bhavati | kenedaṃ viśvaṃ saṃsaratīti | tān u hovāca
brāhmaṇaḥ -- kṛṣṇo vai paramaṃ daivatam | govindān mṛtyur bibheti | gopī-jana-
vallabha-jñānenākhilaṃ jñātaṃ bhavati | svāhayedaṃ saṃsaratīti | tam u hocuḥ | kaḥ
kṛṣṇo govindaḥ ko'sau gopī-jana-vallabhaḥ kaḥ kā svāheti | tān uvāca brāhmaṇaḥ
pāpa-karṣaṇo go-bhūmi-veda-vidito veditā gopī-janāvidyā-kalā-prerakas tan-māyā
ceti | sakalaṃ paraṃ brahmaiva tat | yo dhyāyati rasati bhajati so'mṛto bhavati so'mṛto
bhavatīti | te hocuḥ -- kiṃ tad-rūpaṃ kiṃ rasanaṃ kathaṃ vāho tad-bhajanaṃ | tat
sarvaṃ vividiṣatām ākhyāhīti | tad u hovāca hairaṇyaḥ -- gopa-veśam abhrābhaṃ

children.translated_text: youthful, taking shelter of a wish-fulfilling tree.' (GTU 1.2-8)

Oṃ. The sages indeed said to <s>Brahmā</s>: 'Who is the supreme deity? Of whom is Death afraid? By the knowledge of whom does one know everything? By whom does this universe revolve?' He, <s>Brahmā</s>, said to them: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> indeed is the supreme deity. Death is afraid of <s>Govinda</s>. By the knowledge of the beloved of the <s>gopī</s>-folk, everything becomes known. By <s>Svāhā</s>, this [universe] revolves.' They said to him: 'Who is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>? Who is <s>Govinda</s>? Who is that beloved of the <s>gopī</s>-folk? Who is <s>Svāhā</s>?' <s>Brahmā</s> said to them: 'The remover of sins; known to cows, earth, and the <s>Vedas</s>; the knower; the impeller of the <s>gopī</s>-folk, of <s>avidyā</s> (ignorance), and of <s>kalā</s> (creative power); and his <s>māyā</s> — all this is the supreme <s>Brahman</s> alone. Whoever meditates, relishes, and worships [him] becomes immortal, becomes immortal.' They said: 'What is his form? What is the relishing? How is that worship [to be done]? Tell all this to us who wish to know.' The golden one [<s>Hiraṇya</s>, i.e. <s>Brahmā</s>] then said: 'In the attire of a cowherd, dark as a cloud,

children.text:
kiṃ ca, tatraivāgre --
bhaktir asya bhajanam | tad ihāmutropādhi-nairāsyenaivāmuṣmin manaḥ-kalpanam
| etad eva ca naiṣkarmyam |
children.translated_text: Moreover, further on in the same [text]: 'Devotion (<s>bhakti</s>) is the worship of him. In this [world] and the next, it is the turning of the mind toward him alone, without regard for any limiting condition (<s>upādhi</s>). This alone is freedom from [the bondage of] action (<s>naiṣkarmya</s>).'

children.text:
kṛṣṇaṃ taṃ viprā bahudhā yajanti
govindaṃ santaṃ bahudhārādhayanti |
gopījana-vallabho bhuvanāni dadhre
svāhāśrito jagad ejayjat sva-retāḥ ||161|| (GTU 1.14-15)
children.translated_text: The learned ones worship that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in many ways; the saints adore <s>Govinda</s>, who is being, in many ways. The beloved of the <s>gopī</s>-folk sustains the worlds; depending on <s>Svāhā</s>, he set the universe in motion by his own seed. ||161|| (GTU 1.14-15)

children.text:
vāyur yathaiko bhuvanaṃ praviṣṭo
janye janye pañca-rūpo babhūva |
kṛṣṇas tathaiko'pi jagad-dhitārthaṃ
śabdenāsau pañca-pado vibhāti ||162|| iti | (GTU 1.16)
children.translated_text: Just as the one wind, having entered the world, became fivefold in each and every creature — so too <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, though one, for the welfare of the world, shines as five-footed [i.e., the five-worded <s>mantra</s>] through [sacred] sound. ||162|| (GTU 1.16)
Moreover, in that same [text], after the description of the procedure of worship —

children.text:
eko vaśī sarvagaḥ kṛṣṇa īḍya
eko'pi san bahudhā yo vibhāti |
taṃ pīṭhasthaṃ ye'nubhajanti dhīrās
teṣāṃ sukhaṃ śāśvataṃ netareṣām ||163|| (GTU
children.translated_text: The one controller, omnipresent, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, worthy of praise — though one, he shines as many. Those wise ones who worship him, seated on the [<s>yoga</s>-]<s>pīṭha</s>, [attain] eternal happiness — not others. ||163|| (GTU
The eternal among the eternal, the conscious among the conscious,
the one among the many who fulfills desires —
those wise ones who worship him, seated on the <s>pīṭha</s>,
[attain] eternal perfection — not others. ||164||
Those who are eternally liberated and worship that
supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, not [driven by] desires —
to them, he, in the form of a cowherd, with [their] effort,
reveals his own abode at that very [moment]. ||165||
He who first created <s>Brahmā</s>,

children.text: yo vidyās tasmai gopāyati sma kṛṣṇaḥ |
