children.translated_text: he who protected the knowledge for him — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the cowherd —
that divine [being], the illuminator of the intellect of the self,
one who seeks liberation should indeed take refuge [in him] and follow [him]. ||166||

children.text:
japa-saṅkhyā yathā gautamīya-tantre (15.4)-anena lakṣa-jāpena kṛṣṇaṃ paśyati
cakṣuṣā | aneneti pratyakṣeṇa svarūpeṇa svapnena vā kṛṣṇa-sākṣātkāro bhavatīty
arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: The count of <s>japa</s> (repetitions), as in the <s>Gautamīya-tantra</s> (15.4): 'By one <s>lakṣa</s> (one hundred thousand) repetitions of this [<s>mantra</s>], one sees <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with one's eyes.' 'By this' means: the direct vision (<s>sākṣātkāra</s>) of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> occurs either through direct perception, in one's own form, or in a dream — this is the meaning.

children.text:
puraścaraṇādi-vidhis tu śrī-brahma-saṃhitā-gopāla-tāpanī-hari-bhakti-vilāsa-
ṭīkāyāṃ draṣṭavyaḥ | sa tu viśeṣato yoga-pīṭhe draṣṭavyaḥ |
children.translated_text: The procedure of <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preparatory rites) and the like should be seen in the commentary on the <s>Śrī Brahma-saṃhitā</s>, <s>Gopāla-tāpanī</s>, and <s>Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</s>. And that should especially be consulted regarding the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>.
Those who repeat the five-worded <s>mantra</s>
of <s>Govinda</s>, preceded by <s>Oṃkāra</s> —
to them he reveals his own form;
therefore, one who seeks liberation should practice [it] constantly for eternal peace. ||167||
After that, other <s>mantras</s> of <s>Govinda</s>
for human beings arose from the five-worded [<s>mantra</s>];
the ten-syllabled and other [<s>mantras</s>] are also properly
practiced by those desiring prosperity, along with <s>Saṅkrandana</s> (<s>Indra</s>) and others. ||168||

children.text:
kiṃ ca tatraiva-
tad u hovāca brāhmaṇo'sāv anavarataṃ me dhyātaḥ stutaḥ parārdhānte so'budhyata
| gopa-veśo me puruṣaḥ purastād āvirbabhūva | tataḥ praṇatena mayā'nukūlena
hṛdā mahyam aṣṭādaśārṇaṃ svarūpaṃ sṛṣṭaye dattvāntarhitaḥ | punaḥ sisṛkṣā me
prādurabhūt | teṣv akṣareṣu bhaviṣyaj-jagad-rūpaṃ prakāśayat | tad iha kād āpo
| lāt pṛthivī | īto'gniḥ | bindor induḥ | tan-nādād arka iti klīṃ-kārād asṛjam |
kṛṣṇād ākāśaṃ yad vāyur ity uttarāt surabhiṃ vidyāṃ prādurakārṣam | tad-uttarāt
tad-uttarāt strī-pumādi cedaṃ sakalam idaṃ iti ||169||
children.translated_text: from the next — male and female and so on — all this.' ||169||

Moreover, in the same [text]: '<s>Brahmā</s> said: He was constantly meditated upon and praised by me. At the end of a <s>parārdha</s> [half of Brahmā's lifespan], he awoke. A person in cowherd attire appeared before me. Then, bowed down by me with a favorable heart, having given me the eighteen-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>] — his own form — for the sake of creation, he disappeared. Again the desire to create arose in me. In those syllables, the form of the future world became manifest: from <s>ka</s> — water; from <s>la</s> — earth; from <s>ī</s> — fire; from the <s>bindu</s> (dot) — the moon; from the <s>nāda</s> (resonance) of that — the sun. Thus from <s>klīṃ</s> I created. From <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — space, which is wind — [thus] from the next [syllable] I brought forth the <s>surabhī</s> knowledge. From the next —
Similarly, in the <s>Gautamīya</s> —

children.text: klīṃ-kārād asṛjad viśvam iti prāha śruteḥ śiraḥ |
children.translated_text: The crest of <s>Śruti</s> (the <s>Upaniṣad</s>) declares: 'From <s>klīṃ</s> he created the universe.'
From <s>la</s>, earth was born; from <s>ka</s>, the origin of water. ||170||

children.text: ī-kārād vahnir utpanno nādād āyur ajāyata |
children.translated_text: From <s>ī</s>, fire was produced; from <s>nāda</s>, wind was born;
from <s>bindu</s>, the origin of space — thus the <s>mantra</s> is of the nature of the [five] elements.

children.text: svā-śabdena ca kṣetrajño heti cit-prakṛtiḥ parā |
children.translated_text: By the word '<s>svā</s>', the <s>kṣetrajña</s> (knower of the field, i.e. the soul); by the [syllable] '<s>hā</s>', the supreme conscious nature (<s>cit-prakṛti</s>);
the syllable denoting the face-covering [i.e. <s>svāhā</s>] is born from the union of those two.

children.text: ataeva hi viśvasya layaḥ svāhārṇake bhavet ||171||
children.translated_text: Therefore indeed, the dissolution of the universe takes place in the syllable <s>svāhā</s>. ||171||

children.text:
punaś ca sā śrutiḥ --
etasyaiva yajanena candra-dhvajo gata-moham ātmānaṃ vedayitvā oṃkārāntarālakaṃ
manum āvartayat saṅga-rahito'bhyānayat | tad viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padaṃ sadā paśyanti
sūrayaḥ | divīva cakṣur ātatam | tasmād enaṃ nityam abhyaset ||172|| ity ādi |
children.translated_text: And again, that <s>Śruti</s> [states]: 'By the worship of this very [<s>Govinda</s>], the one whose banner is the moon [<s>Śiva</s>], having become free from delusion, having known himself, repeated the <s>mantra</s> preceded by <s>Oṃkāra</s>; freed from attachment, he drew near [<s>Govinda</s>]. "The wise ones always behold that supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, like an eye spread across the sky." Therefore one should always practice this [<s>mantra</s>].' ||172|| And so on.
Further on in the same [text] —
From whose first syllable (<s>pada</s>) earth [arises], from the second, the origin of water,
from the third, brilliance was born, from the fourth, the wind-bearer (air), ||173||
from the fifth, the origin of sky — one should practice that [<s>mantra</s>] alone.
<s>Candradhvaja</s> [<s>Śiva</s>] attained the imperishable supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. ||174||
Then, the pure, the stainless,
the sorrowless, freed from all attachment to greed and the like —

children.text: yat tat padaṃ pañca-padaṃ tad eva
children.translated_text: that very abode, [expressed by] the five words (<s>pañca-pada</s>),
is <s>Vāsudeva</s>; beyond him nothing else exists. ||175||

children.text:
tam ekaṃ govindaṃ sac-cid-ānanda-vigraham pañca-padaṃ vṛndāvana-sura-bhūruha-
talāsīnaṃ satataṃ sa-marud-gaṇo'haṃ paramayā stutyā toṣayāmi ||176|| iti |
children.translated_text: That one <s>Govinda</s>, whose form is being, consciousness, and bliss (<s>sac-cid-ānanda-vigraha</s>), [expressed by] the five words, seated beneath the wish-fulfilling tree of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — together with the host of <s>Maruts</s>, I constantly glorify him with the supreme hymn of praise. ||176||
Moreover, immediately after the hymn —

children.text:
amuṃ pañcapadaṃ mantram āvartayed yaḥ sa yāty anāyāsataḥ kevalaṃ tat padaṃ tat
| anejad ekaṃ manaso javīyo naitad devā āpnuvan pūrvam arśāt |
tasmāt kṛṣṇa eva paro devas taṃ dhyāyet taṃ raset taṃ yajed iti oṃ tat sad iti |
children.translated_text: One who repeats this five-worded <s>mantra</s> goes effortlessly to that very abode alone. 'Unmoving, one, swifter than the mind — the gods could not reach it, as it went before [them].' Therefore, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> alone is the supreme deity; one should meditate on him, relish him, worship him. Oṃ tat sat.
[the following passage occurs] —
The lord of <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s>, <s>kāma</s>, and <s>mokṣa</s>, the lord of the universe —
his glorious <s>avatāras</s> are thousands.
And in the <s>Trailokya-saṃmohana-tantra</s>, in the context of the eighteen-syllable [<s>mantra</s>] spoken by Śrī <s>Mahādeva</s> to the Goddess —
Among those <s>avatāras</s>, the childhood [form] is exceedingly rare;

children.text: amānuṣāṇi karmāṇi tāni tāni kṛtāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and various superhuman deeds were performed [by him].
He by whom everything is established through the power of cursing and blessing —
I shall now declare his <s>mantra</s>, unsurpassed, complete with all its limbs and sub-limbs.
By the mere knowledge of which, a person attains omniscience;

children.text: putrārthī putram āpnoti dharmārthī labhate dhanam ||
children.translated_text: one desiring a son obtains a son; one desiring <s>dharma</s> obtains wealth.
One becomes a master of the meaning of all <s>śāstras</s> — without doubt;
and one can bring the three worlds under one's control, and set the universe into agitation.

children.text: mohayet sakalaṃ so'pi mārayet sakalān ripūn |
children.translated_text: He would enchant all, and would also destroy all enemies.

children.text: bahunā kim ihoktena mumukṣur mokṣam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: What more need be said here? One who desires liberation attains <s>mokṣa</s>. ||

children.text: yathā cintāmaṇiḥ śreṣṭho yathā gauś ca yathā satī |
children.translated_text: Just as the <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gem) is the best, just as the cow, just as a faithful wife,

children.text: yathā dvijo yathā gaṅgā tathāsau mantra uttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: just as a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, just as the <s>Gaṅgā</s> — so is this <s>mantra</s> supreme. ||

children.text: yathāvad akhila-śreṣṭhaṃ yathā śāstraṃ tu vaiṣṇavam |
children.translated_text: Just as the best of all in every respect, just as the <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> scripture,

children.text: yathā susaṃskṛtā vāṇī tathāsau mantra uttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: just as well-refined speech — so is this <s>mantra</s> supreme. ||
Moreover —

children.text: ato mayā sureśāni pratyahaṃ japyate manuḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, O Queen of the gods, this <s>mantra</s> is chanted by me every day.

children.text: naitena sadṛśaḥ kaścid jagaty asmin caracare ||
children.translated_text: There is nothing in this world of moving and unmoving [beings] equal to this. ||
In the <s>Sanatkumāra-kalpa</s> also —
The <s>mantras</s> pertaining to <s>Gopāla</s> are thirty-three in their varieties.

children.text: teṣu sarveṣu mantreṣu mantra-rājam imaṃ śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: Among all those <s>mantras</s>, hear this king of <s>mantras</s>. ||
This most gracious <s>mantra</s>, in the <s>tantra</s> called <s>Sammohana</s> —
should be kept secret by you with effort, O best of sages. ||
By this king of <s>mantras</s>, <s>Purandara</s> (<s>Indra</s>) attained
the sovereignty of <s>Mahendra</s> — directly given by <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the God of gods. ||
Formerly, afflicted by misfortune due to the curse of <s>Durvāsas</s>,

children.text: sa eva subhagavatvaṃ vai tenaiva punar āptavān ||
children.translated_text: he again attained good fortune by that very [<s>mantra</s>]. ||
What more need be said here? Even without the practices of <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preparatory rites),
by chanting alone, one obtains all that is desired. ||
I bow to the Lord <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, the supreme <s>guru</s>,

children.text: kathañcid āśrayād yasya prākṛto'py uttamo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: by somehow taking shelter of whom, even a common person becomes exalted. ||

children.text: kathanam | tatra mantroddhāraṇaṃ ca yathā brahma-saṃhitāyāṃ (5.24) ca-
children.translated_text: Therein, the extraction of the <s>mantra</s>, as in the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (5.24) —
Thus, in the <s>Śrī Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</s>, in the narration of the greatness of <s>mantras</s>, [this is] the narration of the greatness of the <s>Śrī Gopāla-mantra</s>.

children.text: kāmaḥ kṛṣṇāya govinda ṅe gopī-jana ity api |
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s> (klīṃ), <s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, the ending [<s>ṅe</s>], '<s>gopī-jana</s>' also,

children.text: vallabhāya priyā vahner mantram te dāsyati priyam ||
children.translated_text: '<s>vallabhāya</s>' — the beloved of fire (<s>svāhā</s>) will give you the dear <s>mantra</s>. ||

children.text:
ka-kāro līlā-śaktiḥ | la-kāro bhū-śaktiḥ | ī-kāraḥ śrī-śaktiḥ ma-kāras tattva-
viśiṣṭaḥ | kṛṣṇāyeti sarva-cittākarṣakāyeti | athavā-
children.translated_text: The <s>ka</s>-syllable is the <s>līlā-śakti</s> (play-potency). The <s>la</s>-syllable is the <s>bhū-śakti</s> (earth-potency). The <s>ī</s>-syllable is the <s>śrī-śakti</s> (splendor-potency). The <s>ma</s>-syllable is distinguished by the tattva-principle. '<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>' means: to the one who attracts all minds. Alternatively —

children.text:
kṛṣi-śabdaś ca sattārtho ṇaś cānanda-svarūpakaḥ |
sukha-rūpo bhaved ātmā bhāvānanda-mayatvataḥ || iti |
children.translated_text:
The word '<s>kṛṣ</s>' has the meaning of 'existence,' and '<s>ṇa</s>' has the nature of bliss.
The <s>ātman</s> is of the nature of happiness, because of being made of the bliss of being. || Thus.

children.text:
govindāyeti pūrvavat | gām indriya-kulaṃ vindatīti govindaḥ | gāṃ govardhanam
uddhṛtya paramaiśvarya-pradatvena rakṣati pālayatīti govindas tasmai | gopī-jana-
vallabhāyeti-
children.translated_text: '<s>Govindāya</s>' — as before. He who finds (<s>vindati</s>) the family of senses (<s>indriya-kula</s>) is <s>Govinda</s>. He who, having lifted <s>Govardhana</s>, protects and sustains [the devotees] by bestowing supreme lordship — to that <s>Govinda</s>. '<s>Gopī-jana-vallabhāya</s>' —

children.text:
gopīti prakṛtiṃ vidyāj janas tattva-samūhakaḥ |
anayor āśrayo vyāptyā kāraṇatvena ceśvaraḥ |
children.translated_text:
'<s>Gopī</s>' should be known as <s>Prakṛti</s> (primordial nature); '<s>jana</s>' is the aggregate of <s>tattvas</s> (principles).
The Lord, by pervading and by being the cause, is the shelter of both of these.

children.text:
pūrvārthe svāhety asya tathā-tathābhūtāyātmānaṃ samarpayāmi | tatra krama-
dīpikāyām (1.1)-
children.translated_text: In the former sense, '<s>svāhā</s>' [means]: 'I offer myself to the One who is thus-and-thus.' Therein, in the <s>Krama-dīpikā</s> (1.1) —
He whose form has been attained by a particle of <s>Māyā</s> obtained from [His own] art (<s>kalā</s>),
who is charming with the melodious sound of the sweetly resonating flute,
who, having entered the heart, agitates the three worlds —
may that <s>Gopī-jana-vallabha</s> (beloved of the <s>gopī</s>-folk) be for your prosperity! ||
Now, the extraction [of the <s>mantra</s>] from the <s>Sammohana-tantra</s> —
<s>Vāgbhava</s> (the seed of speech), <s>Madana-śakti</s> (the power of desire),
joined with <s>Indirā</s> (Lakṣmī), adorned with all <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) —
this <s>mantra</s>, uttered as the syllable of the universe,
in reversed order, accomplishes all that is desired. ||
Now, the characteristics of <s>mantra-siddhi</s> (perfection of the <s>mantra</s>) —

children.text: ādāv ṛṣy-ādi-nyāsaḥ syāt kara-śuddhis tataḥ param |
children.translated_text: First, there should be the <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) of the seer and the like; then, the purification of the hands.
The <s>nyāsa</s> pervading the fingers, and indeed the <s>nyāsa</s> of the heart and the like. ||

children.text: tāla-trayaṃ ca dig-bandhaḥ prāṇāyāmas tataḥ param |
children.translated_text: The three claps, the binding of the directions, and then <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control),

children.text: dhyāna-pūjā japaś caiva sarva-tantreṣv ayaṃ vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: meditation, worship, and chanting — this is the procedure in all <s>tantras</s>. ||

children.text:
nyāsa-vidhiḥ-śrī-vrajācārya-śrīmad-rūpa-gosvāmi-bhajanānusāreṇa |
ahaṅkārādhiṣṭhātṛtvād bhūta-śuddher adhidevāya saṅkarṣaṇāya namaḥ | he
saṅkarṣaṇa-deva prasīda kṛpāṃ kuru | asya janasya deha-rūpeṇa pariṇataṃ bhūta-
pañcakaṃ yathā sadyaḥ śudhyed upāsanopayuktaṃ syāt tathā kṛpāṃ kuru |
children.translated_text:
The procedure of <s>nyāsa</s> — according to the worship-practice of the preceptor of <s>Vraja</s>, <s>Śrīmad Rūpa Gosvāmin</s>.
'Because of being the presiding deity of the ego-principle, salutations to <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, the presiding deity of elemental purification (<s>bhūta-śuddhi</s>). O Lord <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>! Be pleased, bestow grace. May the five elements transformed into the form of this person's body be immediately purified and made fit for worship — thus bestow grace.'
Now, the meditation on <s>Mātṛkā</s> (the Mother of syllables) —
With peacock-feathers arranged in the hair, with full, high breasts,
in the right hand, a jewel-like knowledge in the form of a lotus,
in the left hand, bearing a pot of yogurt and the lofty <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge) —
I praise the form of <s>Mātṛkā</s>, with the radiance of nectar-rays. ||
The meditation on <s>Keśava-kīrti</s> and the like —
With the corner-glance of wide-beautiful eyes, licking each other with charming [glances],
each embracing [the other] with one arm, with abundant horripilation,
fair and dark, wearing a pair of garments — dark and fair —
I remember <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with unbridled longing [born of] the sport of desire. ||

children.text:
tat-tan-māsasya vāsudevo'dhiṣṭhātā | sa stoka-kṛṣṇo'tra jñeyaḥ | tasya dhyānam
ucyate-
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsudeva</s> is the presiding deity of each respective month. He should be known here as <s>Stoka-Kṛṣṇa</s>. His meditation is stated —
Dark as a cloud, with garments bright as lightning,
smiling, with a hand radiant with a playful lotus,
with a peacock-feather crest-ornament, in the form of <s>Vāsudeva</s> —
I bow to <s>Stoka-Kṛṣṇa</s>, dearest to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. ||

children.text:
ānanda-ghanaṃ smaren manasvī | tatra kuṭṭima-vare sphuṭa-dīpta-yoga-pīṭhaṃ
vicintya-
children.translated_text: The wise one should meditate on the mass of bliss. Therein, upon the excellent pavement, having visualized the brightly shining <s>Yoga-pīṭha</s> —
Therein, upon the vast, blazing pericarp,
resplendent, the abodes of steadfast bliss —
with radiance mocking fresh clouds and gold —
I meditate upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rādhā</s>. ||

children.text: mantrārthaṃ mantra-caitanyaṃ yoni-mudrāṃ na vetti yaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who does not know the meaning of the <s>mantra</s>, the consciousness of the <s>mantra</s>, and the <s>yoni-mudrā</s> —
even by a hundred crore chantings, perfection does not arise for him. ||
Again, in the extraction of the <s>mantra</s>, the ten consecrations (<s>saṃskāras</s>), as [stated] in the <s>Śāradā-tilaka</s> —

children.text: jananaṃ jīvanaṃ ceti tāḍanaṃ rodhanaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: Generation, vivification, striking, restraining,
then bathing, purification, nourishment again,
satiating, illuminating, and concealing — these are the ten consecrations of the <s>mantra</s>. ||
And again —
Seven methods should be performed therein, as spoken by <s>Śaṅkara</s>:
revolving, restraining, subjugating, tormenting, nourishing and withering, ||

children.text: dahanāntaṃ kramāt kuryāt tataḥ siddho bhaven manuḥ |
children.translated_text: ending with burning — one should perform [them] in order; then the <s>mantra</s> becomes perfected.

children.text: japāt siddhir japāt siddhir japāt siddhir na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Perfection from chanting! Perfection from chanting! Perfection from chanting — there is no doubt! ||

children.text: aharniśaṃ japed yas tu mantrī niyata-mānasaḥ |
children.translated_text: One who chants day and night, the <s>mantrin</s> with a controlled mind —

children.text: sa paśyati na sandeho gopa-veśa-dharaṃ harim ||
children.translated_text: he beholds, without doubt, <s>Hari</s> wearing the garb of a cowherd. ||
Now, the procedure of sectional (<s>khaṇḍa</s>) <s>puraścaraṇa</s> (preparatory observance) —
Beginning from sunrise until the next sunrise,

children.text: tāvat kālaṃ manuṃ japtvā sarva-siddhīśvaro bhavet ||
children.translated_text: having chanted the <s>mantra</s> during that period, one becomes the lord of all perfections. ||

children.text:
prathamam udayodayam | dvitīye udayāstam | tṛtīye niṣkāmāṇāṃ prati satodayam
| caturthe astāstam | tatra-
children.translated_text: The first [type] is sunrise-to-sunrise. The second is sunrise-to-sunset. The third, for the desireless, is always sunrise. The fourth is sunset-to-sunset. Therein —
For the desireless, by this alone, direct realization will come about.

children.text: artha-siddhiḥ sakāmānāṃ sarvā vai bhaktim ālabhet ||
children.translated_text: For those with desires, the attainment of their goals — and all [of them] shall attain devotion. ||

children.text: pañcāṅgam etat kurvīta yaḥ puraścaraṇaṃ budhaḥ |
children.translated_text: The wise one who performs this five-limbed <s>puraścaraṇa</s> —
he indeed is victorious in the world, with learning, lordship, sons, and the like. ||

children.text:
evaṃ grāsād vimukti-paryantam ityādi-khaṇḍa-karoparāgādi-puraścaraṇādi-
prayogam āha |
children.translated_text: Thus, from [the method using] a morsel [of food as offering] up to liberation — thus the practice of sectional, eclipse-based, and other <s>puraścaraṇa</s> observances is stated.
The observance of <s>Vaiśākha</s>, in the <s>Bṛhad-Gautamīya</s> —
By this <s>lakṣa</s>-chanting (one hundred thousand repetitions), one sees <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> with one's own eyes.
Beginning from the first day of the dark fortnight of <s>Vaiśākha</s> until the full moon. ||

children.text:
atha pañca-divasī-prayogam āha-
caitre'thavā vaiśākhe śuklaikādaśyām
ārabhya paurṇamāsī-paryantam |
japa-niyamam ayuta-dvayaṃ manau
tathā catvariṃśat sahasraṃ daśārṇe || iti |
children.translated_text:
Now he states the five-day practice:
Beginning from the bright <s>ekādaśī</s> (eleventh) of <s>Caitra</s> or <s>Vaiśākha</s> until the full moon.
The chanting rule is twenty thousand of the <s>mantra</s>,
and forty thousand of the ten-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>]. || Thus.
He states the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> practice called 'preliminary service' in the <s>Krama-dīpikā</s> (5.49-69) —

children.text: sāyāhne vāsudevaṃ yo nityam eva yajen naraḥ |
children.translated_text: He who in the evening always worships <s>Vāsudeva</s> —

children.text: sarvān kāmān avāpyānte sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: having obtained all desires, he goes at the end to the supreme destination. ||
If at night, [one should worship] the son of <s>Devakī</s>, whose mind is overcome by desire (<s>Manmatha</s>),
fatigued from the <s>rāsa</s>-dance, situated in the midst of the circle of <s>gopīs</s>. ||
On a broad, well-rounded, smooth [platform], of a span's height, having fixed
a post into the ground,
stepping with both feet, hands grasped by one another —
this circular [dance] is indeed the <s>rāsa-goṣṭhī</s> (assembly of the <s>rāsa</s>-dance). ||51||
On the broad, pure bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
laden with the mass of pollen-bearing land-lotuses,
with the abundance of spray-droplets' nets,
inhabited [by breezes] that remove affliction — ||52||
Agitated by hundreds of millions of women
struck by the arrows of the bodiless one (<s>Kāma</s>) at night's end,
with the moon's tusks illuminating the directions,
with swarms of wandering she-bees — ||53||
With <s>Vidyādharas</s>, <s>Kinnaras</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>, gods,
<s>Gandharvas</s>, serpents, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>,
accompanied by their wives, mounted on splendid aerial chariots,
at ease, showering cascades of beautiful flowers — ||54||
In the arrangement of the <s>rāsa</s>-sport, with women
grasping each other's hands,
though [His form] also goes to the jewel-post, with that body
He has manifold fashioned His own divine form — ||55||
Going separately between each pair of beautiful-eyed [<s>gopīs</s>],
with both arms bound to the groups of beloveds,
of those whose limbs burn with the fire of desire (<s>Anaṅga</s>) expanding from His own contact,
[their bodies] glistening with rows of horripilation — ||56||
With various <s>śrutis</s> (microtones) yielding more and more enchanting
seven-note scales, modulations, and rhythmic patterns,
revolving with those [<s>gopīs</s>], more beautiful still from the jingling
of bright jeweled ornaments — ||57||
Thus, with forms diversified, assembled with jewels,
as if a golden <s>bhārakata</s> [necklace],
situated in the center of a jewel-made shining post,
in the midst of a vast red lotus — ||58||
With a body [dark] like the <s>atasī</s> (flax) blossom, youthful,
with eyes [like] the petals of a fresh reddish lotus,
with hair bound with the beautifully clustered, glistening
peacock feathers of new sprouts — ||59||
With playful brows, a moon-like face,
cheeks adorned with jeweled <s>kuṇḍalas</s> (earrings),
with lip-coverings resembling the color of a hare's blood,
with many kinds of jewel-shining ornaments — ||60||
With garments brilliant as the coverings of the <s>asana</s>-tree blossoms,
the abode of graceful play,
with soles of hands and feet [red] like fresh coral,
with a body adorned with bee-crowded garlands — ||61||
With a chest reddened by the saffron-paste from the embrace of young women's breasts,
with the gait of a bull,
devoted to the song produced by the auspicious flute,
agitated by desire — the sole teacher of the universe — ||62||
On the excellent seat first established, properly,
one should worship thus the formless, unborn, [yet] possessing form;
first worshipping the attendants of His body,
one should then worship the couples steeped in <s>rasa</s> (aesthetic sentiment). ||63||
On the sixteen petals, the group of vowels with their potencies,
together with their <s>śaktis</s> (energies), [placed] in the supreme <s>rāsa</s>,
<s>Saramā-Madana</s> together with their own <s>kalās</s> (arts),
the couples by name, then <s>Indra</s>-chief and <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-chiefs. ||64||
Thus, having properly worshipped that <s>Hari</s>,
surrounded by four enclosures, with a moistened mind,
in a silver-and-precious-stone-adorned cup, [one should offer] with sugar
well-boiled milk as <s>naivedya</s> (food-offering). ||65||
When there are means, in separate golden
cups — sixteen in number, in order,
having offered milk with sugar to the couples,
one should perform, as before, then everything [else]. ||66||
He who regularly [performs] this all-world-enchanting rite
night after night, with a generous heart —
he indeed, honored by all the world,
having obtained incomparable prosperity, goes to the Infinite. ||67||
At night or at the end of the day,
one should worship the Imperishable (<s>Acyuta</s>) constantly with devotion.
Both [times] yield equal fruit; therefore,
one who desires to cross the ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s> [should worship thus]. ||68||

children.text: ity evaṃ manu-vigrahaṃ madhu-ripuṃ yo vā trikālaṃ yajet
children.translated_text: Thus, one who worships the enemy of <s>Madhu</s>, the embodiment of the <s>mantra</s>, at the three times [of day] —
for him, the beloved of all living beings, in the abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s>,
in his hands are the trees of <s>dharma</s>, pleasure, wealth, and liberation, well-sought by the six [noble qualities],
whose rows of fruits pour forth the flowing nectar of the great <s>rasa</s> of dense bliss. ||69||
He states the practice of the daily rites (<s>nitya-kṛtya</s>) —

children.text:
oṃ namaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇāya |
om asya śrī-bhagavad-gītā-mālā-matrasya bhagavān veda-vyāsa ṛṣor anuṣṭup-
chandaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ paramātmā devatā jape viniyogaḥ |
aśocyān anvaśocas tvaṃ prajñāvādāṃś ca bhāṣase (2.11) iti bījam |
sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja (18.66) iti śaktiḥ |
ahaṃ tvā sarvapāpebhyo mokṣayiṣyāmi mā śucaḥ (18.66) iti kīlakam |
ūrdhva-mūlam adhaḥ-śākham aśvatthaṃ prāhur avyayam (15.1) iti kavacam|
amuka-karmaṇi viniyogaḥ |
nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ (2.27) ity aṅguṣṭābhyāṃ namaḥ
|
na cainaṃ kledayanty āpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ (2.27) iti tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s>, salutations to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. <s>Oṃ</s>, of this <s>Śrī Bhagavad-gītā</s> garland-<s>mantra</s>, the Lord <s>Veda-Vyāsa</s> is the sage (<s>ṛṣi</s>); the meter (<s>chandas</s>) is <s>anuṣṭubh</s>; <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātmā</s>), is the deity; its application is in <s>japa</s> (chanting). 'You grieve for those who should not be grieved for, and yet you speak words of wisdom' (2.11) — this is the seed (<s>bīja</s>). 'Abandoning all <s>dharmas</s>, take refuge in Me alone' (18.66) — this is the power (<s>śakti</s>). 'I shall liberate you from all sins; do not grieve' (18.66) — this is the bolt (<s>kīlaka</s>). 'They speak of an imperishable <s>aśvattha</s> tree with roots above and branches below' (15.1) — this is the armor (<s>kavaca</s>). Its application is in such-and-such a ritual act. 'Weapons do not cut it, fire does not burn it' (2.27) — with 'to the thumbs, salutations.' 'Waters do not wet it, nor does the wind dry it' (2.27) — with 'to the index fingers, salutations.'

children.text:
acchedyo'yam adāhyo'yam akledyo'śoṣya eva ca (2.24) iti madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ
|
nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇur acalo'yaṃ sanātanaḥ (2.24) iti anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ |
paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi śataśo'tha sahasraśaḥ (11.5) iti kaniṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ |
nānāvidhāni divyāni nānāvarṇākṛtīni ca (11.5) iti kara-tala-pṛṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ
|
nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi iti hṛdayāya namaḥ |
na cainaṃ kledayanty āpo iti śirase svāhā |
acchedyo'yam adāhyo'yam iti śikhāyai vaṣaṭ |
nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuḥ iti kavacāya hūṃ |
paśya me pārtha rūpāṇi iti netra-trayāya vauṣaṭ |
nānāvidhāni divyāni ity astrāya phaṭ | śrī-kṛṣṇa-prīty-arthaṃ jape viniyogaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'It cannot be cut, it cannot be burned, it cannot be wetted, and it cannot be dried' (2.24) — with 'to the middle fingers, salutations.' 'It is eternal, all-pervading, immovable, and primeval' (2.24) — with 'to the ring fingers, salutations.' 'Behold, O <s>Pārtha</s>, My forms, by the hundreds and thousands' (11.5) — with 'to the little fingers, salutations.' 'Of many kinds, divine, of various colors and shapes' (11.5) — with 'to the front and back of the palms, salutations.' 'Weapons do not cut it' — with 'to the heart, salutations.' 'Waters do not wet it' — with 'to the head, <s>svāhā</s>.' 'It cannot be cut, it cannot be burned' — with 'to the topknot, <s>vaṣaṭ</s>.' 'It is eternal, all-pervading, immovable' — with 'to the armor, <s>hūṃ</s>.' 'Behold, O <s>Pārtha</s>, My forms' — with 'to the three eyes, <s>vauṣaṭ</s>.' 'Of many kinds, divine' — with 'to the weapon, <s>phaṭ</s>.' Its application is in <s>japa</s> for the pleasure of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>.
(The Greatness of the <s>Śrī Gītā</s>) —
That which was taught to <s>Pārtha</s> (Arjuna) by the Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> Himself,
compiled by <s>Vyāsa</s>, the sage of the <s>Purāṇas</s>, in the midst of the <s>Mahābhārata</s>,
raining the nectar of non-duality, divine, consisting of eighteen chapters —
O Mother, I contemplate You, <s>Bhagavad-gītā</s>, the destroyer of worldly existence.
Salutations to you, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, of vast intellect,
whose eyes are like the petals of a fully-bloomed lotus.
By you, the lamp of knowledge
was lit, filled with the oil of the <s>Bhārata</s> [epic].
To the wish-fulfilling tree of those who take refuge, who holds only a goad and a switch in His hand,
to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who bears the gesture of knowledge (<s>jñāna-mudrā</s>), who milks the nectar of the <s>Gītā</s> — salutations.
All the <s>Upaniṣads</s> are the cows, the milker is the son of the cowherd (<s>Gopāla-nandana</s>),

children.text: pārtho vatsaḥ sudhīr bhoktā dugdhaṃ gītāmṛtaṃ mahat ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pārtha</s> (Arjuna) is the calf, the person of good intellect is the enjoyer, and the milk is the great nectar of the <s>Gītā</s>.
I bow to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the divine son of <s>Vasudeva</s>, the crusher of <s>Kaṃsa</s> and <s>Cāṇūra</s>,
the supreme bliss of <s>Devakī</s>, the teacher of the world.
The banks [of the river of battle] are <s>Bhīṣma</s> and <s>Droṇa</s>; the water is <s>Jayadratha</s>; the blue lotus is <s>Gāndhārī</s>;
the crocodile is <s>Śalya</s>; the current is <s>Kṛpa</s>; the tide is <s>Karṇa</s>;
<s>Aśvatthāman</s> and <s>Vikarṇa</s> are the terrible sea-monsters; <s>Duryodhana</s> is the whirlpool —
this river-ocean of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> was indeed crossed, with <s>Keśava</s> as the boatman.
The words of the son of <s>Parāśara</s> (<s>Vyāsa</s>) — a pure lotus, fragrant with the meaning of the <s>Gītā</s>,
with filaments of various narratives, opened by the discourse of <s>Hari</s>'s stories —
sipped day after day with delight by the noble bees in the world —
may this lotus of the <s>Bhārata</s> be for the well-being [of all], destroying the impurities of <s>Kali</s>.

children.text: mūkaṃ karoti vācālaṃ paṅguṃ laṅghāyate girim |
children.translated_text: [He] makes the mute eloquent and the lame cross mountains —
by His grace, I bow to that <s>Mādhava</s> of supreme bliss.

children.text: yaṃ brahmā varuṇendra-rudra-marutaḥ stunvanti divyaiḥ stavair
children.translated_text: Whom <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Indra</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and the <s>Maruts</s> praise with divine hymns,
whom the singers of the <s>Sāman</s> sing with the <s>Vedas</s>, along with their auxiliary texts, <s>pada</s> and <s>krama</s> recitations, and <s>Upaniṣads</s>,
whom the <s>yogins</s> behold with their minds absorbed in meditation, directed toward Him —

children.text: yasyāntaṃ na viduḥ surāsura-gaṇā devāya tasmai namaḥ || (12.13.1)
children.translated_text: He whose end the hosts of <s>devas</s> and <s>asuras</s> know not — to that <s>Deva</s>, salutations. (12.13.1)
Thus [ends] the <s>nyāsa</s> (consecration) procedure.
My nature is afflicted by the fault of faintheartedness,
my mind confused about <s>dharma</s> — I ask You,

children.text: yac chreyaḥ syān niścitaṃ brūhi tan me
children.translated_text: tell me decisively what is best;

children.text: śiṣyas te'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam || (2.7)
children.translated_text: I am Your disciple — instruct me, who have taken refuge in You. (2.7)

children.text: japa-niyama-saṅkhyā aṣṭottara-śatam | athavā sahasram | prayogam āha-
children.translated_text: The prescribed number of <s>japa</s> repetitions is one hundred and eight. Or one thousand. He states the application —
(The <s>Śrī Gopāla-kavaca</s>)
<s>Pulastya</s> said:
O blessed one, O knower of all <s>dharmas</s>, the armor (<s>kavaca</s>) that was revealed,
named 'Auspiciousness of the Three Worlds' (<s>Trailokya-maṅgala</s>), mercifully, to <s>Brahmā</s> in ancient times,

children.text: brahmaṇā kathitaṃ mahyaṃ paraṃ snehād vadāmi te |
children.translated_text: was told to me by <s>Brahmā</s> out of supreme affection — I tell it to you:
the most secret of all secrets, the reality that is the embodiment of the aggregate of <s>Brahman</s>-<s>mantras</s>.

children.text: yad dhṛtvā paṭhanād brahmā sṛṣṭiṃ vitanute sadā |
children.translated_text: By wearing and reciting which, <s>Brahmā</s> always extends creation;

children.text: yad dhṛtvā paṭhanād pāti mahā-lakṣmīr jagat trayam ||
children.translated_text: by wearing and reciting which, <s>Mahā-Lakṣmī</s> protects the three worlds;
by reciting and wearing which, <s>Śambhu</s> (Śiva) is the destroyer, the knower of all realities;
the mother of the three worlds, <s>Durgā</s>, the great <s>asuras</s> such as <s>Mahiṣa</s> and the like —
those who were arrogant with boons, she slew by reciting and wearing [this kavaca];
similarly, <s>Indra</s> and all the others attained all sovereignty.
One should reveal [this] to a disciple endowed with devotion, to a practitioner;
but to a deceitful person, to another's disciple, to a critic,
to one devoid of devotion to <s>Hari</s>, to one attached to another's wife,
to a miser, to one of bad conduct — [if one] gives [it to such people], one meets death.
Of this 'Auspiciousness of the Three Worlds' armor, <s>Prajāpati</s> (Brahmā)

children.text: ṛṣiś chandaś ca gāyatrī devo nārāyaṇaḥ svayam ||
children.translated_text: is the sage; the meter is <s>Gāyatrī</s>; the deity is Lord <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> Himself.
Its application is proclaimed in [the pursuit of] <s>dharma</s>, <s>artha</s> (wealth), <s>kāma</s> (desire), and <s>mokṣa</s> (liberation).

children.text: oṃ praṇavo me śiraḥ pātu namo nārāyaṇāya ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃ</s> — may the <s>praṇava</s> protect my head; 'Salutations to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>' —
may the eight-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>], the giver of devotion and liberation, protect my forehead and pair of eyes.
<s>Klīṃ</s> — may the single-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>], which enchants all, protect my pair of ears.

children.text: klīṃ kṛṣṇāya sadā ghrāṇaṃ govindāyeti jihvikām |
children.translated_text: '<s>Klīṃ Kṛṣṇāya</s>' — may it always [protect] the nose; '<s>Govindāya</s>' — the tongue;
the word '<s>gopī-jana</s>' [followed by] '<s>vallabhāya svāhā</s>' — [may it protect] my face.
May the eighteen-syllabled <s>mantra</s> [protect] the throat; the ten-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>],
the word '<s>gopī-jana</s>' [followed by] '<s>vallabhāya svāhā</s>' — [may it protect] my two arms.

children.text: klīṃ glauṃ klīṃ karau pāyāt klīṃ kṛṣṇāyāṅgajo'vatu |
children.translated_text: '<s>Klīṃ Glauṃ Klīṃ</s>' — may it protect my hands; '<s>Klīṃ Kṛṣṇāya</s>' — may the body-born one protect

children.text: hṛdayaṃ śrī-bhuvaneśaḥ klīṃ kṛṣṇāya klīṃ stanau mama ||
children.translated_text: my heart; <s>Śrī Bhuvaneśa</s> — '<s>Klīṃ Kṛṣṇāya Klīṃ</s>' — [may it protect] my breasts.
'<s>Gopālāya</s>' born of fire — may it always protect my pair of flanks.

children.text: klīṃ kṛṣṇāya sadā pātu pārśva-yugmaṃ manūttamaḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Klīṃ Kṛṣṇāya</s>' — may the supreme <s>manu</s> (mantra) always protect my two sides.
'<s>Kṛṣṇa-Govinda</s>' — may the <s>manus</s> beginning with <s>smara</s> (desire), joined with <s>ṅe</s>, protect [me].

children.text: aṣṭādaśākṣaraḥ pātu nābhiṃ kṛṣṇeti dvy-akṣaro manuḥ |
children.translated_text: May the eighteen-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>] protect the navel; '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' — the two-syllabled <s>manu</s>

children.text: pṛṣṭhaṃ klīṃ kṛṣṇa-kaṅkālaṃ klīṃ kṛṣṇāya dvi-ṭhāntakaḥ |
children.translated_text: [may protect] the back; '<s>Klīṃ Kṛṣṇa</s>-skeleton' — '<s>Klīṃ Kṛṣṇāya</s>' ending in two <s>ṭha</s>s —

children.text: sakthinī satataṃ pātu śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ ṭha-dvayam ||
children.translated_text: may '<s>Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ</s>' with the two <s>ṭha</s>s always protect the thighs.
May the seven-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>] protect the upper legs; may the thirteen-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>] protect [me].

children.text: śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ padato gopī-jana-padaṃ tataḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ</s>' [then] '<s>gopī-jana</s>,' then

children.text: vallabhāya svāheti pātu klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ca daśārṇakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: '<s>vallabhāya svāhā</s>' — may '<s>Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ</s>' and the ten-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>] protect the feet.

children.text: jānunī ca sadā pātu hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ ca daśākṣaraḥ |
children.translated_text: May '<s>Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ</s>' and the ten-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>] always protect the knees.
May the thirteen-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>] protect the shins; may [the Lord], whose weapon is the discus and the like, [protect me].
The eighteen-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>] preceded by '<s>Hrīṃ Śrīṃ</s>' — the twenty-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>]

children.text: sarvāṅgaṃ me sadā pātu dvārakā-nāyako balī |
children.translated_text: — may it always protect all my limbs; may the mighty lord of <s>Dvārakā</s> [protect me].
'Salutations to the Lord' and then '<s>Vāsudeva</s>' after that —

children.text: tārād yo dvādaśārṇo'yaṃ prācyāṃ māṃ sarvadāvatu |
children.translated_text: this twelve-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>] beginning with <s>Oṃ</s> — may it always protect me from the east.

children.text: śrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ daśavarṇas tu klīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ ṣoḍaśākṣaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: '<s>Śrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ</s>' — the ten-syllabled; '<s>Klīṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ</s>' — the sixteen-syllabled —

children.text: gadādyadāyudho viṣṇur mām agner diśi rakṣatu |
children.translated_text: may <s>Viṣṇu</s>, bearing the mace and other weapons, protect me from the direction of fire (southeast).

children.text: hrīṃ śrīṃ daśākṣaro mantro dakṣiṇe māṃ sadāvatu ||
children.translated_text: May the '<s>Hrīṃ Śrīṃ</s>' ten-syllabled <s>mantra</s> always protect me from the south.
'<s>Oṃ</s>, salutations to the Lord, the beloved of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>,
<s>svāhā</s>' — may this sixteen-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>] protect me from the southwest direction.

children.text: klīṃ padaṃ hṛṣīkeśāya namo māṃ vāruṇ'vatu |
children.translated_text: '<s>Klīṃ</s>' [followed by] '<s>Hṛṣīkeśāya namaḥ</s>' — may it protect me from the west [direction of <s>Varuṇa</s>].
May the eighteen-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>] ending with <s>Kāma</s> always protect me from the northwest.

children.text: śrīṃ māyā kāma-kṛṣṇāya hrīṃ govindāya dvi-ṭho manuḥ |
children.translated_text: '<s>Śrīṃ</s> <s>Māyā</s> <s>Kāma-Kṛṣṇāya</s> <s>Hrīṃ</s> <s>Govindāya</s>' — the <s>manu</s> ending in two <s>ṭha</s>s,
the twelve-syllabled — may <s>Viṣṇu</s> always protect me from the north.

children.text: vāg bhavaṃ kāma-kṛṣṇāya hrīṃ govindāya tataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: 'Speech, existence, desire-<s>Kṛṣṇāya</s>, <s>Hrīṃ Govindāya</s>' and then,

children.text: śrīṃ gopī-jana-vallabhāya svāhā iti tataḥ param |
children.translated_text: '<s>Śrīṃ</s> <s>gopī-jana-vallabhāya svāhā</s>' and then —
may this thirty-two-syllabled <s>mantra</s> always protect me from the northeast.

children.text: kālīyasya phaṇā-madhye divyaṃ nṛtyaṃ karoti tam |
children.translated_text: He who performs divine dance upon the hood of <s>Kāliya</s>,
I bow to the son of <s>Devakī</s>, the eternal king, <s>Acyuta</s> (the infallible).
May this also thirty-two-syllabled <s>mantra</s>, the first, protect me below and on all sides.
'<s>Klīṃ</s>, we know <s>Kāmadeva</s>; we meditate on the bearer of flower-arrows;

children.text: tan no'naṅgaḥ pracodayād eṣa māṃ pātu cordhvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Anaṅga</s> (the bodiless Cupid) inspire us' — may this [<s>Gāyatrī</s>] protect me from above.
This armor called 'Auspiciousness of the Three Worlds,' of the form of <s>Brahman</s> —
thus it has been told to you, O brāhmaṇa, the embodiment of all <s>mantras</s> and medicines,
heard from the mouth of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> by the chief lords headed by <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Īśa</s> (Śiva).

children.text: tava snehān mayākhyātaṃ pravaktavyaṃ na kasyacit |
children.translated_text: Out of affection for you, it has been told by me; it should not be revealed to anyone [else].

children.text: guruṃ praṇamya vidhivat kavacaṃ prapaṭhed yadi ||
children.translated_text: If, having bowed to the <s>guru</s> in the prescribed manner, one recites the <s>kavaca</s>,
once, twice, or thrice, according to one's understanding — he becomes full of all austerities.

children.text: mantreṣu sakaleṣv eva deśiko nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He becomes an <s>ācārya</s> (preceptor) in all <s>mantras</s> — there is no doubt about this.
Its preliminary ritual (<s>puraścaryā</s>) procedure is declared to be one hundred and eight [recitations].

children.text: havanādīn daśāṃśena kṛtvā tat sādhayed dhruvam |
children.translated_text: Having performed oblations and the like at one-tenth [of that count], one should certainly accomplish that [ritual].

children.text: yadi cet siddhi-kavaco vibhur eva bhavet svayam ||
children.translated_text: If [one becomes] one whose armor is perfected, he becomes the Lord Himself.
The perfection of the <s>mantra</s> comes to him through the procedure of <s>puraścaryā</s>.
For one whose mind is endowed with faith and purity, <s>Lakṣmī</s> (fortune) and <s>Vāṇī</s> (speech/Sarasvatī) dwell in his mouth.
Having offered eight handfuls of flowers, if one recites [the <s>kavaca</s>] once with the root <s>mantra</s>,
one obtains the fruit of worship of ten thousand years.

children.text:
bhūrje vilikhya guṭikāṃ svarṇasthāṃ dhārayed yadi
kaṇṭhe vā dakṣiṇe bāhau so'pi viṣṇur na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: If one writes [the <s>kavaca</s>] on birch-bark, places it in a gold case, and wears it on the neck or the right arm — he verily becomes <s>Viṣṇu</s>, without doubt.
Thousands of <s>Aśvamedha</s> [sacrifices] and hundreds of <s>Vājapeya</s> [sacrifices],

children.text: mahā-dānāni yāny eva prādakṣiṇye bhavas tathā ||
children.translated_text: and whatever great gifts [there are], and circumambulations of <s>Bhava</s> (Śiva's realm) —

children.text: kalāṃ nārhanti tāny eva sakṛd uccādaṇādataḥ |
children.translated_text: they do not amount even to a fraction [of the merit] of a single recitation [of this kavaca].
By the grace of the <s>kavaca</s>, a person becomes liberated while living (<s>jīvan-mukta</s>).
He agitates the three worlds and becomes the conqueror of the three worlds.

children.text: idaṃ kavacam ajñātvā bhajed yaḥ puruṣottamam |
children.translated_text: One who worships <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person) without knowing this <s>kavaca</s>,
even if the <s>mantra</s> is chanted a hundred <s>lakṣa</s> (ten million) times, it does not bestow perfection.

children.text:
iti sanat-kumāra-tantre navama-paṭale śrī-nārada-pañcarātre (4.5)
trailokya-maṅgalaṃ nāma śrī-gopāla-kavacaṃ samāptam |
children.translated_text: Thus, in the <s>Sanat-kumāra-tantra</s>, ninth chapter, in the <s>Śrī Nārada-pañcarātra</s> (4.5), the <s>Śrī Gopāla-kavaca</s> named 'Auspiciousness of the Three Worlds' is complete.

children.text:
atha puraścaraṇa-saṅkalpādi-vidhiḥ | śrī-viṣṇur viṣṇur namo'sya amuka-māse
amuka-pakṣe bhāskare amuka-tithau amuka-gotro'muka-dāsas trailokya-saṃmohana-
tantrokta-śrī-kṛṣṇa-devatāyās trailokya-saṃmohana-kavaca-siddhi-kāmas tat
kavacasyāṣṭottara-śata-japa-tad-daśāṃśa-homa-tad-daśāṃśa-tarpaṇa-tad-
daśāṃśābhiṣeka-tad-daśāṃśa-brāhmaṇa-bhojana-rūpa-puraścaraṇam ahaṃ kariṣye
| eka-divase kārya-siddhiḥ | prayogaḥ śrīmad-bhāgavatānusāreṇa daśārṇa-mantra-
prathame śrī-bhāgavata-maṅgalācaraṇe |
children.translated_text: Now the procedure for the preliminary rite (<s>puraścaraṇa</s>), resolution (<s>saṅkalpa</s>), and the like: '<s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, salutations. In such-and-such a month, such-and-such a fortnight, on a day [governed by] the sun, on such-and-such a lunar day, I, such-and-such servant of such-and-such <s>gotra</s>, desiring the perfection of the 'Enchantment of the Three Worlds' armor described in the <s>Trailokya-saṃmohana-tantra</s> with <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> as the deity — I shall perform the preliminary rite consisting of one hundred and eight <s>japa</s> recitations of that <s>kavaca</s>, oblation (<s>homa</s>) at one-tenth of that, libation (<s>tarpaṇa</s>) at one-tenth of the oblation, ablution (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) at one-tenth of the libation, and feeding of brāhmaṇas at one-tenth of the ablation.' The accomplishment of the purpose [takes] one day. The application is according to the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s>, with the ten-syllabled <s>mantra</s>, first [reciting] the auspicious invocation of the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>.

children.text: The following section is perhaps not in all manuscripts.
children.translated_text: The following section is perhaps not in all manuscripts.
Now he states the fruit of beholding the shadow-person (<s>chāyā-puruṣa</s>) —

children.text: pūrvāhne sūrya-bimbārkaṃ pṛṣṭhe kṛtvā naraḥ śuciḥ |
children.translated_text: In the forenoon, a pure person, having placed the orb of the sun at his back,

children.text: animiṣo hi sva-cchāyāṃ galād ūrdhvaṃ vilokayet ||
children.translated_text: should gaze without blinking at his own shadow from the throat upward.
If there he sees a person arisen from the shadow,
endowed with all limbs — that is considered auspicious for the duration of a year.
[If] the hand or ear is not seen, the person [has the result reaching] up to the heart.
For the living being, [the durations are respectively] those of the sun, horse, direction, moon, fire, and eye, in order.

children.text: śirasy ādṛṣṭe ṣaṇmāsaṃ sarandhre hṛdi saptakam ||
children.translated_text: If not seen at the head, [the duration is] six months; if [not seen] at the opening (aperture), seven at the heart.
This knowledge is supremely divine; one should not tell it to a wicked disciple.
Thus ends the third section (<s>prakāśa</s>) of the <s>Daivajña-cintāmaṇi</s> composed by <s>Śrī Kaṃsāri Miśra Yaśodhara</s>.
The <s>Gāyatrī</s> mantra, the mantra of <s>Rādhā</s>, the mantra of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — supreme beyond that,
the excellent mantra of <s>Mahāprabhu</s>, and likewise the <s>Hari-nāma</s> (holy name),
and the excellent mental worship (<s>mānasī sevā</s>) — [these are] known as the five sacraments (<s>pañca-saṃskāra</s>).

children.text:
ahaṅkārādhiṣṭhātṛtvād bhūta-śuddher adhidevāya saṅkarṣaṇāya namaḥ he
saṅkarṣaṇa sadyaḥ śudhyed upāsanopayuktaṃ syāt tathā kṛpāṃ kuru |
children.translated_text: Because of being the presiding deity of ego-sense (<s>ahaṅkāra</s>), obeisance to <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, the presiding deity of purification of the elements (<s>bhūta-śuddhi</s>). O <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, may [the practitioner] be purified immediately [and] become fit for worship — please bestow [Your] grace thus.
Now the meditation on <s>Mātṛkā</s> —
With a peacock feather set in her hair, with full, high breasts,
holding in her right hand a lotus-shaped [symbol of] knowledge shining like water-[lilies],
and in her left, bearing a pot of yogurt — the exalted <s>Vidyā</s> —
of the radiance of the nectar-rayed [moon], I praise the form of <s>Mātṛkā</s>.
Meditation on <s>Keśava-kīrtikā</s> and others —
With a broad, charming sidelong glance, mutually licking each other with enchanting [glances],
embraced by one arm each, [their bodies] bristling with profuse horripilation,
fair and dark, wearing a pair of garments — dark and golden —
I remember <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose unbounded longing plays with <s>Smara</s> (the god of love).

children.text:
tatra nyāsasya vāsudevo'dhiṣṭhātā sa stoka-kṛṣṇo'tra jñeyas tad-dhyānam ucyate
|
children.translated_text: Therein, the presiding deity of the <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) is <s>Vāsudeva</s>; He should be known as <s>Stoka-kṛṣṇa</s> (little <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). His meditation is stated:
Dark as a rain-cloud, with a garment blazing like lightning,
smiling, with a hand made beautiful by a playful lotus,
with a peacock-feather crest-ornament, in the form of <s>Vāsudeva</s> —
I bow to <s>Stoka-kṛṣṇa</s>, the most beloved of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
During <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control), one should contemplate one's own chosen deities, the divine couple.
With arms placed upon each other's shoulders, bristling [with joy], of vermilion and golden hue,
wearing a foursome of silk garments, radiant with beauty, with blooming lotus-faces,
gathering [for] a pleasure-outing with their retinue, adorned with forest-ornaments gathered [for them],
of golden and dark bodily radiance, with sweet smiling faces — I bow to <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Mukunda</s>.
Having made the tortoise-shaped hand-gesture (<s>kara-kacchapikā</s>), then one should meditate upon one's own deity.
By the accomplished <s>Siddhas</s>, gods, and sages — too awed even to ask [questions],
standing at a distance, composed, offering bows, praised with [reverential] excitement —
by the attendants of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and others, whose beauty is gazed upon with longing —
She who has taken the vow of spreading the wonder of sweetness through the three worlds.
With troughs overflowing with sprouts of fresh grass,
with gleaming girdles [of hills], with the splendor of streaks of all minerals,
with caves furnished as dwellings, with mountains from which waterfalls spring up,
here and there adorned — as if stations for worship, not quite manifest.
Of <s>kāraṇḍava</s> birds cooing in groves of blooming lotuses,
of rivers with exceedingly charming waters carrying unlimited yogurt and milk,
whose tips of small wavelet-arms seem to caress the trees,
with the dense cloud-like appearance of the streams broken open by their currents.
With graceful <s>sārasa</s> cranes swaying with intoxication,
with the readily flowing juices of the delightful [ponds],
with the splendor of lotuses grown [upon them],
the ponds are made glorious by the clusters [of lotuses].
[line missing]
by groups of companion-bees of the ocean-born [Lakṣmī], delighted by fragrance, seen for a moment;
with trees full of the beauty of coral-like tender shoots resembling the young sun, of the sweetness of nectar,
with fruits that destroy pride, abundantly spreading, blocking the sunlight.
With <s>madhūlī</s> (honey-trees), whose buzzing of intoxicated bee-wives in swarms
creates a stupor as if breaking the pleasure-grove of the enemy of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Cupid's foe, <s>Śiva</s>),
with creepers bending under the weight of fully blooming flower-clusters on all sides,
the banks are marked all around by broad vine-swings.
By <s>kapiñjala</s> (partridges), <s>valākikā</s> (cranes), <s>caṭaka</s> (sparrows), <s>cātaka</s> (rainbirds), <s>upayaṣṭikā</s> (wagtails),
by <s>pikas</s> (cuckoos), <s>madana-sārikās</s> (love-mynahs), <s>śukas</s> (parrots), <s>kaliṅgas</s> (Indian robins), and <s>pārāvatas</s> (pigeons),
by <s>śatacchada</s> (hundred-feathered) and <s>śitacchada</s> (sharp-feathered) birds, <s>karaṭas</s> (crows), <s>khañjarīṭas</s> (wagtails), and others —
by birds whose calls are unrestrained, [the forest] is made to resound within.

children.text:
ābhīrāṇām ānanda-vṛndāni cakoraiś
candrātmatvā lālasayā hātum aśakyā |
children.translated_text: The assemblies of bliss of the cowherd women, like <s>cakora</s> birds unable to abandon [the moonlight] out of longing for the moon-natured [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>];

children.text:
tāsāṃ labdhaṃ kuntala-sāmyaṃ piñcha-samūhair
yadbhir nṛtyānuccair matta-mayūra-prakaraiḥ |
kiṭi-kirīṭibhiḥ śalyair bhalla-plavaṅga-kuraṅgamaiḥ
sṛmara-camarair golāṅgulaiḥ samūrucamūrubhir
urubhir urubhiḥ pārīndroghaiḥ sarāru-bhayojjhitaiḥ

children.translated_text: by animals as if released from evil — with <s>gaḍḍara</s> (rams) blocking the pathways,
with horns [making sounds of] stupor and clamor, with milk-giving [she-goats] and also with nanny-goats,
and with rows of buffaloes resembling [moving] boulders — [the forest is] surrounded.

those [women] whose tresses are equaled by the clusters of peacock feathers — by whom the intoxicated peacock-flocks dance aloft; by <s>kiṭi</s>-birds, crowned ones, porcupines, wild boars, monkeys, and deer, by <s>sṛmara</s> (yak-deer), <s>camara</s> (yak), and <s>golāṅgula</s> (langurs), with great and mighty thighs, by herds of lions, free from fear of enemies —
With ground-surfaces in some places firm, gleaming with crystal pavements,
in some places brilliant with lawns as if made of emeralds,
whose own coral-like sweetness surpasses the beauty of palaces,
and lovely with clusters of excellent bowers laden with flowers.

children.text:
ārādhitā kila kalinda-sutāravinda-
syandānubandha-rasikena samīraṇena |
ānanda-tundila-carācara-jīva-vṛndā
vṛndāṭavī prathamam ucca-rucir vicityām || kulakam |
children.translated_text: Worshipped by the breeze — passionate with the association of the lotus-streams of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), / with all moving and stationary beings swelling with bliss — / <s>Vṛndā</s>'s forest, supremely radiant, is to be meditated upon first. // <s>Kulaka</s> verse //
With the full, beautiful, buzzing melodic collections
of swarms of bees pervading [it], I should remember
this flower-garden, whose roots are drenched with dense honey,
whose fragrance anoints the directions.
Here, a coral-like [trunk of] coral, with leaves of emerald, with buds of fine diamond,
with fruits of ruby, streaming with flows of nectar — the wise one should remember the wish-fulfilling tree.

children.text: ṛtubhir mahitasya tasya nityaṃ prakaṭaṃ hema-taṭī-madhye vicintya-
children.translated_text: Ever honored by the seasons, amidst the golden banks of that [garden], one should meditate —
upon the most excellent eight-petaled [lotus], shining like the rising sun,
one should contemplate here this supreme lotus.
A jeweled pavement gleaming therein —
dense with supreme bliss, the wise one should remember.

children.text: tatra kuṭṭima-vare sphuṭa-dīptau yogapīṭham api vincintya-
children.translated_text: There, upon that excellent pavement, in manifest radiance, having meditated upon the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> also —
upon its brilliant great whorl (<s>karṇikā</s>),
upon which are seated the two who possess bliss, resplendent,
whose radiance mocks fresh rain-clouds and gold —
I meditate upon <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rādhā</s>.
With a peacock-feather bound on the crest, gleaming,
with curly locks, made beautiful by the flute,
marked with a <s>tilaka</s>, radiant with brilliant saffron,
adorned with beautiful ornamental marks (<s>viśeṣaka</s>) of musk.
With bees delighted by the enchanting, loving fragrance,
of the radiance of ear-ornaments fashioned from sparkling flower-clusters,
with swinging <s>makara</s>-earrings illuminating full, blossoming cheeks —
her ear-edges licked by the splendor of variegated jeweled ear-ornaments.

children.text:
śarad-abhimuditāra-vinda-dyuti-
damanāyata-lohitāñcalāṅkam
alaghu-caṭula-dīrgha-dṛṣṭi-khelā-
madhurima-kharvita-khañjarīṭa-yuvām
vala-lalāṭa-kṛtārdha-śaśi-prabhuṃ
dvi-kalasīti-kara-sphuritālikām |
kusuma-kārmuka-kārmuka-vibhramo-
ddhati-vidhūnana-dhurya-tara-bhruvo
citra-paṭṭa-ghaṭikopama-sphurat-
pāśa-varya-parivīta-mastakam
nāsikā-śikhara-lambi-vartula-
sthūla-mauktika-rucāñcitānanām
children.translated_text: With eyes whose brilliance rivals the autumn-gladdened lotus, / with long reddish edges subduing [all comparison], / with the charm of heavy, playful, long, sidelong glances / humbling even the [most graceful] wagtail-couple; / Him whose forehead bears the radiance of a half-moon, / her whose brow-ornament (<s>alikā</s>) shines with two pitcher-like [marks]; / whose eyebrows rival the play of the flower-bow of <s>Kāma</s>, / surpassing [all] in the fluttering of the shaking [brow-movements]; / whose heads are encircled by excellent braids resembling the ornamental bands on variegated silken head-pieces; / her whose face is beautified by the splendor of round, large pearls hanging from the tip of the nose.
Whose facial beauty is victorious [over] the charm of the lord of the full-moon autumn night,
whose noses are radiant with the beauty of freshly blooming sesame-flowers and <s>damana</s> [blossoms],
whose excellent radiance mocks the resplendent <s>bimba</s> fruit, humbling the cheek-surfaces,
whose great luster rivals fully blossoming jewel-mirrors — the wealth of their smiles.
Him whose voice is deep like a divine kettledrum, her whose prattle is melodious with a tender, sweet throat; / with shoulders encircled by fresh creeper-like [arms], with garlands of flowers;

children.text:
suṣṭhu-labdha-paripāka-dāḍimī-
bīja-rāja-vijayi-dvijārciṣe |
kambukaṇṭha-viluṭhan-maṇi-ratna-
ratna-niṣka-pariśobhita-kaṇṭhām |
unnati-prathima-sulalitāṃsaṃ
snigdhayor ucita-rāmavanamrām |
children.translated_text: Him whose row of teeth conquers the royal seeds of a well-ripened pomegranate, / her whose throat is adorned with jewel-necklaces, gems, and golden medallions rolling upon her conch-shell neck; / Him of lofty, broad, graceful shoulders, / her bowing charmingly in a manner befitting the tender pair.
Him by whose pair of arms the serpents [of comparison] are put to shame,
her who steals beauty with her gleaming armlets,
both having hands adorned with shining jeweled rings on their most lovely fingers,
with hands beautified by gleaming bracelets.
Him whose hard, broad chest is like the door-panel of emerald,
with a forest-garland meeting rows of <s>guñjā</s>-berry [necklaces] and pearl-strings,
her whose pair of breasts rival the firm pomegranate-fruit,
with a gentle pearl-strand becoming the crest of the two summits of her bosom.
Him whose row of body-hair, victorious over the still line of bees,
three folds adorning the slender, lovely middle — of beautiful form,
victorious over the great whirlpool of the divine river <s>Gaṅgā</s> descending upon the sister of <s>Yama</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>),
both possessing the beauty of a deep navel-region and the splendor of a broad belly.
With heavy hips mocking [all comparison], with a jeweled girdle
encircling a charming yellow silk garment,
her with a beautiful hip-region embraced by a red silk
garment adorned with a jeweled waist-chain.

children.text:
atinava-mada-bhara-manthara-sindhura-kara-bandhuroru-vimānau jaṅghābhyāṃ
racita-rucau suvartulābhyāṃ gūḍhenāpy anupama-gulpha-yugmakena padbhyām apy
aruṇa-nakhojjvalābhyāṃ maṇimaya-nūpurāñcitābhyāṃ |
children.translated_text: With thighs graceful like the sluggish trunk of a freshly intoxicated elephant, with calves beautiful and well-rounded, with an incomparable pair of ankles though hidden, with feet radiant with reddish nails, adorned with jeweled anklets.
Him whose back is caressed all around by the arm of His beloved,
standing with a joyfully thrilling right [arm];
her whose head rests at the root of the beloved's left arm,
with a pair of sidelong glances playing at the edge of His lotus-face.
Him with neck slightly turned toward something — toward the lotus-face of His beloved,
with a long sidelong glance darting [toward her], with a flute sounding at His gleaming lower lip,
with a slender waist, the right foot crossing over the left above,
with swaying eyebrow-garlands, with a flower-ornament placed at the edge of His arm.
Her whose eyes are captivated by the beauty of the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, whose skin thrills exceedingly at His touch,
whose ears open eagerly at His speech, whose nostrils are touched by His fragrance,
whose tongue delights at His lower lip, whose lotus-face droops [toward Him],
whose great composure, uttered by pride, is externally agitated by [uncontrollable] transformations.
Of the flute caressed by the breeze of breath slightly exhaled from His mouth,
from which emerge <s>grāmas</s> (musical scales) that drain the fortitude and grandeur of the world,
which, though interrupted internally by helplessness at the touch of His beloved,
He skillfully brings back to its own [musical] mode in an instant.
Her whose waist-knot is loosened, whose girdle upon the sandbank-like hips is obstructed by the alliance of perspiration,
whose high arena [of the bosom] is the stage [of their sport],
whose heart melts with the initial flow, who has forgotten all [other] states,
who is understood to be in extreme agitation fashioned by the accumulation of deep longing.
Both with bodies bristling [with joy], with streams of tears
bathing their lotus-faces, both trembling,
for a moment with voices choked with deeply hidden sobs,
with minds maddened by the intoxication of <s>Madana</s> (Love) — them I remember.
Adorned with nine finger-holes, shining,
of a stature equal to a <s>guravī</s>-seed,
with a reddish lower-lip — held in the hand,
the straight flute (<s>veṇu</s>).
Praiseworthy, measurable by one's own fist within,
of a beautiful form measuring three hand-spans,
mostly possessed of dark luster,
the stick (<s>yaṣṭi</s>) and the like supporting the right elbow.
Dark, of a curved nature,
broad at the base, and fashioned [with care] at the front,
whose body is bound in a cloth-covering,
the excellent horn (<s>śṛṅga</s>) — the [city/place] is served by [it].
Her who wards off bees made restless by the weight of fragrance from her dear friend's face,
with a tender, playful lotus;
whose moon-like face is gazed upward [at] —
<s>Lalitā</s>, with a sidelong glance spreading a flood of <s>rasa</s>.
<s>Viśākhā</s>, with a hand shining with fresh, beautiful, <s>cāmara</s>-like
flower-clusters,
and <s>Citrā</s> indeed, from the right and left,
fanning the bodies [of the divine couple] playfully.
With a lotus-palm displaying a betel-packet
wrapped in a <s>nāga-vallī</s> (betel) leaf,
<s>Campakalatā</s>, trembling [with devotion],
beholds the beauty of the back-sides [of the divine couple].
With melodious singing blended with the lovely notes of <s>Ramyendulekhā</s>,
harmonizing with the play of the flute, by [<s>Raṅgadevī</s>] who is a connoisseur of musical qualities,
with the spreading sounds of the <s>vīṇā</s>, [she who stands] before [them]
who had begun their performance, with the exalted <s>Tuṅgavidyā</s>.
By the swaying-limbed <s>Raṅga Devī</s>
on the left, and by <s>Su Devī</s> slowly on the right,
the sweat and tear-streams being wiped away
with gentle touching and rubbing, with the edge of a garment.
<s>Smaraṇa-Maṅgala-Stotra</s> (Auspicious Hymn of Remembrance)
The <s>prema-sevā</s> of the lotus feet of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>'s life-bond, inaccessible to <s>Keśa</s> (Brahmā), <s>Śeṣa</s>, and others,
which is the goal to be achieved, obtainable only through intense longing by those devoted to the pastimes of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text: sā syāt prāptā yayā tāṃ prathayitum adhunā mānasīm asya sevāṃ
children.translated_text: may that [<s>sevā</s>] be attained; to make it known, I now praise

children.text: bhāvyāṃ rāgādhva-pānthair vrajam anucaritaṃ naityikaṃ tasya naumi ||1||
children.translated_text: this mental (<s>mānasī</s>) service, to be contemplated by travelers on the path of <s>rāga</s>, the daily round of His pastimes in <s>Vraja</s>. //1//

children.text: kuñjād goṣṭhaṃ niśānte praviśati kurute dohanānnāśanādyāṃ
children.translated_text: At night's end, He enters the cowshed from the bower, performs milking, breakfast, and the like;

children.text: prātaḥ sāyaṃ ca līlāṃ viharati sakhibhiḥ saṅgave cārayan gāḥ |
children.translated_text: in the morning and evening He sports in <s>līlā</s>, and in the forenoon He herds the cows with His companions;

children.text: madhyāhne cātha naktaṃ vilasati vipine rādhayāddhāparāhne
children.translated_text: at midday and at night He revels in the forest, with <s>Rādhā</s> in the afternoon;

children.text: goṣṭhaṃ yāti pradoṣe ramayati suhṛdo yah sa kṛṣṇo'vatān naḥ || 2 ||
children.translated_text: He goes to the cowshed at dusk and delights His friends — may that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> protect us! //2//
At night's end, awakened by the many loud cries uttered by the alarmed <s>Vṛndā</s>, and by the verses of parrots and <s>śārī</s>-birds,

children.text: padyair hṛdyair ahṛdyair api sukha-śayanād utthitau tau sakhībhiḥ |
children.translated_text: delightful and undelightful, the two arose from their blissful bed;
seen by the <s>sakhīs</s>, they were joyful, their love kindled at that moment, graceful — yet apprehensive of <s>Kakkhāṭī</s>'s words —

children.text: rādhā-kṛṣṇau sa-tṛṣṇāv api nija-nija-dhāmny āpta-talpau smarāmi ||3||
children.translated_text: I remember <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, still longing, yet arrived at their own respective beds in their own abodes. //3//
I remember <s>Rādhā</s> — bathed and adorned, summoned early by the <s>sakhīs</s> to the mother-in-law's house in <s>Vraja</s>,
preparing cooked food in that house, eating the remnants of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s [meal];
and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — awakened, having reached the cow-shed, having completed the milking of the cows,

children.text: susnātaṃ kṛta-bhojanaṃ sahacarais tāṃ cātha taṃ cāśraye || 4 ||
children.translated_text: well-bathed, having eaten with His companions — I take refuge in Her and in Him. //4//
In the forenoon, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, followed into the forest by His cow-companions and accompanied by the people of the cowshed,
eager to meet <s>Rādhā</s>, arriving at the shore of Her pond (<s>kuṇḍa</s>) for the purpose of a rendezvous;
and <s>Rādhā</s>, catching sight of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, having gone home and being directed to perform the worship of the sun-god,
yet her eyes dispatched along the path of her own <s>sakhīs</s> sent [to arrange] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s approach — I remember [them]. //5//
At midday, bewildered by the various transformations and ornaments arising from their mutual union,
agitated by coyness and longing, [finding] comfort through the playful jesting of <s>Lalitā</s> and other friends at the love-sacrifice;
with pastimes of swinging, forest, water, flute-play, love-sport, wine-drinking, sun-worship, and the like,
I remember <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, full of longing, served by the group of their retinue. //6//
<s>Śrī Rādhā</s>, having returned home, having prepared various offerings for Her beloved,
well-bathed, beautifully dressed, filled with joy from beholding the lotus-face of Her beloved;
and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the afternoon, having set out from <s>Vraja</s> with herds of cows and friends,
satisfied by the sight of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>, meeting His father's face, caressed by His mother — I remember [them]. //7//
In the evening, <s>Rādhā</s>, having sent through Her <s>sakhī</s> many food-preparations for Her beloved,

children.text: sakhyānīteśa-śeṣāśana-mudita-hṛdaṃ tāṃ ca taṃ ca vrajendum |
children.translated_text: her heart gladdened by eating the Lord's remnants brought by the <s>sakhī</s> — Her and Him, the moon of <s>Vraja</s>;

children.text: susnātaṃ ramya-veśaṃ gṛham anu jananī lālitaṃ prāpta-goṣṭhaṃ
children.translated_text: well-bathed, beautifully dressed, caressed by His mother at home, having arrived at the cowshed,

children.text: nirvyūḍhosrāli-dohaṃ sva-gṛham anu punar bhuktavantaṃ smarāmi || 8 ||
children.translated_text: having completed the milking of the cows, having eaten again at home — I remember [Him]. //8//
<s>Rādhā</s>, at dusk, ending [the company of] Her friends, dressed appropriately for the dark and bright portions of the night,
guided by the messenger <s>Vṛndā</s>'s instructions, having gone to the bower of the wish-fulfilling tree on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>;
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, with the cowherds in the assembly, having watched the artists' performances, brought by His affectionate mother
with effort, put to sleep, then secretly arriving at the bower — I remember [them]. //9//
The two, eager, having met, served with many attentions by <s>Vṛndā</s>,
with songs, playful riddles, pleasant conversations, dances, <s>rāsa</s>-dance and other performances;
shining with their dearest <s>sakhīs</s>, their minds absorbed in love, having drunk fine <s>mādhvīka</s> wine,
sporting in the bower, engaging in various love-battles, aroused and spread out at the end. //10//
With betel, fragrances, garlands, fanning, cool milk-drink, foot-massaging, and the like,
lovingly served by the assembly of affectionate companions, finding comfort,
with sweet words of love-quarrel, with intimate love-sentiments, the group of friends sleeping in the bower,
I remember <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> at night, having fallen asleep on a bed of lovely flowers. //11//

children.text:
iti śrī-rūpa-gosvāmi-viracitā smaraṇa-paddhatiḥ |
śrī-rūpo jayati |
iti smaraṇa-maṅgalaṃ samāptam |
iti caturtha-kakṣā
children.translated_text:
Thus [ends] the <s>Smaraṇa-Paddhati</s> composed by <s>Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī</s>.
Glory to <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>!
Thus the <s>Smaraṇa-Maṅgala</s> is complete.
Thus [ends] the fourth section (<s>kakṣā</s>).
Fifth Section (<s>Kakṣā</s>)

children.text:
atha paramaiśvarya-mādhurya-pīyūṣāmṛta-vāridheḥ svayaṃ bhagavataḥ katamaṃ
tad-dhāma yatrāsau bhagavān viharati | ity apekṣāyām āhākare-
children.translated_text: Now, which is that abode of the Lord Himself, who is the ocean of the nectar of supreme sovereignty and sweetness, where that Lord sports? In answer to this expectation, [it is stated] in the <s>Ākāra</s>:
His abode is famous in the <s>Purāṇas</s> and the like as four places:

children.text: vraje madhupure dvāravatyāṃ goloka eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vraja</s>, <s>Madhupurī</s> (Mathurā), <s>Dvāravatī</s> (Dvārakā), and <s>Goloka</s> itself.
Thus in the <s>Skānda</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>]:

children.text:
yā yathā bhuvi vartante puryo bhagavataḥ priyāḥ |
tās tathā santi vaikuṇṭhe tat-tal-līlārtham ādṛtāḥ || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
'As many cities dear to the Lord exist on earth,
so do they exist in <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, honored for the purpose of their respective <s>līlās</s>.' — and so forth.
The arrangement of those [abodes] is stated in the <s>Ākāra</s> (<s>Laghu Bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 1.4.497–8, 502):

children.text: dhāmāsya dvividhaṃ proktaṃ māthuraṃ dvārvatī tathā |
children.translated_text: His abode is declared to be twofold: <s>Māthura</s> (Mathurā) and <s>Dvāravatī</s>.

children.text: māthuraṃ ca dvidhā prāhur gokulaṃ puram eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Māthura</s> is said to be twofold: <s>Gokula</s> and the City (Mathurā proper).

children.text: yat tu goloka-nāma syāt tac ca gokula-vaibhavam |
children.translated_text: That which is called <s>Goloka</s> is the splendor (<s>vaibhava</s>) of <s>Gokula</s>;
and its being the self-splendor of that [<s>Gokula</s>] is because of its exalted glory.

children.text:
asyārthaḥ-gokula-vaibhavaṃ goikulaiśvaryaṃ prakāśa-rūpam | tasya gokulasya tad-
ātma-vaibhavatvaṃ sa goloka ātmanaḥ svasya vaibhavaṃ yasya | tan-mahimonnates
tasmād golokān mahimonnater hetoḥ | anyathā golokasya gokulāprakaṭa-
prakāśatve sthāna-catuṣṭayatā-siddhiḥ | yady aprakaṭatvena sthānatvāt tadā
madhupurī-dvārakayor aprakaṭa-prakāśābhyāṃ sthāna-ṣaṭtā syāt | tarhi golokasya
kutra sthitir ity āha | para-vyomopari sarvordhva-bhāga eva | śrī-brahma-
saṃhitāyām-
children.translated_text: The meaning of this: the splendor of <s>Gokula</s> means the majesty of <s>Gokula</s> in the form of a manifestation. <s>Goloka</s> is that whose own self's splendor is that of <s>Gokula</s> — [this is so] because of its exalted glory beyond that <s>Goloka</s>. Otherwise, if <s>Goloka</s> were the unmanifest manifestation of <s>Gokula</s>, the four-fold [classification of] abodes would be established. But if it were [a separate] abode by virtue of being unmanifest, then with the unmanifest manifestations of <s>Madhupurī</s> and <s>Dvārakā</s> [too], there would be six abodes. Then where is <s>Goloka</s> situated? — he says: above the <s>para-vyoma</s> (spiritual sky), in the topmost region of all. In the <s>Śrī Brahma-Saṃhitā</s>:

children.text:
goloka-nāmni nija-dhāmni tale ca tasya
devi maheśa-hari-dhāmasu teṣu teṣu |
te te prabhāva-nicayā vihitāś ca yena
govindam ādi-puruṣaṃ tam ahaṃ bhajāmi || [BrahmaS 5.43] iti |
children.translated_text: I worship that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Person. [<s>Brahma-Saṃhitā</s> 5.43]

In His own abode called <s>Goloka</s>, and below it,
O goddess, in the abodes of <s>Maheśa</s> and <s>Hari</s> — in each of those,
the respective assemblages of powers have been established by Him —

children.text: śriyaḥ kāntāḥ kāntaḥ parama-puruṣaḥ kalpa-taravo | ity ādi |
children.translated_text: 'The goddesses of fortune are the beloveds, the beloved is the Supreme Person, the trees are wish-fulfilling' — and so forth.

children.text:
sa yatra kṣīrābdhiḥ sravati surabhībhyaś ca su-mahān
nimeṣārdhākhyo vā vrajati na hi yatrāpi samayaḥ |
bhaje śvetadvīpaṃ tam aham iha golokam iti yaṃ
vidantas te santaḥ kṣiti-virala-cārāḥ katipaye || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
'Where the great milk-ocean flows from the <s>surabhī</s> cows,
and where not even a moment passes that could be called half a blink —
I worship that <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, which those few saintly souls,
rare upon the earth, know as <s>Goloka</s>.' — and so forth.

children.text:
ataeva śrī-bhāgavate (10.2.7) gaccha devi vrajaṃ bhadre iti, śrī-caitanya-caritāmṛte
(ādi 4.29) mo-viṣaye gopī-gaṇra upapati-bhāve ity ādi prakaṭa-līlānusāreṇa śrī-
goloka-nātha-vākyam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> (10.2.7), 'Go, O goddess, to <s>Vraja</s>, O blessed one,' and in the <s>Śrī Caitanya-Caritāmṛta</s> (<s>Ādi</s> 4.29), 'The <s>gopīs</s>' mood of paramour-love toward Me' — and so forth — this is the statement of the Lord of <s>Goloka</s> in accordance with the manifest <s>līlā</s>.

children.text:
atra goloke śry-ādayo'nuvāda-rūpāḥ | kāntādayo vidheya-rūpāḥ | param apīti
goloke śvetadvīpa-vaikuṇṭhādayo'py anuvāda-rūpāḥ | vṛndāvana-gokulādayo
vidheya-rūpāḥ | tataḥ kṛṣṇo'yaṃ nārāyaṇasya vilāsī goloka-para-vyomopari vartata
iti dṛṣṭyā janānāṃ jhaṭiti pravṛtti-durghaṭā syāt | ataeva tad-gata parikarāṇām
ayaṃ sarveśvaro'smākaṃ prabhur iti sadā sphūrtiḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, in <s>Goloka</s>, the <s>śrī</s>-prefixed [terms] and the like are in the form of the given subject (<s>anuvāda</s>); 'beloved' and the like are in the form of the predicate (<s>vidheya</s>). Furthermore, 'even beyond' — in <s>Goloka</s>, <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, and the like are also in the form of the given subject; <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, <s>Gokula</s>, and the like are the predicates. Therefore, from the perspective that this <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the <s>vilāsa</s> (sportive expansion) of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, situated above <s>Goloka</s> and <s>para-vyoma</s> — the sudden devotional engagement of people would be difficult. Therefore, for His associates there, 'this is the Lord of all, our master' — such is the constant awareness.

children.text:
kiṃ ca, goloka-gata kaiśora-līlāyā aiśvarya-mayatvāt tal-līlā-valitasya goloka-
nāthasya bālya-paugaṇḍa-dharmābhāvāt kaiśora-gatatvena līlāyā eka-vidhatvam
| tasmiṃś ca sati, ayaṃ parama-puruṣaḥ śaktimān vayam asya śaktayaḥ iti sphūrteḥ
pāṇi-grahaṇābhāvāc ca dānābhisārādayo līlā na santi | tatra nimeṣārdhākhyo vā
vrajati na hi yatrāpi samayaḥ iti |
children.translated_text: Moreover, because the <s>kaiśora-līlā</s> (adolescent pastimes) in <s>Goloka</s> are permeated with <s>aiśvarya</s> (divine majesty), and because the Lord of <s>Goloka</s>, enveloped by those pastimes, lacks the qualities of childhood (<s>bālya</s>) and boyhood (<s>paugaṇḍa</s>), the <s>līlā</s> in <s>Goloka</s> is of one kind only, being situated in the <s>kaiśora</s> stage. And when this is so — 'He is the Supreme Person, the possessor of power; we are His powers' — because of such awareness, and because of the absence of the <s>pāṇi-grahaṇa</s> (marriage ceremony), pastimes such as <s>dāna</s> (toll-collection), <s>abhisāra</s> (tryst), and so on do not exist [there]. There, 'not even a moment passes that could be called half a blink.'

children.text:
dina-rātrer abhāvād rātri-vilāsitvābhāvena tal-līlānām abhāvaḥ | gauṇa-samañjasa
rati-matībhis tad-gata-strībhis tad ayogyatvāt | tasmād dvārakāto'pi golokasya
children.translated_text: Because of the absence of day and night, because of the absence of nocturnal-sport-nature, those pastimes are absent. Because of the <s>gauṇa</s> (secondary) and <s>samañjasa</s> (seemly) affections of the women there, they are unfit for those [pastimes]. Therefore, <s>Goloka</s> is even inferior to <s>Dvārakā</s>. Nevertheless, from <s>Śrī Dāsa Gosvāmī</s>'s <s>Śrī Stavāvalī</s> (<s>Vraja-Vilāsa</s> 5):

children.text: vaikuṇṭhād api sodarātmaja-vṛtā dvāravatī sā priyā
children.translated_text: More dear than <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> is that <s>Dvāravatī</s>, surrounded by kinsmen and sons,
where the Lord sports with multitudes of chief queens, each surpassing a hundred <s>Śrīs</s>;

children.text: prema-kṣetram asau tato'pi mathurā śreṣṭhā harer janmato
children.translated_text: the field of <s>prema</s> — even more excellent than that is <s>Mathurā</s>, because of <s>Hari</s>'s birth [there];

children.text: yatra śrī-vraja eva rājatitarāṃ tām eva nityaṃ bhaje ||
children.translated_text: and where <s>Śrī Vraja</s> alone reigns supreme — I eternally worship that [<s>Vraja</s>].

children.text:
evaṃ paraspara-sambandhatvena mathurāto'pi dvārakāyā nyūnatvam | atha śruti-
smṛti-saṃmataṃ sarvotkṛṣṭaṃ tu māthuram | yathā padma-purāṇe-
children.translated_text:
Thus, by virtue of mutual relationship, <s>Dvārakā</s> is inferior even to <s>Mathurā</s>. Now, the <s>Māthura</s> [abode], approved by <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, is the most excellent of all. As in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>:
'Ah, blessed is <s>Madhupurī</s>, greater even than <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>!
Thus, among the seven cities, the most excellent is <s>Māthura</s>.
Hear its glory, O goddess — it is the highest of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> realms.'

children.text:
aho madhupurī dhanyā vaikuṇṭhāc ca garīyasī |
evaṃ sapta-purīṇāṃ tu sarvotkṛṣṭaṃ tu māthuram |
śrūyatāṃ mahimā devi vaikuṇṭha-bhuvanottamaḥ || iti |
sañjāyamānādara-gaurava-darśanena sva-mano na tṛpyet | tad yathā (2.4.110-113)-
children.translated_text: [finds that] his own mind is not satisfied. Namely thus (2.4.110–113):
Therefore, in the <s>Śrī Bṛhad-Bhāgavatāmṛta</s>, the cowherd boy in <s>Goloka</s>, seeing the reverence and awe of the attendants there,
That very one, the crest-jewel of omniscience, the Lord,
the Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, who is indeed the son of <s>Nanda</s>,
the beloved of <s>Lakṣmī</s> and others — I recognize <s>Rādhikā</s>
