and Her face, and the groups of servants and the boys of <s>Vraja</s>.
Yet, in this land of <s>Vraja</s>, the Lord with His retinue,

children.text: viharantaṃ tathā nekṣe bhidyate tena manmathaḥ ||
children.translated_text: sporting thus — I do not see [Him there as here]. By this, my heart breaks.
Sometime, in the groves there, playfully
thus shining, surrounded by herds of cows,
I see Him sometimes standing
on His own throne, exactly like His own Lord, in every way.
Yet, because of the awareness of Supreme Lordship
in that Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> who is <s>Nanda</s>'s son,
through the reverence and awe that arises,
my mind is not satisfied, as that [reverence] diminishes <s>prema</s>.
And in the <s>Śrī Stava-Mālā</s> (<s>Nandāpaharaṇam</s> 19):
There is no realm more delightful anywhere than <s>Vṛndāṭavī</s> (the forest of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>) —
thus clearly [He showed] to His kinsmen.
He who, having properly shown <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>,

children.text: ninye goṣṭhaṃ pātu sa tvāṃ mukundaḥ ||
children.translated_text: led [them] back to the cowshed — may that <s>Mukunda</s> protect you!
As in the Tenth [Canto] (<s>Bhāgavata</s> 10.28.10):
<s>Nanda</s>, having seen the supersensory great opulence of the world-protectors,

children.text: kṛṣṇe ca sannatiṃ teṣāṃ jñātibhyo vismito'bravīt ||
children.translated_text: and their obeisance to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, spoke to his kinsmen in amazement.

children.text:
atha ṭīkā-vismitaḥ parama-mādhuryāviṣṭatvenaiśvaryānusandhānābhāvāt | ataḥ
parama-kāruṇikaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇaḥ sva-bandhu-vargaṃ nandādikaṃ golokaṃ sandarśya
punar gokulaṃ nītavān | golokaṃ bhū-vṛndāvanādikaṃ śrī-daśame nandādīnāṃ
vaikuṇṭha-darśanānantaraṃ vrajāgamanaṃ vyaktam evāsti | ataeva svayaṃ-prakāśa-
bhū-vṛndāvanasya sadā prakaṭāprakaṭatve virājamānatve sasmād gokulākhyād
vṛndāvanād golokaya pṛthaktvaṃ nyūnatvaṃ ca spaṣṭam madhuraiśvaryayor
abhāvāt | madhuraiśvaryaṃ ca-ye daityā duḥśakā hantuṃ ity ādeḥ | kvacid aiśvarya-
sāmyena dhāmnor goloka-goṣṭhayor aikyaṃ darśitam indrādyair mādhuryāṇām
akovidaiḥ | aikyaṃ tu golokasya gokula-vaibhava-prakāśa-rūpatvāt | prakāśas tu na
bhedeṣu gaṇyate sa hi no pṛthak (LBhāg 1.1.20), tatra ca karoti yāḥ prakāśeṣu
koṭiśo'prakaṭeṣv api (LBhāg 1.5.451) |
children.translated_text: Now the commentary — 'amazed': because of being absorbed in supreme sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>), there was no contemplation of <s>aiśvarya</s> (majesty). Therefore, the supremely compassionate <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, having shown <s>Goloka</s> to His kinsmen <s>Nanda</s> and the others, led them back to <s>Gokula</s>. That <s>Goloka</s> is the earthly <s>Vṛndāvana</s> and the like is clear from the Tenth Canto — after the vision of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> by <s>Nanda</s> and the others, their return to <s>Vraja</s> is quite evident. Therefore, since the self-manifest earthly <s>Vṛndāvana</s> eternally shines in both manifest and unmanifest forms, the distinctness and inferiority of <s>Goloka</s> from that <s>Vṛndāvana</s> called <s>Gokula</s> is clear — because of the absence of sweetness (<s>mādhurya</s>) and [combined] majesty (<s>aiśvarya</s>). And the sweet-majesty [is referenced in]: 'Those demons who were difficult to kill' and so forth. Sometimes, by the equality of majesty in the two abodes — <s>Goloka</s> and the cowshed — their identity is shown by <s>Indra</s> and others, who are unskilled in sweetness. The identity, however, is because <s>Goloka</s> is the manifestation-form of the splendor of <s>Gokula</s>. 'A manifestation is not counted as a difference; for it is not separate' (<s>Laghu Bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 1.1.20); 'And there [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] performs [pastimes] in manifestations, in tens of millions, even in the unmanifest [realms]' (<s>Laghu Bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 1.5.451).

children.text:
yadyapi svayaṃ-prakāśa-prakāśyānāṃ madhye bhedo gaṇyate tathāpi caitanya-
caritāmṛte (madhya 8.83) taṭastha ha-iyā vicārile āche taratama | tatra ca mahā-
rāsa-prasaṅge tāra madhye eka mūrti rahe rādhā-pāśa iti pūrve vicārito'sti | yad vā
viśeṣato śrī-caritāmṛte madhya-līlāyāṃ viṃśati-paricchede śrī-sanātana-gosvāmi-
śikṣā-prasaṅge vivṛtam asti | athavā acintya-śakti-prabhāveṇa samādheyaḥ |
children.translated_text: Although the distinction among the self-manifest and the manifested [forms] is counted, nevertheless, in the <s>Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s> (Madhya 8.83), 'from a neutral standpoint, there is a gradation among them.' And therein, in the context of the great <s>rāsa</s>-dance, 'among them, one form remains beside <s>Rādhā</s>' — this has been discussed earlier. Or, this is explained in particular in the <s>Śrī Caritāmṛta</s>, Madhya-līlā, twentieth chapter, in the context of the instructions to <s>Śrī Sanātana Gosvāmin</s>. Alternatively, it should be reconciled through the power of the inconceivable potency.
Moreover —
Just as, even when four-armed, He does not abandon the nature of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s form —

children.text: ataḥ prakāśa eva syāt tasyāsau dvibhujasya ca || (LBhāg 1.1.23)
children.translated_text: therefore, that [four-armed form] must be a <s>prakāśa</s> (manifest expansion) of the two-armed one. || (<s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 1.1.23)

children.text:
ity-ādi-nyāyāt brahma-mohanādi-kartṛtvābhāvāt mathurā-dvārakā-gata-śrī-kṛṣṇa-
prakāśe śrī-gokula-gata-pūrṇatama-rūpa-mādhuryābhāve'pi prakāśatvam, tathā
goloke'pi śrī-vṛndāvana-gata-madhuraiśvarya-mādhuryayor abhāve'pi prakāśatvam
| aprapañca-prapañca-gocaratvam aprākṛta-prākṛta iva śrī-gokula-
bhūrūpo'nuvādatayā cintāmaṇy-ādi-rūpo vidheyatayā, sa tu māthura-bhū-rūpaḥ
paricchinno'py athādbhutaḥ ity ādeḥ |
children.translated_text: By principles such as these — because of the absence of being the agent of the bewilderment of <s>Brahmā</s> and the like — even in the expansion of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> who went to <s>Mathurā</s> and <s>Dvārakā</s>, despite the absence of the most complete sweetness of the form in <s>Śrī Gokula</s>, the status of <s>prakāśa</s> (expansion) holds. Similarly, even in <s>Goloka</s>, despite the absence of the sweet majesty and sweetness [found] in the <s>Vṛndāvana</s> [of this world], the status of expansion holds. The nature of being both within and beyond the phenomenal world — just as, being <s>aprākṛta</s> (supramundane) yet appearing <s>prākṛta</s> (mundane), the land-form of <s>Śrī Gokula</s> is mentioned predicatively as having the form of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems) and the like, while stated as the topic — and 'that <s>Mathurā</s> land-form, though delimited, is nevertheless wondrous' — and so forth.

children.text:
māthuro śrī-gokulaḥ-
māthuraṃ ca dvidhā prāhur gokulaṃ puram eva ca (LBhāg 1.5.497) ity ādeḥ |

children.translated_text: Therefore, its eternal nature is heard of in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> as well:

children.text: nityaṃ me mathurāṃ viddhi vanaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ tathā iti |
children.translated_text: 'Know <s>Mathurā</s> to be eternal, as well as the forest <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.' Thus.
Herein, even the garland of cosmic eggs finds its limit;
[this <s>Vṛndāvana</s>], even in its semblance, is experienced by <s>Brahmā</s>. ||

The <s>Mathurā</s> [region includes] <s>Śrī Gokula</s> —
'<s>Mathurā</s> is said to be of two kinds: <s>Gokula</s> and the city itself' (<s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 1.5.497) — and so forth.

children.text: ity ato rāsa-līlāyāṃ puline tatra yāmune |
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>rāsa</s>-dance, on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,

children.text: pramadā-śata-koṭyo'pi mamūr yat tat kim adbhutam ||
children.translated_text: that hundreds of crores of women appeared — what wonder is that? ||

children.text: svaiḥ svair līlā-parikarair janair dṛśyāni nāparaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Visible [only] to their own respective pastime-associates, not to others,
[these divine pastimes] are indeed fit to manifest at the occasions of their respective pastimes. ||
It is wondrous that, though existing simultaneously in one place,
they are certainly always mutually untouched in their essential natures. ||
Adorned on all sides with the pastimes of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s childhood and the like,
the forms of the hills, cow-pastures, forests, and the like are manifold. ||
A region of His, though full of pastimes, is sometimes perceived

children.text: śūnya evekṣate dṛṣṭi-yogyair apy aparair api ||
children.translated_text: as empty by some — even by those qualified to see — and by others too. ||

children.text: ataḥ prabhoḥ priyāṇāṃ ca dhāmnaś ca samayasya ca |
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the inconceivable power of the Lord,

children.text: avicintya-prabhāvatvād atra kiṃ ca na durghaṭam ||
children.translated_text: of His beloveds, of His abode, and of the occasion — what is impossible here? ||
(<s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 1.5.506-7, 509-515)

children.text: caturdhā mādhurī tasya vraja eva virājate |
children.translated_text: His fourfold sweetness shines forth in <s>Vraja</s> alone —
of majesty, of play, of the flute, and of the sacred image. || (<s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 1.5.526)

children.text:
tasmāt yā yathā bhuvi vartante ityādi-diśā dvārakā mathurā-gokula-nāmāni
svatanvāṇy eva bhagavato dhāmāni | gokula-tad-vaibhava-prakāśatvena prasiddho
goloka iti nāma para-vyomoparīti śāstra-prasiddhaṃ, yathā hari-vaṃśe śakra-
vacanam-
children.translated_text: Therefore, it is fitting — 'whose abode is celebrated in the <s>Purāṇas</s> and the like as being in four places.' Moreover — because of the specific designations 'My shelter,' 'My lord,' 'My possession' — here even <s>Brahmā</s> and the other [gods] have no authority, what to speak of others? And elsewhere it is seen that in the sacred field of <s>Śrī Puruṣottama</s>, measuring ten <s>yojanas</s>, in the conch-shaped [area] of five <s>krośas</s>, even the ruler of that region has no independent authority. What more [need be said]? Therefore, the supreme attainability, supreme secrecy, and supreme beauty of the self-manifest land of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — as in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> (10.21.10) —

children.text: tatra soma-gatiś caiva jyotiṣāṃ ca mahātmanām ||
tasyopari gavāṃ lokaḥ sādhyās taṃ pālayanti hi |
sa hi sarva-gataḥ kṛṣṇa mahākāśa-gato mahān ||
upary upari tatrāpi gatis tava tapomayī |
yāṃ na vidmo vayaṃ sarve pṛcchanto'pi pitāmaham |
brāhmye tapasi yuktānāṃ brahma-lokaḥ parā gatiḥ |
gavām eva tu yo loko durāroho hi sā gatiḥ ||
sa tu lokas tvayā kṛṣṇa sīdamānaḥ kṛtātmanā |
dhṛto dhṛtimatā vīra nighnatopadravān gavām || [HV 2.19.29-35] iti |

indras tu brahma-mohanādau gokula-paramaiśvaryaṃ jñātvāpi parama-mādhurya-
darśanena brahmaṇa iva punar mohitaḥ san tasyaivāścarya-prakāśaṃ golokaṃ
varṇayitvā tasyāpi gokulena sahābhedavan nirdeśenāha-- sa tu lokas tvayā kṛṣṇa iti
| ataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-vākyaṃ śrī-bhāgavate (10.25.18)-

tasmān mac-charaṇaṃ goṣṭhaṃ man-nāthaṃ mat-parigraham |
gopāye svātma-yogena so'yaṃ me vrata āhitaḥ || iti |

tasmād yuktam eva-yasya vāsaḥ purāṇādau khyātaḥ sthāna-catuṣṭaye iti | kiṃ ca-
mac-charaṇaṃ man-nāthaṃ mat-parigraham iti viśeṣaṇād atra brahmādīnām apy
adhikāro nāsti, kā kathānyeṣām ? dṛśyate cānyatra daśa-yojanātmake śrī-
puruṣottama-kṣetre śaṅkākāre krośa-pañcake tad-deśādhipateḥ
svatantreṇādhikāro nāsti | kiṃ bahunā, ataḥ svayaṃ-prakāśa-bhū-vṛndāvanasya
parama-prāpyatvaṃ parama-rahasyatvaṃ parama-ramaṇīyatvaṃ ca tathā śrī-
bhāgavate (10.21.10)-

vṛndāvane sakhi bhuvo vitanoti kīrtiṃ
yad devakī-suta-padāmbuja-labdha-lakṣmi |
children.translated_text:
'<s>Vṛndāvana</s>, O friend, spreads the glory of the earth,
having obtained the fortune from the lotus-feet of the son of <s>Devakī</s>.'
Again, in the same [canto], in <s>Brahmā</s>'s hymn of praise (10.14.34) —

children.text: tad bhūri-bhāgyam iha janma kim apy aṭavyāṃ
children.translated_text: 'How greatly fortunate is any birth in this forest —
which in <s>Gokula</s> [received] the consecration of the dust of some [divine] foot;

children.text: yaj jīvitaṃ tu nikhilaṃ bhagavān mukundas
children.translated_text: whose entire life is <s>Bhagavān Mukunda</s>,
the dust of whose feet is sought even by the <s>Śruti</s> (Vedas) to this day.' ||
Again, in the same [canto], in the words of <s>Śrīmad Uddhava</s> (10.47.61) —

children.text:
āsām aho caraṇa-reṇu-juṣām ahaṃ syāṃ
vṛndāvane kim api gulma-latauṣadhīnām | iti |
children.translated_text:
'Oh, may I be any one of the bushes, creepers, or herbs in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
which enjoy the dust of the feet of these [<s>gopīs</s>].' Thus.
In the <s>Ādi-purāṇa</s> —

children.text: trailokye pṛthivī dhanyā yatra vṛndāvanaṃ purī |
children.translated_text: 'In the three worlds, the earth is blessed, where <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is the city;

children.text: tatrāpi gopikā pārtha yatra rādhābhidhā mama ||
children.translated_text: and therein the <s>gopīs</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s> — [especially] she who is called <s>Rādhā</s>, who is Mine.' ||
As follows —

children.text: vraja na gopikā bhinnā mattaḥ paśyanti kevalam |
children.translated_text: 'The <s>gopīs</s> in <s>Vraja</s> are not different from Me; they see [Me] alone.
The cowherds, the cows, and the [other residents] there are embodiments of My own bliss.' ||

children.text: ye vrajasthān aho bhinnān mat paśyanti tu kecana |
children.translated_text: 'Those who, alas, see the residents of <s>Vraja</s> as different from Me —

children.text: na teṣāṃ mūḍha-buddhīnāṃ gatir naiva paratra ca ||
children.translated_text: for those deluded souls, there is no destination, neither here nor hereafter.' ||
In the <s>Brahma-saṃhitā</s> (5.56) —
'The trees [are made of] wish-fulfilling gems, the ground of <s>cintāmaṇi</s>, the water of nectar,

children.text: kathā gānaṃ nāṭyaṃ gamanam api vaṃśī priya-sakhi
children.translated_text: the speech is song, the movement is dance, the flute is the dear companion —

children.text: cid-ānandaṃ jyotiḥ param api tad āsvādyam api ca ||
children.translated_text: [all is] consciousness-bliss, the light is supreme, and that too is to be relished.' ||

children.text: śrī-gopāla-tāpanyāṃ ca (2.36)-tāsāṃ madhye sākṣād brahma gopāla-purī iti |
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Śrī Gopāla-tāpanī</s> (2.36) — 'In their midst is directly <s>Brahman</s>, the city of <s>Gopāla</s>.' Thus.
In the <s>Bṛhad-gautamīya</s> —

children.text: idaṃ vṛndāvanaṃ ramyaṃ mama dhāmaiva kevalam |
children.translated_text: 'This charming <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is My abode alone.

children.text: atra ye paśavaḥ pakṣi-vṛkṣā kīṭā narāmarāḥ |
children.translated_text: Here, whatever animals, birds, trees, insects, humans, or immortals —

children.text: ye vasanti mamādhiṣṇye mṛtā yānti mamālayam ||
children.translated_text: those who dwell in My realm, upon dying, go to My abode.' ||

children.text: atra yā gopa-kanyāś ca nivasanti mamālaye |
children.translated_text: 'Here, whatever cowherd-maidens dwell in My abode —

children.text: yoginyas tā mayā nityaṃ mama sevā-parāyaṇāḥ ||
children.translated_text: they are <s>yoginīs</s>, eternally devoted to My service.' ||
'This forest of five <s>yojanas</s> is the form of My body.
This <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā) is called <s>Suṣumnā</s>, the bearer of supreme nectar.' ||

children.text: atra devāś ca bhūtāni vartante sūkṣma-rūpataḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Here, the <s>devas</s> and beings exist in subtle form.

children.text: sarva-deva-mayaś cāhaṃ na tyajāmi vanaṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: And I, who am all the <s>devas</s>, never abandon this forest.' ||

children.text: āvirbhāvas tirobhāvo bhaven me 'tra yuge yuge |
children.translated_text: 'My manifestation and disappearance occur here in every age.
This charming [<s>Vṛndāvana</s>], made of effulgence, is invisible to the fleshly eye.' ||
'The twelfth <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, protected by <s>Vṛndā</s>,
presided over by <s>Hari</s>, served by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others.' ||
In the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s> —
'That sacred <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, sheltered by <s>Vṛndā-devī</s>,
presided over by <s>Hari</s>, served by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and others.' ||

children.text: yathā lakṣmīḥ priyatamā yathā bhakti-parā narāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Just as <s>Lakṣmī</s> is most beloved, just as persons devoted to <s>bhakti</s>,
so is <s>Vṛndāvana</s> on earth most dear to <s>Govinda</s>.' ||
There, in <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>, is [the place] called <s>Śrī Govinda-sthala</s>. As in the <s>Śrī Govinda-līlāmṛta</s> (21.28) —
'This bank called <s>Śrī Govinda-sthala</s>, pure, the seat of union with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
the crest of <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s>, gradually sloping on all sides, resembling the site of a tortoise-seat,
rich with rows of bower-petals, with a good pericarp of a jeweled mansion, with golden plantain-
rows as filaments — she beheld it, equal to a thousand-petaled lotus.' ||

children.text:
ataeva smaraṇa-maṅgale kuñjāt ity atra kuñjād iti kuñja-prādhānyāt śrī-govinda-
sthala-gataḥ kuñjo jñeya iti |
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the <s>Smaraṇa-maṅgala</s>, 'from the bower' — here 'from the bower' means: because of the prominence of the bower, the bower located at <s>Śrī Govinda-sthala</s> should be understood.
In the <s>Skānda Purāṇa</s>, <s>Mathurā-khaṇḍa</s> (<s>Mathurā-māhātmya</s> 399-401) —
'In that <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is the sacred abode of <s>Govinda</s>,
filled with His servants — there I remain.
On earth, the <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> of <s>Govinda</s> is in that <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, O King,
where <s>Vṛndā</s> and other servants, eager for <s>Govinda</s>, abide.' ||
'Those supreme souls who have seen the great abode
of <s>Govinda</s> in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, O King — they have fulfilled their purpose on earth.' ||

children.text: tatra yoga-pīṭhe śrī-govinda-devasya dhyānaṃ, yathā krama-dīpikāyām (3.1-36)-
children.translated_text: Therein, the meditation on <s>Śrī Govinda-deva</s> at the <s>Yoga-pīṭha</s>, as in the <s>Krama-dīpikā</s> (3.1-36) —
Now, with trees whose branches bend with clusters of new sprouts
and buds bursting with manifested, charming fragrance, [dripping with] honey —
wrapped with lovely vines blooming with fresh flower-clusters —

children.text: smarec chiśiritaṃ śivaṃ sita-matis tu vṛndāvanam ||1
children.translated_text: let the pure-minded one meditate on the cool, auspicious <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. ||1||
Made melodious within by the buzzing sounds of hovering
bees, delighting in savoring the beauty of blossoming flowers,
resounding here and there with pigeons, parrots, <s>śārikā</s>-birds, and other cuckoos and the like,
bustling with the dancing of the enemy of serpents (peacocks). ||2||
Constantly attended by breezes, carried by the splashing waves
of the daughter of <s>Kalinda</s> (Yamunā), dusty with the pollen
from the interior of awakened lotuses in the pools,
stirring the garments of the women of <s>Vraja</s> whose desire is kindled. ||3||
With coral-like new sprouts, emerald-like leaves, diamond-and-pearl
cluster-like buds, ruby-like various fruits —
massive, constantly attended by all seasons, wish-fulfilling —
within that, let one meditate on the wish-fulfilling tree (<s>kalpakāṅghri</s>) raised high. ||4||
Beneath it, a golden ground, brilliant as the rising sun
[reflected] from a row of golden peaks, showering nectar-drops,
with a pavement of blazing jewels, brilliant with heaps of flower-pollen —
let the wise one meditate again, unwearyingly, free from the six enemies (<s>ṣaḍ-ripus</s>). ||5||
On the great <s>Yoga-pīṭha</s> set in that jeweled pavement,
having visualized a red eight-petaled lotus,
in its center, radiant with the luster of the rising sun,
let one then meditate on <s>Mukunda</s>, seated in bliss. ||6||
With a radiance equal to a freshly dark blue lotus
[born from] a heap of collyrium-clouds strung on threads of jewels,
with locks of very glossy, dark, densely curled hair,
resplendent with a crest of charming, glistening peacock-feathers. ||7||
With a face beautiful as the full autumn goad-[marked] moon-disc,
with wide lotus-petal eyes,
with cheek-surfaces [like] mirrors lit by the rays of gem-sparkling
crocodile-shaped <s>kuṇḍalas</s> (earrings), with an elevated, beautiful nose. ||8||
With lips more beautiful than <s>sindūra</s> (vermillion), with body
illumined by the radiance of gentle smiles [bright as] moon, <s>kunda</s>, and <s>mandāra</s> flowers,
with a conch-like throat, charming and lustrous with a necklace (<s>graiveyaka</s>)
fashioned from an abundance of forest coral-blossoms and flowers. ||9||
With shoulders adorned with a garland-string
of <s>santāna</s>-tree blossoms and saffron, attended by intoxicated bees,
with a broad chest resplendent with rows of necklaces [like] constellations,
with the <s>Kaustubha</s> gem shining like a sun on the expanse of the celestial chest. ||10||
Marked well with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> sign, with raised shoulders,
with well-formed, full, rounded arms reaching to the knees,
with a waist slender up to the navel, with a generous, deep navel —
a line of body-hair beautiful as rows of female bees. ||11||
Armlets and bangles fashioned with various gems,
necklaces, fine garments, anklets, and waist-ornament bands,
His body-staff anointed with two kinds of fragrant paste,
His rounded hips wrapped in a yellow garment. ||12||
Beautiful thighs and knees, well-proportioned and delightful calves,
lovely raised insteps that put to shame the beauty of a tortoise,
toenails gleaming like ruby mirrors, rows of resplendent
jeweled toes, and beautiful lotus-feet. ||13||
The soles of His reddish feet, charming with the marks of
fish, goad, wheel, flag, barley-grain, lotus, and thunderbolt,
His limbs fashioned from the essence of all gracefulness,
His bodily beauty surpassing the beauty of <s>Manobhava</s> (Cupid). ||14||
From the holes of the flute filling His lotus-face,
through divine melodies set in motion by His swaying fingertips,
perpetually melting and attracting the continuous lineage of all creatures —
an ocean of infinite bliss. ||15||
Now, of the graceful and beautiful cowherd maidens (<s>gopīs</s>),
whose broad girdle-zones make their hips move languidly,
whose three folds of skin on the belly, pressed by the heavy weight of their breasts,
are accompanied by an expanding line of body-hair, ||23||
drinking from their feet the nectar of the blossoming of desire
produced by the sweet and charming flute-music of His,
their creeper-like bodies adorned by the arising of goose-bumps
in clusters of buds, ||24||
from the ocean of passion swelled by the moonlight
of His exceedingly beautiful gentle smile,
the drops of spray from the breaking of the swiftest waves —
their continuous beads of perspiration born of exertion, ||25||
by the rain of arrows of <s>Māra</s> (Cupid) — sharp glances
shot from His exceedingly graceful, gently arched eyebrows —
all their vital points pierced, their limbs overwhelmed,
afflicted with unbearable trembling, ||26||
with both their languidly trembling lotus-eyes
eager for the ceremony of drinking the nectar of the beauty
of His exceedingly lovely form and actions,
rivers flowing with the flood of loving tears, ||27||
their loosened braids of hair shedding full-bloomed flowers,
constantly attended by swarms of bees greedy for the honey [dripping from those flowers],
their soft words faltering with the intoxication of love's madness, their girdles swaying,
their silk garments at the hips loosening to reveal the luster of their hips, ||28||
the jingling of their gem-studded ankle-ornaments from the gentle tapping of their stumbling lovely lotus-feet
filling all directions,
their lower lips trembling, their budding dewy-lashed eyes —
a pair of lotuses in a lake — their earrings gleaming, ||29||
the tender sprouts of their reddish lips wilting
from the heat of the wind of their deep sighing,
their lotus-hands splendid with various offerings —
surrounded on all sides by such <s>sakhīs</s> (female companions), always attended. ||30||
Of those [<s>gopīs</s>], their entire bodies worshipped with garlands of
fully-bloomed blue lotuses [like] their long, moving, dark eyes — the abode of various amorous sports,
bearing [upon His body] the delightful swarm of bees — their love-intoxicated eyes —
savoring the honey flowing from their enchanting lotus-faces — a captivating garland. ||31||
One should meditate on the <s>gopīs</s>, cowherds, and cattle outside [the circle],
and in front of Him, the assembly of the <s>devas</s>,
desirous of wealth, led by <s>Viriñci</s> (Brahmā), the Three-eyed (<s>Śiva</s>),
and <s>Śatamanyu</s> (Indra), devoted to hymns of praise. ||32||
To His right, a host of sages,
firm in [their desire for] <s>dharma</s>, devoted to the scriptures;
then behind, the chief <s>yogīs</s>, desiring
liberation, <s>Sanaka</s> and others, absorbed in meditation. ||33||
To His left, the <s>Yakṣas</s>, <s>Siddhas</s>,
<s>Gandharvas</s>, <s>Vidyādharas</s>, and <s>Cāraṇas</s>,
along with the <s>Kinnaras</s> and the chief <s>Apsarases</s>,
desirous of pleasures, [worshipping] with dance, song, and music. ||34||
White as a conch, moon, and <s>kunda</s> flower, knowing all the sacred scriptures,
with a mass of matted locks tawny as streaks of lightning,
desiring unwavering devotion directed toward His lotus feet,
having completely abandoned all other attachments — ||35||
with melodious modulations belonging to the system of three <s>grāmas</s> (scales) of the seven <s>rāgas</s> (musical modes)
accompanied by various <s>śruti</s> groupings,
delighting Him with these great [melodies] —
one should meditate on the son of <s>Dhātṛ</s> (Brahmā), the chief of sages (<s>Nārada</s>), in the sky. ||36||
Here, a chapter from the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s> (5.69.4-118) is written in order —
<s>Pārvatī</s> said:
Of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who abides within and beyond infinite millions of universes,

children.text: viṣṇoḥ sthānaṃ paraṃ teṣāṃ pradhānaṃ varam uttamam ||4||
children.translated_text: the supreme abode — the foremost, best, and highest among them — ||4||

children.text: yat paraṃ nāsti kṛṣṇasya priyaṃ sthānaṃ manoramam |
children.translated_text: that which is the supreme, beloved, and delightful abode of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — beyond which there is nothing —

children.text: tat sarvaṃ śrotum icchāmi kathayasva mahā-prabho ||5||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear about all of that; please tell me, O great Lord. ||5||
<s>Īśvara</s> (Śiva) said:
More secret than the most secret, supremely bliss-bestowing,

children.text: atyadbhutaṃ rahaḥ sthānam ānandaṃ paramaṃ param ||6||
children.translated_text: most wondrous, a hidden place of supreme, ultimate bliss. ||6||

children.text: durlabhānāṃ ca paramaṃ durlabhaṃ mohanaṃ param |
children.translated_text: The supremely rare among the rare, the supremely enchanting,
O Goddess, full of all powers, concealed in all abodes — ||7||
the foremost abode of the <s>Sātvatas</s> (devotees), exceedingly rare even for <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
eternally situated above the universe — [that is] named <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. ||8||
The complete <s>Brahman</s>, blissful sovereignty, eternal, imperishable bliss —
<s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> and the like are mere portions of portions of that; <s>Vṛndāvana</s> itself [is present] on earth. ||9||
Whatever sovereignty of <s>Goloka</s> exists, that is established in <s>Gokula</s>;
whatever splendor of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> exists, that is established in <s>Dvārikā</s>. ||10||
That supreme <s>Brahman</s>-sovereignty, eternally sheltered in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> —
the supreme abode of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, especially in the midst of the forest. ||11||

children.text: tasmāt trailokya-madhye tu pṛthvī dhanyeti viśrutā |
children.translated_text: Therefore, among the three worlds, the earth is celebrated as blessed,
because the region called <s>Māthura</s> is exclusively dear to <s>Viṣṇu</s>. ||12||
His own abode, named par excellence, is the <s>Māthura-maṇḍala</s> (district of <s>Mathurā</s>),
a hidden, varied abode situated within the city. ||13||
The <s>Māthura-maṇḍala</s> is in the form of a thousand-petaled lotus,
a wonderful abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, revolving with <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s discus. ||14||
The expanse of the pericarp and petals is called the 'secret tree.'
The twelve chief forests are narrated in order [with their] greatness. ||15||
<s>Bhadra</s>, <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Loha</s>, <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s>, <s>Mahātāla</s>, <s>Khadiraka</s>,

children.text: bakulaṃ kumudaṃ kāmyaṃ madhu vṛndā vanaṃ tathā ||16||
children.translated_text: <s>Bakula</s>, <s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Kāmya</s>, <s>Madhu</s>, <s>Vṛndāvana</s> likewise — ||16||
twelve is the count; seven are to the west of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā),

children.text: pūrve pañca-vanaṃ proktaṃ tatrāsti guhyam uttamam ||17||
children.translated_text: five forests are said to be on the east — therein is the supreme secret. ||17||
The great forest called <s>Gokula</s>, <s>Madhu</s>, <s>Vṛndāvana</s> likewise,
and another called a sub-forest — the place of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s playful <s>rasa</s> [pastimes]. ||18||
<s>Kadamba-khaṇḍa</s>, <s>Nanda-vana</s>, <s>Nandīśvara</s> likewise,
<s>Nanda-nandana-khaṇḍa</s>, and [groves of] <s>palāśa</s>, <s>aśoka</s>, and <s>ketakī</s>. ||19||
<s>Sugandha</s>, <s>Mānasa</s>, <s>Kaila</s>, <s>Amṛta</s>, the dining-place,
<s>Sukha-prasādhana</s>, <s>Vatsa-haraṇa</s> (the stealing of the calves), <s>Śeṣa-śāyika</s> (where <s>Śeṣa</s> sleeps). ||20||
<s>Śyāma-pūrva</s>, <s>Dadhi-grāma</s> (the village of yogurt), <s>Cakra-bhānu-pura</s> likewise,
<s>Saṃketa</s>, <s>Dvipada</s>, and <s>Bāla-krīḍana-dhūsara</s> (dusty from childhood play). ||21||
<s>Kāma-druma</s> (the wish-fulfilling tree), <s>Sulalita</s> (the graceful), <s>Utsuka</s> (the eager) — these forests,
places of various kinds of playful <s>rasa</s>, various pastimes and <s>rasa</s>. ||22||
The expanse of the great tree — the 'secret tree' is so called;
the thousand-petaled lotus called <s>Gokula</s> is the great abode. ||23||

children.text: karṇikā tan mahad dhāma govinda-sthānam uttamam |
children.translated_text: The pericarp [of that lotus] is that great abode — the supreme place of <s>Govinda</s>;
there, upon a golden platform, adorned with a jeweled pavilion. ||24||

children.text: karṇikāyāṃ kramād dikṣu vidikṣu dalam īritam |
children.translated_text: From the pericarp, in the [cardinal] directions and intermediate directions, the petals are described in order.

children.text: yad dalaṃ dakṣiṇe proktaṃ paraṃ guhyottamottamam ||25||
children.translated_text: The petal that is said to be in the south is supremely, most excellently secret. ||25||
On that petal is a great seat, inaccessible to the <s>Nigamas</s> and <s>Āgamas</s>,

children.text: yogīndrair api duṣprāpaṃ sarvātmā yac ca gokulam ||26||
children.translated_text: difficult to reach even for the greatest <s>yogīs</s> — and that is <s>Gokula</s>, the Self of all. ||26||

children.text: dvitīyaṃ dalam āgneyyāṃ tad rahasya-dalaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: The second petal is in the southeast — that is also a secret petal;

children.text: saṃketaṃ dvipadaṃ caiva kuṭī dvau tat-kule sthitau ||27||
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃketa</s>, <s>Dvipada</s>, and two <s>kuṭīs</s> (cottages) situated in that region. ||27||

children.text: pūrvaṃ dalaṃ tṛtīyaṃ ca pradhāna-sthānam uttamam |
children.translated_text: The eastern petal is the third — the primary, supreme place;
from the touch of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and all sacred waters, it is remembered as a hundredfold [more sacred]. ||28||

children.text: caturthaṃ dalam aiśānyāṃ siddha-pīṭhe'pi tat- padam |
children.translated_text: The fourth petal is in the northeast — a <s>siddha-pīṭha</s> (seat of perfection) as well;
a new <s>gopī</s> who exercises [devotion] there obtains <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as her husband. ||29||
The stealing of garments and ornaments is mentioned in that petal.
The fifth [petal] is said to be in the north — the best among all petals. ||30||
The [place of the] twelve <s>Ādityas</s> (suns) is right here on this petal, equal to the pericarp.

children.text: vāyavyāṃ tu dalaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ tatra kālī-hradaḥ smṛtaḥ ||31||
children.translated_text: The sixth petal is in the northwest — there <s>Kālī-hrada</s> (the pool of <s>Kāliya</s>) is located. ||31||
The most excellent among excellent petals — the primary place is so called;
and the best of all petals is the seventh, in the west. ||32||
It grants the desired boons to the groups of <s>yajña-patnīs</s> (the wives of the sacrificing brāhmaṇas);
here even an <s>asura</s> (demon) attained liberation, which is rare even for the <s>devas</s>. ||33||
The bewildering of <s>Brahmā</s> [took place] here; the petal has the <s>Brahma-hrada</s> (pool of Brahmā);

children.text: nairṛtyāṃ tu dalaṃ proktam aṣṭamaṃ vyoma-ghātanam ||34||
children.translated_text: the eighth petal is said to be in the southwest — the 'sky-striking' [place]. ||34||
The slaying of <s>Śaṅkhacūḍa</s> [took place] there — a place of various playful <s>rasa</s> pastimes.
Thus the eight petals are described, situated within <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> (the forest of <s>Vṛndā</s>). ||35||
The beautiful <s>Śrīmad Vṛndāvana</s>, [accessed by] circumambulation of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
with a <s>Śiva-liṅga</s> as its presiding deity, known by the name <s>Gopīśvara</s>. ||36||

children.text: tad-bāhye ṣoḍaśa-dalaṃ śriyā pūrṇaṃ tam īśvaram |
children.translated_text: Beyond that, sixteen petals, filled with splendor — that Lord,

children.text: sarvāsu dikṣu yat proktaṃ prādakṣiṇyād yathā kramam ||37||
children.translated_text: described in all directions, in order of circumambulation. ||37||
The great abode, the great <s>dhāman</s>, known as 'His own abode' —
the first single petal, the most excellent, whose greatness equals the pericarp. ||38||
There, on the beautiful <s>Govardhana</s> hill, the eternal abode of <s>rasa</s>,
on the pericarp are the great pastimes, the deep recesses of those <s>rasa</s>-pastimes. ||39||
Where <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> becomes the Lord of the eternal <s>Vṛndā</s>-forest,

children.text: kṛṣṇo govindatāṃ prāptaḥ kim anyair bahu-bhāṣitaiḥ ||40||
children.translated_text: where <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> attained the status of <s>Govinda</s> — what need of further words? ||40||
The third petal is called the most excellent of all, the best of the best;
the fourth petal is called the place of most wondrous <s>rasa</s>. ||41||
The beautiful <s>Nandīśvara</s> forest — there the abode of <s>Nanda</s> is remembered;
the greatness of the pericarp-petal — the fifth petal is described. ||42||
The presiding deity there is <s>Gopāla</s>, devoted to the tending of cows;

children.text: ṣaṣṭhaṃ dalaṃ yad ākhyātaṃ tatra nanda-vanaṃ smṛtam ||43||
children.translated_text: the sixth petal is described — there <s>Nanda-vana</s> is remembered. ||43||
The seventh, <s>Bakulāraṇya</s> (the <s>bakula</s> forest), is proclaimed as a beautiful petal;
there the eighth is <s>Tāla-vana</s> (the palm-tree forest) — there the slaying of the [bull-demon] <s>Dhenu</s> is remembered. ||44||
The ninth, <s>Kumudāraṇya</s> (the water-lily forest), is proclaimed as a beautiful petal;
the tenth is <s>Kāmāraṇya</s> (the desire-forest), the primary [cause], the cause of all. ||45||
There is the 'decoration of <s>Brahmā</s>' and the display of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s disguise;
a primary petal, the abode of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s playful <s>rasa</s>. ||46||
The eleventh petal is described — the cause of grace to devotees;
the construction of the bridge, a place consisting of various forests. ||47||
<s>Bhāṇḍīra</s> is the twelfth petal — a beautiful, enchanting forest;
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, delighting in play, is there surrounded by <s>Śrīdāman</s> and others. ||48||

children.text: trayodaśaṃ dalaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tatra bhadra-varaṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: The thirteenth petal, the most excellent — there <s>Bhadra-vara</s> is remembered;
the fourteenth petal is described — a place granting all perfections. ||49||
There is the beautiful <s>Śrī-vana</s> (the forest of <s>Śrī</s>), the cause of all sovereignty,
consisting of the petals of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s play, increasing beauty, glory, and fame. ||50||

children.text: dalaṃ pañcadaśaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ tatra loha-vanaṃ smṛtam |
children.translated_text: The fifteenth petal, the most excellent — there <s>Loha-vana</s> (the iron forest) is remembered;
the sixteenth petal is narrated — its greatness equal to the pericarp. ||51||

children.text: mahā-vanaṃ tatra gītaṃ tatrāsti guhyam uttamam |
children.translated_text: There is <s>Mahā-vana</s> (the great forest) — therein is the supreme secret;
there [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] delights in childhood play, surrounded by calf-tenders. ||52||
There [occurred] the slaying of <s>Pūtanā</s> and others, and the breaking of the twin <s>Arjuna</s> trees.
The presiding deity there is the child <s>Gopāla</s>, five years of age. ||53||
He is called <s>Dāmodara</s> by name, an ocean of the rasa of <s>premānanda</s> (blissful love).
The petal is well-known, declared to be the supreme best of all petals. ||54||
The play of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the filament; it is called the pastime-petal.
And it is also called the filament-petal presided over by the <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings). ||55||
<s>Pārvatī</s> said:

children.text: vṛndāraṇyasya māhātmyaṃ rahasyaṃ vā kim adbhutam |
children.translated_text: What is the greatness of <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> (Vṛndāvana forest), the secret, the wonderful?

children.text: tad ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi kathayasva mahā-prabho ||56||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear that — tell me, O great Lord! ||56||
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
I have told you, O most beloved, the highest of the most secret,

children.text: rahasyānāṃ rahasyaṃ yad durlabhānāṃ ca durlabham ||57||
children.translated_text: the secret of secrets, the rarest of the rare. ||57||
O <s>Devī</s>, it is hidden from the three worlds, supremely worshipped by the lords of the gods,
desired by <s>Brahmā</s> and others, served by <s>suras</s> (gods), <s>siddhas</s>, and the rest. ||58||

children.text: yogīndrā hi sadā bhaktyā tasya dhyānaika-tat-parāḥ |
children.translated_text: The foremost <s>yogīs</s> are always devoted to meditation upon it with devotion,
and by <s>apsarases</s> (celestial nymphs) and <s>gandharvas</s> (celestial musicians), dance and song are unceasing there. ||59||
Glorious <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is delightful, the abode of the rasa of perfect bliss (<s>pūrṇānanda</s>).
Its ground is abundant with <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems), its water is <s>amṛta</s> (nectar) filled with rasa. ||60||
Its trees are wish-fulfilling trees (<s>guru-druma</s>), served there by hosts of <s>Surabhī</s> (wish-fulfilling) cows.
The woman there is <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the man is <s>Viṣṇu</s> — everything arises from a tenth part of Him. ||61||
There, in eternal <s>kaiśora</s> (adolescent) form, an embodiment of bliss always,
with movements like dance, speech like art, and a smiling face unceasingly — ||62||
with pure-natured <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> full of <s>prema</s> (divine love), who have taken shelter of that forest,
absorbed in the bliss of the full <s>Brahman</s>, resplendent with His manifest forms and pervaded by Him. ||63||
Enchantingly beautiful with the cooing of intoxicated cuckoos, bees, and the like,
with the songs of parrots at His cheeks, and with thousands of maddened bee-swarms. ||64||
Rich with the dance of peacocks (enemies of serpents), with enchanting movements of all fragrances,
filled with the pollen of flowers of various colors. ||65||
The full moon always rises there; the sun serves with gentle rays.
Free from suffering, it severs all sorrow; it is devoid of old age and death. ||66||
Free from anger, devoid of jealousy, undivided, and without ego,
it is the rasa of the nectar of perfect bliss, an ocean of the joy of complete <s>prema</s>. ||67||
Beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (qualities of nature), the great abode, the very form of complete <s>prema</s>,
where even the trees and the like manifest horripilation and rain tears of blissful love. ||68||

children.text: kiṃ punaś cetanā-yuktair viṣṇu-bhaktaiḥ kim ucyate |
children.translated_text: What then need be said of conscious beings, of the devotees of <s>Viṣṇu</s>?
From the touch of the dust of <s>Govinda's</s> feet, <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is eternally [sanctified] on earth. ||69||
The <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> (Vṛndāvana forest) is the pericarp of the thousand-petalled lotus;
by its mere touch, the earth is blessed among the three worlds. ||70||

children.text: guhyād guhyataraṃ ramyaṃ madhye vṛndāvanaṃ bhuvi |
children.translated_text: More secret than the most secret, delightful, in the center is <s>Vṛndāvana</s> on earth,
imperishable, the supreme bliss, the eternal abode of <s>Govinda</s>. ||71||
Non-different from the body of <s>Govinda</s>, the full <s>Brahman</s>, the abode of bliss —

children.text: muktis tatra rajaḥ sparśāt tan-māhātmyaṃ kim ucyate ||72||
children.translated_text: liberation comes from the touch of its dust — what can be said of its greatness? ||72||

children.text: tasmāt sarvātmanā devi hṛdi-sthaṃ tad vanaṃ kuru |
children.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Devī</s>, with your entire being, establish that forest in your heart.
In the pastimes of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, [meditate upon] <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in His <s>kaiśora</s> (adolescent) form. ||73||
The <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā river) circumambulates around its pericarp,
its water is deep with the depths of divine play and liberation, enchanting with fragrance, ||74||
a dense abode of nectar mixed with the <s>amṛta</s> of bliss and honey,
brilliantly resplendent with flowers such as lotuses and water-lilies of various colors. ||75||
With <s>cakravāka</s> birds and other fowl, with sweet and varied melodious calls,
its resplendent water is delightful within, captivating to the mind. ||76||
Both its banks are beautiful, made of pure gold;
[the Kālindī] is said to possess ten million times the merit of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>; even the touch of its shore is a boon. ||77||
At its pericarp, [the merit is] ten million times greater, where <s>Hari</s> is engaged in play;
the pericarp of the <s>Kālindī</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> are non-different, one form. ||78||
<s>Pārvatī</s> said:
What is the wonder of <s>Govinda's</s> form of beauty?

children.text: tad ahaṃ śrotum icchāmi kathayasva dayā-nidhe ||79||
children.translated_text: I wish to hear that — tell me, O treasure of compassion! ||79||
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
In the center of delightful <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, adorned with sweet anklets,
decorated with branches and leaves of excellent trees extending for <s>yojanas</s> — ||80||
in its midst, in a beautiful pavilion, the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s> shines resplendently,
constructed in an octagonal form, enchanting with various splendors. ||81||
Upon it is a beautiful ruby-jewelled lion-throne,
on it a lotus with unfolded petals, at the pericarp a seat of bliss. ||82||

children.text: govindasya paraṃ sthānaṃ kim asya mahimocyate |
children.translated_text: It is the supreme abode of <s>Govinda</s> — how can its greatness be told?
It is served by the host of <s>gopīs</s> (cowherd-women) who abide in the glorious <s>Govinda-mantra</s>. ||83||
In the divine <s>Vraja</s> form, of youthful beauty — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
the prince of <s>Vraja</s> with eternal sovereignty, the sole beloved of the boys of <s>Vraja</s>. ||84||
In adolescence (<s>kaiśora</s>) blossoming with youth, with a form wondrous in age,
without beginning yet the origin of all, the beloved son of <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd. ||85||
Sought by the <s>Śrutis</s> (Vedas), unborn, eternal, enchanting the minds of the <s>gopīs</s>,

children.text: paraṃ dhāma paraṃ rūpaṃ dvibhujaṃ gokuleśvaram ||86||
children.translated_text: the supreme abode, the supreme form, two-armed, the Lord of <s>Gokula</s>. ||86||
One should meditate upon the delight of the cowherd-women — the sole cause of that which is beyond the <s>guṇas</s> —
most beautiful, ever-fresh, pure, the dark-complexioned abode, enchanting, ||87||
lustrous like a row of fresh rain-clouds, with beautiful earrings,
whose touch is as blissful as a blooming blue lotus, bestowing happiness. ||88||
Smooth like crushed collyrium, of dark enchantment,
with lustrous, dark, curly tresses, entirely fragrant. ||89||
Above that, on the right side at the time [of dressing], a dark crest-jewel enchanting [the eye],
brilliant with various colors, adorned with radiant peacock-tail feathers. ||90||
Adorned with a beautiful <s>mandāra</s> flower and a graceful cow-tail ornament at the crest — a charming embellishment,
sometimes decorated with a crown made of a row of large leaves. ||91||
Sometimes adorned with a diadem of many jewels and rubies,
framed by swaying locks of hair, His face shining like ten million moons. ||92||
With a <s>kastūrī</s> (musk) <s>tilaka</s> mark, shining, adorned with beautiful <s>gorocanā</s> (saffron paste),
His eyes are lustrous like dark blue lotuses, long and wide-petalled. ||93||
With dancing brow-creepers, a smile, and sidelong glances,
with an elegantly raised nose of surpassing beauty, supremely enchanting. ||94||
The pearl-luster at the tip of His nose charms the three worlds,
with lower lips of <s>sindūra</s>-red hue, lustrous and supremely enchanting. ||95||
With earrings of various colors, gleaming, of golden <s>makara</s> (crocodile) shape,
their clusters of rays shining on His beautiful cheeks like mirrors. ||96||
His ears adorned with lotuses, beautiful <s>mandāra</s> flowers, and <s>makara</s>-shaped crest ornaments,
His chest bears the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark and the <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel, His throat resplendent with pearl necklaces. ||97||
Gleaming with divine rubies mixed beautifully with gold,
with bracelets and armlets on His hands, His waist adorned with tinkling bells. ||98||
His blessed feet are splendid with beautiful anklets of sweet sound,
anointed with <s>karpūra</s> (camphor), <s>aguru</s> (aloe), <s>kastūrī</s> (musk), and <s>candana</s> (sandalwood) and the like. ||99||
His divine limbs painted with mixed <s>gorocanā</s> (saffron paste) and other pigments,
His lustrous yellow garment shining, making people sway [in ecstasy]. ||100||
With a deep navel-lotus, a line of hair like a bowing garland,
with well-rounded knees, with lotus-feet that are enchanting. ||101||
His hands and feet adorned with the marks of flag, thunderbolt, goad, and lotus,
the rays of His crescent-moon-like nails being the sole cause of the full <s>Brahman</s>. ||102||

children.text: kecid vadanti tasyāṃśaṃ brahma cid-rūpam advayam |
children.translated_text: Some say that <s>Brahman</s>, the non-dual consciousness-form, is His partial manifestation;
the wise declare that <s>Mahā-Viṣṇu</s> is a tenth part of Him. ||103||

children.text: yogīndraiḥ sanakādyaiś ca tad eva hṛdi cintyate |
children.translated_text: The foremost <s>yogīs</s> such as <s>Sanaka</s> and others meditate upon Him alone in their hearts —
standing in triple-bend (<s>tri-bhaṅga</s>) pose, gracefully constituted as the essence of all creation, ||104||
with His neck slightly tilted, surpassing the beauty of tens of millions of <s>Kandarpas</s> (Cupids),
with a shining golden earring touching His beautiful cheek resting on His left shoulder. ||105||
With a smile accompanied by sidelong glances, more beautiful than ten million <s>Manmathas</s> (Cupids),
with His flute placed upon His pursed lower lip, producing sweet melodious sounds, ||106||
enchanting the three worlds, immersed in the ocean of nectar of <s>prema</s> (divine love).
Śrī <s>Pārvatī</s> said:
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is the supreme cause, known as <s>Govinda</s>, the great abode — ||107||
the Lord of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, eternal, the sole cause of that which is beyond the <s>guṇas</s> —

children.text: tat tad rahasya-māhātmyaṃ kim āścaryaṃ ca sundaram ||108||
children.translated_text: what is the wondrous and beautiful secret glory of that? ||108||

children.text: tad brūhi devadeveśa śrotum icchāmy ahaṃ prabho |
children.translated_text: Tell me that, O Lord of the lords of gods! I wish to hear, O Master!
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
The greatness of the moonbeam-rays from His toenails cannot be fathomed — ||109||

children.text: tan-māhātmyaṃ kiyad devi procyate tvaṃ mudā śṛṇu |
children.translated_text: how much of His greatness can be told, O <s>Devī</s>? Listen joyfully!
In the infinite tens of millions of <s>brahmāṇḍas</s> (cosmic eggs), in the infinite rising of the three <s>guṇas</s>, ||110||
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s> are fractional parts of His ten-millionth portion,
engaged in creation, maintenance, and the rest — they exist as His glories. ||111||
Ten-millionth fractional portions of His form, [appearing as] embodiments of <s>Kandarpa</s> (Cupid),
create the enchantment of the world, situated within their respective cosmic eggs. ||112||
The all-pervading Lord is a ten-millionth part of the splendor emanating from His body,
and the suns are rays that are ten-millionth parts of His effulgence. ||113||
By the rays of His own body, which are the nectar of supreme bliss,
of the form of supreme fragrance and consciousness, the sole causes of that which is beyond the <s>guṇas</s> — ||114||
the <s>jīvas</s> (individual souls), who are of the nature of rays, live as ten-millionth parts of His portion,
their radiance being that of the moon-like jewels of His pair of lotus-feet's nails. ||115||
They declare that even the cause of the full <s>Brahman</s> is difficult to reach through the <s>Vedas</s>;
a ten-millionth part of the fragrance of His portion enchants the entire universe. ||116||
The various fragrances of flowers and the like arise from the touch of Him;

children.text: tat-priyā prakṛtis tv ādyā rādhikā kṛṣṇa-vallabhā ||117||
children.translated_text: His beloved is the primordial <s>Prakṛti</s> (nature), <s>Rādhikā</s>, the beloved of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. ||117||
<s>Durgā</s> and others, possessed of the three <s>guṇas</s>, are ten-millionth fractional parts of Her;
from the touch of the dust of Her feet, tens of millions of <s>Viṣṇus</s> arise. ||118||
By the touch of Her lotus feet, you are blessed, O fair-faced one!

Thus ends the Glories of Śrī <s>Vṛndāvana</s> from the <s>Padma-purāṇa</s>.
As stated in the <s>Bṛhad-gautamīya</s>:

children.text:
devī kṛṣṇamayī proktā rādhikā para-devatā |
sarva-lakṣmī-mayī sarva-kāntiḥ sammohinī parā || iti |
children.translated_text:
'The <s>Devī</s> is declared to be of the nature of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; <s>Rādhikā</s> is the supreme deity.
She is the embodiment of all <s>Lakṣmīs</s>, all beauty, the supreme enchantress.' Thus.
Likewise, from the <s>Matsya</s> and <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇas]:
In <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, [She is] <s>Viśālākṣī</s>; in <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Purī), <s>Vimalā</s>;

children.text: rukmiṇī dvāravatyāṃ tu rādhā vṛndāvane vane ||
children.translated_text: in <s>Dvāravatī</s> (Dvārakā), <s>Rukmiṇī</s>; and in the forest of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, <s>Rādhā</s>.
Now the <s>Puruṣa-bodhinī Śruti</s> (the Śruti that reveals the Supreme Person)

Śrī Śrī <s>Rādhā-Govinda</s> are victorious!
First section (<s>prapāṭhaka</s>).

children.text:
oṃ atha suṣuptau rāmaḥ subodham ādhāya iva kiṃ me devi kvāsau kṛṣṇaḥ, yo'yaṃ
mama bhrāteti | tasya kānti-cchāye brūhīti |
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ</s>. Then, in deep sleep, <s>Rāma</s>, having established clear awareness, [asked]: "O <s>Devī</s>, where is that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, who is my brother?" Tell me of His splendor and shadow.'

children.text:
sā vaiṣṇavy uvāca-rāma ! śṛṇu | bhūr bhuvaḥ svar mahaḥ janas tapaḥ satyam atalaṃ
vitalaṃ sutalaṃ rasātalaṃ talātalaṃ mahātalaṃ pātālam eva pañcāśat-koṭi-yojana-
bahulaṃ svarṇāṇḍaṃ brahmāṇḍam iti | ananta-koṭi-brahmāṇḍānām upari kāraṇa-
jalopari mahā-viṣṇor nitya-sthalaṃ vaikuṇṭham |
children.translated_text: The <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> (goddess devoted to Viṣṇu) said: '<s>Rāma</s>, listen! <s>Bhūḥ</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, <s>Svaḥ</s>, <s>Mahaḥ</s>, <s>Janaḥ</s>, <s>Tapaḥ</s>, <s>Satyam</s>; <s>Atala</s>, <s>Vitala</s>, <s>Sutala</s>, <s>Rasātala</s>, <s>Talātala</s>, <s>Mahātala</s>, <s>Pātāla</s> — this golden cosmic egg (<s>brahmāṇḍa</s>) extending fifty <s>koṭi</s> (five hundred million) <s>yojanas</s>. Above the infinite tens of millions of <s>brahmāṇḍas</s>, above the causal waters, is <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, the eternal abode of <s>Mahā-Viṣṇu</s>.'
He asks: 'How [does it exist] unsupported in the void?'

children.text:
sāpy uktā-padmāsanāsīnaḥ kṛṣṇa-dhyāna-parāyaṇaḥ śeṣa-devo'sti | tasyānanta-
roma-kūpeṣu ananta-koṭi-brahmāṇḍāni ananta-koṭi-kāraṇa-jalāni | tasya
mastakopari sahasrāśramitā phaṇāni | phaṇopari rudra-lokaṃ śiva-vaikuṇṭham iti
daśa-koṭi-yojana-vistīrṇaṃ rudra-lokam | tad upari viṣṇulokaṃ, sapta-koṭi-yojana-
vistīrṇaṃ viṣṇu-lokam | trad-upari sudarśana-cakraṃ tri-koṭi-yojana-vistīrṇaṃ, tad-
upari gokulākhyaṃ mathurā-maṇḍalaṃ sudhā-maya-samudreṇāveṣṭitam iti |
children.translated_text: She replied: 'Seated in the lotus posture, devoted to the meditation of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, is <s>Śeṣa-deva</s>. In His infinite hair-pores are infinite tens of millions of <s>brahmāṇḍas</s> and infinite tens of millions of causal waters. Upon His head are a thousand hoods. Above the hoods is <s>Rudra-loka</s>, [also called] <s>Śiva-Vaikuṇṭha</s>, extending ten <s>koṭi</s> (one hundred million) <s>yojanas</s>. Above that is <s>Viṣṇu-loka</s>, extending seven <s>koṭi</s> (seventy million) <s>yojanas</s>. Above that is the <s>Sudarśana-cakra</s> (discus), extending three <s>koṭi</s> (thirty million) <s>yojanas</s>. Above that is [the realm] called <s>Gokula</s>, the <s>Mathurā-maṇḍala</s>, surrounded by an ocean of nectar.'

children.text:
tatrāṣṭa-dala-keśara-madhye maṇimaya-saptāvaraṇakaṃ kiṃ rūpaṃ sthānaṃ, kiṃ
padmaṃ kiṃ yantraḥ kiṃ sevakāḥ kim āvaraṇāḥ ity ukte sāpy uktā-gokulākhye
mathurā-maṇḍale vṛndāvana-madhye sahasra-dala-padma-madhye kalpa-taror mūle
aṣṭa-dala-keśare govindo'pi śyāmaḥ pītāmbaro dvibhujo mayūra-piccha-śiro veṇu-
vetra-hasto nirguṇaḥ saguṇo nirākāraḥ sākāro nirīhaḥ saceṣṭo virājate iti |

dve pārśve candrāvalī rādhā ceti yasyāṃśena lakṣmī-durgādikā śaktir iti paścime
sammukhe lalitā, vāyavye śyāmalā, uttare śrīmati, aiśanyāṃ haripriyā, pūrve
viśākhā, cāgnau śraddhā, yāmyāṃ padmā nairṛtyāṃ bhadrā | ṣoḍaśa-dalāgre
candrāvalī, tad-vāme citrarekhā, tat-pārśve śrī-śaśirekhā, tat-pārśve kṛṣṇapriyā,
tat-pārśve kṛṣṇa-vallabhā, tat-pārśve candrāvatī, tat-pārśve manoharā, tat-pārśve
yogānandā, tat-pārśve parānandā, tat-pārśve premānandā citra-karā, tat-pārśve
madana-sundarī nandā, tat-pārśve satyānandā, tat-pārśve candrā, tat-pārśve
kiśorīvallabhā, karuṇā, kuśalā evaṃ vividhā gopyaḥ kṛṣṇa-sevāṃ kurvantīti veda-
vacanaṃ bhavatīti veda-vacanaṃ bhavati |

mānasa-pūjayā japena dhyānena kīrtanena stuti-mānasena sarveṇa nitya-sthalaṃ
prāpnoti nānyeneti nānyeneti |

sāpy uktā-tasya bāhye śata-dala-patreṣu yoga-pīṭheṣu rāma-krīḍānuraktā gopyas
tiṣṭhanti | *** | etac caturdvāraṃ lakṣa-sūrya-samujjvalam | tatra samākīṛṇaḥ | tatra
prathamāvaraṇe paścime saṃmukhe svarṇa-maṇḍape gopa-kanyā | dvitīye
śrīdāmādiḥ | tṛtīye kiṅkiṇy-ādiḥ | caturthe lavaṅgādiḥ | pañcame kalpataror mūle
uṣā-sahito'niruddho'pi | ṣaṣṭhe devāḥ | saptame rakta-varṇo viṣṇur iti dvārapālam
| etad bāhye rādhā-kuṇḍam | tatra snātvā rādhāṅgaṃ bhavati, īśvarasya darśana-
yogyaṃ bhavati | tatra snātvā nārada īśvarasya nitya-sthala-samīpa-yogyo bhavati
| rādhā-kṛṣṇayor ekāsane eka-buddhir ekaṃ mana ekaṃ jñānam eka ātmā eka-
padmaikākṛtir ekaṃ brahmatayāsanaṃ hema-muralīṃ vādayan hema-svarūpām
anurāga-saṃvalitāṃ kalpa-taror mūle surabhi-vidyām arakṣita-vimalāśrur iva
paramā siddhā sāttvikā śuddhā sāttvikī guṇātīta-sneha-bhāva-rahitā | ataeva
dvayor na bhedaḥ kāla-māyā-guṇātītaṃ syāt |

tad eva spaṣṭayati atheti | athānantaraṃ maṅgale vā | atra śrī-vṛndāvana-madhye
ṛg-yajuḥ-sāma-svarūpaṃ rūpātmako ma-kāraḥ | yajur-ātmaka u-kāraḥ | śrī-rāma-
rasātmako'pi a-kāraḥ | śrī-kṛṣṇo'rdhamātrātmako'pi yaśodā iva bidnuḥ para-
brahma-saccidānanda-rādhā-kṛṣṇayoḥ paraspara-sukhābhilāṣa-rasāsvādana iva tat
saccidānandāmṛtaṃ kathyate | etal-lakṣaṇaṃ yat praṇavaṃ brahma-viṣṇuṃ
śivātmakaṃ svecchākhya-jñāna-śakti-niṣṭhaṃ kāyika-vācika-mānasika-bhāvaṃ
sattva-rajas-tamaḥ-svarūpaṃ satya-tretā-dvāparānugītaṃ turīyaṃ gokula-mathurā-
dvārakāṇāṃ turīyam eva tad divyaṃ vṛndāvanam iti puraivoktaṃ sarva-
sampradāyānugataṃ trayam |

dvādaśa-vanāni | kālindyāḥ paścime sapta-vanāni pūrve pañca-vanāni | uttare tu
guhyam astīti | mahā-vanaṃ gokulākhyaṃ mathurā madhuvanam iti | khadiravanaṃ
bhāṇḍīravanaṃ nandīśvara-vanaṃ nandanānanda-khaṇḍeva vanaṃ palāśāśoka-
vanaṃ ketadruma-bhadravana-śeṣa-śāyi-krīḍā-vana utsava-vanāny eteṣu caturaś
caturviṃśa vanāni nānā-līlayā nitya-sthalāni kṛṣṇaḥ krīḍati |

tasya vasanta-ṛtu-sevitaṃ nandādy-upavana-yuktam | tatra duḥkhaṃ nāsti, sukhaṃ
nāsti, jarā nāsti, maraṇaṃ nāsti, krodhaṃ nāsti | tatra purṇānanda-mayaḥ śrī-
kaiśoraḥ kṛṣṇaḥ śikhaṇḍa-dala-lambita-triyugma-guñjāvataṃsa-maṇimaya-kirīṭī-
śiro gorocanā-tilakaḥ karṇayor makara-kuṇḍale vanya-sragvī mālatī-dāma-bhūṣita-
śarīraḥ kare kaṅkaṇaḥ keyūraṃ kaṭyāṃ kiṅkiṇī-pītāmbara-dharo gambhīra-
nābhi-kamalaḥ suvṛtta-nāsā-yugalo dhvaja-vajrādi-cihnita-pāda-padmas tad-
aṃśāṃśena koṭi-mahā-viṣṇur iti | evaṃ-rūpaṃ kṛṣṇa-candraṃ cintayen nityaśaḥ
sudhīr iti |

tasya ādyā prakṛtiḥ rādhikā nityā nirguṇā sarvālaṅkāra-śobhitā prasannā aneka-
lāvaṇya-sundarī | evaṃ bhūtasya siddhi-mahimnā sukha-sindhur aśonotpanna iti
mānasa-pūjayā japena dhyānena kīrtanena stuti-mānasena sarveṇa nitya-sthalaṃ
prāpnotīti nānyeneti nānyeneti veda-vacanaṃ bhavatīti veda-vacanaṃ bhavatīti veda-
vacanaṃ bhavatīti |

atha puruṣottamasyāniśaṃ turīyaṃ sākṣād brahma | yatra parama-saṃnyāsa-
svarūpaḥ kṛṣṇa-nyagrodhaḥ kalpa-pādapaḥ | yatra lakṣmīr jāmbavatī-rādhikā-
vimalā-candrāvalī-sarasvatī-lalitādibhir iti sākṣād brahma-svarūpo jagannāthaḥ |
ahaṃ subhadrāśeṣāṃśo jyotīrūpaḥ sudarśano bhaktaś ca | evaṃ brahma pañcadhā
vibhūtir yatra mathurā-gokula-dvārakā-vaikuṇṭha-purī-śvetadvīpa-purī-rāmapurī
| etāḥ devatās tiṣṭhanti | yatra surasā-pātāla-gaṅgā-śveta-gaṅgā-rohiṇī-kuṇḍam
amṛta-kuṇḍam ity ādi nānāpurī | yatrānnaṃ siddhānnaṃ brahma-sparśād doṣa-
rahitaṃ śūdrādi-saṃskārāpekṣā-rahitam | yatra śrī-jagannāthasya yogyam ity arthaḥ
| anya-varṇodīrita-nānābhyāsī sīdati mantraḥ | annapāt te'nnasya iti mantraḥ |
annādyāya vyūhadhvaṃ somo rājāya magaman sa me sukhaṃ pramāyaṃ tejasā ca
balena ca ity anena mantraḥ | viśva-karmaṇe svāhā iti mantreśāyojyo raso'mṛtaṃ
brahme bhūr bhuvaḥ svar om | pṛthvī te pātrandho'pidhānaṃ brāhmaṇasya mukhe
amitaṃ amṛtaṃ juhomi svāhā | ity anena mantreṇa anna-brahmeti śrutir iti vaikalpaṃ
muktir ucyate |

yatrānnaṃ brahma paramaṃ pavitraṃ śānto rasaḥ kaivalyaṃ muktiḥ siddhā bhūr
buddhir hi tattvam ity ādi | yatra bhārgavī yamunā samudram amṛta-mayaṃ vāso
vṛndāvanāni nīla-parvato govardhanaṃ | siṃhāsanaṃ yoga-pīṭha-prāsāda-maṇi-
maṇḍapaṃ vimalādi-ṣoḍaśa-caṇḍikā gopī | yatra samudra-tīre niraṃśakā
māghano'ṣṭedaṃ | yatra nṛsiṃhādayo devatā āvaraṇāni | yatra na jarā na mṛtyur
na kālo na bhaṅgo na yamo na vivādo na hiṃsā na bhrāntir na svapna evaṃ līlā-
kāma-bharā svavinodārthaṃ bhaktāḥ sotkaṇṭhitāḥ | asyāṃ krīḍati kṛṣṇaḥ |

mānasa-pūjayā japena dhyānena kīrtanena stuti-mānasena sarveṇa nitya-sthalaṃ
prāpnotīti nānyeneti nānyeneti veda-vacanaṃ bhavatīti veda-vacanaṃ bhavatīti veda-
vacanaṃ bhavatīti |
tat sukhaṃ nityam icchantī vapuṣā vacasā dhiyā ||2||
sa yathā gokule sākṣād vrajendra-suta īryate |
tasya kāntā tathā sākṣād vṛṣabhānu-sutā smṛtā ||3||
tadā tathaiva kurvatī tenaiva saha dīvyati ||4||
mauna-mudrāṃ dhṛte kṛṣṇe vraje'smin prakaṭaṃ gate |
svayā tan-maudrayā yuktā tat pūrvaṃ prakaṭaṃ gatā ||5||
atrāpi śrūyate kācit kathā paurātanī śubhā |
yad iyaṃ karuṇā yasyās tatra kiñcin na durghaṭam ||7||
sākṣyaṃ dātuṃ brāhmaṇasya svapadābhyāṃ yato gataḥ ||8||
kartuṃ na kartuṃ tat kartuṃ samartho harir īśvaraḥ |
yathā haris tathā seyaṃ tat-priyā parameśvarī ||9||
rūpa-dvārā vraje tasminn idānīṃ prakaṭaṃ gataḥ ||14||
śīghraṃ yāsyāmi tatrāhaṃ nocitātra sthitir mama |
nāmnā gadādharaḥ khyāto mad-rūpaḥ paṇḍitaḥ sudhīḥ ||15||

children.translated_text: by the wise pair of beloved disciples of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Gadādhara</s>. //17//
Having served again and again along the way, the supreme goddess was brought.
When my mistress <s>Rādhā</s> comes to the left side of <s>Govinda</s>,
then indeed His special beauty increases. //18//
The authority for this [is found] in the <s>Śrī Govinda-līlāmṛta</s> (13.32) —
When <s>Rādhā</s> is in His company, then He is <s>Madana-mohana</s> (the enchanter of Cupid);
otherwise, though He enchants the entire universe, He Himself is enchanted by <s>Madana</s> (Cupid).
And in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>, 'therein He shone exceedingly with them' (10.33.6).
Her beauty, sweetness, noble character, and the like —

children.text: darśanād eva jñātavyaṃ tasmān nātra vilikhyate ||19||
children.translated_text: are to be known from direct seeing alone; therefore they are not written here. //19//

children.text:
yathā rādhā tathā viṣṇos tasyāḥ kuṇḍaṃ priyaṃ tathā |
sarva-gopīṣu saivaikā viṣṇor atyanta-vallabhā || iti pādmoktāt |
children.translated_text:
As is <s>Rādhā</s>, so is [she to] <s>Viṣṇu</s>; as [dear as] she [is to Him], so is her pond (<s>kuṇḍa</s>) dear [to Him].
Among all the <s>gopīs</s>, she alone is the most intensely beloved of <s>Viṣṇu</s>. — Thus stated in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>.

children.text: sattvaṃ tattvaṃ paratvaṃ ca tattva-trayam ahaṃ kila |
children.translated_text: Being (<s>sattva</s>), reality (<s>tattva</s>), and supremacy (<s>paratva</s>) — these three principles am I indeed.
She who is the embodiment of these three principles — that <s>Rādhikā</s> is my beloved.
I am beyond <s>Prakṛti</s> (material nature), and she too is the embodiment of my power (<s>śakti</s>).
Thus, from the words of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> in the <s>Bṛhad-Gautamīya</s>.
Like <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, she is the abode of eternal beauty, cleverness, and other qualities,
the manifestress of the assemblies of <s>gopīs</s>, the assemblies of chief queens, and the assemblies of <s>Lakṣmīs</s>.

children.text:
sadaiva madhyālakṣaṇākrāntā, tathā kamalāṣṭa-dala-bhāgbhiḥ arva-sakhī-varga-
mukhyābhiḥ parameṣṭābhiḥ śrī-lalitādy-aṣṭa-sakhībhiḥ saha virājamānā śrī-
rādhikaiva śrī-vṛndāvaneśvarī mahārājñī, yathā bṛhad-gautamīye-
children.translated_text: She is ever characterized as <s>madhyā</s> (the middle heroine), and together with the chief among all groups of <s>sakhīs</s> (companions) — the supreme eight <s>sakhīs</s> beginning with <s>Śrī Lalitā</s>, like the eight petals of the lotus of <s>Kamalā</s> — <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> alone is the supreme queen, the empress of <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>. As in the <s>Bṛhad-Gautamīya</s> —

children.text:
devī kṛṣṇa-mayī proktā rādhikā para-devatā |
sarva-lakṣmī-mayī sarva-kāntiḥ saṃmohinī parā || iti |
children.translated_text:
The goddess, proclaimed as <s>Kṛṣṇa-mayī</s> (pervaded by <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), <s>Rādhikā</s> is the supreme deity.
She is the embodiment of all <s>Lakṣmīs</s>, all beauty, the supreme enchantress. — Thus.
As [stated] in both the <s>Mātsya</s> and <s>Skānda</s> [Purāṇas] —

children.text:
vārāṇasyāṃ viśālākṣī vimalā puruṣottame |
rukmiṇī dvāravatyāṃ ca rādhā vṛndāvane vane || iti |
children.translated_text:
In <s>Vārāṇasī</s>, [she is] <s>Viśālākṣī</s>; in <s>Puruṣottama</s> (Jagannātha Purī), <s>Vimalā</s>;
<s>Rukmiṇī</s> in <s>Dvāravatī</s>; and <s>Rādhā</s> in the forest of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. — Thus.

children.text:
śrī-vṛndāvaneśvarī rādhikā | tasyām eva parmotkarṣa-parākāṣṭhāyā darśitatvāt
| śrī-prīti-sandarbhe ca-tat prema-vaiśiṣṭyaṃ tad eva mukhyam iti | prema-
vaiśiṣṭyaṃ yathā śrīmad-ujjvale (5.98)-
children.translated_text: <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> is the queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. Because in her alone the utmost pinnacle of excellence is shown. And in the <s>Śrī Prīti-sandarbha</s> [it is said]: 'The distinctive nature of that <s>prema</s> (love) — that alone is the chief.' The distinctive nature of <s>prema</s>, as [stated] in the <s>Śrīmad Ujjvala[-nīlamaṇi]</s> (5.98) —

children.text: kartuṃ śarma kṣaṇikam api me sādhyam ujjhaty aśeṣaṃ
children.translated_text: She who, in order to create even a moment's happiness for me, abandons everything [for herself],

children.text: cittotsaṅge na bhajati mayā datta-khedāpy asūyām |
children.translated_text: who, though given sorrow by me, does not entertain envy in the courtyard of her heart,
and who, upon hearing even a false fragment of news about my suffering, is torn apart within —
<s>Rādhā</s> reigns supreme among all beautiful-eyed women by this excellent quality.

children.text:
śrī-bhāgavate ca (10.30.28)-
anayārādhito nūnaṃ bhagavān harir īśvaraḥ | iti |
children.translated_text:
And in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> (10.30.28) —
'By this one, surely, the Lord <s>Hari</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s> <s>Īśvara</s>, has been worshipped.' Thus.

children.text: yāṃ gopīm anayat kṛṣṇo vihāyānyāḥ striyo vane |
children.translated_text: That <s>gopī</s> whom <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> took away, leaving the other women in the forest —

children.text: sā ca mene tadātmānaṃ variṣṭhaṃ sarva-yoṣitām || (10.30.36)
children.translated_text: she considered herself the best of all women. (10.30.36)

children.text:
tāpanībhyaś ca (2.12)-
tāsāṃ madhye gāndharvā śreṣṭhā iti ca |
children.translated_text:
And from the <s>Tāpanī</s> texts (2.12) —
'Among them, <s>Gāndharvā</s> (i.e. <s>Rādhā</s>) is the foremost.' And so on.

children.text:
kevalaṃ yo bhajed bhakto mādhavaṃ rādhikāṃ vinā |
mādhavo naiva tuṣṭaḥ syāt sādhanaṃ tad vṛthā bhavet || iti |
children.translated_text:
A devotee who worships <s>Mādhava</s> alone, without <s>Rādhikā</s> —
<s>Mādhava</s> would never be pleased [with him]; that spiritual practice (<s>sādhana</s>) would be in vain. — Thus.
Likewise, in the <s>Dāna-keli-kaumudī</s> (77) —

children.text:
nāndīmukhī: sahi citte suṇāhi imāe bundāe gadua bhaabadī biṇṇattā "hanta
joesari, bundābaṇa-rajje ahisiñcajjau rāhī | (sakhi citre śṛṇu anayā vṛndayā gatvā
bhagavatī vijñaptā "hanta yogeśvari, vṛndāvana-rājye abhiṣicyatāṃ rādhā |")
children.translated_text: <s>Nāndīmukhī</s>: 'O friend, listen carefully! By this <s>Vṛndā</s>, having gone [to <s>Yogeśvarī</s>], the goddess was informed: "O <s>Yogeśvarī</s>, let <s>Rādhā</s> be consecrated as the queen of the kingdom of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>!"'

children.text:
mattaṇḍa-mahisīe bhaṇidaṃ bhaabadi, aṇadikka-maṇijjaṃ tumha-sāsaṇaṃ ṇiccidaṃ
kkhu amhehiṃ sire gahīdaṃ, kintu kahiṃ mahiṭṭhā esā bacchā rāhī, kahiṃ bā
solaha-kohamettabitthiṇṇaṃ edaṃ bundābaṇa-rajjaṃ tti ṇa suṭṭhu pasīdai me hiaam
| (tataḥ kaniṣṭhayā mārtaṇḍa-mahiṣyā chāyayā bhaṇitaṃ bhagavati
anatikramaṇīyaṃ yuṣmat-śāsanaṃ niścitaṃ khalu asmābhiḥ śirasi gṛhītaṃ kintu kva
mahiṣṭhā eṣā rādhā kva vā ṣoḍaśa-krośa-mātra-vistīrṇam idaṃ vṛndāvana-
rājyam iti | na suṣṭhu prasīdati me hṛdayaṃ | tena sarva-brahmāṇḍādhipatya
evābhiṣicyatām iti bhāvaḥ |)
children.translated_text: Then the youngest queen of <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s> (the Sun), <s>Chāyā</s>, said: 'O goddess, your command is certainly not to be transgressed — we have accepted it upon our heads. But where is this great queen <s>Rādhā</s>, and where is this kingdom of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, extending merely sixteen <s>krośas</s>? — therefore my heart is not fully satisfied.' (The purport being: let her be consecrated as queen of all the universes instead.)
(In Sanskrit:) O friend of the same class, listen well —
Of the sacred traditions, sacrifices, holy places, mantras, austerities, heaven, all the celestial beings,

children.text: siddhīnāṃ mahatāṃ dvayor api tayoś cicchakti-vaikuṇṭhayoḥ |
children.translated_text: of the <s>siddhis</s> (supernatural powers), of the two great ones — <s>Cit-śakti</s> (consciousness-potency) and <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> —

children.text: vīryaṃ yat prathate tato'pi gahanaṃ śrī-māthure maṇḍale
children.translated_text: the power that spreads forth — even more profoundly than that, in the sacred <s>Māthura</s> region,

children.text: dīvyat tatra tato'pi tundilataraṃ vṛndāvane sundari ||
children.translated_text: it shines; and even more swellingly than there, in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, O beautiful one!
Moreover, <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> is in the <s>madhyā</s> (middle) stage — as in the <s>Ujjvala[-nīlamaṇi]</s> (5.42) —

children.text:
prāyaḥ sarva-rasotkarṣo madhyāyām eva yujyate |
yad asyāṃ vartate vyaktā maugdhya-prāgalbhyayor yutiḥ || iti |
children.translated_text:
The summit of all <s>rasas</s> is generally fitting only in the <s>madhyā</s> [heroine],
because in her there manifestly exists the combination of artless innocence (<s>maugdhya</s>) and bold confidence (<s>prāgalbhya</s>). — Thus.
And thus (in <s>Narahari Sarakāra</s>'s <s>Rādhikāṣṭaka</s>, 6) —

children.text: bhaktiṃ na kṛṣṇa-caraṇe na karomi cārtiṃ
children.translated_text: I do not offer devotion at the feet of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, nor [do I experience] anguish;
[but] by the daring of a particle of the dust of <s>Rādhā</s>'s lotus feet,
that [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] who knows the distinctive nature of the fall of her sidelong glance
will, by divine fortune, bestow upon me the mentality of a servant.

children.text:
punaḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-sandarbhe (289) ca--vṛndāvane śrī-rādhikāyām eva svayaṃ-
lakṣmītvam | ataeva satīṣv anyāsv api mukhyābhiprāyeṇaiva tasyā eva
vṛndāvanādhipatyena nāma-grahaṇam |
children.translated_text: Again, in the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha</s> (289) — In <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, in <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> alone resides the nature of being <s>Svayam-Lakṣmī</s> (the original goddess of fortune). Therefore, even among the other chaste women, it is primarily with reference to her alone that the name [<s>Lakṣmī</s>] is used, by virtue of her sovereignty over <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.
And thus in the <s>Śrī Laghu-gaṇoddeśa</s> (135) —
Among the beautiful-browed cowherd women, <s>Rādhā</s> is the foremost, the queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.
Her friends — <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and others — are well-renowned.
And thus in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>, in the <s>Kārttika-māhātmya</s> (5.77.39), in the dialogue of <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Nārada</s> —

children.text:
vṛndāvanādhipatyaṃ ca dattaṃ tasyai pratyuṣyatā |
kṛṣṇenānyatra devī tu rādhā vṛndāvane vane || iti |
children.translated_text:
Sovereignty over <s>Vṛndāvana</s> was given to her when [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>] departed at dawn.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [went] elsewhere, but the goddess <s>Rādhā</s> [remains] in the forest of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. — Thus.

children.text:
anyatra sādhāraṇa-deśe devy-evādhikāriṇī śrī-vṛndāvanābhidha-vane śrī-
rādhikaivety arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: The meaning is: elsewhere, in ordinary places, the goddess (<s>Devī</s>) alone has authority; [but] in the forest called <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>, <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> alone [has authority].
Now in the <s>Śrī Ūrdhvāmnāya</s> —
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Now I shall declare the auspicious mantras of <s>Rādhikā</s>,
by the mere knowledge of which one would bring under one's sway the Lord of <s>Vraja</s>. //1//

children.text: kāmo ramā rādhikā ca ṇetā pāvaka-vallabhā |
children.translated_text: <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Ramā</s>, <s>Rādhikā</s>, the guide, the beloved of <s>Pāvaka</s> (Fire) —
[this is] the great eight-syllabled mantra, the bestower of omniscience. //2//

children.text: agastyo munir etasya chandas tu jagatī smṛtam |
children.translated_text: <s>Agastya</s> is the sage of this [mantra]; the meter is remembered as <s>Jagatī</s>;
the deity is declared to be the beautiful <s>Rādhikā</s>, the supreme goddess. //3//

children.text: māyā-bījaṃ parā śaktiḥ svāhā śaktir udīritā |
children.translated_text: The <s>Māyā</s>-seed is the supreme power (<s>parā śakti</s>); <s>Svāhā</s> is declared as the power;
the pin (<s>kīlaka</s>) is called the <s>Kāma</s>-seed, through the differentiation of six long vowels. //4//
With the <s>Śrī</s>-seed, one should perform the six-limbed [ritual] for the accomplishment of all purposes.
I shall now declare her meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), which brings pleasure to <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. //5//
She who stands in the midst of an <s>aśoka</s> grove, beautiful in every limb,
a cowherd woman of sixteen years, with full, high breasts, //6//
her right hand clasping <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s neck, clinging to Him,
with her left hand twirling a lotus — the beautiful-eyed one, //7//
wearing blue garments, with a body [radiant] like lightning-struck gold,
standing on a jeweled platform in the beautiful shade of the tryst-tree (<s>saṅketa-vaṭa</s>), //8//
attended at the back by a pair of confidential maidservants (<s>ceṭikā</s>),
devoted to mutual kissing, conversation, and embrace, //9//
with a face [beautiful as] a thousand full moons, with a lovely smile —
one should meditate on the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> in this manner, O great goddess! //10//
From the fourteenth of the bright half to the eighth of the dark half — the procedure of reciting one hundred thousand [mantras] is a ten-day practice.

children.text: lakṣa-mātraṃ japen mantraṃ śubhe deśe susaṃyutaḥ |
children.translated_text: One should recite the mantra one hundred thousand times, well-concentrated, in an auspicious place —
at <s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s>, or at the trysting-place, on the glorious <s>Govardhana</s> hill, //11//
or at <s>Mānasa-Gaṅgā</s>, or on the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
or in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, in a great bower, within a <s>mādhavī</s>-vine pavilion. //12//
In <s>Vaiśākha</s>, <s>Kārttika</s>, or in the month of <s>Agrahāyaṇa</s> (<s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>),
indeed, every time is auspicious for the preliminary practices (<s>puraścaryā</s>) such as recitation and the like. //13//

children.text: campakai rakta-padamair vā daśāṃśaṃ juhūyāt tataḥ |
children.translated_text: One should then offer a tenth [of the recitations] as <s>homa</s> (fire-oblation) with <s>campaka</s> [flowers] or red lotuses,
in a fire-pit prepared according to injunction, smeared with three [types of] honey, O great goddess! //14//
With <s>bilva</s> leaves or <s>kiṃśuka</s> [flowers], or with sugar, sesame, and clarified butter —

children.text: tat-tat-kāmena hotavyaṃ tais tair dravyair vidhānataḥ ||15||
children.translated_text: according to one's particular desire, the oblation should be offered with the respective substances, according to the prescribed rules. //15//
For one desiring a kingdom, the oblation should be offered with lotus-seeds and milk-pudding (<s>pāyasa</s>);
for one desiring knowledge, with the flowers of the <s>Brahma</s>-tree. //16//
For one desiring <s>Lakṣmī</s> (wealth), especially with sesame and clarified butter;

children.text: stambhanārthī ca juhuyāt kiṃśukaiś campakais tathā ||17||
children.translated_text: and one desiring immobilization (<s>stambhana</s>) should offer with <s>kiṃśuka</s> and <s>campaka</s> [flowers]. //17//

children.text: vaśyārthī juhuyād devi drākṣayā sitayā punaḥ |
children.translated_text: One desiring subjugation (<s>vaśya</s>) should offer, O goddess, with grapes and white [sugar] again;
for driving away (<s>uccāṭana</s>), with <s>ketakī</s> (screwpine) leaves; in all cases, with sesame and clarified butter. //18//
For one desiring prosperity (<s>bhūti</s>), the oblation should be offered with honey and clarified butter.
Thus, the practitioner whose mantra is perfected should accomplish all that is desired. //19//
Especially by this [mantra], one would certainly attain the power to bring <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> under one's sway.

children.text: yo na jānāti rādhāyā mantraṃ sarvārtha-sādhakam ||20||
children.translated_text: One who does not know the mantra of <s>Rādhā</s>, the accomplisher of all purposes — //20//
even if he recites the <s>Gopāla</s> [mantra] ten million times, it does not grant him success.
Therefore, one should propitiate the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> according to the prescribed method. //21//
The Hymn of 108 Names of <s>Rādhikā</s>
Now I shall declare the 108 names,

children.text: yasya saṃkīrtanād eva śrī-kṛṣṇaṃ vaśayed dhruvam ||1||
children.translated_text: by the mere chanting of which one would certainly bring <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> under one's sway. //1//
<s>Rādhikā</s>, the beautiful one, the <s>gopī</s>, she who brings about union with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>,
the playful-eyed one, the deer-eyed one, <s>Gāndharvī</s>, the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, //2//
she who holds a <s>vīṇā</s>, the smiling-faced one, she whose abode is a red <s>aśoka</s> creeper,
she who roams <s>Govardhana</s>, the hidden one, she whose cowherd-dress is enchanting, //3//
the rival of <s>Candrāvalī</s>, the mirror-faced one, the one skilled in arts (<s>kalāvatī</s>),
the compassionate one, the detached one, the youthful one, she who captivates the heart, //4//
the beloved of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the friend of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, she who delights in reversed love-play,
the skilled one, she who delights in love-making, the moon-faced one, she of beautiful form, //5//
the squinting-eyed one, the beloved of <s>Hari</s>, <s>Mahā-Lakṣmī</s>, she who delights in sport,
she who abides at the tryst-tree, the desirable one and the amorous one, //6//
the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, <s>Rādhā</s>, the adolescent, the creeper-companion of <s>Lalitā</s>,
lightning-vine, golden-hued, maiden, she who dresses artlessly, //7//
<s>Keśinī</s>, the friend of <s>Keśava</s>, she who sells only butter,
sixteen-years-old, complete in arts, the paramour, she who consorts with her paramour, //8//
the joyful one, the showering one, the heroic one, steady-and-unsteady, she who holds the earth,
she who is in the bloom of youth, she who dwells in the forest, the sweet one, she of sweet form, //9//
she who resides in <s>Vṛṣabhānupura</s>, skilled in the play of jealous pride (<s>māna-līlā</s>),
she of the toll-collection play (<s>dāna-līlā</s>), the giver of gifts, the staff-bearing one, she of raised eyebrows, //10//
the full-breasted one, the sweet-faced one, she of <s>bimba</s>-fruit lips, she of the fifth note (<s>pañcama-svara</s>),
skilled in music, the one to be served, she who brings <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> under [her] sway, //11//
the deliverer, the enchantress, the bashful one, she whose play and character are the ornament [of all],

children.text: gopālī dadhi-vikretrī prauḍhā mugdhā ca madhyakā ||12||
children.translated_text: the cowherd woman, the yogurt-seller, the mature one, the artless one, and the <s>madhyā</s> (middle heroine), //12//
she whose husband is under her control (<s>svādhīnapatikā</s>), the slighted one (<s>khaṇḍitā</s>), she who goes on a tryst (<s>abhisārikā</s>),
the connoisseur, the juicy one, the <s>rasa</s>-worthy one, the sole treasury of <s>rasa-śāstra</s>, //13//
the protectress, the caressing one, the modest one, the longing one, the jewel among women,
the many-formed one, the beautiful-formed one, the gracious one, the great-minded one, //14//
she who walks like a swan, the intoxicated one, the counselor, the queen of mantras,
she who is served by the king of mantras alone, the sole bestower of the <s>siddhi</s> of the king of mantras, //15//
she who is the fruit of the eighteen-syllabled [mantra], she who is served by the eight-syllabled [mantra].

children.text: ity etad rādhikā devyā nāmnām aṣṭottaraṃ śatam ||16||
children.translated_text: This is the [hymn of] 108 names of the goddess <s>Rādhikā</s>. //16//
One should chant [it] upon rising in the morning, for the attainment of the power to bring <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> under one's sway.
By the utterance of each single name, <s>Keśava</s> comes under [one's] sway. //17//

children.text: vadane caiva kaṇṭhe ca bāhvor urasi codare |
children.translated_text: On the face, on the throat, on the two arms, on the chest, on the belly,

children.text: pādayoś ca krameṇārṇān nyasen mantrodbhavān pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: and on the feet — in sequence, one should place the syllables born of the mantra, separately.

children.text:
klīṃ śrīṃ rādhikāyai svāhā | asya śrī-rādhikā-mantrasyāgastya-ṛṣir jagatī
chandaḥ | śrī-rādhikā parameśvarī devatā klīṃ bījaṃ svāhā śaktiḥ klīṃ śrīṃ
kīlakaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇavaśyartha-jape viniyogaḥ | agastya-ṛṣaye namaḥ (śirasi) | jagatī-
chandase namaḥ (mukhe) | rādhikā-devatāyai namaḥ (hṛdaye) | klīṃ bījāya namaḥ
(guhye) | śrīṃ svāhā-śaktaye namaḥ (pādayoḥ) | klīṃ śrīṃ kīlakāya namaḥ
(sarvāṅgebhyaḥ) | klīṃ aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | klīṃ tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ | klīṃ
madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ | klīṃ anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ | klīṃ kaniṣṭhābhyāṃ
namaḥ | klīṃ śrī-rādhikāyai svāhā kara-tala-pṛṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | klīṃ hṛdayāya
namaḥ | śrīṃ śirase svāhā | rādhikāyai svāhā śikhāyai vaṣaṭ | klīṃ kavacāya hūṃ
