| śrīṃ rādhikāyai svāhā astrāya phaṭ |
children.translated_text: <s>Klīṃ Śrīṃ Rādhikāyai Svāhā</s>. Of this <s>Śrī Rādhikā mantra</s>, <s>Agastya</s> is the seer (<s>ṛṣi</s>), <s>Jagatī</s> is the meter (<s>chandas</s>), <s>Śrī Rādhikā Parameśvarī</s> is the deity, <s>Klīṃ</s> is the seed (<s>bīja</s>), <s>Svāhā</s> is the power (<s>śakti</s>), <s>Klīṃ Śrīṃ</s> is the pin (<s>kīlaka</s>), the application (<s>viniyoga</s>) is in recitation for bringing <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> under devotional control. Obeisance to <s>Agastya Ṛṣi</s> (on the head). Obeisance to <s>Jagatī</s> meter (on the mouth). Obeisance to <s>Rādhikā</s> deity (on the heart). Obeisance to <s>Klīṃ</s> seed (on the secret parts). Obeisance to <s>Śrīṃ Svāhā</s> power (on the feet). Obeisance to <s>Klīṃ Śrīṃ</s> pin (on all limbs). <s>Klīṃ</s> — obeisance to the two thumbs. <s>Klīṃ</s> — obeisance to the two index fingers. <s>Klīṃ</s> — obeisance to the two middle fingers. <s>Klīṃ</s> — obeisance to the two ring fingers. <s>Klīṃ</s> — obeisance to the two little fingers. <s>Klīṃ Śrī Rādhikāyai Svāhā</s> — obeisance to the palms and backs of the hands. <s>Klīṃ</s> — obeisance to the heart. <s>Śrīṃ</s> — <s>Svāhā</s> to the head. <s>Rādhikāyai Svāhā</s> — <s>Vaṣaṭ</s> to the top-knot. <s>Klīṃ</s> — <s>Hūṃ</s> to the armor. <s>Śrīṃ Rādhikāyai Svāhā</s> — <s>Phaṭ</s> to the weapon.

children.text:
dhyātvā japet | lakṣa-mātraṃ puraścaraṇam | kalau catur-lakṣaṃ japtvā ca
kuśalībhavet |
children.translated_text: Having meditated, one should recite. One hundred thousand [repetitions] is the preliminary observance (<s>puraścaraṇa</s>). In the <s>Kali</s> age, having recited four hundred thousand, one becomes perfected.

children.text:
śrīṃ rādhikāyai vidmahe klīṃ vṛṣabhānujāyai dhīmahi tan no gopī pracodayāt |
priyā gāyatryā brahmā ṛṣir gāyatrī chandaḥ śrī-rādhikā devatā śrī-kṛṣṇa-prītaye
jape viniyogaḥ | śrī-śrī-rādhikāyai vidmahe aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | klīṃ
vṛṣabhānujāyai dhīmahi tarjanībhyāṃ svāhā | tan no gopī pracodayāt
madhyamābhyāṃ vaṣaṭ | śrīṃ rādhikāyai vidmahe anāmikābhyāṃ huṃ | klīṃ
vṛṣabhānujāyai dhīmahi kaniṣṭhābhyāṃ vaṣaṭ | tan no gopī pracodayāt kara-tala-
kara-pṛṣṭhābhyāṃ phaṭ | evaṃ hṛdayādiṣv api |
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīṃ Rādhikāyai vidmahe Klīṃ Vṛṣabhānujāyai dhīmahi tan no Gopī pracodayāt</s>. Of the Beloved's <s>Gāyatrī</s>, <s>Brahmā</s> is the seer, <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the meter, <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> is the deity, the application is in recitation for the pleasure of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. <s>Śrī Śrī Rādhikāyai vidmahe</s> — obeisance to the thumbs. <s>Klīṃ Vṛṣabhānujāyai dhīmahi</s> — <s>Svāhā</s> to the index fingers. <s>Tan no Gopī pracodayāt</s> — <s>Vaṣaṭ</s> to the middle fingers. <s>Śrīṃ Rādhikāyai vidmahe</s> — <s>Hūṃ</s> to the ring fingers. <s>Klīṃ Vṛṣabhānujāyai dhīmahi</s> — <s>Vaṣaṭ</s> to the little fingers. <s>Tan no Gopī pracodayāt</s> — <s>Phaṭ</s> to the palms and backs of the hands. Similarly for the heart and the rest.
Now, the meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>):
One who is in the center of the solar disc, holding a pen and book,
one should meditate three times daily on <s>Rādhikeśvarī</s>, accompanied by <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>.

children.text:
athāṣṭādaśākṣara-mahārāja-mantra-prayogaḥ | oṃ asya śrī-aṣṭādaśākṣara-śrī-
rādhikā-mantrasya saṃmohana-ṛṣir anuṣṭup-chandaḥ śrī-rādhā devatā svāhā
śaktiḥ klīṃ kīlakaṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa-prīty-arthe jape viniyogaḥ | saṃmohana-ṛṣaye namaḥ
(śirasi) | anuṣṭup-chandase namaḥ (mukhe) | śrī-rādhā devatāyai namaḥ
(hṛdaye) | rāṃ rādhike kavacāya huṃ | kṛṣṇa-vallabhe śikhāyai vaṣaṭ | gāyatrī
sarvāṅge | śrī-rādhikāyai vidmahe kṛṣṇa-vallabhāyai dhīmahi tan no gopī
pracodayāt |
children.translated_text: Now, the procedure for the eighteen-syllable great royal <s>mantra</s>. <s>Oṃ</s> — of this <s>Śrī</s> eighteen-syllable <s>Śrī Rādhikā mantra</s>, <s>Saṃmohana</s> (Enchantment) is the seer, <s>Anuṣṭup</s> is the meter, <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> is the deity, <s>Svāhā</s> is the power, <s>Klīṃ</s> is the pin, the application is in recitation for the pleasure of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>. Obeisance to <s>Saṃmohana Ṛṣi</s> (on the head). Obeisance to <s>Anuṣṭup</s> meter (on the mouth). Obeisance to <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> deity (on the heart). <s>Rāṃ Rādhike</s> — <s>Hūṃ</s> to the armor. <s>Kṛṣṇa-Vallabhe</s> — <s>Vaṣaṭ</s> to the top-knot. <s>Gāyatrī</s> [applied] to all limbs. <s>Śrī Rādhikāyai vidmahe Kṛṣṇa-Vallabhāyai dhīmahi tan no Gopī pracodayāt</s>.

children.text:
atha aṅga-nyāsaḥ | śrīṃ aṅguṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | rādhikāyai tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ
| vidmahe madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ | kṛṣṇa-vallabhāyai anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ |
dhīmahi kaniṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | tan no gopī pracodayāt kara-tala-kara-
pṛṣṭhikābhyāṃ namaḥ | śrīṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ | rādhikāyai śirase svāhā | vidmahe
kavacāya hūṃ | kṛṣṇa-vallabhāyai dhīmahi netra-trayāya vauṣaṭ | tan no gopī
pracodayāt astrāya phaṭ |
children.translated_text: Now the <s>aṅga-nyāsa</s> (limb-placement): <s>Śrīṃ</s> — obeisance to the thumbs. <s>Rādhikāyai</s> — obeisance to the index fingers. <s>Vidmahe</s> — obeisance to the middle fingers. <s>Kṛṣṇa-Vallabhāyai</s> — obeisance to the ring fingers. <s>Dhīmahi</s> — obeisance to the little fingers. <s>Tan no Gopī pracodayāt</s> — obeisance to the palms and backs of the hands. <s>Śrīṃ</s> — obeisance to the heart. <s>Rādhikāyai</s> — <s>Svāhā</s> to the head. <s>Vidmahe</s> — <s>Hūṃ</s> to the armor. <s>Kṛṣṇa-Vallabhāyai dhīmahi</s> — <s>Vauṣaṭ</s> to the three eyes. <s>Tan no Gopī pracodayāt</s> — <s>Phaṭ</s> to the weapon.
Now, the meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>):
With the radiance of heated gold, with curled dark hair bound in a crown,
with a face like the autumn moon, with beautiful eyes like dancing <s>cakorī</s> birds,
with beauty in every limb, adorned with all ornaments,
wearing blue garments, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s beloved adolescent girl — I take refuge [in Her].

children.text:
hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ rāṃ rādhikāyai kṛṣṇa-vallabhāyai gopyai svāhā | japa-niyamaṃ
lakṣa-mātram | puraścaraṇaṃ kalau caturguṇam | sākṣātkārāya bhaved ity arthaḥ
| māyā-bījam antaraṅgā-bahiraṅgā-cic-chakti-svarūpam | lakṣmī-bījaṃ para-
brahmānanda-sarva-lakṣmī-sarva-śakti-svarūpam | kāma-bījaṃ sākṣān-manmatha-
manmatha-līlā-vilāsa-śrī-kṛṣṇa-svarūpam | ra-kāraḥ śukla-bhāskara-rūpaḥ | ā-
kāraḥ samastaiśvarya-rūpaḥ | binduḥ samasta-mādhurya-rūpaḥ | kalā samasta-
saṃyoga-rūpaḥ | tatra-
children.translated_text: <s>Hrīṃ Śrīṃ Klīṃ Rāṃ Rādhikāyai Kṛṣṇa-Vallabhāyai Gopyai Svāhā</s>. The rule for recitation is one hundred thousand [repetitions]. In the <s>Kali</s> age, the <s>puraścaraṇa</s> is fourfold. The meaning is: for direct realization. The <s>Māyā</s>-seed (<s>Hrīṃ</s>) is the form of the inner, outer, and spiritual (<s>cit</s>) potencies. The <s>Lakṣmī</s>-seed (<s>Śrīṃ</s>) is the form of the bliss of the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, all fortune, and all powers. The <s>Kāma</s>-seed (<s>Klīṃ</s>) is the very form of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the enchanter of the enchanter (<s>Manmatha-Manmatha</s>), in His pastimes and sports. The letter <s>ra</s> has the form of the bright sun. The letter <s>ā</s> has the form of all sovereignty. The <s>bindu</s> (dot) has the form of all sweetness. The <s>kalā</s> (crescent) has the form of all union. Therein:
The <s>kalā</s> is eternal union; the <s>bindu</s> is considered sweetness;
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>'s own sovereignty [is indicated by] the letter <s>ra</s>, the bright sun.

children.text:
kiṃ ca, prāṇāyama-vidhiḥ-ekenāpūrayed vāme caturbhiḥ | kumbhayed atha | īḍādi-
kramato mantrī tato dvābhyāṃ virecayet |
children.translated_text: Moreover, the method of <s>prāṇāyāma</s>: one should fill [the breath] through the left [nostril] with one [count], retain (<s>kumbhaka</s>) with four; following the order of <s>iḍā</s> and the like, the <s>mantra</s>-practitioner should then exhale with two [counts].

children.text:
atha śrī-rādhikāyāḥ priyatama-śrī-pañcākṣarī-mantra-vidhānaṃ pūrvavat |
atha śrī-gopeśvarī-sādhanam
children.translated_text:
Now, the procedure of <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>'s most beloved five-syllable <s>mantra</s>, as before.
Now, the <s>sādhana</s> of <s>Śrī Gopeśvarī</s>.
Now I shall describe in particular the <s>sādhana</s> of <s>Gopeśvarī</s>:

children.text: rākāyāṃ pūrṇa-candre tu sāyam ārabhya yatnataḥ ||1||
children.translated_text: On the full-moon night (<s>rākā</s>), when the full moon [is visible], beginning from evening, with effort. //1//
Having completed the daily duties, recitation, <s>homa</s>, and the like,
then, when the cold-rayed [moon] has gone to mid-heaven, in a beautiful disc — //2//
below, one should place a wide vessel, of silver or the like;

children.text: tan-madhye pūrayet toyaṃ yāmunaṃ gāṅgam eva vā ||3||
children.translated_text: in the middle of that, one should fill it with water from the <s>Yamunā</s> or the <s>Gaṅgā</s>. //3//
With the <s>Mātṛkā</s> [alphabet] twice, ascending and descending;
or else, in a pure [reservoir] such as <s>Puṣkara</s> and the like, with sacred water, //4//
with a well-composed mind, one should behold the complete lunar disc
reflected [in the water], having become very steady, and visualize it as the <s>pīṭha</s> (seat). //5//

children.text:
dig-bandhaṃ vidhinā kṛtvā vighnān utsārayet sudhīḥ |
pīṭha-nyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryāt sampūrṇe candra-maṇḍale ||6||[*ENDNOTE #11]

children.translated_text: <s>Prakṛti</s>, and the tortoise, and the nectar-ocean, the great vortex,
and the jeweled lamp, and the divine wish-fulfilling gem house, //7//

Having ritually bound the directions, the wise one should dispel obstacles;
then one should perform the <s>pīṭha-nyāsa</s> (seat-installation) on the complete lunar disc. //6//
the <s>Pārijāta</s> [tree], at its base a spacious jeweled altar,
a jeweled throne, in the four directions cowherd maidens well-adorned, //8//
and young deer, and beautiful jeweled staffs,

children.text: dharmaṃ jñānaṃ ca vairāgyam aiśvaryaṃ cāṃsakoruṣu ||9||
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> (virtue), <s>Jñāna</s> (knowledge), <s>Vairāgya</s> (renunciation), and <s>Aiśvarya</s> (sovereignty) on the shoulders and thighs, //9//

children.text: adharmādīn nyased vaktre vāma-pārśve ca nābhitaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Adharma</s> (non-virtue) and the like should be placed on the face, and on the left side from the navel,
and on the right side, having visualized divine <s>gopī</s> forms, //10//
and the bulb of bliss (<s>ānanda-maya</s>), and the stem of consciousness (<s>caitanya</s>-form),
and the all-encompassing lotus, and the leaves of <s>prakṛti</s>-form, //11//
and the filaments called reflection (<s>vicāra</s>), and the pericarp made of the <s>Mātṛkā</s> [alphabet],
and the discs of fire, sun, and moon — one should place [them] one above the other. //12//

children.text: sattvaṃ rajas tamaś caiva nairguṇyāñcāpi vinyaset |
children.translated_text: <s>Sattva</s>, <s>rajas</s>, and <s>tamas</s>, and also the quality-transcendent (<s>nairguṇya</s>), one should place;
the self (<s>ātman</s>), the inner self (<s>antarātman</s>), and the Supreme Self (<s>Paramātman</s>) also. //13//
<s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Rati</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Prīti</s>, <s>Kīrti</s>, and <s>Śānti</s>,

children.text: tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭis tathā caitā vinyaset pīṭha-madhyataḥ ||14||
children.translated_text: <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, and also these — one should place in the middle of the <s>pīṭha</s>. //14//
In the center, one should place the glorious city of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>;
within the appointed bower there, the divine <s>Aśoka</s> vine in the forest. //15//
One should meditate on Her, wearing blue garments, beautiful in every limb,
resplendent with all ornaments, accompanied by the son of <s>Nanda</s>. //16//
Then, having prepared the general [offering] to the half, with pure sacred water,
[one should offer] foot-water (<s>pādya</s>), welcome-water (<s>arghya</s>), sipping-water (<s>ācamanīya</s>), honey-drink (<s>madhuparka</s>), and sprinkling. //17//
Having installed [Her] with the root <s>mantra</s>, one should prepare the sprinkling-offering (<s>vikṣepārghya</s>);
with sugar-water or with cooked milk. //18//
Into that middle, one should place jasmine, cloves, saffron, and the like,
cardamom seeds, camphor — and consecrate [them] with the root <s>mantra</s>. //19//
In the receptacle, on the food, on the milk, [one should place] the discs of fire, sun, and moon;
having worshiped with sandal paste and the like, then one should invoke the Beloved. //20//
Taking up a handful of flowers combined with <s>tulasī</s> and flowers,
carrying the radiance-formed daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> through the nostril, //21//
having brought [Her] within the worship-seat, one should worship with the <s>upacāras</s> (ritual offerings);
foot-water and the like, then one should further invoke [Her] with the respective <s>mudrās</s> (gestures). //22//
With the nectar placed in the special <s>arghya</s>, with the root <s>mantra</s>, sevenfold;
fragrance, flowers, incense, lamp, and food offering, //23//
one should prepare with supreme devotion, and likewise for <s>Śrī Nanda</s>'s son;
with the eighteen-syllable <s>mantra</s>, the <s>upacāras</s> separately each. //24//

children.text: kīrtiṃ ca vṛṣbhānuṃ ca yaśodāṃ nandam eva ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Kīrti</s> and <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> and <s>Yaśodā</s> and <s>Nanda</s> also,

children.text: anyāś ca mātṛkā gopīs tayoḥ pṛṣṭhe prapūjayet ||25||
children.translated_text: and other mother-<s>gopīs</s> — one should worship behind the two [Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa]. //25//
One should worship with devotion the tryst-bower (<s>saṅketa</s>), and the city of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>,
and <s>Varasānu</s>, and then one should worship <s>Nandī-Śaila</s> (Nanda's hill). //26//
Having worshiped <s>Nandagrāma</s>, and the <s>Aśoka</s>-forest vine,
having worshiped <s>Pīyūṣa-Vāpikā</s> (the Nectar Pool), one should worship <s>Māna-Sarovara</s> (the Lake of Honor). //27//
Then, having worshiped <s>Bhānusara</s>, one should worship the flower garden;

children.text: rādhāyāḥ paritaḥ paścāt pūjayed aṣṭa tāḥ sakhīḥ ||28||
children.translated_text: after [worshiping] <s>Rādhā</s>'s surroundings, one should worship the eight <s>sakhīs</s>: //28//

children.text: rādhā kṛṣṇā ca lalitā viśākhā cañcalā tathā |
children.translated_text: <s>Rādhā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, <s>Cañcalā</s>,

children.text: citrā mitrā ca muditā ity etāḥ pūjayet kramāt ||29||
children.translated_text: <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Mitrā</s>, and <s>Muditā</s> — one should worship these in order. //29//

children.text: tad-bāhye pūjayed gopīṃ viśālāṃ subhagāṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: Outside of them, one should worship <s>Gopī Viśālā</s>, <s>Subhagā</s>,
<s>Raṅgavidyā</s>, <s>Raṅgadevī</s>, <s>Gāndharvī</s>, <s>Gāyikā</s>, //30//

children.text: sundarīṃ subhagāṃ śobhāṃ paurṇamāsīṃ ca candrikām |
children.translated_text: <s>Sundarī</s>, <s>Subhagā</s>, <s>Śobhā</s>, <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, <s>Candrikā</s>,

children.text: vīrāṃ vṛndāṃ ca viditāṃ vanditāṃ nanditāṃ tathā ||31||
children.translated_text: <s>Vīrā</s>, <s>Vṛndā</s>, <s>Viditā</s>, <s>Vanditā</s>, <s>Nanditā</s> likewise. //31//
Outside of them, one should carefully worship the <s>gopikās</s> who bestow all happiness:

children.text: candrā candraprabhā kāmyā mādhurī madhurā priyā ||32||
children.translated_text: <s>Candrā</s>, <s>Candraprabhā</s>, <s>Kāmyā</s>, <s>Mādhurī</s>, <s>Madhurā</s>, <s>Priyā</s>, //32//
<s>Preyasī</s>, <s>Preṣitā</s>, <s>Preṣyā</s>, <s>Modinī</s>, <s>Śyāmalā</s>, <s>Amalā</s>,

children.text: śyāmā kāmā ramā rāmā ramaṇī ratna-mañjarī ||33||
children.translated_text: <s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>Kāmā</s>, <s>Ramā</s>, <s>Rāmā</s>, <s>Ramaṇī</s>, <s>Ratna-Mañjarī</s>, //33//
<s>Śṛṅgāra-Mañjarī</s>, <s>Śīlā</s>, <s>Ratnaśālā</s>, <s>Rasā</s>, <s>Ruṣā</s>,

children.text: raṅgiṇī māninī manyā dhīrā dhanyā dharā dhṛtiḥ ||34||
children.translated_text: <s>Raṅgiṇī</s>, <s>Māninī</s>, <s>Manyā</s>, <s>Dhīrā</s>, <s>Dhanyā</s>, <s>Dharā</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>, //34//

children.text: bhāmā suvarṇa-vallī ca ity etāḥ kramaśo yajet |
children.translated_text: <s>Bhāmā</s>, <s>Suvarṇa-Vallī</s> — these should be worshiped in order.
Outside of them, <s>Campakalatā</s>, <s>Mālatī</s>, <s>Mallikā</s>, <s>Aruṇā</s>, //35//
<s>Aśoka-Lalitā</s>, <s>Lolā</s>, <s>Mīnākṣī</s>, <s>Madanā</s>, <s>Mati</s>,

children.text: sumatiḥ supratīkā ca sukhadā kalikā kalā ||36||
children.translated_text: <s>Sumati</s>, <s>Supratīkā</s>, <s>Sukhadā</s>, <s>Kalikā</s>, <s>Kalā</s>, //36//

children.text: kādambinī kiśorī ca yugmikā yugalā yugā |
children.translated_text: <s>Kādambinī</s>, <s>Kiśorī</s>, <s>Yugmikā</s>, <s>Yugalā</s>, <s>Yugā</s>,
<s>Vallabhā</s>, <s>Vallikā</s>, <s>Velā</s>, <s>Vellinī</s>, <s>Ratna-Vallarī</s>, //37//
<s>Kamalā</s>, <s>Komalā</s>, <s>Kulyā</s>, <s>Kalyāṇī</s>, <s>Valayā</s>, <s>Valā</s>,
<s>Dharmā</s>, <s>Sudharmā</s>, <s>Sānandā</s>, <s>Sunandā</s>, <s>Sumukhā</s>, <s>Mukhā</s>, //38//
<s>Suśrī</s>, <s>Surūpā</s>, <s>Kumudā</s>, <s>Kaumudī</s>, <s>Susmitā</s>, <s>Amitā</s>,
<s>Kokilā</s>, <s>Kokilālāpā</s>, <s>Bhāvanī</s>, <s>Suprabhā</s>, <s>Prabhā</s>, //39//
<s>Madaneśī</s>, <s>Mālikā</s>, <s>Kanakā</s>, <s>Kanakāvatī</s>,
<s>Nīlā</s>, <s>Lalāmā</s>, <s>Lalanā</s>, <s>Mādhavī</s>, <s>Madhu-Vibhramā</s>, //40//

children.text: vāsantikā ca sunasā premā premavatī parā |
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsantikā</s>, <s>Sunasā</s>, <s>Premā</s>, <s>Premavatī</s>, <s>Parā</s>,
<s>Śṛṅgāriṇī</s>, <s>Śṛṅganī</s>, <s>Sukacā</s>, <s>Maṇḍanāvalī</s>. //41//
Sixty-four <s>Ramās</s> (beloved <s>gopīs</s>) should be worshiped with offerings combined with the nectar of the special <s>arghya</s>,

children.text: gandhaiḥ puṣpais tathā dhūpair dīpair naivedyakaiḥ pṛthak ||42||
children.translated_text: with fragrances, flowers, incense, lamps, and food offerings, separately each. //42//
Outside of them, one should abundantly worship the great, glorious <s>Śrīmad Vṛndāvana</s>,
<s>Govardhana</s>, the jeweled mountain, the golden mountain, the nectar mountain, //43//
<s>Indra</s> and the other [<s>lokapālas</s>], one should worship afterwards, in ascending order, the wise one.

children.text: evaṃ pūjā-vidhiṃ kṛtvā kuryād ārātrikaṃ mahat ||44||
children.translated_text: Having thus performed the worship procedure, one should perform the great <s>āratrika</s>. //44//
Then, having performed self-offering (<s>ātmārpaṇa</s>), with the dissolution <s>mudrā</s>, repeatedly,

children.text: rādhikāṃ nanda-sūnuṃ ca nije hṛdi visarjayet ||45||
children.translated_text: one should dismiss <s>Rādhikā</s> and <s>Nanda</s>'s son into one's own heart. //45//
The procedure [continues] with recitation and worship of one's chosen <s>mantra</s> until midnight.
Thus, in the <s>Śrī Ūrdhvāmnāya Mahātantra</s>, the procedure of <s>Śrīmad Gopeśvarī</s> is complete.
Now, the procedure of <s>Pañca-Bāṇeśvarī</s> (the Goddess of the Five Arrows) from the <s>Sammohana Tantra</s>:
The daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> Herself is <s>Pañca-Bāṇeśvarī</s>;
agitation (<s>saṃkṣobhaṇa</s>), melting (<s>drāvaṇa</s>), and likewise attraction (<s>ākarṣaṇa</s>), O beloved — //1//
and subjugation (<s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>) as well, and unsurpassed maddening (<s>unmādana</s>) —

children.text: ete pañca mahā-bāṇā nanda-sūnor manaḥ spṛśaḥ ||2||
children.translated_text: These are the five great arrows that touch the mind of the son of <s>Nanda</s>. ||2||
In the casting of the sidelong glance of <s>Rādhikā</s>, from the establishment of <s>Manmatha</s> (Desire),
through the fire-noose of the lord of <s>Atri</s> — the 'agitation' (<s>saṃkṣobhaṇa</s>) is described. ||3||

children.text: tad eva vāma-netrāḍhyaṃ drāvaṇaṃ nāma kīrtanam |
children.translated_text: That very [power], enriched by the left eye, is the utterance called 'melting' (<s>drāvaṇa</s>).
The 'attraction' (<s>ākarṣaṇa</s>) is the desire-seed; the 'subjugation' (<s>vaśīkaraṇa</s>) is stated. ||4||
The third of the <s>pa</s>-group [is] earth, well-adorned on the left ear;
<s>Bhṛgu</s> the creator — O <s>Maheśānī</s> (Great Goddess), the 'intoxication' (<s>unmādana</s>) is described. ||5||

children.text: oṃ namo rādhikāyai ca gopeśvaryai śuci-priyā |
children.translated_text: '<s>Oṃ</s>, salutations to <s>Rādhikā</s>, the queen of cowherds, dear to purity' —
this eighteen-syllabled <s>mantra</s> bestows all perfections. ||6||
<s>Durvāsas</s> is the seer of this [<s>mantra</s>]; the meter is declared to be <s>Anuṣṭubh</s>.

children.text: praṇavo bījam etasya svāhā śaktir udāhṛtā |
children.translated_text: The seed of this is <s>Praṇava</s> (<s>Oṃ</s>); the power is stated to be <s>svāhā</s>.
The meditation, worship, and the like of this are proclaimed as before. ||7||
In exceedingly white garments, with wide eyes,
engaged in various playful sports, together with Her beloved,
seated on a very broad jeweled throne — that young maiden,
the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> — one should always remember Her in the heart. ||8||
With three sections of the <s>mantra</s>, by double repetition, the six-limbed [<s>nyāsa</s> is performed].
Having attained this <s>vidyā</s> (knowledge), <s>Vyāsa</s> and other great sages, ||9||

children.text: brahmādyā devatāś cāpi indrādyāś ca dig-īśvarāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s> and other <s>devatās</s>, <s>Indra</s> and other lords of the directions,

children.text: nārāyaṇas tathaivāhaṃ lakṣmīḥ śeṣas tathā smaraḥ ||10||
children.translated_text: <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> Himself, and I (<s>Śiva</s>), <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s>, and <s>Smara</s> (Desire) — ||10||

children.text: anye ca sakalā devāḥ sakalaiśvaryam āpnuvan |
children.translated_text: and all other <s>devas</s> as well — [all of them] obtained complete sovereignty.

children.text: tantreṣu gopitā pūrvaṃ mayā tubhyaṃ prakāśitā ||11||
children.translated_text: [This <s>vidyā</s> was] formerly concealed in the <s>tantras</s>; by me it has been revealed to you. ||11||
It should not be given to just anyone; it should be concealed even from one's own sons.
It should be given to a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> who is devoted, virtuous, and pure of mind. ||12||
To one who is free from greed, meritorious, and devoted to faith and devotion;

children.text: anyathā siddhi-hāniḥ syāt tasmād yatnena gopayet ||13||
children.translated_text: otherwise, there would be loss of perfection — therefore one should carefully conceal it. ||13||

children.text: pāṇḍityaṃ sukavitvaṃ ca raṇe vāde jayaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: Erudition, excellent poetic skill, victory in battle and debate,
power of subjugation, sovereignty, heaven, and liberation —
[all these] are obtained without effort, O Queen of the gods — there is no doubt. ||15||
As follows —
The five [arrows] having the forms of agitation, melting, attraction, subjugation, and intoxication —
mango, <s>jambu</s>, <s>bakula</s>, <s>campaka</s>, and <s>aśoka</s> trees [are their symbols]. ||16||

children.text:
puṣpavati vasante ca-iti bījaṃ pratikrāmya ra-yutaṃ tathā mūla-mantra-lakṣa-japena
siddhiḥ syāt |
children.translated_text: 'Blossoming in spring' — thus, having traced the seed-syllable joined with '<s>ra</s>,' by chanting the root <s>mantra</s> one hundred thousand times, perfection shall arise.

Thus, in the <s>Sammohana-tantra</s>, [this is] the narration of the <s>mantra</s> of the five-arrowed sovereign <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>.
[In the <s>Ūrdhvāmnāya-tantra</s>, the practice of the five-syllabled (<s>pañcākṣarī</s>) <s>mantra</s>]
Now I shall declare <s>Rādhā</s> in Her five-syllabled form,
by the mere knowledge of which a person can bring <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> under control. ||1||
ending with the <s>rasa</s>-syllable — [this is] the <s>Rādhikā</s> <s>vidyā</s>, which grants the desired aims of devotees. ||2||
Having uttered the <s>Ramā</s>-seed (<s>Śrīṃ</s>), one should then utter '<s>Rādhike</s>'

children.text: sanako'sya ṛṣiḥ prokto jagatī cchanda īritam |
children.translated_text: <s>Sanaka</s> is declared as the seer of this; <s>Jagatī</s> is stated as the meter.
<s>Śrī Rādhā</s> is declared as the deity; the application is for the attainment of all. ||3||

children.text: dvir āvṛttyā tu mantrasya ṣaḍ-aṅga-nyāsam ācaret |
children.translated_text: By double repetition of the <s>mantra</s>, one should perform the six-limbed <s>nyāsa</s>.
One should meditate on the golden (<s>Gaurī</s>) one holding a lotus, standing on the shore of the milk-ocean. ||4||
With Her hand placed on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s neck, with a smiling lotus-face.

children.text: mūrdhni locanayor āsye hṛdaye ca pravinyaset ||5||
children.translated_text: One should place [the syllables] on the head, on the two eyes, on the mouth, and on the heart. ||5||
The five syllables, each one in order, born of the <s>mantra</s>,

children.text: mūlādhāre ramāṃ nyaset svādhiṣṭhāne ca rām iti ||6||
children.translated_text: one should place '<s>Ramā</s>' (<s>Śrīṃ</s>) at the <s>Mūlādhāra</s>, and '<s>Rāṃ</s>' at the <s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s>. ||6||

children.text: maṇipūre tṛtīyaṃ ca nyaset tūryam anāhate |
children.translated_text: The third at the <s>Maṇipūra</s>, the fourth at the <s>Anāhata</s>,

children.text: viśuddhe ca ramāṃ nyasyed ājñāyāṃ sarva-mantrakam ||7||
children.translated_text: and '<s>Ramā</s>' (<s>Śrīṃ</s>) at the <s>Viśuddha</s>, and the complete <s>mantra</s> at the <s>Ājñā</s> [<s>cakra</s>]. ||7||
One should draw a triangle joined with a point (<s>bindu</s>), then an octagon outside it,
then, having drawn a protective enclosure (<s>bhūpura</s>), one should perform the seat-worship. ||8||
At the central point, one should worship directly the supreme daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>.

children.text: trikoṇe pūjayec chyāmāṃ viśākhāṃ lalitām api ||9||
children.translated_text: In the triangle, one should worship <s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and <s>Lalitā</s>. ||9||
<s>Karpūra-mañjarī</s>, <s>Rūpa-mañjarī</s>, <s>Rasa-mañjarī</s>,
<s>Lavaṅga-mañjarī</s>, <s>Prema-mañjarī</s>, <s>Raṅga-mañjarī</s>, ||10||
<s>Ānanda-mañjarī</s>, and also <s>Rati-mañjarī</s> —
having worshipped [them] in the octagon, and the lords of the directions in the protective enclosure. ||11||
Together with the eight <s>Siddhas</s> — then one should cast a flower-offering (<s>puṣpāñjali</s>).
Having thus performed the worship, the <s>mantrin</s> should chant merely ten thousand [times]. ||12||
In the <s>mantra</s> prescribed as described, filled with the five syllables,
one should establish a lamp (<s>dīpa</s>), filled with cow-ghee. ||13||
With ten threads, one should join a wick of unbroken form.

children.text: sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ vāpi tāmraṃ kāṃsya-mayaṃ tathā ||14||
children.translated_text: A golden, silver, or copper or bronze ||14||

children.text: abhāve mārtikaṃ vāpi divyaṃ dīpaṃ prakalpayet |
children.translated_text: — or, in their absence, an earthen — divine lamp should be prepared.

children.text: sādhāraṃ sthāpayed yantraṃ kūrcikāṃ cāpi tan-mayīm ||15||
children.translated_text: One should establish the <s>yantra</s> with its support and a brush made of the same [material]. ||15||
With thread spun by a maiden, one should prepare the wick.

children.text: yāvat pañca-dinaṃ kuryād evaṃ vidhim anuttamam ||16||
children.translated_text: One should perform this supreme procedure for five days. ||16||

children.text: sarvān mano-gatān kāmān avāpnoti na saṃśayaḥ |
children.translated_text: One obtains all desires of the mind — there is no doubt.
In battle, in [worldly] affairs, in disputes, and in accomplishing purposes — ||17||

children.text: amūṃ prayogam ācarya sadyaḥ siddhim avāpnuyāt |
children.translated_text: having practiced this application, one quickly attains perfection.

children.text: anyeṣv api ca kāryeṣu kuryād evaṃ vidhiṃ naraḥ ||18||
children.translated_text: In other affairs as well, a person should perform this procedure. ||18||

children.text:
laṃ raṃ maṃ kṣaṃ vaṃ yaṃ saṃ haṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ eka-varṇam |
laṃ indrāya devādhipataye sāyudhāya sa-vāhanāya sa-śaktikāya sa-parivārāya śrī-
rādhikā-pārṣadāya namaḥ | indra-pādukāṃ pūjayāmi namas tarpayāmi namaḥ |
children.translated_text:
'<s>Laṃ Raṃ Maṃ Kṣaṃ Vaṃ Yaṃ Saṃ Haṃ Hrīṃ Śrīṃ</s>' — a single syllable.
'<s>Laṃ</s>, to <s>Indra</s>, the lord of the gods, with his weapons, with his vehicle, with his <s>śakti</s>, with his retinue, to the attendant of <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>, salutations. I worship the sandals of <s>Indra</s>. Salutations. I offer libation. Salutations.'
Thus, in the <s>Ūrdhvāmnāya</s>, the practice of the five-syllabled (<s>pañcākṣarī</s>) [<s>mantra</s>] is complete.
Therein, the <s>prāṇāyāma</s> (breath-control) —

children.text: ādāv ṛṣādi-nyāsaḥ syāt kara-śuddhis tataḥ param |
children.translated_text: First, there should be the <s>nyāsa</s> (ritual placement) of the seer and the like; then, the purification of the hands.
The <s>nyāsa</s> pervading the fingers, and indeed the <s>nyāsa</s> of the heart and the like. ||

children.text: tāla-trayaṃ ca dig-bandhaḥ prāṇāyāmas tataḥ param |
children.translated_text: The three claps, the binding of the directions, and then <s>prāṇāyāma</s>,

children.text: dhyāna-pūjā japaś caiva sarva-tantreṣv ayaṃ vidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: meditation, worship, and chanting — this is the procedure in all <s>tantras</s>. ||

children.text:
prāṇāyāmaḥ-dakṣiṇa-nāsā-puṭaṃ nirudhya vāmanāsā-puṭena caturvāraṃ pūrake,
ṣoḍaśa-vāraṃ kumbhake, dvayaṃ nāsā-puṭaṃ nirudhyāṣṭa-vāraṃ dakṣa-nāsayā
vāyuṃ recayet |
children.translated_text: <s>Prāṇāyāma</s>: blocking the right nostril, through the left nostril, four [counts] for inhalation (<s>pūraka</s>); sixteen counts for retention (<s>kumbhaka</s>); blocking both nostrils, eight counts of exhalation (<s>recaka</s>) through the right nostril.

children.text:
atha saṅkalpa-vidhiḥ - śrī-viṣṇur viṣṇur namo'dya amuka-māsi amuka-tithau
amuka-gotro'muka-dāsaḥ śrī-rādhikā-devatā amuka-mantra-siddhi-kāmo'muka-
puraścaraṇa-japam ahaṃ kariṣye | asya śrī-rādhikā-pañcākṣarī-mantrasya sanaka-
ṛṣiḥ jagatī-cchandaḥ śrī-rādhā devatā akhilāptaye viniyogaḥ | śrīṃ
aṅguṣṭābhyāṃ namaḥ | rāṃ tarjanībhyāṃ namaḥ | dhīṃ madhyamābhyāṃ namaḥ
| keṃ anāmikābhyāṃ namaḥ | śrīṃ kaniṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | śrī-rādhike śrī-kara-
tala-kara-pṛṣṭhābhyāṃ namaḥ | śrīṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ | rāṃ śirase svāhā | dhiṃ
śikhāyai vaṣaṭ | keṃ kavacāya hūṃ | śrīṃ netra-trayāya vauṣaṭ | śrīṃ rādhike śrīṃ
atrāya phaṭ | iti ṣaḍ-aṅga-nyāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: Now, the procedure of the resolution (<s>saṅkalpa</s>): '<s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, salutations. Today, in such-and-such month, on such-and-such lunar day, I, such-and-such servant of such-and-such <s>gotra</s>, desiring the perfection of such-and-such <s>mantra</s> with <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> as the deity, shall perform such-and-such preliminary chanting (<s>puraścaraṇa-japa</s>). Of this <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> five-syllabled <s>mantra</s>: the seer is <s>Sanaka</s>, the meter is <s>Jagatī</s>, the deity is <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>, the application is for the attainment of all. "<s>Śrīṃ</s>" — to the thumbs, salutations. "<s>Rāṃ</s>" — to the index fingers, salutations. "<s>Dhīṃ</s>" — to the middle fingers, salutations. "<s>Keṃ</s>" — to the ring fingers, salutations. "<s>Śrīṃ</s>" — to the little fingers, salutations. "<s>Śrī Rādhike Śrī</s>" — to the palms and backs of the hands, salutations. "<s>Śrīṃ</s>" — to the heart, salutations. "<s>Rāṃ</s>" — to the head, <s>svāhā</s>. "<s>Dhiṃ</s>" — to the topknot, <s>vaṣaṭ</s>. "<s>Keṃ</s>" — to the armor, <s>hūṃ</s>. "<s>Śrīṃ</s>" — to the three eyes, <s>vauṣaṭ</s>. "<s>Śrīṃ Rādhike Śrīṃ</s>" — to the weapon, <s>phaṭ</s>. Thus the six-limbed <s>nyāsa</s>.

children.text:
śrīṃ mūrdhni | rāṃ dakṣa-netre | dhiṃ vāma-netre | keṃ mukhe | śrīṃ hṛdaye | iti
varṇa-nyāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: "<s>Śrīṃ</s>" on the crown; "<s>Rāṃ</s>" on the right eye; "<s>Dhiṃ</s>" on the left eye; "<s>Keṃ</s>" on the mouth; "<s>Śrīṃ</s>" on the heart. Thus the syllable-placement (<s>varṇa-nyāsa</s>).

children.text:
śrīṃ caturdala-mūlādhāre | vaṃ śaṃ ṣaṃ saṃ | rāṃ ṣaḍ-dale svādhiṣṭhāne kaṃ bhaṃ
maṃ yaṃ raṃ laṃ | dhiṃ daśa-dale maṇi-pūre | ḍaṃ ḍhaṃ ṇaṃ taṃ thaṃ daṃ dhaṃ naṃ
paṃ phaṃ | keṃ dvādaśa-dale anāhate | kaṃ khaṃ gaṃ ghaṃ ṅaṃ caṃ chaṃ jaṃ jhaṃ
ñaṃ ṭaṃ ṭhaṃ | śrīṃ ṣoḍaśa-dale viśuddhe | aṃ āṃ iṃ īṃ uṃ ūṃ ṛṃ ṝṃ ṃ ṃ eṃ aiṃ
oṃ auṃ aṃ aḥ | śrī-rādhike śrī-rādhike śrī-dvidale | lakṣaṃ | ājñāyām iti ṣaṭ-
cakrātmaka-tan-nyāsaḥ |
children.translated_text: "<s>Śrīṃ</s>" at the four-petaled <s>Mūlādhāra</s> [with] <s>Vaṃ Śaṃ Ṣaṃ Saṃ</s>. "<s>Rāṃ</s>" at the six-petaled <s>Svādhiṣṭhāna</s> [with] <s>Kaṃ Bhaṃ Maṃ Yaṃ Raṃ Laṃ</s>. "<s>Dhiṃ</s>" at the ten-petaled <s>Maṇipūra</s> [with] <s>Ḍaṃ Ḍhaṃ Ṇaṃ Taṃ Thaṃ Daṃ Dhaṃ Naṃ Paṃ Phaṃ</s>. "<s>Keṃ</s>" at the twelve-petaled <s>Anāhata</s> [with] <s>Kaṃ Khaṃ Gaṃ Ghaṃ Ṅaṃ Caṃ Chaṃ Jaṃ Jhaṃ Ñaṃ Ṭaṃ Ṭhaṃ</s>. "<s>Śrīṃ</s>" at the sixteen-petaled <s>Viśuddha</s> [with the vowels] <s>Aṃ Āṃ Iṃ Īṃ Uṃ Ūṃ Ṛṃ Ṝṃ Ḷṃ Ḹṃ Eṃ Aiṃ Oṃ Auṃ Aṃ Aḥ</s>. "<s>Śrī Rādhike Śrī Rādhike Śrī</s>" at the two-petaled [<s>Ājñā</s>]; <s>Lakṣaṃ</s>; at the <s>Ājñā</s>. Thus the <s>nyāsa</s> on the six <s>cakras</s>.
The meditation —

children.text:
dhyāyet padma-karāṃ gaurīṃ kṣīra-sāgara-nīragām |
kṛṣṇa-kaṇṭhārpita-karāṃ smayamāna-mukhāmbujām || iti dhyānam |
children.translated_text:
'One should meditate on the golden one holding a lotus, standing on the shore of the milk-ocean,
with Her hand placed on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s neck, with a smiling lotus-face.' Thus the meditation.

children.text:
iti pūrvaṃ kṛtvā guru-mantra-devatānām aikyaṃ vibhāvya mantra-japaṃ kuryāt |
kṛtaitat-tan-mantra-japasya amuka-saṅkhyātmakasya daśāṃśa-homaṃ tad-daśāṃśaṃ
tarpaṇaṃ tad-daśāṃśaṃ mārjanam | tad-daśāṃśam abhiṣekam | tad-daśāṃśaṃ
brāhmaṇa-bhojana-dānam ahaṃ kariṣye | gandhākṣata-kuśodakam ādāya sarva-
nyāsa-jālaṃ vidhāya śrī-rādhikā-devyā vāma-haste ---
children.translated_text:
Having first performed thus and having contemplated the unity of the <s>guru</s>, <s>mantra</s>, and deity, one should perform the <s>mantra</s>-chanting.
'Having performed the chanting of such-and-such count of such-and-such <s>mantra</s>, I shall perform oblation (<s>homa</s>) at one-tenth of that, libation (<s>tarpaṇa</s>) at one-tenth of the oblation, sprinkling (<s>mārjana</s>) at one-tenth of the libation, ablution (<s>abhiṣeka</s>) at one-tenth of the sprinkling, and feeding of <s>brāhmaṇas</s> at one-tenth of the oblation.' Taking sandalwood-paste, unbroken rice, <s>kuśa</s>-grass, and water, and having performed the entire network of <s>nyāsa</s>, in the left hand of <s>Śrī Rādhikā-devī</s> —
'O Protectress of the most secret of secrets, accept this chanting performed by us;

children.text: siddhir bhavatu me devi prasīda śrī-rameśvarī ||
children.translated_text: may perfection arise for me, O Goddess — be pleased, O glorious <s>Rameśvarī</s>!' ||
With this <s>mantra</s>, one should offer the fruit of chanting and the like.
Now he states the practice of lamp-offering (<s>dīpa-dāna</s>) —
<s>Śiva</s> said:
Listen, O Goddess, I shall declare the auspicious procedure of lamp-offering,

children.text: yasmin kṛte bhavet siddhiḥ pañcākṣara-manor dhruvam ||1||
children.translated_text: by performing which, perfection of the five-syllabled <s>mantra</s> is certainly [attained]. ||1||
A nine-<s>yoni</s> (nine-triangle) <s>cakra</s> (diagram), adorned with a point (<s>bindu</s>) in the center,
before it, one should draw a lotus of eight petals, enchanting. ||2||

children.text:
dharaṇī-valayopetaṃ vidikṣv asra-vibhūṣitam |
lalitāyai namaḥ procya maṇḍaleśīṃ prapūjayet ||3|| (4-7)
āvāhanaṃ sthāpanaṃ ca sannidhāpanam eva ca |
children.translated_text: Invocation (<s>āvāhana</s>), establishment (<s>sthāpana</s>), making proximate (<s>sannidhāpana</s>),
and restraining (<s>sannirodana</s>) — one should perform [these] for the goddess of the <s>cakra</s>. ||8||

Equipped with an earth-enclosure (<s>bhūpura</s>), adorned with triangles in the intermediate directions.
Having said 'Salutations to <s>Lalitā</s>,' one should worship the sovereign of the <s>maṇḍala</s>. ||3|| (4-7)
Having performed [these] with the respective <s>mudrās</s>, one should cast a flower-offering.

children.text: atha dīpaṃ samānīya sauvarṇaṃ rājataṃ tathā ||9||
children.translated_text: Then, having brought a lamp — golden or silver, ||9||

children.text: tāmraṃ kāṃsyam ayaṃ cāpi mṛn-mayaṃ śubha-lakṣaṇam |
children.translated_text: or copper, bronze, iron, or earthen — with auspicious marks;
of five <s>tolas</s> weight for subjugation; of ten <s>tolas</s> for attraction; ||10||
of fifteen for enchantment; of twenty for destruction;
with twenty-five <s>tolas</s> for all auspicious purposes; ||11||
in <s>dharma</s>, wealth, pleasure, and liberation, in battle, in victory and debate —
perceiving the gravity of the purpose, [use] thirty <s>tolas</s> and upward. ||12||
Having washed with the weapon-<s>mantra</s>, one should fumigate with the root <s>mantra</s>;
one should worship with sandalwood, flowers, and the like, and consecrate with the root [<s>mantra</s>] alone. ||13||
One should fill [the lamp] with streams of cow-ghee, with the root <s>mantra</s>.
For fierce purposes, O <s>Maheśānī</s>, one should fill [it] with oil as well. ||14||
One should properly prepare [the lamp] with fragrant flowers and the like.
With a wick of sixteen <s>aṅgulas</s> (finger-widths) in measure, one should place it therein. ||15||
Of whatever material the lamp is made, the [wick-holder] too should be made of that [material].
Having prepared another lamp, on the six-pointed <s>maṇḍala</s> — ||16||
from heart [<s>mantra</s>] to weapon [<s>mantra</s>], one should worship in that <s>maṇḍala</s>.

children.text: pradīpe pūjayet tasmin svayaṃ jyotiḥ sanātanam ||17||
children.translated_text: In that lamp, one should worship the eternal Self-effulgent One. ||17||

children.text: sanātanāya svayaṃ jyotiṣe nama ity añjaliṃ kṣipet |
children.translated_text: 'Salutations to the Eternal Self-effulgent One' — one should cast an offering (<s>añjali</s>).
On the ground, one should light the lamp and worship with the prescribed services,
with sandalwood and the like — the sixteen [services]; then one should light the [main] lamp. ||18||
The wick, in left-right order, forming a pair,

children.text: akhaṇḍām eva tāṃ kuryād yāvat pañca-dināvadhi ||19||
children.translated_text: should be made unbroken for the [duration of] five days. ||19||
Made from cotton of wild cotton-plants, white, of firm form,
with thread spun by a maiden — unbroken, strong. ||20||

children.text: vāmāṃ pañcadaśaiḥ sūtrair dakṣiṇāṃ ṣoḍaśair api |
children.translated_text: The left [wick] with fifteen threads, the right with sixteen —
such a wick should indeed be made for the accomplishment of all purposes. ||21||
For subjugation, the right wick should be of eighteen threads;
the left of nineteen. For attraction, with twenty threads; ||22||
the right with one more [than the left]. For enchantment, with twenty-one;
the right with one more [than the left]. For destruction, with twenty-two. ||23||
The right always with one more [than the left] — thus one should prepare in all [cases].
For extremely urgent and grave purposes, the wick [should be] of twenty-five [threads]. ||24||
Thirty, forty, fifty, up to a hundred —
merely by the preparation of this king of lamps, all purposes are accomplished. ||25||

children.text: yad yad hṛdi sthitaṃ vāpi nālabhyaṃ bhuvana-traye |
children.translated_text: Whatever is established in the heart, or even that which is unattainable in the three worlds —
a person accomplishes the bringing under control of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in an instant. ||26||

children.text:
ante ca mahatīṃ pūjāṃ kṛtvā dīpaṃ visarjayet |
putrārthī putram āpnoti dhanārthī labhate dhanam ||27|| ity ādi |
children.translated_text: And at the end, having performed a great worship, one should dismiss the lamp. One who desires a son obtains a son; one who desires wealth obtains wealth. ||27|| — and so on.
Now he states the procedure for the offering of the twin-lamp (<s>yugala-dīpa-dāna</s>) —
<s>Śrī Sanat-kumāra</s> said:
O <s>Brahman</s>, tell me in detail the procedure for the offering of the lamp,
by the mere performance of which <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> are pleased. ||1||
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Listen, dear child, I shall tell you specifically about the lamp-offering,
the sole means for the grace of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — there is no doubt about this. ||2||

children.text: kārttike mārgaśīrṣe vā pauṣe vā māgha-māsake |
children.translated_text: In <s>Kārttika</s>, or <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, or <s>Pauṣa</s>, or <s>Māgha</s>,
or <s>Vaiśākha</s> — it should be performed, preceded by daily bathing. ||3||
Having resorted to a pure place, a perfected sacred field (<s>siddha-kṣetra</s>), charming —

children.text: nanda-grāmaṃ ca saṅketaṃ vara-sānuṃ giriṃ tathā ||4||
children.translated_text: <s>Nanda-grāma</s>, or <s>Saṅketa</s>, or the excellent hillside, the mountain, ||4||
the pure <s>Govardhana</s>, or the wonderful bank of the <s>Yamunā</s> —

children.text: eṣām anyatamaṃ sthānaṃ samāśritya vidhir bhavet ||5||
children.translated_text: having resorted to any one of these places, the ritual procedure should be [performed]. ||5||
In the forenoon, having completed one's daily duties and making a resolution (<s>saṅkalpa</s>) in the prescribed manner,
one should make a large <s>maṇḍala</s> (diagram) suitable for the lamp-offering, O sage. ||6||
Having designed a dot (<s>bindu</s>) with a square, then an eight-pointed [figure],
then making a sixteen-pointed [figure], then make a thirty-two-pointed one. ||7||
And make a large <s>maṇḍala</s> measured with sixty-four points,
and having placed the earth-diagram (<s>bhū-bimba</s>), with five colors in the prescribed manner. ||8||
In the middle of that, one should place a lamp with the sixteen-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>], O child,
of gold or silver — one should prepare the twin-self [lamp]. ||9||
If [the lamp is] to be made of clay, [it should be made] with [clay] from <s>Varasānu</s> (Barsānā),
or with [clay] from <s>Nandagrāma</s> — one should joyfully prepare the lamp. ||10||
One should prepare a lamp made of two metals, born of [those] metals;
therein one should pour a stream of ghee derived from two cows. ||11||

children.text: kṛṣṇāyāś caiva śuklāyā dhenor ājyaṃ nidhāpayet |
children.translated_text: One should place the ghee of a black cow and a white cow,
having consecrated it with the root <s>mantra</s> in the sequential and reverse order. ||12||

children.text: kṛtvā mātṛkayā cājyaṃ vartikāṃ tatra vinyaset |
children.translated_text: Having performed [the consecration] with the <s>mātṛkā</s> (alphabet) and the ghee, one should place the wick therein;

children.text: grāmotthaṃ ca tulaṃ varṇau kāryārambhe prakalpayet ||13||
children.translated_text: one should prepare cotton produced from the village, [as] the two colors, at the commencement of the rite. ||13||

children.text: sthāpayitvā ghṛte samyak karṣaṇīṃ tatra tan-mayīm |
children.translated_text: Having properly placed in the ghee a thread (<s>karṣaṇī</s>) made of the same [material],
having thus prepared the lamp, one should worship the king of <s>yantras</s> (diagrams). ||14||
With the eighteen-syllabled <s>mantra</s>, one should worship the son of <s>Nanda</s>;
with the sixteen-syllabled [<s>mantra</s>], one should worship <s>Rādhikā</s> in the prescribed manner. ||15||
At the end of the worship of all the enclosures (<s>āvaraṇas</s>), one should cast a handful of flowers;
or one may worship <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in their embodied form (<s>mūrti</s>). ||16||
Then one should light the lamp by means of another lamp;
the divine couple residing within the lamp should be worshipped with their respective <s>mantras</s>. ||17||
In the square, one should always worship <s>Lalitā</s> and <s>Viśākhā</s>,
<s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Anurādhā</s>, in the prescribed manner, with fragrant substances and flowers. ||18||

children.text: gopālī pālikā caiva dhyāna-niṣṭhā tathaiva ca |
children.translated_text: <s>Gopālī</s>, <s>Pālikā</s>, and <s>Dhyāna-niṣṭhā</s> (the meditation-devoted),

children.text: somābhā tārakā caiva śaivyā padmā ca bhadrikā ||19||
children.translated_text: <s>Somābhā</s>, <s>Tārakā</s>, and <s>Śaivyā</s>, <s>Padmā</s>, and <s>Bhadrikā</s>. ||19||
In the eight-pointed [figure], one should worship the eight with fragrant substances and flowers in the prescribed manner;

children.text: yonimudrāṃ tato vadhvā praṇamet sādaraṃ mune ||20||
children.translated_text: then, showing the <s>yoni-mudrā</s>, one should bow respectfully, O sage. ||20||
In the sixteen-pointed [figure], one should worship <s>Śyāmā</s>, <s>Mādhavī</s>, <s>Kamalā</s>,

children.text: kalāṃ candrakalāṃ candrāṃ tathā capalatāṃ punaḥ ||21||
children.translated_text: <s>Kalā</s>, <s>Candrakalā</s>, <s>Candrā</s>, and then <s>Capalatā</s>, ||21||

children.text: pramodāṃ padminīṃ pūrṇāṃ paramāṃ subhagāṃ śubhām |
children.translated_text: <s>Pramodā</s>, <s>Padminī</s>, <s>Pūrṇā</s>, <s>Paramā</s>, <s>Subhagā</s>, <s>Śubhā</s>,
<s>Capalā</s>, <s>Vipulā</s>, <s>Vāmā</s> — in order, with fragrant substances and flowers. ||22||
In the thirty-two-pointed [figure], one should worship <s>Veṇī</s>, <s>Vaśinī</s>, <s>Suprabhā</s>, <s>Prabhā</s>,
<s>Mālinī</s>, <s>Śālinī</s>, <s>Śālā</s>, <s>Viśālā</s>, <s>Kanaka-prabhā</s>, ||23||

children.text: maṇḍinīṃ maṇḍalā-mukhyāṃ jyeṣṭhāṃ śreṣṭhāṃ ca bhāminīm |
children.translated_text: <s>Maṇḍinī</s>, <s>Maṇḍalā-mukhyā</s>, <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, <s>Śreṣṭhā</s>, and <s>Bhāminī</s>,
<s>Tvaritā</s>, <s>Prārijāteśī</s>, <s>Sukalā</s>, <s>Surasā</s>, <s>Rasā</s>, ||24||
<s>Veśinī</s>, <s>Keśinī</s>, <s>Keśā</s>, <s>Sukeśā</s>, <s>Mañjaghoṣiṇī</s>,
<s>Śubhāvatī</s>, <s>Kāntimatī</s>, <s>Kāntā</s>, <s>Bhānumatī</s>, <s>Mudā</s>, ||25||
<s>Vasudhā</s> and <s>Vasudhāmā</s> — in order, with fragrant substances and flowers.
In the sixty-four-pointed [figure]: <s>Paddhī-puṣṭā</s> and <s>Poṣiṇī</s>, ||26||
<s>Kañja-prabhā</s>, <s>Kañja-hastā</s>, <s>Varṣiṇī</s>, <s>Harṣiṇī</s>, <s>Harā</s>,
<s>Hāriṇī</s>, <s>Kāriṇī</s>, <s>Dhārā</s>, <s>Dhāriṇī</s>, <s>Citra-lepinī</s>, ||27||
<s>Lalāmā</s>, <s>Lulitā</s>, <s>Lobhadā</s>, and <s>Sulocanā</s>,

children.text: rocinīṃ suruciṃ śobhāṃ śubhrāṃ śobhāvatīṃ sabhām ||28||
children.translated_text: <s>Rocinī</s>, <s>Suruci</s>, <s>Śobhā</s>, <s>Śubhrā</s>, <s>Śobhāvatī</s>, <s>Sabhā</s>, ||28||

children.text: rohitāṃ lohitāṃ līlāṃ śīlāṃ caiva saśīlikām |
children.translated_text: <s>Rohitā</s>, <s>Lohitā</s>, <s>Līlā</s>, <s>Śīlā</s>, and <s>Saśīlikā</s>,
<s>Patriṇī</s>, <s>Pallavābhāsā</s>, <s>Viśuddhā</s>, <s>Viśadā</s>, <s>Balā</s>, ||29||

children.text: sudatīṃ sumukhīṃ vyomāṃ somāṃ sāmāṃ tvarāturām |
children.translated_text: <s>Sudatī</s>, <s>Sumukhī</s>, <s>Vyomā</s>, <s>Somā</s>, <s>Sāmā</s>, <s>Tvarāturā</s>,
<s>Ratnāvalī</s>, <s>Ratnanibhā</s>, <s>Ratnadhāmā</s>, <s>Dayāvatī</s>, ||30||

children.text: prabhāvatīṃ premagāṃ ca kṣemāṃ kṣemāvatīṃ kṣamām |
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāvatī</s>, <s>Premagā</s>, and <s>Kṣemā</s>, <s>Kṣemāvatī</s>, <s>Kṣamā</s>,

children.text: mañjarīṃ khañjarīṭāṃ ca lakṣaṇāṃ ca sulakṣaṇām ||31||
children.translated_text: <s>Mañjarī</s>, <s>Khañjarīṭā</s>, and <s>Lakṣaṇā</s> and <s>Sulakṣaṇā</s>, ||31||

children.text: kāmāṃ kāmavatīṃ vīṇāṃ hīnāṃ vīṇākarāṃ talām |
children.translated_text: <s>Kāmā</s>, <s>Kāmavatī</s>, <s>Vīṇā</s>, <s>Hīnā</s>, <s>Vīṇākarā</s>, <s>Talā</s>,
<s>Triyugā</s>, <s>Śoṇacaraṇā</s>, <s>Cāriṇī</s>, <s>Cārudantinī</s>, ||32||
and <s>Vicitrabhāṣiṇī</s> — one should worship them in order,

children.text: gandhaiḥ puṣpais tathā dūpair dīpair naivedyakais tathā ||33||
children.translated_text: with fragrant substances, flowers, incense, lamps, and food offerings. ||33||
On the earth-diagram (<s>bhū-bimba</s>), one should worship the eight cowherd boys in order:
<s>Subala</s>, <s>Subāhu</s>, <s>Śrīdāma</s>, <s>Śrī Madhumaṅgala</s>,

children.text: mādhavaṃ citralekhaṃ ca śāradaṃ ca vibhāvasum ||34||
children.translated_text: <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Citralekha</s>, <s>Śārada</s>, and <s>Vibhāvasu</s>. ||34||
Then one should worship <s>Citrā</s>, the presiding goddess of the first enclosure;
in the second enclosure, one should worship <s>Vṛndā</s> and <s>Vīrā</s>. ||35||
And the presiding goddess of the third enclosure, <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, one should worship;
in the fourth enclosure, <s>Pālī</s>, the companion of <s>Śrīmad Gāndharvikā</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>). ||36||
And the presiding goddess of the fifth enclosure, <s>Śyāmalā</s>, one should worship;
and the queen of the sixth enclosure, <s>Padmā-devī</s>, one should worship. ||37||
And the presiding goddess of the seventh enclosure, the auspicious <s>Śrīmaj-jyotsnāvatī</s>;

children.text: dīpasya dakṣa-bhāge tu nandaṃ caiva yaśodikāṃ ||38||
children.translated_text: on the right side of the lamp, [one should worship] <s>Nanda</s> and <s>Yaśodā</s>; ||38||

children.text: vāme sampūjayet kīrtiṃ vṛṣabhānuṃ ca gopakam |
children.translated_text: on the left, one should worship <s>Kīrti</s> and <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, the cowherd chief.
Having [thus] worshipped the <s>maṇḍala</s>, one should cast a handful of flowers. ||39||

children.text: dīpaṃ pañca-dinaṃ vāpi kuryād daśa-dinaṃ tathā |
children.translated_text: One may maintain the lamp for five days, or for ten days,

children.text: pakṣaṃ vā rakṣayed dīpaṃ māsaṃ vāpi munīśvara ||40||
children.translated_text: or for a fortnight, or even for a month, O chief of sages. ||40||
Then, the wise person, having completed the daily rites, should dismiss the lamp;
having worshipped the king of lamps, one should cast a handful of flowers. ||41||
In the <s>Yamunā</s> or other auspicious waters, one should set the king of lamps afloat;

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā vidhiṃ sadyaḥ sarvān kāmān avāpnuyāt ||42||
children.translated_text: having thus performed the rite, one immediately obtains all desires. ||42||
One directly beholds the divine couple by the power of the king of lamps;

children.text: pūjanād eva dīpasya nāsādhyaṃ vidyate kvacit ||43||
children.translated_text: by the worship of the lamp alone, nothing is impossible anywhere. ||43||
Thus, in the <s>Sanat-kumāra-saṃhitā</s>, the procedure for the offering of the twin-lamp. Fifth chapter.
One who, enclosed by the five arrows [of Kāmadeva], chants the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Rādhikā</s>,

children.text: tasya sarvārtha-siddhiḥ syāt kṛṣṇaṃ paśyati tat-kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: shall attain the perfection of all purposes, and beholds <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in that very instant.

children.text:
hrīṃ hrīṃ klīṃ brūṃ saḥ kṛṣṇa-priye hrāṃ hrīṃ klīṃ svāhā | iti ṣoḍaśākṣaro
mantraḥ | catuḥṣaṣṭhi-yantra-dīpa-dāna-prayogam āha |
children.translated_text: '<s>Hrīṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Brūṃ Saḥ Kṛṣṇa-priye Hrāṃ Hrīṃ Klīṃ Svāhā</s>' — this is the sixteen-syllabled <s>mantra</s>. He states the application of the sixty-four-<s>yantra</s> lamp-offering.
Now the hymn: [<s>Śrī Rādhā-kṛpā-kaṭākṣa-stava-rāja</s>] (The King of Hymns to the Gracious Sidelong Glance of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>)
O You whose lotus-face is radiant, O You who delight in the pleasure-groves (<s>kuñjas</s>),
O daughter of <s>Vrajendra-Bhānu</s> (<s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>), O You who are united with the son of <s>Vrajendra</s> (the king of <s>Vraja</s>),
when will You make me here the recipient of Your gracious sidelong glance? ||1||
O You who are venerated by hosts of the greatest sages, O remover of the sorrows of the three worlds,
O You whose feet are tender, with the luster of coral sprouts and young leaves,
O You whose hands display the gestures of boon-giving and fearlessness, O abode of abundant prosperity,
when will You make me here the recipient of Your gracious sidelong glance? ||2||
O You who are seated in the bower-pavilion of <s>aśoka</s> trees and creepers,
by the shooting of the arrows from the corners of Your eyes, with coquetry and agitation,
You have perpetually brought under Your control the renowned son of <s>Nanda</s> —
when will You make me here the recipient of Your gracious sidelong glance? ||3||
O You whose gently arched eyebrows are curved in the auspicious sport of the arena of <s>Anaṅga</s> (Cupid),
O You whose facial radiance defeats the orb of millions of autumn moons,
O You whose eyes are like the wonderful and variegated young <s>cakora</s> birds moving about,
when will You make me here the recipient of Your gracious sidelong glance? ||4||
O You whose golden form blazes like lightning, gold, and <s>campaka</s> flowers,
O You who are colored by loving attachment to Your beloved, O You who are expert in the arts of amorous sport,
O You who are skilled in the exclusive, unrivaled amorous games in the kingdom of the <s>kuñjas</s> (groves),
when will You make me here the recipient of Your gracious sidelong glance? ||5||
O You whose super-intoxicated extreme youthfulness is adorned with joyful pride (<s>māna</s>),
O You whose fine breasts rival golden water-vessels [and] elephant foreheads,
O You who are an ocean of happiness filled with the powder of Your gentle smile,
when will You make me here the recipient of Your gracious sidelong glance? ||6||
O You who are adorned with limitless gestures, expressions, steadiness, diamond necklaces,
O You whose dark, playfully swaying eyes glance from the tips of those creepers,
O You who are the refuge of the swaying, rolling, meeting, delightful, innocent, and enchanting,
when will You make me here the recipient of Your gracious sidelong glance? ||7||
O You whose arm-creepers are like waves of tender lotus-fiber tendrils,
O You whose three-stranded auspicious thread gleams with the splendor of three gems,
O You whose swaying dark tresses are threaded with clusters of flowers,
when will You make me here the recipient of Your gracious sidelong glance? ||8||
O You whose conch-like neck is marked with three lines and adorned with golden necklaces,
O You who are beautiful in the midst of a collection of excellent gem-studded tinkling bells,
O You whose fine thighs rival the trunk of a lordly elephant,
when will You make me here the recipient of Your gracious sidelong glance? ||9||
O You whose flower-girdle hangs from the roundness of Your hips,
surpassing the cooing of a flock of royal swans in the assembly,
O You whose beautiful gait mocks a swaying golden creeper,
when will You make me here the recipient of Your gracious sidelong glance? ||10||
O You whose anklets jingle with the sound of many <s>mantras</s>,
O You who grant boons to the daughters of the Himalaya (<s>Pārvatī</s>), <s>Puloman</s> (<s>Śacī</s>), and <s>Viriñci</s> (<s>Sarasvatī</s>),
O You whose toenails are anointed with infinite <s>siddhis</s> (perfections) and <s>ṛddhis</s> (powers),
when will You make me here the recipient of Your gracious sidelong glance? ||11||
O You who are worshipped by <s>Padmajā</s> (Lakṣmī) [who herself is] adored throughout infinite millions of <s>Viṣṇu</s>-worlds,
O Sovereign of the three <s>Vedas</s> and <s>Bhāratī</s> (Sarasvatī)! O Sovereign of authoritative scriptures!
O Sovereign of <s>Ramā</s> (Lakṣmī)! O Sovereign of patience! O Sovereign of the joyful forest!

children.text: vrajeśvari vrajādhipe śrī rādhike namo'stu te ||12||
children.translated_text: O Sovereign of <s>Vraja</s>! O Queen of <s>Vraja</s>! O <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s>, salutations to You! ||12||
O Sovereign of sacrifice! O Sovereign of rites! O Sovereign of offerings! O Sovereign of the <s>devas</s>!
continually make people the recipients of Her gracious sidelong glance.
Then there will be the destruction of the accumulated threefold <s>karma</s>;
then there will be entry into the circle (<s>maṇḍala</s>) of the son of <s>Vrajendra</s>. ||13||
Thus, hearing this wondrous hymn, may the daughter of <s>Bhānu</s> (<s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>)

children.text: rākāyāṃ ca sitāṣṭamyāṃ daśamyāṃ ca viśuddha-dhīḥ |
children.translated_text: On the full moon, and on the eighth of the bright fortnight, on the tenth,

children.text: ekādaśyāṃ trayodaśyāṃ yaḥ paṭhet sa svayaṃ śivaḥ ||14||
children.translated_text: on the eleventh, and on the thirteenth — one who recites [this hymn] with purified mind becomes <s>Śiva</s> (auspiciousness itself). ||14||

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ kāmayate kāmaṃ taṃ tam āpnoti sādhakaḥ |
children.translated_text: Whatever desire a practitioner desires, that he obtains;
by the gracious sidelong glance of <s>Rādhā</s>, having enjoyed [all], one finally attains liberation. ||15||
Standing in the water of <s>Rādhā-kuṇḍa</s> up to the thighs, up to the navel, up to the heart, or up to the neck,

children.text: rādhā-kuṇḍa-jale sthitā yaḥ paṭhet sādhakaḥ śatam ||16||
children.translated_text: the practitioner who recites [this hymn] a hundred times — ||16||

children.text: tasya sarvārtha-siddhiḥ syād vāk-sāmarthyaṃ tathā labhet |
children.translated_text: for him there will be the perfection of all purposes, and he will obtain the power of speech;

children.text: aiśvaryaṃ ca labhet sākṣād dṛśā paśyati rādhikām ||17||
children.translated_text: he will obtain sovereignty, and with his own eyes he will behold <s>Rādhikā</s>. ||17||

children.text: tena sa tat-kṣaṇād eva tuṣṭā datte mahāvaram |
children.translated_text: By that, She, instantly pleased, grants a great boon,
by which one beholds with one's own eyes Her beloved <s>Śyāmasundara</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>). ||18||
The Lord of <s>Śrī Vraja</s> grants entry into the eternal pastimes (<s>nitya-līlā</s>);

children.text: ataḥ parataraṃ prārthyaṃ vaiṣṇavasya na vidyate ||19||
children.translated_text: beyond this, there is nothing more to be desired by a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>. ||19||
Thus, in the <s>Śrīmad Ūrdhvāmnāya</s>, the hymn of the gracious sidelong glance of <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> is complete.
Now the <s>Trailokya-vikrama kavaca</s> (Armor of the Conqueror of the Three Worlds) as stated in the <s>Saṃmohana-tantra</s> is written:
Śrī <s>Pārvatī</s> said:

children.text: yad gopitaṃ tvayā pūrvaṃ tantrādau yāmalādiṣu |
children.translated_text: That which was concealed by You previously, in the <s>Tantra</s> and in the <s>Yāmala</s> and other [texts] —
the wondrous <s>kavaca</s> (protective armor) of <s>Rādhā</s> named 'Conqueror of the Three Worlds' — ||1||

children.text: tan mahyaṃ brūhi deveśa yady ahaṃ tava vallabhā |
children.translated_text: tell that to me, O Lord of gods, if I am Your beloved —
that which directly bestows all <s>siddhis</s> (perfections) and grants the desires of practitioners. ||2||
Śrī <s>Mahādeva</s> said:
Listen, O beloved, I shall declare the <s>kavaca</s> that is rare even for the gods,

children.text: yac ca kasmaicid ākhyātuṃ gopitaṃ bhuvana-traye ||3||
children.translated_text: which is concealed in the three worlds, not to be told to anyone. ||3||
By whose grace, O <s>Devī</s>, I am the lord of all <s>siddhis</s>,

children.text: vāgīśaś ca hayagrīvo devarṣiś caiva nāradaḥ ||4||
children.translated_text: and <s>Hayagrīva</s> is the lord of speech, and the divine sage <s>Nārada</s> [is what he is] — ||4||
by whose grace <s>Viṣṇu</s> is the sustainer of the three worlds,

children.text: brahmā yasya prasādena trailokyaṃ racayet kṣaṇāt ||5||
children.translated_text: and <s>Brahmā</s>, by whose grace, creates the three worlds in an instant — ||5||
I have obtained the power of dissolution — there is no doubt about this.
The <s>kavaca</s> named 'Conqueror of the Three Worlds' is the embodied form of the <s>mantra</s>. ||6||
Listen to it, O <s>Maheśānī</s> (consort of Maheśvara), endowed with devotion and faith.
Of this <s>kavaca</s> of 'Conqueror of the Three Worlds,' the <s>ṛṣi</s> (seer) is <s>Hari</s>; ||7||
the meter is <s>anuṣṭubh</s>; and the deity is <s>Rādhikā</s>, the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>.
Its application is declared to be for the attainment of the love of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. ||8||

children.text: rādhikā pātu me śīrṣaṃ vṛṣabhānu-sutā śikhām |
children.translated_text: May <s>Rādhikā</s> protect my head; may the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> [protect] my crest;

children.text: bhālaṃ pātu sadā gopī netre govinda-vallabhā ||9||
children.translated_text: may the <s>Gopī</s> always protect my forehead; may the beloved of <s>Govinda</s> [protect] my eyes. ||9||

children.text: nāsāṃ rakṣatu ghoṣeśī vrajeśī pātu karṇayoḥ |
children.translated_text: May the Queen of <s>Ghoṣa</s> (the cowherd settlement) protect my nose; may the Queen of <s>Vraja</s> protect my ears;

children.text: gaṇḍau pātu rati-krīḍā oṣṭhau rakṣatu gopikā ||10||
children.translated_text: may She who delights in amorous play protect my cheeks; may the <s>Gopikā</s> protect my lips. ||10||

children.text: dantān rakṣatu gāndharvī jihvāṃ rakṣatu bhāminī |
children.translated_text: May <s>Gāndharvī</s> protect my teeth; may the passionate one (<s>Bhāminī</s>) protect my tongue;
may the daughter of <s>Kīrti</s> protect my neck; may <s>Haripriyā</s> (the beloved of Hari) [protect] the circle of my face. ||11||

children.text: bāhū me pātu gopeśī pādau me gopa-sundarī |
children.translated_text: May the Queen of the cowherds protect my arms; may the beautiful cowherd-woman protect my feet;
may <s>Kuñjeśī</s> (the mistress of the bowers), <s>Rādhikeśvarī</s>, always protect my right side. ||12||
May She who delights in the <s>rāsa</s>-play always protect my left side;
may She who stands at the trysting place protect my back; may She who sports in the forest [protect] my navel. ||13||
May She of fresh youth [protect] my belly; may the beauty of <s>Vraja</s> [protect] my chest;
may the bestower of <s>parakīya-rasa</s> (the sentiment of paramour love) always protect my two shoulders. ||14||
May the protectress of the cows protect my hump (upper back); may the Queen of <s>Gokula</s> [protect] all my limbs;
may the moon-faced one protect my private parts; may <s>Rādhā</s>, beautiful in all limbs, [protect me]. ||15||

children.text: mūlādhāraṃ sadā pātu śrīṃ klīṃ saubhāgya-vardhinī |
children.translated_text: May '<s>Śrīṃ Klīṃ</s>' the increaser of good fortune always protect my <s>mūlādhāra</s> [cakra];

children.text: aiṃ klīṃ śrī-rādhike svāhā svādhiṣṭhānaṃ sadāvatu ||16||
children.translated_text: may '<s>Aiṃ Klīṃ</s> Śrī <s>Rādhike svāhā</s>' always protect my <s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s> [cakra]. ||16||

children.text: klāṃ klīṃ namo rādhikāyai maṇipūraṃ sadāvatu |
children.translated_text: May '<s>Klāṃ Klīṃ</s> salutations to <s>Rādhikā</s>' always protect my <s>maṇipūra</s> [cakra];

children.text: lakṣmī māyā smaro rādhā pātu cittam anāhatam ||17||
children.translated_text: may '<s>Lakṣmī</s> <s>Māyā</s> <s>Smara</s> <s>Rādhā</s>' protect my <s>anāhata</s> (heart) [cakra]. ||17||

children.text: klāṃ klīṃ kāmakalā rādhā viśuddhaṃ sarvadāvatu |
children.translated_text: May '<s>Klāṃ Klīṃ Kāmakalā Rādhā</s>' always protect my <s>viśuddha</s> [cakra];

children.text: ājñāṃ rakṣatu rādhā me haṃsaḥ klīṃ vahni-vallabhā ||18||
children.translated_text: may <s>Rādhā</s> protect my <s>ājñā</s> [cakra] — '<s>Haṃsaḥ Klīṃ</s>, beloved of Fire.' ||18||

children.text: oṃ namo rādhikāyai svāhā sahasrāraṃ sadāvatu |
children.translated_text: May '<s>Oṃ</s> salutations to <s>Rādhikā svāhā</s>' always protect my <s>sahasrāra</s> [cakra];

children.text: aṣṭādaśākṣarī rādhā sarva-deśe tu pātu mām ||19||
children.translated_text: may the eighteen-syllabled <s>Rādhā</s> [mantra] protect me in every place. ||19||

children.text: navārṇā pātu mām ūrdhvaṃ daśārṇāvatu saṃsadi |
children.translated_text: May the nine-syllabled [mantra] protect me above; may the ten-syllabled [mantra] protect me in assemblies;
may the eleven-syllabled [mantra] protect me in gambling and in arguments and disputes. ||20||
At all times and in all places, may the twelve-syllabled [mantra] always protect me;
may the five-syllabled <s>Rādhikeśī</s> always protect me during the day. ||21||

children.text: aṣṭākṣarī ca rādhā māṃ rātrau rakṣatu sarvadā |
children.translated_text: And may the eight-syllabled <s>Rādhā</s> always protect me at night;

children.text: pūrṇā pañcadaśī rādhā pātu māṃ vraja-maṇḍale ||22||
children.translated_text: may the complete fifteen-syllabled <s>Rādhā</s> [mantra] protect me in the <s>Vraja-maṇḍala</s>. ||22||

children.text: ity evaṃ rādhikāyās te kavadaṃ kīrtitaṃ mayā |
children.translated_text: Thus this <s>kavaca</s> of <s>Rādhikā</s> has been proclaimed by me;
it is to be concealed with effort, like one's own origin, O <s>Pārvatī</s>! ||23||
It should not be given to just anyone — it is the bestower of the greatest <s>siddhis</s>;

children.text: abhaktāyāpi putrāya dattvā mṛtyuṃ labhen naraḥ ||24||
children.translated_text: a man who gives it even to a non-devotee son will obtain death. ||24||

children.text: nātaḥ parataraṃ divyaṃ kavacaṃ bhuvi vidyate |
children.translated_text: There exists no divine <s>kavaca</s> on earth greater than this;

children.text: paṭhitvā kavacaṃ paścād yugalaṃ pūjayen naraḥ ||25||
children.translated_text: having recited the <s>kavaca</s>, a person should afterwards worship the divine couple (<s>yugala</s>). ||25||
Then, having offered a handful of flowers, one attains <s>sāyujya</s> (complete union) with <s>Rādhā</s>;
the preliminary rite (<s>puraścaryā</s>) for this is declared to be one hundred and eight [recitations]. ||26||

children.text: aṣṭottara-śataṃ japtvā sākṣād devo bhavet svayam |
children.translated_text: Having recited [it] one hundred and eight times, one directly becomes a god oneself;

children.text: kṛṣṇa-premāṇam apy āśu durlabhaṃ labhate dhruvam ||27||
children.translated_text: one swiftly and surely obtains even the rare <s>Kṛṣṇa-prema</s> (love of Kṛṣṇa). ||27||

children.text:
iti śrī-saṃmohana-tantre śrī-rādhāyās trailokya-vikramaṃ nāma kavacaṃ
sampūrṇam |
children.translated_text: Thus ends the <s>kavaca</s> named 'Conqueror of the Three Worlds' of Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> in the Śrī <s>Saṃmohana-tantra</s>.
Śrī <s>Rādhā-Govinda</s> are victorious!
And thus:
I bow unceasingly to <s>Rādhā</s>, who is accompanied by <s>Govinda</s>, devoted to abundant amorous gestures and sentiments,
the mistress of the <s>yoga-pīṭha</s>.
Now the meditation on [Her] feet (GLA 11.51):
Marked with auspicious signs — conch, half-moon, barley-grain, lotus, elephant, chariot,
plough, goad, fish-hook, flag, bow, <s>svastika</s>, fish, lance, and other such marks —
having conquered all with these, Her great battle-implements anointed with lac,
the pair of feet of Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, adorned with beautiful anklets, shone with the splendor of sovereign majesty.
Now the marks on [Her] hands (GLA 11.66):
With water-pot, lotus, garland, fan, crescent-moon, earring, parasol, sacrificial post,
conch, auspicious tree, altar, seat, flower, creeper, fly-whisk, <s>svastika</s>, and the like —
with Her pair of hands endowed with these marks of good fortune, <s>Rādhikā</s> shines resplendently;
I think that under the pretext of those [marks], She bears the articles of service for Her beloved.
Now [Her] intoxicated laughter (GLA 11.88):
The rows of <s>Hari's</s> qualities, like excellent <s>kalpa</s>-creepers (wish-fulfilling vines),
blossom fully in the garden of <s>Rādhā's</s> heart;
the flowers of those [creepers]
spill outward under the guise of [Her] smiles.
Now <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (amorous adornment) (UN 4.9):
Bathed, with a jewel sparkling at the tip of Her nose, wearing a silk garment, with braided hair tied with a thread,
with a flower behind Her ear, Her body anointed with paste, with flowers in Her hair, wearing garlands, with a lotus in Her hand,
Her chin dotted with clusters of <s>tāmbūla</s> (betel) marks, Her eyes lined with <s>kajjala</s> (kohl), beautifully decorated,
<s>Rādhā</s> with Her feet brilliant with <s>alaktaka</s> (lac-dye), wearing a <s>tilaka</s> mark — She shines in the sixteen modes of adornment.
Now [Her] ornaments (UN 4.10):
A divine chief among crest-jewels; earring-pairs, waist-chains, and necklace-medallions fashioned from gold;
nose-rings, pairs of bracelets and bangles, throat ornaments, and finger-rings;
necklaces resembling stars, armlet-and-girdle sets made of jewels,

children.text: tuṅgā pādāṅgurīya-cchavir iti ravibhir bhūṣaṇair bhāti rādhā ||
children.translated_text: tall toe-rings — with these brilliant ornaments, <s>Rādhā</s> shines resplendently.
And also (ViM 1.10):
This is the season of spring, in which
Him, the complete Lord, who has taken on fresh love —
she, <s>Paurṇamāsī</s>, the concealed presiding [goddess], together with the beautiful <s>Rādhā</s>,
will bring together for the play of love on a full-moon night.
Furthermore (UN 15.4):

children.text: pūrva-rāgas tathā mānaḥ prema-vaicittyam ity api |
children.translated_text: <s>Pūrva-rāga</s> (love prior to meeting), <s>māna</s> (jealous pride), <s>prema-vaicittya</s> (anxiety due to love),
and <s>pravāsa</s> (separation by distance) — thus <s>vipralambha</s> (love-in-separation) is declared to be of four kinds.
(15.191) [<s>Sambhoga</s> (love-in-union)] is known as <s>saṃkṣipta</s> (contracted), <s>saṅkīrṇa</s> (mixed), <s>sampanna</s> (fulfilled), and <s>samṛddhimān</s> (opulent).
Of these, <s>saṃkṣipta</s> (contracted) (15.192):
Where the young couple performs abbreviated
services due to nervousness, modesty, and the like — that is called <s>saṃkṣipta</s> (contracted).
Now <s>saṅkīrṇa</s> (mixed) (15.195):
Where the services are mixed up
due to remembered offenses and the like — that is <s>saṅkīrṇa</s> (mixed), somewhat sweet like heated sugarcane.
Now <s>sampanna</s> (fulfilled) (15.198):

children.text: pravāsāt saṅgate kānte bhogaḥ sampanna īritaḥ |
children.translated_text: When the beloved arrives after being away, the enjoyment is called <s>sampanna</s> (fulfilled);

children.text: dvidhā syād āgatiḥ prādurbhāvaś ceti sa saṅgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the meeting is of two kinds: arrival (<s>āgati</s>) and manifestation (<s>prādurbhāva</s>).
Now <s>samṛddhimān</s> (opulent) (15.206):
When two lovers who are rarely seen by each other, separated due to dependence [on others],
experience an excess of enjoyment — that is proclaimed as <s>samṛddhimān</s> (opulent).
As for example:
I bow to the supreme culmination of the <s>bhāva</s> (spiritual emotion) of Śrī <s>Rādhikā</s> and others,

children.text: vinā viyogaṃ saṃyogaṃ yā tūryam udagād yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: from which the fourth [state] arose, without separation, as union.
There, in the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata</s> (10.31.15):
When You wander in the forest during the day,
a <s>truṭi</s> (moment) becomes like a <s>yuga</s> (age) for us who do not see You;
and when [we behold] Your beautiful face with curling locks,
we consider the creator of eyelids to be foolish [for obstructing our vision even for a blink].

Thus ends the sixth section (<s>kakṣā</s>) of the <s>Bhakti-sādhana-dīpikā</s>, composed by Śrī <s>Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa Dāsa</s>, the follower of the feet of Śrī <s>Haridāsa Gosvāmī</s>, the superintendent of the service of Śrīmad <s>Rādhā-Govinda-deva</s>.
||6||

(7)
Seventh section (<s>kakṣā</s>).

children.text:
atha-
śrī-rādhā-prāṇa-bandhoś caraṇa-kamalayoḥ keśa-śeṣādy-agamyā
yā sādhyā prema-sevā vraja-carita-parair gāḍha-laulyaika-labhyā |
children.translated_text:
Now:
The <s>prema-sevā</s> (loving service) at the lotus feet of the life-companion of Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, which is inaccessible to <s>Śeṣa</s> and others, which is the goal to be attained, obtainable only through intense longing by those devoted to the pastimes of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text:
yad-vāñchayā śrīr lalanācarat tapo vihāya kāmān suciraṃ dhṛta-vratā ity ādeḥ śrī-
kṛṣṇa-līlāyāṃ śrī-rādhāyā anugatve śrīmad-rādhā-govinda-caraṇa-sevanaṃ
sarvotkṛṣṭam | tat tu madhura-rasaṃ vinā na sambhavati | tato madhura-rasasya

children.translated_text: As stated in the <s>Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</s> (2.5.38):

As [stated in the verse beginning] 'Desiring which, <s>Śrī</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) performed austerities, abandoning desires, observing vows for a long time' — the service at the feet of Śrīmad <s>Rādhā-Govinda</s>, following Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> in the <s>līlā</s> of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, is the most exalted of all. But that is not possible without <s>madhura-rasa</s> (the erotic/conjugal sentiment). Therefore the supremacy of <s>madhura-rasa</s>.
Though each successive [rasa] is greater in the special relish of its flavor,

children.text: ratir vāsanayā svādvī bhāsate kāpi kasyacit ||
children.translated_text: the <s>rati</s> (attachment) appears delightful to someone through [previous] <s>vāsanā</s> (impression/inclination).
And in the Śrīmad <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> (1.2):
That [rasa] which was previously mentioned only briefly among the principal <s>rasas</s>, due to its secrecy —

children.text: pṛthag eva bhakti-rasa-rāṭ sa vistareṇocyate madhuraḥ ||
children.translated_text: that king of <s>bhakti-rasas</s>, the <s>madhura</s> (conjugal/erotic), is now expounded at length.

children.text:
iti hetor gaura-līlāyām api tathaiva śrī-rādhā-gadādharasyaivānugatye śrī-gaura-
govindasya bhajanaṃ sarvotkṛṣṭam |
children.translated_text: For this reason, in the <s>Gaura-līlā</s> (pastimes of Caitanya) also, in the same way, the worship of Śrī <s>Gaura-Govinda</s> following Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>-as-<s>Gadādhara</s> is the most exalted of all.

children.text:
nanu śrī-gadādharasya rādhātve śrī-gaurasya govindatve kiṃ pramāṇam iti cet
tatrāha-yathā svayaṃ bhagavataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇasya para-brahmatvaṃ, gūḍhaṃ paraṃ
brahma manuṣya-liṅgam ity ādeḥ, tato'pi gūḍhataraṃ śacīnandanasya, tato
gūḍhatamaṃ preyasīnām | parama-śaktitvaṃ pārṣadānāṃ, tathā śrī-śacīnandanasya
śrī-kṛṣṇatve ārṣa-pramāṇāni bahūni santi | yathā-kṛṣṇa-varṇaṃ tviṣākṛṣṇaṃ
sāṅgopāṅgāstra-pārṣadam, śrī-bhāgavate saptama-skandhe (7.9.78)-
children.translated_text: Now, if one asks: 'What is the proof that Śrī <s>Gadādhara</s> is <s>Rādhā</s> and Śrī <s>Gaura</s> is <s>Govinda</s>?' — to that he says: Just as the Supreme Lordship (<s>para-brahmatva</s>) of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the <s>Bhagavān</s> Himself, [is established by verses such as] 'The hidden Supreme <s>Brahman</s> in human form' and the like — more hidden than that is [the identity of] <s>Śacīnandana</s> (Caitanya); and most hidden of all is [the identity of] His beloveds. [Similarly,] the supreme <s>śakti</s>-nature of His associates [is hidden]. Thus there are many scriptural proofs for the <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-identity of Śrī <s>Śacīnandana</s>. As for example: '<s>Kṛṣṇa-varṇam</s> (describing Kṛṣṇa / of dark complexion), <s>tviṣā akṛṣṇam</s> (with a non-dark luster), with His limbs, sub-limbs, weapons, and associates' — [and] in the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata</s>, seventh <s>skandha</s> (7.9.38):
Thus, through <s>avatāras</s> as humans, animals, sages, gods, and fish,
You illuminate the worlds and destroy those who oppose the universe.
You protect <s>dharma</s>, O Great Person, as appropriate to each <s>yuga</s>;

children.text: channaḥ kalau yad abhavas tri-yugo'tha sa tvam ||
children.translated_text: You were hidden in <s>Kali</s> [yuga] — therefore You are called '<s>Tri-yuga</s>' (He of three ages).

children.text:
kalau prathama-sandhāyāṃ lakṣmīkānto bhaviṣyati | tathā, suvarṇa-varṇa-hemāṅgo
varāṅgaś candanāṅgadī | tathā, sannyāsa-kṛc chamaḥ śānto niṣṭhā-śānti-
parāyaṇaḥ iti tu saṅkṣepato likhitam | viśeṣatas tu smaraṇa-maṅgala-daśa-ślokī-
bhāṣye vivṛtam asti ity ādīni |
children.translated_text: 'In the first <s>sandhyā</s> (juncture) of <s>Kali</s>, the beloved of <s>Lakṣmī</s> will appear.' Also: 'Of golden complexion, with golden limbs, of excellent form, with sandalwood ornaments.' Also: 'The renunciant, peaceful, tranquil, devoted to steadfastness and peace.' This has been written briefly. In detail, it is elaborated in the commentary on the <s>Smaraṇa-maṅgala-daśa-ślokī</s>, etc.

children.text:
preyasīnāṃ parama-śaktitvam atīva-gūḍhatvāt muninā tatra tatra noktaṃ āptaiḥ
khalu svāntaraṅgān prati tad-dvārātidhanyān prati kṛpayā prakaṭitam eva | tad
yathā prākṛta-saṃskṛteṣu ca | tatra śrī-karṇapūra-gosvāmino śrī-gaura-gaṇoddeśe
(147)-
children.translated_text: The supreme <s>śakti</s>-nature of the beloveds [of the Lord], being extremely hidden, was not stated by the sage (Vyāsa) in those places [in the Bhāgavata]; but it has been revealed by the trustworthy authorities out of compassion toward their own intimate associates and, through them, to the most fortunate ones. This is [found] in both Prakrit and Sanskrit [texts]. Of these, in Śrī <s>Karṇapūra Gosvāmī's</s> Śrī <s>Gaura-gaṇoddeśa</s> (147):

children.text: śrī rādhā prema-rūpā yā purā vṛndāvaneśvarī |
children.translated_text: She who was formerly Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>, the embodiment of <s>prema</s>, the Queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
She is Śrī <s>Gadādhara</s>, called '<s>Paṇḍita</s>,' the beloved of <s>Gaura</s>.
Of the very same [author], in the Śrī <s>Caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭaka</s> (3.44):
This one is <s>Lalitā</s> herself, this one is <s>Rādhikā</s> herself,
this is certainly not <s>Gadādhara</s>, the king of the earth-born (brāhmaṇas);
<s>Hari</s> Himself, through His own <s>śakti</s> (power),

children.text: tritayam abhūt sva-sakhī ca rādhikā ca ||
children.translated_text: became threefold — Himself, His own <s>sakhī</s> (intimate companion), and <s>Rādhikā</s>.
In the same <s>Gaṇoddeśa</s> (152):
Others say that <s>Dhruvānanda Brahmacārī</s> is <s>Lalitā</s>;
that opinion is appropriate through the distinction of self-manifestation (<s>sva-prakāśa</s>).
Or rather, the Lord <s>Gaura</s> by His own will assumed a threefold form;
therefore Śrī <s>Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s> is the form of Śrī <s>Rādhikā</s>.
In the Śrī <s>Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s> (1.1.41):
<s>Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s> and others are the Lord's own <s>śaktis</s> (powers);

children.text: tāṅ sabāra caraṇe mora sahasra praṇati ||
children.translated_text: at the feet of all of them, [I offer] a thousand prostrations.
Again, in the same [text] (1.12.90):

children.text:
paṇḍita gosāñira gaṇa bhāgavata dhanya |
prāṇa-vallabha yāṅra śrī-ka-caitanya || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
The company of <s>Paṇḍita Gosāñi</s> are blessed <s>Bhāgavatas</s> (devotees);
their life-beloved is Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa-Caitanya</s>. And so on.

children.text:
yad uktaṃ (1.10.15)-
teṅho lakṣmī-rūpā tāṅra sama keho nāñi ||
children.translated_text:
As stated (1.10.15)—
He is in the form of <s>Lakṣmī</s>; no one equals Her. ||
That, however, is with the intention of [Her being] the original <s>Lakṣmī</s> (<s>mūla-lakṣmī</s>), as in the <s>Bṛhad-Gautamīya</s>—

children.text:
devī kṛṣṇa-mayī proktā rādhikā para-devatā |
sarva-lakṣmī-mayī sarva-kāntiḥ saṃmohinī parā || iti |
children.translated_text:
The Goddess is declared to be <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-natured; <s>Rādhikā</s> is the supreme deity.
She embodies all <s>Lakṣmīs</s>, She is all beauty, She is the supreme enchantress. || Thus. |
And in the <s>Śrī Brahma-saṃhitā</s>—

children.text:
śriyaḥ kāntāḥ kāntaḥ parama-puruṣaḥ kalpa-taravo
drumā bhūmiś cintāmaṇi-gaṇa-mayī toyam amṛtam |
kathā gānaṃ nāṭyam iti |
children.translated_text:
The beloveds are <s>Śrīs</s> (goddesses of fortune), the beloved is the Supreme Person, the trees are wish-fulfilling trees,
the earth is made of hosts of <s>cintāmaṇi</s> (wish-fulfilling gems), the water is nectar,
conversation is song, movement is dance — thus. |
Served with the eagerness of hundreds of thousands of <s>Lakṣmīs</s>. Thus. |

In the same text—
Endowed with narratives of the amorous play of <s>Śrī Vāsudeva</s> — 'this He does.' Thus. |

children.text:
sandarbhe ca (kṛṣṇa-sandarbhe 189)-śrī-vṛndāvane śrī-rādhikāyām eva svayaṃ-
lakṣmītvam iti |
children.translated_text:
And in the <s>Sandarbha</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha</s> 189)—In <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>, in <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> alone
is the nature of being <s>Lakṣmī</s> Herself. Thus. |

children.text:
śrī-jagannātha-vallabha-nāṭake śrī-rāmānanda-rāya-caraṇaiḥ (1.20)-yato
gopāṅganā-śatādhara-madhu-pāna-nirbhara-keli-klamālasāpaghanaḥ kvacit
prauḍha-vadhūs tatnopadhānīya-maṇḍita-hṛdaya-paryaṅka-śāyī pītāmbaro
nārāyaṇaḥ smāritaḥ | ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
By the revered feet of <s>Śrī Rāmānanda Rāya</s>, in the <s>Śrī Jagannātha-vallabha-nāṭaka</s> (1.20)—whereupon,
languid from the exertion of play immersed in drinking the honey of the lips of hundreds of <s>gopī</s>-women,
