somewhere lying on a heart-couch adorned for serving as a pillow, a mature bride,
the yellow-robed <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> is remembered. | And so forth. |

children.text:
evaṃ śrī-vidagdha-mādhave (4.52)-sundari ! nāham kevalaṃ tavādhīnaḥ | kintu
mama daśāvatārāś ca | ity ādi | evaṃ śrī-govinda-līlāmṛte ca (18.10)-
children.translated_text:
Likewise, in the <s>Śrī Vidagdha-Mādhava</s> (4.52)—'O beautiful one! I am not merely subject to you, but
my ten <s>avatāras</s> also [are subject to you].' And so forth. | Likewise, in the <s>Śrī Govinda-līlāmṛta</s> (18.10)—
She who is a mine of jewel-like qualities, an ocean of the nectar of rising <s>prema</s>,
whose glorious deeds are praised by the assemblies of the best virtuous women of the three worlds,
the Queen of Queens of the world-honored <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> (forest of <s>Vṛndā</s>),

children.text: vilasati kila sā śrī-rādhikeha svayaṃ śrīḥ ||
children.translated_text: indeed <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> shines here as <s>Śrī</s> (Fortune) Herself. ||

children.text:
saundarya-lakṣmīr ihakādhya lakṣmīḥ
saṅgīta-lakṣmīś ca harer mude'sti ||
children.translated_text:
The <s>Lakṣmī</s> of beauty, the <s>Lakṣmī</s> of this day's wealth,
and the <s>Lakṣmī</s> of music — exist for <s>Hari</s>'s delight. ||
And by <s>Śrī Dāsa Gosvāmī</s> in the <s>Sva-niyama-daśaka</s> (10)—
whose radiant <s>Lakṣmī</s> triumphs over the <s>Lakṣmīs</s> of <s>Vraja</s>,
the bodily beauty of <s>Gāndharvā</s> (Rādhā) and the shining mountain of their manifold amorous sports,
I shall eagerly arrange various attendant services in the groves and other places,
as the last servant of that dearest person named <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>. ||
In <s>Śrī Svarūpa Gosvāmī</s>'s notebook (<s>kaḍacā</s>)—

children.text:
avani-sura-varaḥ śrī-paṇḍitākhyo yatīndraḥ
sa khalu bhavati rādhā śrīla-gaurāvatāre |
narahari-sarakārasyāpi dāmodarasya
prabhu-nija-dayitānāṃ tac ca sāraṃ mataṃ me || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
The best among earth-dwelling <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the great <s>yatīndra</s> named <s>Śrī Paṇḍita</s>,
he indeed becomes <s>Rādhā</s> in the avatāra of <s>Śrīla Gaura</s>.
Of <s>Narahari Sarakāra</s> and also <s>Dāmodara</s>,
among the Lord's own beloveds, that is the essence — such is my view. || And so forth. |
By <s>Śrī Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya</s> in the <s>Śata-nāma-stotra</s> (14)—
The life-lord of <s>Gadādhara</s>, the remover of affliction, the granter of refuge. | And so forth. |

children.text:
śrī-sarakāra-ṭhakkureṇa bhajanāmṛte-iha mataṃ me, yathā kali-yuga-
pāvanāvatāra-karuṇāmaya-śrī-śrī-caitanya-candraḥ vrajarājakumāras tatahiva
niḥsīma-śuddha-praṇaya-sāra-ghanībhūta-mahābhāva-svarūpa-rasamaya-parama-
dayitaḥ śrī-gadādhara eva rādhā |
children.translated_text:
By <s>Śrī Sarakāra Ṭhakkura</s> in the <s>Bhajanāmṛta</s>—'This is my view, that the compassionate <s>Kali-yuga</s>-
purifying avatāra <s>Śrī Śrī Caitanya-candra</s> is the Prince of <s>Vraja</s>, and therefore
from Him alone, the condensation of the essence of boundless pure love, the embodiment of <s>mahābhāva</s>,
the supremely dear one of <s>rasa</s> nature, <s>Śrī Gadādhara</s> is indeed <s>Rādhā</s>.'

And in the <s>Vaiṣṇavābhidhāna</s> (4)—
The life-lord of <s>Gadādhara</s>, the husband of <s>Lakṣmī-Viṣṇu-Priyā</s>. Thus. |
And in the <s>aṣṭaka</s> of <s>Śrī Paramānanda Gosvāmī</s>, as composed by <s>Śrī Madhu Paṇḍita Gosvāmī</s>—
Whose mind wanders in the form of a bee at the lotus-feet of <s>Gopīnātha</s>,
to that ocean of compassionate nectar, to Lord <s>Paramānanda</s>, I offer my obeisance. ||
By <s>Śrī Paramānanda Gosvāmī</s> himself—
He who, on the banks of the daughter of Mount <s>Kalinda</s> (<s>Yamunā</s>), in clusters of bowers,
having assumed the form of the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, extended abundant playful <s>rasa</s>,
having drunk the auspiciousness of <s>Vraja</s>, became <s>Gaura</s>-formed here —

children.text: sa me diśatu bhāvukaṃ prabhu-gadādharaḥ śrī-guruḥ ||
children.translated_text: may that Lord <s>Gadādhara</s>, <s>Śrī Guru</s>, bestow upon me devotional sentiment. ||
In the <s>Śrī Caitanya-carita-kāvya</s> (6.12-14)—
The illustrious <s>Gadādhara</s>, of great wisdom, exceedingly generous,
glorious, sweet by nature, of deeply serene form,
slept near the Lord in the night at a high place;
'This <s>nirmālya</s> (used garland), spread it upon the chest for them.' ||

children.text: itthaṃ sa yad yad adadāt pramadena yasmai
children.translated_text: Thus, whatever He gave with delight, to whomever,

children.text: yasmai janāya tad idaṃ sa gadādharo'pi |
children.translated_text: to whichever person — that same <s>Gadādhara</s> also
constantly gave each morning to the ever-joyful one,
the <s>mahā-prasāda</s> released by the Great Lord. ||
Having strung garlands of flowers in heaps, having carefully prepared
a paste of fine fragrant substances, camphor, and other excellent ingredients,

children.text: aṅgeṣu tasya parito jayati sma nityaṃ
children.translated_text: [and applied them] on His limbs all around — triumphant constantly,
with yearning, there <s>Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s> was foremost in this. ||
Therein also (5.55)—
<s>Śrīvāsa</s> then spoke to <s>Gadādhara</s>:
'O <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>, chief of all, let all that be brought there.'

children.text: ity uktaḥ sa ca sakalaṃ nināya tatra
children.translated_text: Thus told, he brought everything there,
drenched in <s>prema</s>, endlessly, having forgotten his own bodily actions. ||
Therein also (5.128-9)—
That best of men, <s>Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s>,
constantly in close and good company with Him,
day after day worships his own life's dearest,
that most beloved one, with extreme longing. ||
At night, having gone near Him, steadfast,
he eagerly makes his sleeping arrangements.
The nectar of sporting with Him, constantly,
was always well-enjoyed by him, without cessation. ||
Therein also (11.22-24)—
When that [drama] had concluded, with various enacted women's roles adorning him,
the one named <s>Gadādhṛk</s> (<s>Gadādhara</s>), his hands brilliant with bangles and conch-shell bracelets,

children.text: praviṣṭo gāyadbhir laghu laghu mṛdaṅge mukharite
children.translated_text: entered, while others sang, with the <s>mṛdaṅga</s> softly, softly sounded,

children.text: tathā tālair mānair naṭana-kalayā tatra vibhavau ||
children.translated_text: and with cymbals and rhythmic meters, in the art of dance — there the two were resplendent. ||
Then, as he danced, resplendent in his sweet costume of radiant beauty,
with the musical melody of hundreds of broken <s>mṛdaṅga</s> rhythms,
the people, again and again plunged into an ocean of bliss, blinking,
surrounded on all sides — what nectar was attained with limbs frozen in stunned stillness! ||
The daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, <s>Rādhā</s>, beloved of <s>Śyāmasundara</s>,
in <s>Kali</s>-yuga is known as <s>Gadādhara</s>, the son of <s>Mādhavānanda</s>.
Born in the house of <s>Mādhava</s>, on the new-moon day of <s>Mādhava</s> (Vaiśākha),
<s>Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s> is <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> in a wondrous form. ||
Now, <s>Śrī Vāsudeva Ghoṣa Ṭhakkura</s>—

children.text: akhila brahma-para veda upara, nā jāne pāṣaṇḍī mati-bhorā ||
children.translated_text: The entire <s>Brahman</s> is paramount in the <s>Vedas</s> — the heretics of dull intellect do not know this. ||

children.text: nitya nityānanda caitanya govinda paṇḍita gadādhara rādhe |
children.translated_text: Eternal <s>Nityānanda</s>, <s>Caitanya</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, <s>Paṇḍita Gadādhara</s>, <s>Rādhā</s> —

children.text: caitanya yugala-rūpa kevala rasera kūpa avatāra sadā-śiva sādhe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Caitanya</s> is the dual-form (<s>yugala-rūpa</s>), solely a well of <s>rasa</s>; the avatāra that eternal <s>Śiva</s> aspires to attain. ||

children.text: antare nava-ghana bāhire gaura-tanu yugala-rūpa parakāśe |
children.translated_text: Internally a fresh rain-cloud, externally a golden body — the dual-form is manifest.

children.text: kahe vāsudeva ghoṣa yugala-bhajana-rase janame janame rahu āśe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsudeva Ghoṣa</s> says: In the <s>rasa</s> of dual-worship (<s>yugala-bhajana</s>), may I remain in hope birth after birth. ||
<s>Gaurāṅga</s> sports in supreme bliss,

children.text: nityānanda kari saṅge gaṅgā-pulina-raṅge hari hari bole nija-vṛnde |
children.translated_text: with <s>Nityānanda</s> in company, on the sport-ground of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>-bank, 'Hari! Hari!' calls His own group.

children.text: kāṅcā kāñcana-maṇi gorā-rūpa tāhe jini ḍagamagi-prema-taraṅga |
children.translated_text: Raw golden gems — <s>Gorā</s>'s form outshines them; waves of love sway and glitter.

children.text: o nava kusuma-dāma gale dole anupāma helana narahari aṅga ||
children.translated_text: O, a garland of fresh flowers swings incomparably at His neck — embracing <s>Narahari</s>'s body. ||

children.text: bhāve bharala tanu pulaka kadamba janu garaha-i yaichana siṃhe |
children.translated_text: His body filled with ecstasy, clusters of horripilation — as if a lion is seizing [its prey];

children.text: priya gadādhara dhariyā se bāma kara nija-guṇa-gāna govinde ||
children.translated_text: beloved <s>Gadādhara</s> He holds with His left hand, [while] <s>Govinda</s> sings of His own qualities. ||

children.text: aruṇa-nayana-koṇe īṣat hāsiyā khene royata kibā abhilāṣa |
children.translated_text: With reddened corner of the eye, slightly smiling at moments, weeping — what is the desire?

children.text: soṅari se saba khelā śrī-vṛndāvana-rasa-līlā ki bolaba vāsudeva ghoṣe ||
children.translated_text: All those games are the <s>rasa-līlā</s> of <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s> — what more can <s>Vāsudeva Ghoṣa</s> say? ||
Now, the <s>rasa</s> of <s>vāsaka-sajjā</s> (the heroine adorned and awaiting her beloved) (356)—

children.text: aruṇa-nayane dhārā bahe | aruṇita māla māthe gora rahe ||
children.translated_text: Streams flow from His reddened eyes. | Reddened garlands remain on <s>Gorā</s>'s head. ||

children.text: ki bhāva paḍiyāche mane | bhūmi gaḍi paḍe kṣaṇe kṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: What mood has fallen upon His mind? | He falls to the ground again and again. ||

children.text: kamala pallava bichāiyā | rahe gorā dheyāna kariyā ||
children.translated_text: Having spread lotus petals, | <s>Gorā</s> remains in meditation. ||

children.text: vāsaka-sajjāra bhāva kari | virale basiyā ekeśvarī ||
children.translated_text: Assuming the mood of <s>vāsaka-sajjā</s>, | sitting alone, the sole mistress. ||

children.text: vāsudeva ghoṣa tā dekhiyā | bole kichu caraṇe dhariyā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsudeva Ghoṣa</s>, seeing that, | speaks something, grasping His feet. ||
Now, the <s>dāna-līlā</s> (toll-collecting pastime) (<s>Gaura-pada</s>)—
What mood has today fallen upon <s>Gorā-cāṅda</s> (Moon-like Gaura)!
On the road of <s>Nadīyā</s>, <s>Gorā</s> set up a toll-collection! ||

children.text: ki rasera dāna cāhe gorā dvija-maṇi |
children.translated_text: What <s>rasa</s>-toll does <s>Gorā</s>, jewel among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, demand?
Blocking the way with His arm, He detains the young women. ||

children.text: dāna deha bali ghane ghane ḍāke |
children.translated_text: 'Give the toll!' — again and again He calls out.
All the city women fell into the predicament. ||
'I am the avatāra of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>! I have collected the toll!'

children.text: se bhāva paḍila mane vāsudeva gāna ||
children.translated_text: That mood fell upon His mind — <s>Vāsudeva</s> sings. ||
Now, water-play (<s>jala-krīḍā</s>) (2649)—
Water-play fell upon <s>Gorā-cāṅda</s>'s mind.
Taking His companions along, He plunged into the water. ||

children.text: gorā-aṅge keho keho jala pheli māre |
children.translated_text: On <s>Gorā</s>'s body some people splash and strike with water.
<s>Gaurāṅga</s>, splashing water, strikes <s>Gadādhara</s>. ||
<s>Gorā</s> plays water-sports with a delighted mind.
Cheering and tumbling, person to person. ||

children.text: gaurāṅga cāṅdera līlā kahana nā yāya |
children.translated_text: The pastimes of <s>Gaurāṅga-cāṅda</s> (Moon-like Gaura) cannot be told.
<s>Vāsudeva Ghoṣa</s> sings these qualities of <s>Gorā</s>. ||
Now, the dice-game (<s>pāśā-khelā</s>) (2671)—
A dice-game fell upon <s>Gorā-cāṅda</s>'s mind.
Taking the dice, <s>Gorā</s> set up the game. ||

children.text: priya gadādhara saṅge gorā khele pāśā sāri |
children.translated_text: With beloved <s>Gadādhara</s>, <s>Gorā</s> plays dice in rows.

children.text: khelite lāgila pāśā hāri jini kari ||
children.translated_text: They began playing dice, winning and losing. ||
'Two-four!' calling, <s>Gadādhara</s> throws.
'Five-three!' calls out <s>Gaurāṅga-sundara</s>. ||

children.text: dui jane magana bhela nava pāśā rase |
children.translated_text: Both became absorbed in the fresh <s>rasa</s> of the dice-game.

children.text: jaya jaya diyā gāya vāsudeva ghoṣe ||
children.translated_text: Chanting 'Jaya! Jaya!' sings <s>Vāsudeva Ghoṣa</s>. ||
Now, sandalwood-anointing (<s>candana</s>) (<s>Gaura-pada</s>)—
Anointing <s>Gorā</s>'s body with <s>aguru</s> (aloe) and sandalwood.

children.text: priya pāriṣada gaṇa gorā guṇa gāya ||
children.translated_text: The dear companions sing <s>Gorā</s>'s qualities. ||

children.text: āni salila keha dhari nija kare |
children.translated_text: Someone brings water, holding it in their own hands,
and with the mind's devotion, pours it over <s>Gorā</s>. ||

children.text: cāṅda jiniyā mukha adhika kari sāje |
children.translated_text: His moon-defeating face is adorned even more beautifully.
A garland of <s>mālatī</s> flowers adorns <s>Gorā</s>'s body. ||
Crimson garments are adorned with various ornaments.
<s>Vāsudeva</s> gazes upon <s>Gorā</s>'s form. ||
Now, the flower-pastime (<s>phula-līlā</s>) (1525)—
Seeing a flower-garden, <s>Gorā-cāṅda</s>'s eyes [lit up].

children.text: phulera samara gorāra paḍi gela mane ||
children.translated_text: A flower-battle fell upon <s>Gorā</s>'s mind. ||
With beloved <s>Gadādhara</s> and also <s>Nityānanda</s>,
<s>Gorā</s> found bliss in the flower-battle. ||
The Lord sports with <s>Gadādhara</s>.
<s>Vāsudeva</s> says: He has manifested the <s>rasa</s>. ||
Now, the <s>Holikā</s> sport (color-throwing festival)—

children.text: sahacara mili phāgu māre gorā gāya |
children.translated_text: Companions gather and throw colored powder on <s>Gorā</s>'s body.

children.text: candana picakā bhari keho keho dhāya ||
children.translated_text: Some rush about filling sandalwood-syringes. ||
Various instruments beautifully assembled by <s>Śrīnivāsa</s>,
with <s>Gadādhara</s> and others He sports. ||

children.text: hari buli bhuja tuli nāce haridāsa |
children.translated_text: Calling 'Hari!' raising His arms, <s>Haridāsa</s> dances.
<s>Vāsudeva Ghoṣa</s> has revealed the <s>rasa</s>. ||

children.text:
āre more dvija-maṇi
rādhā rādhā bali gaurā loṭāya dharaṇī ||
children.translated_text:
'O my jewel among <s>brāhmaṇas</s>!'
Calling 'Rādhā! Rādhā!' <s>Gaura</s> rolls upon the earth. ||
<s>Gorā</s> chants the name of <s>Rādhā</s> with utmost effort.
Graceful streams flow from His reddened eyes. ||

children.text: kṣaṇe kṣaṇe gorā cāṅda bhūme gaḍi yāya |
children.translated_text: Again and again <s>Gorā-cāṅda</s> falls to the ground.
Seeing the face of <s>Rādhikā</s>, He faints in a moment. ||
His body filled with horripilation, His words faltering,

children.text: kahe vāsu gorā mora baḍa utarola ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāsu</s> says: '<s>Gorā</s>, my [Lord], is greatly overwhelmed!' ||

children.text: gaurāṅga viraha jvara hiyā chaṭa phaṭa kare
children.translated_text: The fever of separation from <s>Gaurāṅga</s> — the heart burns and shatters,
life cannot hold together.

children.text: nā heriyā cāṅda mukha vidarite cāhe buka
children.translated_text: Without seeing that moon-like face, the chest wants to burst open —
how can one maintain this love?

children.text: prāṇera hari hari kaha more jīvana upāya |
children.translated_text: 'O <s>Hari</s> of my life! <s>Hari</s>! Tell me the means of survival!'

children.text: e dukhe dukhita ye e dukha jānaye se
children.translated_text: One who is grieved by this grief, who knows this sorrow, that one —
to whom else shall I make my appeal?

children.text: gaurāṅga mukhera hāsi sudhā khase rāśi rāśi
children.translated_text: The smile on <s>Gaurāṅga</s>'s face — nectar drips in heaps and heaps,
yet I cannot see it.

children.text: yata chila bandhu gaṇa sabhe bhela nikaruṇa
children.translated_text: All the kinsmen that were — they have all become merciless.
What pleasure do I gain by staying alive?

children.text: gadādhara ādi kari nā dekhiyā prāṇe mari
children.translated_text: Not seeing <s>Gadādhara</s> and the others, I die within —
'He is dead! He is dead!' <s>Madhumatī</s> [cries], not seeing [Him].

children.text: ye more karita dayā se gela niṭhura hañā
children.translated_text: He who would have shown me mercy, He has gone and become cruel.
<s>Vāsu</s> [laments]: 'Why did I not go and die [with Him]?' ||

children.text:
yathā svayaṃ bhagavān śrī-vrajendra-nandanaḥ svasya kāya-vyūha-prakāśa-vilāsa-
parāvastha-prābhava-vaibhava-rūpaiḥ śrī-baladeva-śrī-mathurā-dvārakā-goloka-
paravyoma-nātha-nṛsiṃha-raghunāthādibhiḥ svāvatārāvalībhis tat tat pārṣadaiś ca
śrīman-nityānandādvaita-śrīvāsaṃ kṛtvā kalau śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-mahāprabhuḥ
san kṛpayā prakaṭo'bhūt | tathā tena rasika-maṇḍala-śekhareṇa svasya mahā-śakti-
hlādinī-sāra-rūpā sarva-lakṣmī svarūpā-śrī-vṛṣabhānu-nandinī śrīmatī rādhaiva
śrī-gopī-gaṇa-mahiṣī-gaṇa-lakṣmī-gaṇaiḥ svaysa kāya-vyūha-prakāśa-rūpaiḥ
sahitā śrī-gadādhara-paṇḍita-rūpeṇāvatāritābhūt | prabhutvāt tasyaiva |
children.translated_text: Just as the Supreme Lord <s>Śrī Vrajendra-nandana</s> (son of the king of Vraja) Himself, through His <s>kāya-vyūha</s> (bodily expansion), <s>prakāśa</s> (manifestation), <s>vilāsa</s> (sportive expansion), <s>parāvastha</s> (transcendent state), <s>prābhava</s> (powerful), and <s>vaibhava</s> (opulent) forms — namely <s>Śrī Baladeva</s>, the Lord of <s>Śrī Mathurā</s>-<s>Dvārakā</s>-<s>Goloka</s>-<s>Paravyoma</s>, <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, <s>Raghunātha</s>, and others — through His succession of incarnations and their respective attendants, having made <s>Śrīman Nityānanda</s>, <s>Advaita</s>, and <s>Śrīvāsa</s>, appeared mercifully in the age of <s>Kali</s> as <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu</s>. Similarly, by that crest-jewel of connoisseurs, His great <s>Hlādinī Śakti</s> (bliss-potency) in essence, the form of all fortune — <s>Śrī Vṛṣabhānu-nandinī</s>, <s>Śrīmatī Rādhā</s> Herself — accompanied by the <s>gopī</s>-groups, queen-groups, and <s>Lakṣmī</s>-groups in the form of Her <s>kāya-vyūha</s> and <s>prakāśa</s> — was brought down in the form of <s>Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s>. Because of His lordship over Her.

children.text:
śaktiś ca aghaṭana-ghaṭanā-paṭīyasī yogamāyā vaibhavena yadā yad icchāṃ karoti
tat kim api durghaṭaṃ na bhavati avatīrya saṅkīrtanānandāveśena tat tat pūrva-
bhāvaṃ sva-sva-vilāsa-śakti-pārṣadaṃ prati darśitavān | etat tu śrī-karṇapūra-śrī-
vṛndāvana-dāsa-śrī-vāsudeva-śrī-narahari-ṭhakkurādi-śrī-rūpa-sanātana-śrī-
kṛṣṇadāsa-śrī-kavirāja-śrī-locanadāsa-prabhṛtibhiḥ sva-sva-granthe likhitvā
sthāpitam asti | tasmāt sarveṣāṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-pārṣadānāṃ mate śrī-
gadādhara-paṇḍita eva śrī-vṛṣabhānu-nandinī śrī-rādhā | kiṃ bahu-vicāritena |
children.translated_text: And His power, <s>Yogamāyā</s>, most expert in making the impossible possible, by her opulence, whenever He wills anything, nothing is impossible. Having descended, in the ecstasy of <s>saṅkīrtana</s>, He showed the respective prior moods to each of His sportive-power attendants. This has been written and established in their respective works by <s>Śrī Karṇapūra</s>, <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana Dāsa</s>, <s>Śrī Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Śrī Narahari Ṭhakkura</s>, and others, <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa</s>, <s>Śrī Kavirāja</s>, <s>Śrī Locanadāsa</s>, and others. Therefore, in the view of all the attendants of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, <s>Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s> alone is <s>Śrī Vṛṣabhānu-nandinī Śrī Rādhā</s>. What need of much deliberation?

children.text:
kiṃ ca, adyāpi śrī-vṛndāvane upāsanā-prāpti-sthāne śrīmad-rādhā-govinda-śrī-
rādhā-madana-gopāla-sevādhikārī śrī-rūpa-sanātanānugatye rādhā-gadādhara-
caritram eva dṛśyate | śrī-caitanya-bhāgavate śrī-ṭhakkura-vṛndāvana-varṇane
madhya-khaṇḍe (18.101-119)-
children.translated_text: Moreover, even today in <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>, at the place of worship-attainment, the authority for service of <s>Śrīmad Rādhā-Govinda</s> and <s>Śrī Rādhā-Madana-Gopāla</s>, in the line of <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> and <s>Sanātana</s>, the character of <s>Rādhā-Gadādhara</s> is seen. In the <s>Śrī Caitanya Bhāgavata</s>, in the description of <s>Śrī Ṭhākura Vṛndāvana</s>, in the Middle Section (<s>Madhya-khaṇḍa</s>) (18.101–119):
In the first watch, this special festivity;
in the second watch, <s>Gadādhara</s> entered in an ecstatic state.
<s>Suprabhā</s> is his <s>sakhī</s>, keeping her own company,
<s>Brahmānanda</s> is his elderly maidservant, immersed in delight.

children.text: hāte laḍi kāṅkhe ḍāli neta paridhāna |
children.translated_text: With bangles on the wrists and sari draped over the shoulder, wearing a cloth,
<s>Brahmānanda</s> is present as such an elderly woman.

children.text: ḍāki bole haridāsa ke saba tomarā |
children.translated_text: Calling out, <s>Haridāsa</s> says: 'Who are all of yours?'
<s>Brahmānanda</s> says: 'We are going to Mathurā.'
<s>Śrīnivāsa</s> says: 'Whose wife are you?'
<s>Brahmānanda</s> says: 'Why do you ask such questions?'
<s>Śrīnivāsa</s> says: 'It is not improper to know.'
'It is so' — saying this, <s>Brahmānanda</s> nods his head.
<s>Gaṅgādāsa</s> says: 'Where will you stay today?'
<s>Brahmānanda</s> says: 'You will give me a place.'
<s>Gaṅgādāsa</s> says: 'You asked too much —'

children.text: jijñāsāra kāja nāhi jhāṭa tumi naḍa ||
children.translated_text: 'there is no need for questioning — you are just a nuisance!'

children.text: advaita bolaye eta vicāra ki kāja |
children.translated_text: <s>Advaita</s> says: 'What is the use of all this deliberation?'
'A woman of another [household] is like a mother — why do you shame [her]?'

children.text: nṛtya gīte pīta baḍa āmāra ṭhākura |
children.translated_text: 'My Lord is very fond of singing and dancing —'
'dance here, O virtuous one, and you will receive abundant wealth.'
Hearing <s>Advaita</s>'s words, with supreme delight,
<s>Gadādhara</s> dances, manifesting <s>prema</s> (divine love).
In the ecstasy of <s>rasa</s>, <s>Gadādhara</s> dances enchantingly;
the attendants sing songs appropriate to the occasion.

children.text: gadādhara nṛtya dekhi āche kona jana |
children.translated_text: Is there anyone who, seeing <s>Gadādhara</s>'s dance,
does not become overwhelmed and weep?
A river of <s>prema</s> flows from <s>Gadādhara</s>'s eyes;

children.text: pṛthivī ha-iyā sikta dhanya hena māne ||
children.translated_text: the earth, becoming wet [with tears], considers itself blessed.
<s>Gadādhara</s> became as if the <s>Gaṅgā</s> embodied;
truly, truly, <s>Gadādhara</s> is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s consort (<s>prakṛti</s>).
<s>Caitanya</s> Himself has said again and again:
'<s>Gadādhara</s> is My <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> associate.'

children.text: ye gāya ye dekhe sabhe bhāsilena prema |
children.translated_text: All who sing, all who watch, were flooded with <s>prema</s>;

children.text: caitanya prasāde keho bāhya nāhi jāne ||
children.translated_text: by <s>Caitanya</s>'s grace, no one retained external awareness.

children.text: hari hari boli kāṅde saba vaiṣṇava maṇḍala |
children.translated_text: The entire assembly of <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> weeps, crying '<s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>!'
Taking all the devotees together, <s>Govinda</s> creates an uproar.
In all four directions, the weeping of <s>Kṛṣṇa-prema</s> is heard;
the son of <s>Mādhava</s> dances in the dress of <s>gopikās</s>.
And thus —
One day, <s>Gadādhara</s>, taking betel,
came joyfully to the Lord, entering His presence.
Seeing <s>Gadādhara</s>, the Lord inquires:
'Where is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the dark one in yellow garments?'

children.text: se ārti dekhite sarva hṛdaya vidare |
children.translated_text: Seeing that anguish, everyone's heart is rent;

children.text: ke ki balibeka prabhu bādha nāhi sphure ||
children.translated_text: who can say anything? The Lord's [grief] finds no expression.
With reverence, the great <s>Gadādhara</s> speaks:
'<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is ceaselessly in Your heart.'
Hearing the words '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is in [Your] heart,'

children.text: āpana hṛdaya prabhu cire naka diyā ||
children.translated_text: the Lord [tries to] tear open His own heart with His nails.
In great haste, <s>Gadādhara</s> seizes the Lord's hand;

children.text: ārti dekhi gadādhara mane ta vicāre ||
children.translated_text: seeing the anguish, <s>Gadādhara</s> reflects in his mind.

children.text: ei āsibena kṛṣṇa sthira hao khāni |
children.translated_text: '<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is about to come — be steady for a moment!'
<s>Gadādhara</s> says: 'Mother, come and see for yourself!'

children.text: baḍa tuṣṭa hailā āi gadādhara prati |
children.translated_text: Mother was very pleased toward <s>Gadādhara</s>;

children.text: emata śiśura buddhi nāhi āra kati ||
children.translated_text: 'How many children have such intelligence!'

children.text: muñi bhaye nāhi pāro sammukha ha-ite |
children.translated_text: 'I could not stand before [Him] out of fear;'

children.text: śiśu ha-i kemane prabodhilā bhāla mate ||
children.translated_text: 'being a child, how well [you] consoled [Him]!'

children.text: āi bole bāpa tumi sarvadā thākibā |
children.translated_text: Mother says: 'Child, you should always stay;'

children.text: chāḍiyā uhāra saṅga kothāha nā yābā ||
children.translated_text: 'do not go anywhere, leaving His company.'
And thus, in the Middle Section:

children.text: prabhu bole kon jana gṛhera bhitara |
children.translated_text: The Lord says: 'Who is inside the house?'
The <s>brahmacārī</s> says: 'Your <s>Gadādhara</s>.'
Bowing his head, <s>Gadādhara</s> weeps;
seeing this, the Lord <s>Viśvambhara</s> speaks with satisfaction:
'<s>Gadādhara</s>, yours is the good fortune!'
'From childhood, your mind has been firmly fixed on <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.'

children.text: āmāra se hena janma gela vṛthā rase |
children.translated_text: 'My own life of such kind has gone to waste;'

children.text: nā pāila amūlya nidhi dīna-hīna doṣe ||
children.translated_text: 'I did not obtain the priceless treasure, due to the fault of being poor and lowly.'
And thus, in the Middle Section:

children.text: ei saba adbhuta sei navadvīpe haye |
children.translated_text: All these wonders happen in <s>Navadvīpa</s>,

children.text: tathāpi o bhakta ba-i anya nā jānaye ||
children.translated_text: yet no one besides the devotee knows.
The most wonderful stories of the Middle Section —
He spoke of <s>tattva-jñāna</s> (knowledge of reality) through a dead body.
In such a manner, <s>Śrī Gaurasundara</s> in <s>Navadvīpa</s>
sports ceaselessly in the bliss of <s>saṅkīrtana</s>.
In the ecstasy of <s>prema-rasa</s>, the Lord has no awareness of the world;

children.text: anyera ki dāya viṣṇu pūjite nā pāre ||
children.translated_text: what to say of others — He cannot even worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: snāna kari baise prabhu śrī-viṣṇu pūjite |
children.translated_text: Having bathed, the Lord sits down to worship <s>Śrī Viṣṇu</s>;

children.text: prema jale sakala śrī-aṅga vastra tite ||
children.translated_text: all His sacred limbs and garments are soaked with the water of <s>prema</s>.

children.text: bāhira ha-iyā prabhu se vastra chāḍiyā |
children.translated_text: Coming outside, the Lord, removing that garment,

children.text: puna anya vastra pari viṣṇu pūje giyā ||
children.translated_text: puts on another garment and goes to worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> again.

children.text: puna premānanda jale tite se vasana |
children.translated_text: Again, the garment is soaked with the water of blissful <s>prema</s>;
again He comes out and washes His body.

children.text: ei mata vastra parivarta kare mātra |
children.translated_text: In this manner, He merely keeps changing garments;

children.text: preme viṣṇu pūjite nā pāre tila mātra ||
children.translated_text: in <s>prema</s>, He cannot worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> even for a sesame-seed's [moment].
Finally, He spoke these words to <s>Gadādhara</s>:

children.text: tumi viṣṇu pūja mora nāhika saubhāgya ||
children.translated_text: 'You worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> — I have no such fortune.'
In this manner, the Lord of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, in the ecstasy of <s>bhakti-rasa</s>,
sports in <s>Navadvīpa</s>, night and day.
And thus —
<s>Nityānanda Svarūpa</s>, embracing everyone,
bathed everyone's body with the water of His eyes.
Then all the devotees, seeing <s>Jagannātha</s> with delight,
went joyfully for the <s>darśana</s> of <s>Gadādhara</s>.
The love between <s>Nityānanda</s> and <s>Gadādhara</s> within —

children.text: ihā kahibāre śakti īśvare se dhare ||
children.translated_text: only the Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) has the power to describe it.
In <s>Gadādhara</s>'s house, the enchanting <s>Gopīnātha</s> —
who is present there as the son of <s>Nanda</s> Himself.
<s>Caitanya</s> Himself embraced Him;

children.text: atibaḍa pāṣaṇḍī se vigraha dekhi bhule ||
children.translated_text: even the greatest atheist, seeing that divine form, would be bewildered.
Seeing the sacred flute-face and the gestures of the body,
<s>Nityānanda</s>'s tears of bliss know no limit.
Knowing of <s>Nityānanda</s>'s arrival, <s>Gadādhara</s>
left off reading the <s>Bhāgavata</s> and came swiftly.
The two, merely seeing each other's sacred faces,
embraced each other and began to weep.
The two Lords offer obeisance to each other;
the two speak of each other's glory.

children.text: duṅhu bole āji haila locana nirmala |
children.translated_text: Both say: 'Today our eyes have become pure.'

children.text: duṅhu bole janma āji āmāra saphala ||
children.translated_text: Both say: 'Today our birth has become fruitful.'

children.text: bāhya jñāna nāhi duṅhu prabhura śarīre |
children.translated_text: Neither of the two Lords has external awareness in their bodies;

children.text: duṅhu prabhu bhāse nija ānanda sāgare ||
children.translated_text: both Lords float in their own ocean of bliss.
Such was the manifestation of <s>prema-bhakti</s>;
seeing it, all the servants fall down weeping in all four directions.
What wondrous love between <s>Nityānanda</s> and <s>Gadādhara</s>!

children.text: ekera apriya āre sambhāṣā nā kare ||
children.translated_text: One who is disliked by one of them — the other does not speak to him.
This is the resolve of <s>Gadādhara Deva</s>:
<s>Nityānanda</s> does not look at the face of anyone who blasphemes [the other].
One who has no love for <s>Nityānanda Svarūpa</s> —

children.text: dekhā jo nā dena tāre paṇḍita gosāñi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Paṇḍita Gosāñi</s> does not give him <s>darśana</s>.

children.text: tabe dui prabhu sthira ha-i eka-sthāne |
children.translated_text: Then the two Lords, becoming steady in one place,
sat down for the auspicious <s>saṅkīrtana</s> of <s>Caitanya</s>.
Now, in the Final Section (<s>Śeṣa-khaṇḍa</s>):
In such a manner, on the shore of the ocean, <s>Śrī Gaurasundara</s>
dances all night, most enchantingly.
<s>Gadādhara</s> ceaselessly remains in His company;
there is never any separation of the Lord from <s>Gadādhara</s>.

children.text: ki bhojane ki śayane kibā paryaṭane |
children.translated_text: Whether eating, sleeping, or wandering,
<s>Gadādhara</s> serves the Lord at every moment.
<s>Gadādhara</s> reads the <s>Bhāgavata</s> before the Lord;
hearing it, the Lord becomes supremely intoxicated with <s>prema-rasa</s>.

children.text: gadādhara vākye mātra prabhu sukhī haya |
children.translated_text: The Lord is happy only by <s>Gadādhara</s>'s words;
He wanders with <s>Gadādhara</s> to the abodes of <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>.
And thus —

children.text: ei mata prabhu priya gadādhara saṅge |
children.translated_text: In this way, the Lord, with His dear <s>Gadādhara</s>,

children.text: tān mukhe bhāgavata kathā śune raṅge ||
children.translated_text: hears the narration of the <s>Bhāgavata</s> from his mouth with delight.
<s>Gadādhara</s> reads the <s>Bhāgavata</s> from his own mouth —
the story of <s>Prahlāda</s> and the story of <s>Dhruva</s>.
Having it repeated a hundred times, He listens attentively;
the Lord never has any other business.
The reading of the <s>Bhāgavata</s> is <s>Gadādhara</s>'s province;
the <s>kīrtana</s> (singing) always belongs to <s>Dāmodara Svarūpa</s>.
The one lord <s>Śrī Dāmodara Svarūpa</s> sings;
the King of <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, becoming overwhelmed, dances.

children.text: aśru kampa hāsya mūrcchā pulaka huṅkāra |
children.translated_text: Tears, trembling, laughter, fainting, horripilation, roaring —
whatever transformations of <s>prema-bhakti</s> exist,
all stand embodied in the Lord's presence.
<s>Caitanya-candra</s> (the moon of <s>Caitanya</s>) dances here with all of them.
In the loud <s>saṅkīrtana</s> of <s>Dāmodara Svarūpa</s>,

children.text: śunile nā thāke bāhya nāce sei kṣaṇe ||
children.translated_text: upon hearing, one cannot maintain external awareness — one dances at that very instant.
And thus —

children.text: ye nā māne bhāgavata se yavana sama |
children.translated_text: One who does not honor the <s>Bhāgavata</s> is the same as a barbarian (<s>yavana</s>);

children.text: tāra śāstā āche prabhu janme janme yama ||
children.translated_text: his punisher, O Lord, is <s>Yama</s> (the god of death), birth after birth.
And thus, in that same [section] —

children.text: sei rātri tathāha thāki tabe āra dine |
children.translated_text: Staying there that night, then the next day

children.text: gṛhe āilena prabhu lakṣmī devī sane ||
children.translated_text: the Lord came home with <s>Lakṣmī Devī</s>.
Together with <s>Śrī Lakṣmī</s>, the Lord, mounted on a swing,
the people of <s>Nadīyā</s> all rush to see.
Fragrance, garlands, ornaments, sandal paste on the crown,
with collyrium, the two shine as <s>Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa</s>.
And thus, in that same [section] —
<s>Kāśīnātha</s>, seeing the royal <s>paṇḍita</s> himself,
brought a seat and offered it with reverence.
With supreme honor, performing the proper formalities,
the <s>paṇḍita</s> asked: 'For what purpose have you come?'
<s>Kāśīnātha</s> says: 'There is a certain matter;'

children.text: citte laya yadi tabe karaha sarvathā ||
children.translated_text: 'if it agrees with your heart, then do it in every way.'
'<s>Viśvambhara Paṇḍita</s> — your daughter —'
'give [her to him]; the match is fitting in every way.'

children.text: tomāra kanyāra yogya sei divya pati |
children.translated_text: 'He is a divine husband worthy of your daughter;'
'and this great <s>satī</s> (chaste woman) is a fitting wife for him.'
'Just as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Rukmiṇī</s> are fitting for each other,'
'so are <s>Viṣṇu-Priyā</s> and <s>Nimāi Paṇḍita</s>.'

children.text: śuni vipra patnī ādi āpta-varga sahe |
children.translated_text: Hearing this, the <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s wife and relatives

children.text: lāgila karite yukti ke budhi ki kahe ||
children.translated_text: began to deliberate — 'who says what with what wisdom?'

children.text: sabhe bulilena āra ki kārya vicāre |
children.translated_text: All said: 'What more is there to deliberate?'

children.text: sarvathā e karma giyā karaha satvare ||
children.translated_text: 'Go and perform this deed at once, in every way.'
And thus, in that same [section] —
Having eaten, on an auspicious, pleasant night —
<s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> remained together in delight. ||
Together with the assembly of <s>Sanātana Paṇḍita</s> —

children.text: ye sukha pāilā tāhā ke pāre barṇite ||
children.translated_text: who can describe the happiness that was obtained? ||
<s>Nagnajit</s>, <s>Janaka</s>, <s>Bhīṣmaka</s>, <s>Jāmbūvanta</s> —
just as they formerly became fortunate — ||
that same fortune, together with the assembly, <s>Sanātana</s>
obtained, by reason of the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> from ancient times. ||
As follows, in the same [source] —
With dancing, singing, instrumental music, and showers of flowers,
in supreme bliss, [they] came by every path. ||

children.text: tabe śubha kṣaṇe prabhu sakala maṅgale |
children.translated_text: Then, at an auspicious moment, the Lord, with all auspiciousness,

children.text: putra vadhū gṛhe ānilena harṣa ha-iyā ||
children.translated_text: brought the son and daughter-in-law to the home with joy. ||
<s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> arrived and sat down in the home.
Cries of 'Victory! Victory!' resounded at that time. ||
Now, in the <s>Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s> as well —

children.text:
bhagavānera bhakta yata śrīvāsa pradhāna
tāṅ'-sabhāra pāda-padme sahasra praṇāma
advaita ācārya prabhura aṃśa-avatāra
tāṅra pāda-padme koṭi praṇati āmāra
nityānanda-rāya prabhura svarūpa-prakāśa
tāṅra pāda-padma vando yāṅra muñi dāsa
gadādhara-paṇḍitādi prabhura nija-śakti
tāṅ'-sabāra caraṇe mora sahasra praṇati
śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya prabhu svayaṃ-bhagavān
tāṅhāra padāravinde ananta praṇāma
children.translated_text:
The devotees of the Lord, foremost among whom is <s>Śrīvāsa</s> —
a thousand prostrations at the lotus feet of their assembly.
<s>Advaita Ācārya</s> is a partial incarnation of the Lord —
tens of millions of prostrations at his lotus feet.
<s>Nityānanda Rāya</s> is the <s>svarūpa-prakāśa</s> (own-form-manifestation) of the Lord —
I worship his lotus feet, whose servant I am.
<s>Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s> and others are the Lord's own potencies (<s>nija-śakti</s>) —
a thousand prostrations at the feet of their assembly.
<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Prabhu</s> is <s>Svayaṃ Bhagavān</s> (the Lord Himself) —
infinite prostrations at His lotus feet.
As follows, in the same [source] —

children.text:
pañca-tattvātmakaṃ kṛṣṇaṃ
bhakta-rūpa-svarūpakam
bhaktāvatāraṃ bhaktākhyaṃ
namāmi bhakta-śaktikam
children.translated_text:
'I bow to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who is the <s>Pañca-tattva</s> (five principles),
who assumes the forms of devotee, devotee-manifestation,
devotee-incarnation, and one called a devotee —
I bow to Him who is endowed with devotee-potency.'
As follows, in the same [source] —
The internal, external, and marginal [potencies] — [they are] so called.
The internal potency (<s>svarūpa-śakti</s>) is foremost among all. ||
<s>Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosāñi</s> is the incarnation of the [internal] potency.
He is reckoned as the internal <s>svarūpa-śakti</s>. ||
As follows, in the <s>Ādi-khaṇḍa</s> (First Division), twelfth chapter —

children.text:
śrī-gadādhara paṇḍita śākhāte mahottama
tāṅra upaśākhā kichu kari ye gaṇana
paṇḍitera gaṇa saba bhāgavata dhanya
prāṇa-vallabha sabāra śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya
ei tina skandhera kailuṅ śākhāra gaṇana
yāṅ-sabā-smaraṇe bhava-bandha-vimocana
yāṅ-sabā-smaraṇe pāi caitanya-caraṇa
yāṅ-sabā-smaraṇe haya vāñchita pūraṇa
ataeva tāṅ-sabāra vandiye caraṇa
caitanya-mālīra kahi līlā-anukrama
children.translated_text:
<s>Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s> is the greatest branch.
I enumerate some of his sub-branches.
The associates of <s>Paṇḍita</s> are all blessed devotees of the <s>Bhāgavata</s>.
The life-beloved of all is <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>.
Of these three trunks, I have enumerated the branches —
by remembering all of whom, the bondage of existence is dissolved.
By remembering all of whom, one attains the feet of <s>Caitanya</s>.
By remembering all of whom, one's desires are fulfilled.
Therefore, I worship the feet of all of them.
I narrate in sequence the pastimes of the gardener <s>Caitanya</s>.

children.text:
tathā hi madhya-khaṇḍe -
caṇḍī-dāsa vidyāpati rāyera nāṭaka gīti
karṇāmṛta śrī gīta govinda
mahāprabhu rātri dine svarūpa-rāmānandera sane
nāce gāya parama ānanda
children.translated_text:
As follows, in the <s>Madhya-khaṇḍa</s> (Middle Division) —
'The songs of <s>Caṇḍīdāsa</s>, <s>Vidyāpati</s>, the dramas of <s>Rāya</s>,
the <s>Karṇāmṛta</s>, the <s>Śrī Gīta-govinda</s> —
<s>Mahāprabhu</s>, day and night, together with <s>Svarūpa</s> and <s>Rāmānanda</s>,
dances and sings in supreme bliss.'

children.text:
purī gosāñira vātsalya mukhya rāmānandera śuddha sakhya
govindādyera śuddha dāsya rase
gadādhara jagadānanda svarūpera mukhya rasānanda
ei cāri bhāve prabhu vaśa

ataḥ śrī-bhagavat-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-devasyāntaraṅga-śakti-varga-mukhyatamaḥ śrī-
gadādhara-paṇḍitaḥ | ataḥ śrī-nīlācale sva-sevādhi-kāritvena śrī-bhāgavata-kathā-
kathanādhikāritvena ca tena sa ca nirūpitaḥ | evaṃ gauḍa-deśa-mukhya-pradeśa-sva-
prakaṭa-sthala-navadvīpe tayā sarva-dhāma-pravara-śrī-vṛndāvane'pi | iti tu śrī-
caitanya-bhāgavate śrī-caitanya-caritāmṛtādau prasiddhaṃ vartate | tatra śrī-
caitanya-bhāgavate śrī-navadvīpa-līlāyāṃ śrīmahāprabhor ājñā -
children.translated_text: Therefore, <s>Śrī Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s> is the foremost of the internal potency-group of the Lord <s>Śrī Bhagavat Kṛṣṇa Caitanya-deva</s>. Therefore, at <s>Śrī Nīlācala</s> (Purī), he was designated by Him as having authority over His personal worship and as having authority over narrating the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>. Similarly, at <s>Navadvīpa</s> — the foremost site of self-manifestation in the principal region of <s>Gauḍa-deśa</s> — and also in the most excellent of all abodes, <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s>. This is well known in the <s>Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata</s>, the <s>Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s>, and the like. Therein, in the <s>Śrī Caitanya-bhāgavata</s>, in the pastimes at <s>Śrī Navadvīpa</s>, the command of <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s> —
At the end, He spoke these words to <s>Gadādhara</s>:

children.text: tumi viṣṇu pūja mora nāhika se bhāgya ||
children.translated_text: 'You should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> — I do not have that fortune.' ||
And also, at <s>Nīlācala</s> (Purī) —
The recitation of the <s>Bhāgavata</s> is the domain of <s>Gadādhara</s>.
The <s>kīrtana</s> (devotional singing) of <s>Dāmodara Svarūpa</s> is constant. ||

children.text:
tatra ca śrī-vṛndāvane śrī-śrī-sevādhikāras tu pūrvaṃ likhito'sti | tathā hi ṣoḍaśa-
paricchede śrī-vṛndāvana-gamane (CC 2.16.130-144)-
children.translated_text: And the authority of worship in <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s> has been written previously. As follows, in the sixteenth chapter, in the journey to <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s> (CC 2.16.130-144) —

children.text:
gadādhara-paṇḍita yabe saṅgete calilā
kṣetra-sannyāsa nā chāḍiha prabhu niṣedhilā
paṇḍita kahe yāhāṅ tumi sei nīlācala
kṣetra-sannyāsa mora yāuka rasātala
prabhu kahe iṅhā kara gopīnātha sevana
paṇḍita kahe koṭi-sevā tvat-pāda-darśana
prabhu kahe sevā chāḍibe āmāya lāge doṣa
iṅhā rahi sevā kara āmāra santoṣaṛ
paṇḍita kahe saba doṣa āmāra upara
tomā-saṅge nā yāiba yāiba ekeśvara
āike dekhite yāiba nā yāiba tomā lāgi
pratijā-sevā-tyāga-doṣa tāra āmi bhāgīṛ
eta bali paṇḍita-gosāi pṛthak calilā
kaṭaka āsi prabhu tāṅre saṅge ānāilā
paṇḍitera gaurāṅga-prema bujhana nā yāya
pratijā śrī-kṛṣṇa-sevā chāḍila tṛṇa-prāya
tāṅhāra caritre prabhu antare santoṣa
tāṅhāra hāte dhari kahe kari praṇaya-roṣa
pratijā sevā chāḍibe e tomāra uddeśa
se siddha ha-ila chāḍi āilā dūra deśa
āmāra saṅge rahite cāha vācha nija-sukha
tomāra dui dharma yāya āmāra haya duḥkha
mora sukha cāha yadi nīlācale cala
āmāra śapatha yadi āra kichu bala
eta bali mahāprabhu naukāte caḍilā
mūrcchita hañā paṇḍita tathāi paḍilā
paṇḍite laā yāite sārvabhaume ājā dilā
bhaṭṭācārya kahe uṭha aiche prabhura līlā
tumi jāna kṛṣṇa nija-pratijā chāḍilā
bhakta kṛpā-vaśe bhīṣmera pratijā rākhilā
children.translated_text:
'When <s>Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s> set out to go along [with the Lord],
the Lord forbade him: "Do not abandon the renunciation of your sacred place."
<s>Paṇḍita</s> said: "Wherever You are, that is <s>Nīlācala</s>.
Let my renunciation of the sacred place go to the underworld!"
The Lord said: "Stay here and serve <s>Gopīnātha</s>."
<s>Paṇḍita</s> said: "Ten million services [are equal to] the sight of Your feet."
The Lord said: "If you abandon the service, fault will attach to Me.
Stay here, serve — that is My satisfaction."
<s>Paṇḍita</s> said: "All faults rest upon me.
I shall not go with You — I shall go to <s>Ekeśvara</s>.
I shall go to see [You at <s>Ekeśvara</s>], not for Your sake.
The fault of abandoning the vow and service — I shall bear that myself."
Saying this, <s>Paṇḍita Gosāñi</s> departed separately.
Coming to <s>Kaṭaka</s>, the Lord brought him along again.
The love of <s>Paṇḍita</s> for <s>Gaurāṅga</s> cannot be understood.
He abandoned his vow and the service of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> as if [they were] a blade of grass.
The Lord was inwardly pleased at his conduct.
Holding his hand, He spoke with affectionate anger:
"To abandon your vow and service — that was your intention.
That has been accomplished — you have left and come from a distant land.
You desire to stay with Me — you seek your own happiness.
Your two religious duties are lost — that causes Me sorrow.
If you desire My happiness, go to <s>Nīlācala</s>.
My oath [stands] — if you say anything more —"
Saying this, <s>Mahāprabhu</s> boarded the boat.
<s>Paṇḍita</s> fainted and fell right there.
The Lord commanded <s>Sārvabhauma</s> to take <s>Paṇḍita</s> back.
<s>Bhaṭṭācārya</s> said: "Rise! Such are the pastimes of the Lord.
You know that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> abandoned His own vow,
[but] out of compassion for the devotee, He upheld the vow of <s>Bhīṣma</s>."'

children.text:
tathā hi sva-nigamam apahāya mat-pratijñāmṛtam adhikartum (BhP 1.9.37) ity ādi
| tathā hi saptama-paricchede (CC 3.7.148-173)-
children.translated_text: As follows — 'Setting aside His own Vedic injunction, [He upheld] the nectar of my vow' (<s>Bhāgavata</s> 1.9.37) — and so forth. As follows, in the seventh chapter (CC 3.7.148-173) —

children.text:
vallabha-bhaṭṭera haya vātsalya-upāsana
bāla-gopāla-mantre teṅho karena sevana
paṇḍitera sane tāra mana phirigela
kiśora-gopāla-upāsanāya mana dila
paṇḍitera ṭhāñi cāhe mantrādi śikhite
paṇḍita kahe ei karma nahe āmā haite
āmi paratantra āmāra prabhu gauracandra
tāṅra ājñā vinā āmi nā ha-i svatantra'
tumi ye āmāra ṭhāñi kara āgamana
tāhātei prabhu more dena olāhanaṛ
ei-mata bhaṭṭera katheka dina gela
śeṣe yadi prabhu tāre suprasanna haila
nimantraṇera dine paṇḍite bolāilā
svarūpa jagadānanda govinde pāṭhāilā
pathe paṇḍitere svarūpa kahena vacana
parīkṣite prabhu tomāre kailā upekṣaṇa
tumi kene āsitāṅre nā dilā olāhana
bhīta-prāya hañā kāṅhe karilā sahana
paṇḍita kahena prabhu svatantra sarvajña-śiromaṇi
tāṅra sane'haṭhakari bhāla nāhi māni
yei kahe sei sahi nija-śire dhari
āpane karibena kṛpā guṇa-doṣa vicāri
eta balipaṇḍita prabhura sthāne āilā
rodana kariyā prabhura caraṇe paḍilā
īṣat hāsiyā prabhu kailā āliṅgana
sabāre śunāñā kahena madhura vacana
ṛāmi cālāiluṅ tomā tumi nā calilā
krodhe kichu nā kahilā sakala sahilā
āmāra bhaṅgīte tomāra mana nā calilā
sudṛḍha sarala-bhāve āmāre kinilāṛ
paṇḍitera bhāva-mudrā kahana nā yāya
gadādhara-prāṇa-nāthanāma haila yāya
paṇḍite prabhura prasāda kahana nā yāya
gadāira gaurāṅgabaliyāṅre loke gāya
caitanya-prabhura līlā ke bujhite pāre
eka-līlāya vahe gaṅgāra śata śata dhāre
paṇḍitera saujanya brahmaṇyatā-guṇa
dṛḍha prema-mudrā loke karilā khyāpana
abhimāna-paṅka dhuñā bhaṭṭere śodhilā
sei-dvārā āra saba loke śikhāilā
antare anugraha bāhye upekṣāra prāya
bāhyārtha yei laya sei nāśa yāya
nigūḍha caitanya-līlā bujhite kā'ra śakti
sei bujhe gauracandre yāṅra dṛḍha bhakti
dināntare paṇḍita kaila prabhura nimantraṇa
prabhu tāhāṅ bhikṣā kaila lañā nija-gaṇa
tāhāṅi vallabha-bhaṭṭa prabhura ājñā laila
paṇḍita-ṭhāñi pūrva-prārthita saba siddhi haila
ei takahiluṅ vallabha-bhaṭṭera milana
yāhāra śravaṇe pāya gaura-prema-dhana
śrī-rūpa-raghunātha-pade yāra āśa
caitanya-caritāmṛta kahe kṛṣṇadāsa
children.translated_text:
'<s>Vallabha Bhaṭṭa</s>'s worship is in the <s>vātsalya</s> (parental) mood.
He serves through the child-<s>Gopāla</s> <s>mantra</s>.
His mind changed through [contact with] <s>Paṇḍita</s> —
his mind became devoted to the worship of adolescent <s>Gopāla</s>.
He wished to learn the <s>mantra</s> and the like from <s>Paṇḍita</s>.
<s>Paṇḍita</s> said: "This task is not within my capacity.
I am dependent — my Lord is <s>Gauracandra</s>.
Without His command, I am not independent.
Even your coming to me —
because of that, the Lord rebukes me."
In this way, some days of <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> passed.
When at last the Lord became well-pleased with him,
on the day of the invitation, He summoned <s>Paṇḍita</s>.
He sent <s>Svarūpa</s>, <s>Jagadānanda</s>, and <s>Govinda</s>.
On the way, <s>Svarūpa</s> said to <s>Paṇḍita</s>:
"To test you, the Lord disregarded you.
Why did you not rebuke him when he came?
Why, being frightened as it were, did you endure it?"
<s>Paṇḍita</s> said: "The Lord is independent, the crest-jewel of omniscience.
I do not consider it good to be obstinate with Him.
Whatever He says, I bear it upon my own head.
He Himself will show mercy, considering virtues and faults."
Saying this, <s>Paṇḍita</s> came to the Lord's presence.
Weeping, he fell at the Lord's feet.
With a slight smile, the Lord embraced him.
Making everyone hear, He spoke sweet words:
"I tried to lead you astray, but you did not budge.
In anger, you said nothing — you endured everything.
Your mind was not moved by My pretense.
With firm, straightforward devotion, you have purchased Me."
The nature of <s>Paṇḍita</s>'s devotional mood cannot be described.
The name '<s>Gadādhara-prāṇanātha</s>' (the Lord of <s>Gadādhara</s>'s life) became established.
The grace of the Lord upon <s>Paṇḍita</s> cannot be described.
People sing of him as '<s>Gadāira Gaurāṅga</s>' (the <s>Gaurāṅga</s> of <s>Gadāi</s>).
Who can understand the pastimes of <s>Caitanya Prabhu</s>?
In one pastime, hundreds upon hundreds of streams of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> flow.
The graciousness, <s>brāhmaṇa</s>-virtue, and quality of <s>Paṇḍita</s>,
the seal of firm love — he made known to the world.
Washing away the mud of false ego, He purified <s>Bhaṭṭa</s>;
through that, He taught all the other people as well.
Inwardly [there was] grace, outwardly [it appeared] like neglect.
One who takes the external meaning is destroyed.
Who has the power to understand the deep pastimes of <s>Caitanya</s>?
He alone understands who has firm devotion to <s>Gauracandra</s>.
On another day, <s>Paṇḍita</s> invited the Lord.
The Lord took His meal there with His own associates.
There, <s>Vallabha Bhaṭṭa</s> received the Lord's command.
From <s>Paṇḍita</s>, all the previously requested perfections were attained.
Thus I have narrated the meeting with <s>Vallabha Bhaṭṭa</s>,
by hearing which one obtains the treasure of love for <s>Gaura</s>.
He whose hope rests at the feet of <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> and <s>Raghunātha</s> —
<s>Kṛṣṇadāsa</s> narrates the <s>Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s>.'
In the <s>Śrī Caitanya-maṅgala</s>, <s>Madhya-khaṇḍa</s> — in <s>Rāga-Baroḍī</s> (the <s>Dhulā-khelā</s> festival) —

children.text:
āra aparūpa kathā śuna gorā-guṇa-gāthā
  loke vede agocara vāṇī
aveśera veśe kara bhakti-yoga paracāre
  karuṇā vigraha guṇa-maṇi
śuna kathā mana diyā āna kathā pāsariyā
  aparūpa kahibāra belā
nija jana saṅge kari śrī-viśvambhara hari
  śrī candraśekhara bāḍi gelā
kathā parasaṅge kathā gopikāra guṇa-gāthā
  kahite se gadagada bhāṣa
aruṇa varuṇa bhela du-nayane bhare jala
  sei rasāveśera vilāsa
kamalā yāhāra pada sevā kare avirata
  hena pahuṅ bhāve gopikāre
parasaṅge haya bhorā hena bhakti kaila tārā
  kathā mātre se āveśa dhare
tabe viśvambhara hari gopikāra veśa dhari
  śrī candraśekharācārya ghare
nācaye ānande bhorā śrīnivāsa hena belā
  nārada āveśe bhela tāre
prabhure praṇāma kare vinaya vacane bole
  dāsa kari jāniha āmāre
e bola boliyā vāṇī tabe sei mahā-muni
  gadādhara paṇḍitere bole
śunaha gopikā tumi ye kichu kahiye āmi
  āpanā marama kichu jāna
apūrva kahiye āmi jagate durlabha tumi
  tora kathā śuna sāvadhāne
āmi to sabhāra kathā kahi śuna guṇa-gāthā
  gokule janmila jane jane
chāḍi nija pati suta sevā kara avirata
  abhimata pāñā vṛndāvane
aichana karili bhakti keho nā jānaye yukti
  parama nigūḍha tina loke
brahmā maheśvara kibā lakhimī ananta-devā
  tatodhika parasāda toke
prahlāda nārada śuka sanātana sa-sanaka
  keho nā jānaye bhakti-leśa
trailokya lakhimī pati tore māge pirīti
  aṅge baraye vara-veśa
lakhimī jāhāra dāsī tora prema prati āśī
  hṛdaye dharaye anurāga
sakala bhuvana pati bhulāili pirīti
  dhani dhani bhāva to svabhāva
torā se jānili tattva prabhura marma mahattva
  priīte bāṅdhili bhāla-mate
uddhava akrūra ādi saba tora pada sādhi
  anugraha nā chāḍiha cite
eteka kahila vāṇī śrīnivāsa dvijamaṇi
  śuni ānandita saba jana
sakala vaiṣṇava mili kari kare kolākuli
  dekhi viśvambharera caraṇa
āchaye ānande bhorā preme garagara tārā
  hena bele āilā haridāsa
daṇḍa eka kari kare sammukhe dāṇḍāyā bole
  guṇa gāya parama ullāsa
hari guṇa kīrtana kara bhāi anukṣaṇa
  ihā buli aṭṭa aṭṭa hāse
hari guṇa gāne bhorā du-nayane bahe dhārā
  ānande phiraye cāri diśe
śuni haridāsa vāṇī sakala vaiṣṇava maṇi
  amṛta siñcila yena gāya
haraṣite nāce gāya mājhe kari gorā rāya
  kāṅdiyā dharaye rāṅgā pāya
tabe sarva-guṇa-dhāma advaita ācārya nāma
āilā sarva vaiṣṇavera rājā
rūpe ālo kari mahī sammukhe dāṅḍāiyā rahi
  prabhu aṃśe janma mahā-tejā
hari hari bali ḍāke camaka paḍila loke
  ānande nācaye prema-bhare
pulakita saba gāya āpāda mastaka yāya
  prema-vāri du-nayane jhare
viśvambhara caraṇe neharaye ghane ghane
  huhuṅkāra māre mālasāṭa
sakala vaiṣṇava mili premera pasarā ḍāli
  pasārila aparūpa hāṭa
children.translated_text: Now listen to another wondrous tale, the song of <s>Gorā's</s> (Gaura's) glories — words beyond the reach of the world and the <s>Vedas</s>. In the guise of ecstatic possession, He propagates <s>bhakti-yoga</s> — the embodiment of compassion, a jewel of virtues. Listen with your mind, forgetting all other topics — it is time to tell wondrous things. Together with His own people, Śrī <s>Viśvambhara Hari</s> went to the house of Śrī <s>Candraśekhara</s>. In the course of conversation, the song of the <s>gopīs'</s> (cowherd-women's) virtues — His voice choked as He spoke. His eyes reddened and filled with tears — this was the play of that ecstatic immersion in <s>rasa</s>. He before whose feet <s>Kamalā</s> (<s>Lakṣmī</s>) ceaselessly performs service — such a Lord was overwhelmed by the sentiment of the <s>gopīs</s>. He became absorbed in the course of conversation — such devotion He displayed, taking on that ecstasy merely upon speaking of it. Then <s>Viśvambhara Hari</s>, donning the garb of a <s>gopī</s>, danced in the house of Śrī <s>Candraśekhara Ācārya</s>, lost in bliss. At that time, <s>Śrīnivāsa</s> became possessed by the spirit of <s>Nārada</s>. He offered prostrations to the Lord and spoke with humble words: 'Know me as Your servant.' Having spoken these words, that great sage then addressed <s>Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s>: 'Listen, O <s>Gopī</s>! Whatever I say — know something of your own inner nature. I speak of something unprecedented — you are rare in the world. Listen carefully to your own story. I speak the story of everyone — listen to the song of [your] glories. In <s>Gokula</s>, person by person, [you] took birth. Abandoning your own husband and sons, [you] served [Kṛṣṇa] ceaselessly, having attained [your] heart's desire in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. Such devotion you performed — no one knows the secret of it, supremely hidden in the three worlds. <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Maheśvara</s>, or <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Ananta-deva</s> — [yet] even greater grace falls upon you. <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Śuka</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, <s>Sanaka</s> and the rest — none of them knows even a fraction of [your] devotion. The Lord of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, the master of the three worlds, seeks love from you, adorning His body with fine garments. <s>Lakṣmī</s>, who is a maidservant [compared to you] — she yearns for your <s>prema</s>, holding love in her heart. You have enchanted the Lord of all worlds with [your] love — blessed, blessed is your nature and temperament! You alone have understood the truth, the inner secret and greatness of the Lord; you have bound [Him] well with love. <s>Uddhava</s>, <s>Akrūra</s>, and all others seek the dust of your feet — do not withdraw your grace from [your] heart.' <s>Śrīnivāsa</s>, the jewel among brāhmaṇas, spoke these words — hearing them, all were filled with joy. All the <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> gathered together, embracing one another, beholding the feet of <s>Viśvambhara</s>. They were immersed in bliss, overwhelmed with <s>prema</s>. At that time <s>Haridāsa</s> arrived. Standing for a moment with folded hands before [the Lord], he sang the glories with supreme delight: 'O brothers, ceaselessly perform <s>kīrtana</s> of <s>Hari's</s> qualities!' — saying this, he laughed loudly and heartily. Absorbed in singing <s>Hari's</s> qualities, streams flowed from his two eyes; in bliss he moved in all four directions. Hearing <s>Haridāsa's</s> words, all the jewels among <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> felt as if nectar were sprinkled on their bodies. Dancing and singing in rapture, with <s>Gorā Rāya</s> (Lord Gaura) in their midst, weeping, they embraced His reddened feet. Then <s>Advaita Ācārya</s>, the abode of all virtues, arrived — the king of all <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>. Illuminating the earth with his form, standing before [the Lord] — born from the Lord's portion, of great radiance. Calling out '<s>Hari! Hari!</s>', the people were struck with wonder; in bliss he danced, filled with <s>prema</s>. Horripilation covered his entire body from foot to head; tears of <s>prema</s> streamed from his two eyes. At the feet of <s>Viśvambhara</s>, he gazed lovingly again and again, roaring loudly, his garlands swinging. All the <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> gathered together, spreading a marketplace of <s>prema</s>, opening a wondrous bazaar.
A song in <s>Gaura-pada</s> (meter celebrating Gaura):

children.text:
holi khelata gaura kiśora
rasavatī nārī gadādhara kora
sveda-bindu mukhe pulaka śarīra
bhāva bhare galatahi locana nīra
vraja rasa gāota narahari saṅge
mukunda murāri vāsu nācata raṅge
kṣaṇe kṣaṇe muruccha-i paṇḍita kora
hera-ite sahacarī sukhe bhela bhora
nikuñja mandire pahuṅ karala bithāra
bhūme paḍi kahe kāṅhā muralī hāmāra
kāṅhā govardhana āra yamunāra kula
nikuñja mādhavī yuthī mālatīka phula
śivānanda kahe pahuṅ śuni rasa vāṇī
yāṅhā pahuṅ gadādhara tāṅhā rasa khāni
children.translated_text: <s>Gaura</s> the youth plays <s>Holī</s> (the festival of colors), with <s>Gadādhara</s> resting in His lap, the woman full of <s>rasa</s>. Drops of sweat on [His] face, horripilation on [His] body — filled with emotion, tears flow from [His] eyes. He sings of the <s>rasa</s> of <s>Vraja</s> in the company of <s>Narahari</s>; <s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Murāri</s>, and <s>Vāsu</s> dance with delight. Again and again <s>Paṇḍita</s> [Gadādhara] faints in His lap; the companions are filled with happiness seeing this. The Lord made His abode in the bower-temple; falling to the ground, He cries: 'Where is My flute? Where is <s>Govardhana</s> and the bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>? Where are the bowers of <s>mādhavī</s>, <s>yūthī</s>, and <s>mālatī</s> flowers?' <s>Śivānanda</s> says: 'O Lord! Hear the words of <s>rasa</s> — wherever the Lord is with <s>Gadādhara</s>, there is the mine of <s>rasa</s>.'
Now [a song] by <s>Ṭhākura Vṛndāvana</s> [Dāsa]:

children.text:
gaurāṅga nāce āpanāra sukhe
yāṅhāra anubhava se se jānaye
  kahane nā yāya śata mukhe
gaurāṅga aṅge śobhe kanayā kadamba
  aichana pulaka ābhā
ānande bhulala ṭhākura nityānanda
  dkehiyā bhāiyāra śobhā
ke jāne kemana o cāṅda vadana
  niśi diśi parakāśe
vāme rahala paṇḍita gadādhara
  ḍāhine narahari dāse
hena avatāre ye jana vañcita
  tāre kṛpā karu nāthe
śrī-kṛṣṇa caitanya ṭhākura nityānanda
  guṇa gāna vṛndāvana dāse
children.translated_text: <s>Gaurāṅga</s> dances in His own bliss — whoever experiences it, that one alone knows; it cannot be told even with a hundred mouths. On <s>Gaurāṅga's</s> limbs shines a golden <s>kadamba</s>-like [splendor] — such is the glow of His horripilation. In bliss, <s>Ṭhākura Nityānanda</s> was enraptured, seeing the beauty of His brother. Who can know the nature of that moon-like face that illumines all directions? On the left stood <s>Paṇḍita Gadādhara</s>, on the right <s>Narahari Dāsa</s>. In this <s>avatāra</s>, those who are cheated [of faith] — show mercy to them, O Lord! <s>Vṛndāvana Dāsa</s> sings the glories of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s> and <s>Ṭhākura Nityānanda</s>.

children.text:
priya gadādhara saṅge kari kautuke kaupīna pari
  veda nigūḍha avatāra
ha-ila ākāśa vāṇī avatāra śiromaṇi
  tribhuvane deya jaya jayakāra
prakāśila ṣaḍ-bhuja dekhila pratāparudra
  o rase vañcita sārvabhaume
saṅge nityānanda rāya vṛndāvana dāsa gāya
  muñi se vañcita gora-preme
children.translated_text: Together with beloved <s>Gadādhara</s>, playfully wearing a loincloth — the <s>avatāra</s> hidden by the <s>Vedas</s>. There was a voice from the sky: 'The crown-jewel of <s>avatāras</s>' — giving victory cries throughout the three worlds. He manifested a six-armed form, which <s>Pratāparudra</s> beheld, but <s>Sārvabhauma</s> was deprived of that <s>rasa</s>. In the company of <s>Nityānanda Rāya</s>, <s>Vṛndāvana Dāsa</s> sings: 'I am deprived of the love of <s>Gorā</s> (Gaura).'
And in the prayer composed by <s>Narottama Ṭhākura</s>:

children.text:
dhana mora nityānanda pati mora goracandra
  deva mora yugala kiśora
advaita ācārya bala gadādhara mora kula
  narahari vilāa ye mora
parama kāruṇya dhāma nitya japa harināma
  śrī-guru vaiṣṇava kari dhyāna
śrī-vaiṣṇava pada-dhuli tāhe mora snāna keli
  tarapaṇa tāṅ sabhāra nāma
hena anumāni mane bhakti rasa āsvādane
  madhyastha purāṇa bhāgavata
vaiṣṇavera ucchiṣṭa tāhe mora ha-u nīṣṭhā
  kuṭumbitā tā sabhāra sātha
vṛndāvane ca-utarā tāṅhā yāṅu nitya tvarā
  mane rahuṅ sevā abhilāṣa
muñi atihīna-jana mora ei nivedana
  kahe dīna narottama dāsa
children.translated_text: My wealth is <s>Nityānanda</s>, my Lord is <s>Goracandra</s> (Gaura), my deities are the youthful divine couple (<s>Yugala-kiśora</s>). <s>Advaita Ācārya</s> is my strength, <s>Gadādhara</s> is my family — <s>Narahari</s> is my delight. The supreme abode of compassion — I constantly chant <s>Harināma</s> (the holy name of Hari), meditating on Śrī <s>Guru</s> and the <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>. My bathing and sport is the dust of the feet of Śrī <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>; their names are my libation (<s>tarpaṇa</s>). Thus I think in my mind — in relishing the <s>rasa</s> of devotion, the <s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> is the impartial [guide]. May my steadfastness be in the remnants of the <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>; my family is in the company of all of them. The <s>Cautarā</s> (raised platform) in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> — there I go constantly in haste, keeping in my mind the desire for service. I am a most lowly person — this is my submission — says the humble <s>Narottama Dāsa</s>.
Now, from the <s>Phāguyā-vasanta</s> narrative (1465) by Śrī <s>Govinda Kavirāja</s>:

children.text:
nīlācale kanakācala gorā govinda phāgu-raṅge bhela bhorā
deva kumārī nārī gaṇa saṅga pulaka kadamba karambita aṅga
phāguyā khelata gaura tanu prema sudhā sindhu murati janu
phāgu aruṇa tanu aruṇahi cīra aruṇa nayāne bahe aruṇahiṅ nīra
kaṇṭhahiṅ lolata aruṇita māla aruṇa bhakata saba gāoye rasāla
kata kata bhāva vitharala aṅga nayana ḍhulāota prema taraṅga
heri gadādhara lahu lahu hāsa so nāhi samujhala govinda dāsa
children.translated_text: In <s>Nīlācala</s> (Purī), on the golden mountain, <s>Gorā</s> (Gaura) and <s>Govinda</s> became absorbed in the play of <s>Phāgu</s> (Holī). In the company of divine and mortal women, His limbs were mixed with <s>kadamba</s>-like horripilation. Playing <s>Phāgu</s>, <s>Gaura's</s> body was as if the embodiment of an ocean of <s>prema</s>-nectar. The <s>Phāgu</s> dye is crimson, His body crimson, His garment crimson, from His crimson eyes flows crimson water. On His throat sways a reddened garland; reddened devotees all sing melodiously. In how many ways are His limbs suffused with emotion! Eyes overflow with waves of <s>prema</s>. Seeing <s>Gadādhara's</s> soft, soft laughter — that <s>Govinda Dāsa</s> could not comprehend.

children.text:
atha vraje yaḥ svayaṃ bhagavataḥ śrī-nanda-nandanasya kāyavyūhya [?] śrī-
balarāmaḥ, yaś ca jagat-kartā mahā-viṣṇuḥ, sarve śrī-prabhoḥ saṅginaḥ śrī-
nityānandādvaitādi-rūpeṇa jātā vartante | tatra pramāṇaṃ śrī-vṛndāvana-
dāsādīnāṃ śrī-caitanya-bhāgavate śrī-caitanya-caritāmṛte ca prasiddham | tatra
śrī-caitanya-bhāgavate-
children.translated_text: Now, He who in <s>Vraja</s> is the <s>kāya-vyūha</s> (bodily expansion) of the <s>Bhagavān</s> Himself, Śrī <s>Nanda-nandana</s> (the son of Nanda) — namely Śrī <s>Balarāma</s> — and He who is the creator of the universe, <s>Mahā-Viṣṇu</s> — all the associates of Śrī Prabhu (the Lord) appeared in the forms of Śrī <s>Nityānanda</s>, <s>Advaita</s>, and others. The evidence for this is well-known in the works of Śrī <s>Vṛndāvana Dāsa</s> and others — in the Śrī <s>Caitanya-bhāgavata</s> and the Śrī <s>Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s>. From the Śrī <s>Caitanya-bhāgavata</s>:

children.text:
ei mata nityānanda bālaka jīvana
vihvala karite lāgilena śiśu gaṇa
māse keo śiśu gaṇa nā kare āhāra
dekhite lokera citte lāge camatkāra
ha-ilena vihvala sakala bhakta vṛnda
sabhāra rakṣaka ha-ilena nityānanda
putra prāya kari prabhu sabhāre dhariyā
karāyena bhojana āpane hasta diyā
kāreo vā bāṅdhiyā rākhena nija pāśe
mārena bāṅdhena mahā aṭṭa aṭṭa hāse
eka dina gadādhara dāsera mandire
āilena tāṅra prīti karibāra tare
gopī bhāve gadādhara dāsa mahāśaya
ha-iyāchena vihvala parānanda maya
mastake kariyā gaṅgā jalera kalasa
niravadhi ḍākena ki kinibe go rasa
śrī-bāla gopālera mūrti tāna devālaya
sarva gaṇe hari dhvani viśāla karaya
huṅkāra kariyā nityānanda malla rāya
karite lāgilā nṛtya gopāla līlāya
dāna khaṇḍa gāyena mādhavānanda ghoṣa
śuni avadhūta siṃha parama santoṣa
bhāgyavanta mādhavera hena divya dhvani
śunite āviṣṭa hana avadhūta maṇi
sukṛti śrī gadādhara dāsa kari saṅge
dāna khaṇḍa nṛtya prabhu kare nija raṅge
gopī bhāve bāhya nāhi gadādhara dāse
niravadhi āpanāre gopī hena vāse
dāna khaṇḍa līlā śuni nityānanda rāya
ye nṛtya karena tāhā varṇana nā yāya
prema bhakti vikārera yata āche nāma
sarva prakāśiyā nṛtya kare anupāma
vidyutera prāya nṛtya gatira bhaṅgimā
kibā se adbhuta bhuja cālana mahimā
kibā se nayana bhaṅgī ki sundara hāsa
kibā se adbhuta saba kemana vilāsa
eke eke kari dui caraṇa sundara
ki se jāḍe jāḍe lampha dena manohara
ye dike cāhena nityānanda prema rase
sei dike kṛṣṇa rase strī puruṣa bhāse
hena se karen kṛpā dṛṣṭi atiśaya
parānande deha smṛti kāro nā thākaya
ye bhakti vāñchaye yogīndrādi muni gaṇe
nityānanda prasāde tāhā bhuñje jane jane
hasti sama jala nā khāila tina dina
calite nā pāre deha haya ati kṣīṇa
eka māsa eka śiśu nā kare āhāra
tathāpi siṃhera prāya sarva vyavahāra
hena śakti prakāśe śrī-nityānanda rāya
tathāpi nā bujhe keho caitanya māyāya
ei mata katho dina premānanda rase
gadādhara dāsera mandire prabhu baise
children.translated_text: In this manner, <s>Nityānanda</s>, whose life was that of a child, began to send the children into ecstasy. For a month, some children did not eat food — seeing which, wonder arose in people's hearts. All the hosts of devotees became overwhelmed; <s>Nityānanda</s> became the protector of all. Treating [them] as if they were [His own] sons, the Lord held everyone and personally fed them with His own hand. Some He tied up and kept at His side; He beat [them] and bound [them], laughing loudly and heartily. One day, He came to the temple of <s>Gadādhara Dāsa</s> to show affection to him. In the mood of a <s>gopī</s>, the great soul <s>Gadādhara Dāsa</s> had become overwhelmed, filled with supreme bliss. Placing a pot of <s>Gaṅgā</s> water on his head, he called out ceaselessly: 'Who will buy <s>rasa</s> (juice/aesthetic nectar)?' The deity in his temple was the image of the child <s>Gopāla</s> (Kṛṣṇa). The entire assembly raised a great cry of '<s>Hari!</s>' Roaring, <s>Nityānanda</s>, the champion wrestler, began to dance in the play of <s>Gopāla</s>. <s>Mādhavānanda Ghoṣa</s> sang the <s>Dāna-khaṇḍa</s> (episode of the toll-tax). Hearing it, the lion-like <s>Avadhūta</s> (Nityānanda) was supremely delighted. What fortunate, divine voice was <s>Mādhava's</s> — hearing it, the jewel among <s>Avadhūtas</s> became possessed. Together with the meritorious <s>Gadādhara Dāsa</s>, the Lord danced the <s>Dāna-khaṇḍa</s> play in His own delight. In the mood of a <s>gopī</s>, <s>Gadādhara Dāsa</s> had no external awareness — he ceaselessly considered himself a <s>gopī</s>. Hearing the <s>Dāna-khaṇḍa līlā</s>, <s>Nityānanda Rāya</s> danced in a manner that cannot be described. Whatever names exist for the transformations of loving devotion — manifesting all of them, He danced incomparably. His dance movements were like lightning — what wondrous majesty in the movements of His arms! What glances of the eyes! What beautiful laughter! What wondrous — what manner of play was all this! One by one, [He moved] His two beautiful feet — what enchanting leaps He made, thud by thud! In whatever direction <s>Nityānanda</s> looked with <s>prema-rasa</s>, in that direction men and women were flooded with the <s>rasa</s> of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. Such was the extraordinary glance of grace He cast that in supreme bliss no one retained bodily awareness. The devotion that the foremost <s>yogīs</s> and sages desire — by <s>Nityānanda's</s> grace, person by person enjoyed it. For three days, [they] did not drink even water like elephants; they could not walk, their bodies became extremely emaciated. For one month, a child did not eat food, yet his conduct was like that of a lion in every respect. Such power did Śrī <s>Nityānanda Rāya</s> manifest — yet no one understands, due to the <s>māyā</s> of <s>Caitanya</s>. In this manner, for many days, in the ecstasy of blissful <s>prema</s>, the Lord resided in the temple of <s>Gadādhara Dāsa</s>.
And in the Śrī <s>Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s> (1.1.7):
<s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, He who lies on the causal waters,
and He who lies on the <s>Garbhodaka</s> ocean, and He who lies on the ocean of milk,
and <s>Śeṣa</s> — all of whom are <s>aṃśas</s> (portions) and <s>kalās</s> (fractions) of Him —
may that <s>Rāma</s> named <s>Nityānanda</s> be my refuge!

children.text:
sei vīrabhadra-gosāñira la-inu śaraṇa
yāṅhāra prasāde haya abhīṣṭa-pūraṇa
śrī-rāmadāsa āra gadādhara dāsa
caitanya-gosāñira bhakta rahe tāṅra pāśa
nityānande ājñā dila yabe gauḍe yāite
mahāprabhu ei dui dilā tāṅra sāthe
ataeva dui-gaṇe duṅhāra gaṇana
mādhava-vāsudeva ghoṣerao ei vivaraṇa
gadādhara dāsa gopībhāve pūrṇānanda
yāṅra ghare dānakeli kaila nityānanda
children.translated_text: I have taken shelter of that <s>Vīrabhadra Gosāñi</s>, by whose grace all desires are fulfilled. Śrī <s>Rāmadāsa</s> and <s>Gadādhara Dāsa</s>, devotees of <s>Caitanya Gosāñi</s>, stayed by his side. When <s>Nityānanda</s> was ordered to go to <s>Gauḍa</s> (Bengal), <s>Mahāprabhu</s> gave these two to accompany him. Therefore both are counted in the retinues of both [Nityānanda and Caitanya]. This is also the account of <s>Mādhava-Vāsudeva Ghoṣa</s>. <s>Gadādhara Dāsa</s>, in the mood of a <s>gopī</s>, was full of bliss — in whose house <s>Nityānanda</s> performed the <s>Dāna-keli</s> (toll-collecting pastime).
And there also:

children.text: mahā-viṣṇur jagat-kartā māyayā yaḥ sṛjaty adaḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Mahā-Viṣṇu</s>, the creator of the universe, who creates this [world] through <s>māyā</s> —
His <s>avatāra</s> (incarnation) indeed is this <s>Advaita Ācārya Īśvara</s>.
In the same [text]:

children.text:
acyutānanda baḍa śākhā ācārya-nandana
ājanma sevilā teṅho caitanya-caraṇa
yei yei bhakta-gaṇa la-ila acyutānandera mata
sei ācāryera gaṇa mahā-bhāgavata
sei sei ācāryera kṛpāra bhājana
anāyāse pāila sei caitanya caraṇa
children.translated_text: <s>Acyutānanda</s>, a great branch, the son of the <s>Ācārya</s> [Advaita] — from birth he served the feet of <s>Caitanya</s>. All those devotees who accepted the view of <s>Acyutānanda</s>, that assembly of the <s>Ācārya's</s> retinue are great <s>Bhāgavatas</s> (devotees). They are the recipients of that <s>Ācārya's</s> grace — effortlessly they attained the feet of <s>Caitanya</s>.
Thus, in the Śrī <s>Caitanya-bhāgavata</s>, final section (<s>Śeṣa-khaṇḍa</s>) (3.4.xx):

children.text:
kṣaṇeke acyutānanda advaita kumāra
prabhura caraṇe āsi haila namaskāra
prema-jale dhuilena tāṅra kalevara
acyutere prabhu nā dhāḍena vakṣa haite
acyuto praviṣṭa hailā caitanya dehete
acyutere dekhi dekhi sarva-bhakta-gaṇa
preme sabhe lāgilena karite krandana
caitanyera yata priya pāriṣada-gaṇa
nityānanda svarūpera prāṇera samāna
gadādhara paṇḍitera śiṣyete pradhāna
ihāṅre se bali yogya advaita nandana
yena pitā yena putra ucita milana
children.translated_text:
In a moment, <s>Acyutānanda</s>, <s>Advaita Kumāra</s>,
came to the feet of the Lord and offered obeisance.
He washed His body with tears of <s>prema</s> (divine love).
The Lord would not release <s>Acyuta</s> from His chest.
<s>Acyuta</s> entered into the body of <s>Caitanya</s>.
Seeing <s>Acyuta</s> again and again, all the devotees
began to weep in <s>prema</s>.
All the dear associates of <s>Caitanya</s> —
<s>Nityānanda</s>, equal to the very life of <s>Svarūpa</s>,
the foremost disciple of <s>Gadādhara Paṇḍita</s> —
he is called the worthy son of <s>Advaita</s>;
as is the father, so is the son — a fitting meeting.

children.text:
kiṃ ca yathā vraje pañca-vidha-sakhī-varga-mukhyābhiḥ śrī-lalitā-viśākhādyābhiḥ
sihitayā śrī-rādhayā saha sukham āsvādyate, tathā śrī-gaura-govinda-devaḥ śrī-
svarūpa-śrī-rāmānanda-rāya-śrī-narahari-sarakāra-prabhṛtibhiḥ saha tat sukham
āsvādyate | tat tu śrī-caitanya-caritāmṛtādau prasiddham eva | tataḥ keṣāṃcit
pārṣadānāṃ pūrva-nāmāni yathā-śrutābhiprāyeṇa prakāśyate | tad yathā-
children.translated_text: Furthermore, just as in <s>Vraja</s>, the bliss is relished by Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> accompanied by the chief ladies of the five kinds of <s>sakhī</s> groups — Śrī <s>Lalitā</s>, <s>Viśākhā</s>, and the rest — so too Śrī <s>Gaura-Govinda-deva</s> relishes that same bliss together with Śrī <s>Svarūpa</s>, Śrī <s>Rāmānanda Rāya</s>, Śrī <s>Narahari Sarakāra</s>, and others. This is well known in the Śrī <s>Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s> and other texts. Therefore, the former names of some associates are disclosed here according to what has been traditionally heard. Namely:
Among the <s>prāṇa-preṣṭha-sakhīs</s> (most beloved companions), she who was formerly <s>Viśākhā</s> in <s>Vraja</s>,
she is now <s>Svarūpa Gosvāmī</s>, the beloved and best of Śrī <s>Caitanya</s>.
As in the Śrī <s>Gaura-gaṇoddeśa</s> (160):

children.text: kalām aśikṣayad rādhāṃ yā viśākhā vraje purā |
children.translated_text: She who formerly taught the arts to <s>Rādhā</s> as <s>Viśākhā</s> in <s>Vraja</s>,
she is now <s>Svarūpa Gosvāmī</s>, endowed with the pastimes of those very <s>bhāvas</s> (spiritual moods).
In the same text (120, 122):

children.text: priya-narma-sakhā kaścid arjuno yaḥ purā vraje |
children.translated_text: He who was formerly a certain <s>priya-narma-sakhā</s> (intimate humorous companion) named <s>Arjuna</s> in <s>Vraja</s>,
he has now become <s>Rāmānanda Rāya</s>, the beloved of the Lord.

children.text: lalitety āhur eke yat tad eke nānumanyante |
children.translated_text: Some say [he was] <s>Lalitā</s>; but others do not accept that.
In the same text (177):
She who formerly dwelt in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> as <s>Madhumatī</s>, a <s>prāṇa-sakhī</s> (life-companion),
she is now the one known as <s>Narahari Sarakāra</s>, the beloved of the Lord.
As in a verse composed by Śrī <s>Rūpa</s>:
She who dwells in Śrī <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, full of <s>rasa</s>, of <s>Rādhā</s> and dark <s>Śyāma</s>,
she who was formerly <s>Madhumatī</s>, of the essence of the <s>rasa</s> of the bliss of the <s>rāsa</s> dance, a follower of the <s>siddha</s> [<s>sakhīs</s>],
he is this Śrī <s>Sarakāra Ṭhakkura</s>, worshiped as the most excellent, the bestower of <s>prema</s>,
an ocean of the bliss of <s>prema</s> — may he be victorious in the land of <s>Śrīkhaṇḍa</s>!
As in a verse composed by Śrī <s>Karṇapūra</s>:
The worthy vessel of the honey-wine of the supreme mercy of Śrī <s>Caitanya Mahāprabhu</s>,
engulfed in the succession of intense <s>prema</s>, his speech blossoming with joy,
who established his abode in <s>Śrīkhaṇḍa</s>, constantly worshiped with sandal-paste in <s>Śrīkhaṇḍa</s>,
I worship a certain great soul born of <s>prema</s>, adorned with the title <s>Madhumati</s>.
<s>Narahari</s>, equal to the life of <s>Gadādhara</s>, is his [associate] even today;
the Lord of the life of both is Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, the Supreme Lord.
This very thing is the secret:
The learned <s>Gadādhara</s>, with hymns filled with the nectar of <s>prema</s>,
having extolled the qualities of the nature of the son of the King of <s>Vraja</s>,

children.text: patre vilihya tad dhīmān prabhoḥ pārśvam upāgataḥ |
children.translated_text: the wise one, having written them on a leaf, approached the side of the Lord.
Knowing him to be filled with shyness and fear, the crown-jewel of omniscients,

children.text: tad-dhastāt patram ānīya stavarājaṃ vilokya saḥ |
children.translated_text: taking the leaf from his hand and beholding the king of hymns (<s>stava-rāja</s>),
the Lord spoke to <s>Paṇḍita</s> with words of reassurance:

children.text: tvayi kṛto mayā pūrvaṃ śakteḥ saṃcāra eva yat |
children.translated_text: 'The transmission of <s>śakti</s> (spiritual power) that I previously performed upon you —
from that, this king of hymns (<s>stava-rāja</s>) has been manifested through your mouth.'

children.text: ity uktvā śrī-stavasyānte sva-nāmāpy alikhat prabhuḥ || iti |
children.translated_text: Having said this, at the end of the illustrious hymn, the Lord also inscribed His own name. Thus.
[Of Śrī <s>Raghunandana Ṭhakkura</s>:

children.text: gopīnāṃ kuca-kuṅkumena nicitaṃ vāsaḥ kim asyāruṇaṃ
children.translated_text: His garment reddened with the <s>kuṅkuma</s> (saffron) from the breasts of the <s>gopīs</s>,
His body golden from the embrace of the <s>rāsa</s> connoisseur whose beauty defeats gold,
horripilation is seen due to the tight embrace of their arms —

children.text: āścaryaṃ sakhi paśya lampaṭa-guroḥ sannyāsa-veṣaṃ kṣitau ||
children.translated_text: O <s>sakhī</s>, behold the wonder — on this earth, the garb of a <s>sannyāsī</s> worn by the master of lovers!
As also in the <s>Vāyu Purāṇa</s>:
All who were formerly women have now become men;

children.text: iti yasmāt kalau viṣṇus tad-arthe puruṣaṃ gataḥ ||]
children.translated_text: since in <s>Kali</s> [yuga] <s>Viṣṇu</s> has assumed a male form for their sake.]

Thus ends the seventh section (<s>kakṣā</s>) of the <s>Bhakti-sādhana-dīpikā</s>, composed by Śrī <s>Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa Dāsa</s>, the follower of the feet of Śrī <s>Haridāsa Gosvāmī</s>, the superintendent of the service of Śrīmad <s>Rādhā-Govinda-deva</s>.
||7||

(8)
Eighth section (<s>kakṣā</s>).
Obeisance to Śrī Śrī <s>Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa</s>.
I repeatedly bow to the pair of lotus feet of Śrīmad <s>Rūpa</s>,
by whose grace even an ignorant person may become possessed of knowledge of his doctrine.
He who, by the command of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, his own home of <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: tyaktvā svargopamaṃ sadya prayāge taṃ dadarśa ha ||
children.translated_text: having abandoned [it] — equal to heaven — at once beheld Him at <s>Prayāga</s>.
Seeing him, supremely delighted, Śrī <s>Śacīnandana Hari</s>,
out of affection, instructed him in the sweetness of the doctrines of <s>bhakti</s>.
The truth of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the truth of <s>bhakti</s>, the truth of <s>rasa</s> — each separately;

children.text: sañcārya śaktiṃ svāṃ tasmin kṛpayā karuṇā-nidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: transmitting His own <s>śakti</s> (power) into him out of mercy, that treasury of compassion,

children.text: punas taṃ kathayāmāsa gaccha tvaṃ vṛndikā-vanam |
