children.translated_text: again spoke to him: 'Go to the forest of <s>Vṛndā</s> (<s>Vṛndāvana</s>);
reveal there the enchanting <s>sevā</s> (worship) of Śrī <s>Govinda</s>.
Of the <s>Bhagavān</s> (Supreme Lord) Himself, who bears the seal of silence —
from the mere sight of Him, <s>prema-bhakti</s> (loving devotion) shall arise in the people.'
'The revelation of the lost sacred sites (<s>tīrthas</s>), and likewise of the scriptures of <s>bhakti</s>,
and the protection of the destitute devotees in every way' —
hearing the words of <s>Mahāprabhu</s>, Śrī <s>Rūpa</s>, afflicted by separation,

children.text: patitvā daṇḍavad bhūmau nanāma ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: falling like a rod upon the ground, bowed again and again.
For the purpose of carrying out the Lord's command, having gone to the interior of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,

children.text: na dṛṣṭvā śrī-vapus tatra cintitaḥ svāntare sudhīḥ ||
children.translated_text: not seeing the Lord's divine form there, the wise one pondered within himself.

children.text: vraja-vāsi-janānāṃ tu gṛheṣu ca vane vane |
children.translated_text: In the homes of the people of <s>Vraja</s>, and in forest after forest,

children.text: grāme grāme na dṛṣṭvā tu roditaś cintito budhaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: village after village — not seeing [Him], he wept, and the wise were worried.

children.text: ekadā vasatas tasya yamunāyās taṭe śucau |
children.translated_text: One day, while he was dwelling on the pure bank of the <s>Yamunā</s>,
a certain beautiful person in the form of a resident of <s>Vraja</s> arrived.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā kathitaṃ tena he yate duḥkhito nu kim |
children.translated_text: Seeing him, that person said: 'O renunciant, are you troubled?'
Hearing his words, his heart drawn by affection,
with a voice deep with <s>prema</s>, having dispelled the fatigue of his mind,
he told him everything — the instruction of Śrī <s>Mahāprabhu</s>.

children.text: sa śrutvā sarva-vṛttāntam āgaccheti dhruvann amum |
children.translated_text: Having heard the whole account, urging him 'Come!',

children.text: gumāṭilā iti khyāte tatra nītvābravīt punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: taking him to the place known as <s>Gumāṭilā</s>, [the Vrajavāsī] spoke again:

children.text: atra kācid gavāṃ śreṣṭhā pūrvāhne samupāgatā |
children.translated_text: 'Here, a certain excellent cow comes in the forenoon;

children.text: dugdha-śrāvaṃ vikurvāṇāpy ahany ahani yāti bhoḥ ||
children.translated_text: she pours forth a stream of milk day after day.'

children.text: sva-manasi vimṛśyaitad ucitaṃ kuru yāmy aham |
children.translated_text: 'Reflecting on this in your own mind, do what is fitting — I depart.'

children.text: śrī-rūpas tad-vacaḥ śrutvā rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca mūrcchitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Śrī <s>Rūpa</s>, hearing his words and seeing his form, fainted.
Then, after a moment, the steadfast one, gathering his courage, reflected;
though he knew the full secret, he acted in conformity with the ways of the world.
He told the residents of <s>Vraja</s>: 'Śrī <s>Govinda</s> is present here!'

children.text: etac chrutvā tu te sarve prema-sambhinna-cetasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Hearing this, all of them, their hearts overwhelmed with <s>prema</s>,

children.text: militvā bāla-vṛddhaiś ca tāṃ bhūmiṃ samaśodhayat |
children.translated_text: gathering together with young and old, cleared that ground.

children.text: yoga-pīṭhasya madhyasthaṃ paśyan taṃ kṛṣṇam īśvaram ||
children.translated_text: Seeing that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the Lord, situated in the center of the <s>Yoga-pīṭha</s> —
directly the son of the King of <s>Vraja</s>, enchanting millions of <s>Manmathas</s> (Cupids) —
they carefully secured that ground, following the command of <s>Rāma</s> (Balarāma).
On the bank of <s>Brahma-kuṇḍa</s>, <s>Vṛndā-devī</s> was revealed.
By the power of the Lord's command, by Śrī <s>Rūpa</s>, the ocean of mercy,
the illustrious <s>sevā</s> was entrusted to my <s>guru</s>, known as <s>Haridāsa</s>.
As also in the Śrī <s>Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s>:

children.text:
paṇḍita gosāñira śiṣya ananta ācārya
kṛṣṇa-prema-maya-tanu udāra mahā ārya
tāṅhāra ananta guṇa ke karu prakāśa
tāṅhāra priya śiṣya paṇḍita haridāsa
children.translated_text:
The disciple of <s>Paṇḍita Gosāñi</s> is <s>Ananta Ācārya</s>,
whose body is filled with the love of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, generous and greatly noble.
Who can reveal his infinite qualities?
His dear disciple is <s>Paṇḍita Haridāsa</s>.
In the same text:

children.text:
sevāra adhyakṣa śrī-paṇḍita haridāsa
yāṅra yaśa guṇa srava-jagate prakāśa
children.translated_text:
The superintendent of <s>sevā</s> is Śrī <s>Paṇḍita Haridāsa</s>,
whose fame and virtues are celebrated throughout all the worlds.
In the same text also:

children.text:
pāñā yāṅra ājñā-dhana vrajera vaiṣṇava-gaṇa
vando tāṅra mukhya haridāsa
children.translated_text:
The <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> community of <s>Vraja</s>, who received his command as their wealth,
I worship their chief, <s>Haridāsa</s>.
May the pair of feet of Śrīmad <s>Rūpa</s> always manifest in my heart,
by a mere particle of whose grace one becomes qualified for <s>rāgānuga</s> [<s>bhakti</s>] (spontaneous devotion).
May Śrī <s>Rūpa-mañjarī</s> bestow her incomparable mercy upon me,
by which the attainment of the lotus feet of the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>) would be obtained.
<s>Svarūpa</s>, <s>Haridāsa</s>, <s>Rūpa</s> and the others, <s>Raghunātha</s>,

children.text: rūpaḥ sanātanaḥ śrīmān janma-janmani me gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rūpa</s>, the illustrious <s>Sanātana</s> — are my refuge birth after birth.

children.text:
tatra akhila-bhagavad-dhāmasu mukhyatama-brahmādi-vandya-lakṣmyādy-aprāpya-
śruty-ādy-anveṣaṇīya-śrīmad-rādhā-govinda-caraṇaika-nilaya-śrīmad-vraja-
maṇḍalācāryaḥ śrī-rūpa eva śrī-rādhikāyāḥ priya-narma-sakhī-vargeṣu śrī-rūpa-
rati-mañjary-ādiṣu mukhyā śrī-rūpa-mañjarī | asyā evānugatye śrī-rādhā-prāṇa-
bandhoś caraṇa-kamalayoḥ keśa-śeṣādy-agamyā iti yā prema-sevā saiva syāt | atra
pramāṇāni śrī-raghunātha-dāsa-gosvāmi-pādānāṃ manaḥ-śikṣāyām-
children.translated_text: There, among all the abodes of the Lord, the foremost — worshiped by <s>Brahmā</s> and others, unattainable by <s>Lakṣmī</s> and others, to be sought through the Śruti and other scriptures — the <s>ācārya</s> of the illustrious <s>Vraja-maṇḍala</s>, the sole abode of the feet of Śrīmad <s>Rādhā-Govinda</s>, is Śrī <s>Rūpa</s> himself. He is the foremost among Śrī <s>Rūpa-rati-mañjarī</s> and others in the groups of <s>priya-narma-sakhīs</s> of Śrī <s>Rādhikā</s> — [namely] Śrī <s>Rūpa-mañjarī</s>. Only through following her does the <s>prema-sevā</s> (loving service) at the lotus feet of the life-companion of Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> — which is inaccessible to <s>Śeṣa</s> and others — become possible. The proofs for this are in the <s>Manaḥ-śikṣā</s> of Śrī <s>Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī</s>:
This excellent elevenfold instruction to the mind (<s>Manaḥ-śikṣā</s>),
whoever sings it aloud in a sweet voice, having attained all purposes,
being in the company [of devotees], a follower of Śrī <s>Rūpa</s> here in the forest of <s>Gokula</s> —
that person obtains the jewel of the incomparable worship of <s>Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa</s>.
In the Śrī <s>Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī</s> (10.1):
For the delight of the illustrious <s>Caitanya-Rūpa</s>, the virtuous one, all this
is written by the power of his command alone — may it so be!
In the Śrīmad <s>Bṛhad-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> (1.1.11):
I am a compilation of the essence of the scriptures of devotion to the Lord,
of what has been experienced in Lord <s>Caitanya</s> in the form of His beloved <s>Rūpa</s>.
In the same text, in the commentary on the first section (1.1.1):
Obeisance to Lord <s>Caitanya</s>, who delights in the nectar of His own name,

children.text: yad rūpāśrayaṇād yasya bheje bhakti-mayaṃ janaḥ ||
children.translated_text: by taking shelter of <s>Rūpa</s> of whom, people attained devotion.
In the same commentary, at the end:
By all these labors of writing of mine, which were set in motion by Himself,
may the illustrious Lord <s>Caitanya-Rūpa</s> be forever pleased!

children.text:
asya ṭīkā-śrīmān caitanyaś caitanya-saṃjñayā prasiddhaḥ śrī-śacīnandanas tat-
svarūpas tan-mūrtir vā bhagavān śrī-kṛṣṇa-devaḥ | pakṣe śrīmān caitanyasya
tasyaiva priya-sevako rūpas tat-saṃjñako vaiṣṇava-varaḥ | tataś ca bhagavān iti |
children.translated_text: The commentary on this: 'Śrīmān <s>Caitanya</s>' — famous by the name <s>Caitanya</s>, Śrī <s>Śacīnandana</s>, whose <s>svarūpa</s> (essential nature) or <s>mūrti</s> (form) is the Lord Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa-deva</s>. Alternatively: 'Śrīmān,' the illustrious; '<s>Caitanya</s>sya' — of that very one, the dear servant called <s>Rūpa</s>, the best among <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s> known by that name. And therefore 'Bhagavān' [is used] thus.

children.text:
āyatiṃ niyatiṃ caiva bhūtānām āgatiṃ gatim |
vetti vidyām avidyāṃ ca sa vāco bhagavān iti || ity abhiprāyeṇeti dik |
children.translated_text:
He who knows the future, destiny, the coming and going of beings,
knowledge and ignorance — he is called <s>Bhagavān</s>. This is indicated by such intentions.

children.text:
yathā bhrātṛ-sambandhe śrī-kṛṣṇa-līlāyāṃ kṛṣṇa-baladevau ca gaura-līlāyāṃ
caitanya-nityānandau ca virājataḥ, tat-tat-parikaratve tat-tad-anusāreṇa rūpa-
sanātanau prasiddhāv eva | yadyapi teṣāṃ madhye bhedaḥ ko'pi nāsti, tathāpi līlā-
śakty-anusāreṇa śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanya-rūpa-pādānāṃ mukhyaṃ matam idaṃ jñeyam
| tathā hi caitanya-caritāmṛte śrī-mahāprabhor ājñā-
children.translated_text: Just as in the brotherly relationship: in Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> <s>līlā</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Baladeva</s>; and in <s>Gaura-līlā</s>, <s>Caitanya</s> and <s>Nityānanda</s> are resplendent. Correspondingly, in their respective associate roles, <s>Rūpa</s> and <s>Sanātana</s> are well known. Although among them there is no difference whatsoever, nevertheless, in accordance with the <s>līlā-śakti</s> (pastime-potency), this principal doctrine of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa-Caitanya-Rūpa</s> should be understood. As in the <s>Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s>, the command of Śrī <s>Mahāprabhu</s>:

children.text:
āji ha-ite nāma duṅhāra rūpa sanātana
dainya chāḍi tomāra dainye phāṭe mora mana
children.translated_text:
From today the names of you two are <s>Rūpa</s> and <s>Sanātana</s>.
Abandon your self-abasement — your humility breaks my heart.
In the Śrī <s>Sandarbha</s> and other texts:
May those two saints, the illustrious <s>Rūpa</s> and <s>Sanātana</s>, be satisfied;
by the southern <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> (<s>Jīva Gosvāmī</s>), this is again carefully examined.
In Śrī <s>Dāsa Gosvāmī's</s> own <s>Sva-niyama-daśaka</s> (1):

children.text:
gurau mantre nāmni prabhu-vara-śacī-garbhaja-pade
svarūpe śrī-rūpe gaṇa-yuji tadīya-prathamaje | ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
'In the <s>guru</s>, in the <s>mantra</s>, in the Name, at the feet of the illustrious son of <s>Śacī's</s> womb,
in <s>Svarūpa</s>, in Śrī <s>Rūpa</s>, in the associated group, in his foremost [disciple]' — and so on.

As follows, at the end of the <s>Śrī Sandarbha</s> — '<s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>' and so forth — the followers of the feet of the Lord <s>Śrī Bhagavat Kṛṣṇa Caitanya-deva</s>, worthy of the honor of the assembly of the universal kings of <s>Vaiṣṇavas</s>.
Therein, [the verse] of the great soul <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja</s> —

children.text:
hā rādhe kva nu kṛṣṇa kva lalite kva tvaṃ viśākhe'si hā
hā caitanya-mahāprabho kva nu bhavān hā śrī-svarūpa kva vā |
hā śrī-rūpa-sanātanety anudinam ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
'Alas, O <s>Rādhā</s>! Where is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>? Where are You, O <s>Lalitā</s>? Where are You, O <s>Viśākhā</s>? Alas!
Alas, O <s>Caitanya Mahāprabhu</s>! Where are You? Alas, O <s>Śrī Svarūpa</s>, where?
Alas, <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>!' — thus daily, and so forth.

children.text:
tatra-
śivānanda senera putra kavi karṇapūra
duṅhāra milana granthe likhiyāchena pracura
children.translated_text:
Therein —
'<s>Kavi Karṇapūra</s>, the son of <s>Śivānanda Sena</s>,
has written copiously about the meeting of those two in his treatise.'
In his <s>Caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭaka</s>, the meeting of those two [is described], as (9.38) —
In time, the accounts of the pastimes in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>
became lost — in order to make them known especially,
the Lord sprinkled with the nectar of His grace
<s>Rūpa</s> and <s>Sanātana</s> right there. ||
Therein, regarding <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> in particular, as (9.29) —

children.text: yaḥ prāg eva priya-guṇa-gaṇair gāḍha-baddho'pi mukto
children.translated_text: He who, though previously deeply bound by the ropes of beloved qualities, was [yet] liberated;

children.text: gehādhyāsād rasa iva paro mūrta evāpy amūrtaḥ |
children.translated_text: though residing in a household, was transcendent like <s>rasa</s>; though embodied, was formless —
with words of love, with embraces of the firmest affection, at <s>Prayāga</s> —
the Lord graced that <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, together with his incomparable [brother]. ||9.29||
Therein, the transmission of potency (<s>śakti-sañcāra</s>), as (9.30) —
In the dear own-form, in the beloved own-form,
in the love-form, in the naturally beautiful form,
in His own matching form, the Lord, in one form,
extended unto <s>Rūpa</s> His own pastime-form. ||
As also in the <s>Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s> —

children.text:
loka-bhiḍa-bhaye gosāñi daśāśvamedha yāñā
rūpa-gosāñike śikṣā karān śakti sañcāriyā
kṛṣṇa-tattva bhakti-tattva rasa-tattva prānta
saba śikhāilā prabhu bhāgavata-siddhānta
children.translated_text:
'For fear of crowds, <s>Gosāñi</s> went to <s>Daśāśvamedha</s> [ghāṭ],
and instructed <s>Rūpa Gosāñi</s>, transmitting potency.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-<s>tattva</s>, <s>bhakti</s>-<s>tattva</s>, <s>rasa</s>-<s>tattva</s> to the end —
the Lord taught all, the conclusions of the <s>Bhāgavata</s>.'
Again, in the same [work], in the narration-summary of the Madhya-līlā —
'Among those, the transmission of potency to <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>.
In the twentieth chapter, the meeting with <s>Sanātana</s>.' ||
Therein, the verse composed by <s>Śrīla Rūpa Pāda</s> —
'This is that very <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, O companion, met at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>;

children.text: tathāhaṃ sā rādhā tad idam ubhayoḥ saṅgama-sukham |
children.translated_text: and I am that same <s>Rādhā</s>; this is the joy of union of both of us.
Yet my heart yearns for the grove on the bank of the <s>Kālindī</s> (Yamunā),
which delights in the sweet fifth note of the flute playing within.' ||

children.text:
mūḍha mora hṛdaya tumi jānilā kemane
eta buli rūpe kailā premāliṅgane
sei śloka prabhu la-iyā svarūpe dekhāilā
rūpera parīkṣā lāgi tāhāre puchilā
mora antara vārtā rūpa jānila kemane
svarūpa kahe tumi kṛpā kariyācha āpane
anyathā e artha kāro nāhi haya jñāna
tumi pūrve kṛpā kariyācha kari anumāne
prabhu kahe mohe ihoṅ prayāge mililā
yogya-pātra jāni ihāṅya mora kṛpā hailā
tabe śakti sañcāriyā kailuṅ upadeśa
tumiha kahiya ihāra rasera viśeṣa
svarūpa kahe yabe ei śloka dekhila
tumi kṛpā kariyācha tavahiṅ jānila ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
'"How did the fool of my heart become known to You?"
Saying this, He embraced <s>Rūpa</s> with loving embrace.
The Lord took that verse and showed it to <s>Svarūpa</s>.
To test <s>Rūpa</s>, He asked him:
"How did <s>Rūpa</s> come to know My inner secret?"
<s>Svarūpa</s> said: "You Yourself have bestowed grace.
Otherwise, no one has knowledge of this meaning.
I infer that You have previously bestowed grace."
The Lord said: "He met Me at <s>Prayāga</s>.
Knowing him to be a worthy vessel, My grace fell upon him.
Then, having transmitted potency, I gave instruction.
You too should tell him the special aspects of <s>rasa</s>."
<s>Svarūpa</s> said: "When I saw this verse,
I understood at once that You had bestowed grace."' And so forth.
By the feet of <s>Śrīmaj Jīva Gosvāmin</s> (in the <s>Śrī Mādhava-mahotsava</s>, 2.106) —
'Me, the most despicable among all people, with a heart full of grace,
having brought to the region near his own lotus-feet,
he who would set me on the paths of his own worship abundantly —
that exalted <s>Rūpa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>-<s>Rūpa</s> (the form of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) — I serve him here.' ||
In the <s>Śrī Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī</s> (commentary on 10.19.16) —

children.text:
gopīnāṃ paramānanda āsīd govinda-darśane iti ṭīkāyām-bhāva-prema-sneha-
praṇaya-māna-rāgānurāga-mahābhāvākhyatayā saptama-kakṣām ārūḍhāyā rateḥ
prapākaḥ śrīmad-anuja-varair viracitojjvala-nīlam anāvalokanīyaḥ |
children.translated_text: 'The supreme bliss of the <s>gopīs</s> was in beholding <s>Govinda</s>' — in the commentary: 'The maturation of <s>rati</s> (divine love) which has ascended to the seventh stage, designated as <s>bhāva</s>, <s>prema</s>, <s>sneha</s>, <s>praṇaya</s>, <s>māna</s>, <s>rāga</s>, <s>anurāga</s>, and <s>mahābhāva</s> — should be examined in the <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> composed by my eminent younger [brother].'

children.text:
tatraiva kṛtvā tāvantam ātmānaṃ yāvatīr gopa-yoṣitaḥ iti ṭīkāyāṃ etac ca śrī-
lalita-mādhavādau mad-anuja-varaiḥ spaṣṭaṃ likhitam | ṭippaṇī ca-so'sau krama-
janmato'nujaḥ paramārthato varaḥ | tathā hi manuḥ-
janmadaḥ brahma-dātā ca garīyān brahma-daḥ pitā |
children.translated_text: In the same [commentary], on 'making Himself as many as the cowherd-women' — in the commentary: 'And this has been clearly written by my eminent younger [brother] in the <s>Śrī Lalita-Mādhava</s> and the like.' The footnote: 'He is younger by order of birth, but eminent in ultimate truth. As <s>Manu</s> [says]: "The giver of birth and the giver of <s>Brahman</s> — the giver of <s>Brahman</s> is the greater, [being] the father."'
And in the <s>Rudra-yāmala</s> —

children.text:
janmadaś ca guruḥ prokto brahmadaḥ paramo guruḥ |
parātpara-gurus tasmāt parameṣṭhī tataḥ param || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
'The giver of birth is called <s>guru</s>; the giver of <s>Brahman</s> is the supreme <s>guru</s>;
the <s>guru</s> beyond the supreme is <s>Parameṣṭhin</s>; and beyond that [is yet higher].' And so forth.
In the <s>Śrī Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</s> (1.2) —
'He who gathers the pastimes of devotion, the disciple
of <s>Prabodhānanda</s>, dear to the Lord —
<s>Gopāla Bhaṭṭa</s>, pleasing <s>Raghunātha Dāsa</s>
and <s>Rūpa</s> and <s>Sanātana</s>.' ||
Authoritative [persons] too have said —

children.text: na rādhāṃ na ca kṛṣṇaṃ vā na gaurāṅgam ahaṃ bhaje |
children.translated_text: 'I worship neither <s>Rādhā</s> nor <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> nor <s>Gaurāṅga</s>;
may I be a dust-particle at the lotus feet of <s>Śrīmad Rūpa</s>, birth after birth.' ||
'Those good people who are devoted to the service of the feet of the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>,
who are supremely relishing in the service of the son of <s>Śrī Nanda</s>, who take shelter of the feet of <s>Caitanya</s> —

children.text: te rūpānugatiṃ sadā vidadhatas tiṣṭhanti vṛndāvane
children.translated_text: they, always following <s>Rūpa</s>, abide in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>;
<s>Śrī Gopāla</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, and others rejoice by his command.' ||
'One who is endowed with the five consecrations should not worship other deities.
Free from <s>jñāna</s> (speculative knowledge) and <s>karma</s> (ritualism) and the like — he is indeed a wise follower of <s>Rūpa</s>.' ||
'The <s>Gāyatrī-mantra</s> pertaining to <s>Rādhā</s>; the <s>mantra</s> of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>; supreme [among them];
the excellent <s>mantra</s> of <s>Mahāprabhu</s>; the <s>Hari-nāma</s> as well;
and the supreme mental service (<s>mānasī-sevā</s>) — these are called the five consecrations.' ||
'<s>Gopāla Bhaṭṭa</s>, <s>Raghunātha Dāsa</s>,
<s>Śrī Lokanātha</s>, <s>Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa</s> —
followers of <s>Rūpa</s>, devoted to the service of the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>,
<s>Śrīla Sanātana</s> and others.' ||
Moreover —
'I bow again and again to the pair of lotus feet of <s>Śrī Sanātana</s>,
by a fraction of whose grace, the <s>rasa</s> of devotion to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> arises.' ||
In the <s>Śrī Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> (1.1) —
'He whose nature is attracted to the name, who by His character always kindles bliss,
who gives the festival of His own form — the <s>Sanātana</s>-self — may the Lord be victorious!' ||
Therein, in the <s>Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</s> (1.1.3) —
'May this Ocean of the Nectar of Devotion (<s>Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</s>)
be always for the delight of my Lord, whose eternal body is the resting-place [<s>Sanātana</s>].' ||
Elsewhere —
'I worship <s>Gopāla Bhaṭṭaka</s>, whose all-in-all is the feet of <s>Govinda</s>,
by whom, at the command of <s>Śrīmad Rūpa</s>, a separate worship was revealed.' ||
'<s>Śrī Rādhā-Ramaṇa-deva</s> is considered the object of worship;
He was fashioned by the meritorious <s>Śrīla Rūpa</s>.' ||

children.text: ājñāyāḥ kāraṇaṃ prāmāṇika-mukhāc chrutam | tat tu prasiddham eva |
children.translated_text: The reason for the command was heard from the mouths of authoritative [persons]. And that is indeed well known.
'I bow to <s>Śrīmad Gopāla Bhaṭṭa</s>, the abode of compassion,
the nephew of <s>Śrīmat Prabodhānanda</s>, a resident of <s>Śrī Vraja</s>.' ||
'I always worship <s>Śrī Jīva</s>, a resident of <s>Vraja</s>,
who is attached to the pair of feet of <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, who gives joy even to the lowly.' ||
'The <s>Rādhā-Dāmodara</s> deity, fashioned by the hand of <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>,
was given by <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, the ocean of compassion, to <s>Jīva Gosvāmin</s>.' ||
'Here are victorious the feet of <s>Śrīmad Bhūgarbha Gosvāmin</s>,
the nephew of <s>Lokanātha</s>, in the <s>Vraja-maṇḍala</s>.' ||
'The <s>Śrīla Raghunātha</s>-named <s>Bhaṭṭaka</s>, dear to <s>Śrīmad Rūpa</s>,
by whom the <s>Vaṃśī-kuṇḍala</s> (flute-earring) was offered to <s>Śrī Govinda</s>.' ||
This is described in the <s>Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s> —
'I worship the excellent <s>Dāsa Gosvāmin</s>, whose body is non-different from <s>Rūpa</s>,
for whom tens of thousands of lives' all-in-all is the pair of feet of <s>Śrī Govinda</s>.' ||
Similarly —
'I worship <s>Śrī Paramānanda Bhaṭṭācārya</s>, the abode of <s>rasa</s>,
and <s>Rāmabhadra</s>, and <s>Vāṇī-vilāsa</s> the instructor.' ||
'I worship those dear to <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, who take shelter of the feet of <s>Śrī Govinda</s>:
<s>Śrīmat Kāśīśvara</s>, <s>Lokanātha</s>, <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa</s>.' || Thus in the <s>Śrī Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī</s>.
'Dearest to <s>Śrī Caitanya</s>, <s>Śrīmad Rādhā-Gadādhara</s> —
the worship of <s>Śrī Govinda</s>, who has the form of His retinue.' ||
'<s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, the ocean of compassion, is the true vessel of true love of those two.

children.text: tat-pāda-kamala-dvandve ratir me syād vraje sadā ||
children.translated_text: May my attachment to his pair of lotus feet always remain in <s>Vraja</s>.' ||
'The <s>Paṇḍita</s> named <s>Śrīmad Gaurīdāsa</s> is an associate of <s>Hari</s>,
full of love for <s>Caitanya</s> and <s>Paṇḍita Śrī Gadādhara</s>.' ||
'Therefore, <s>Śrī Hṛdayānanda Caitanya</s>, His servant,
was asked [for] and personally taken [by him], manifesting that friendship.' ||
'The ocean of compassion gave him the authority of his own worship —
whom they call <s>Śrīmad Gaurīdāsa</s>, [who is] <s>Śrī Subala</s>.' ||
Of <s>Śrī Karṇapūra Gosvāmin</s> (in the <s>Ārya-śataka</s>, 1) —
'A blue lotus for the ears, collyrium for the eyes,
a great sapphire necklace for the chest —
the all-ornament of the women of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> —
<s>Hari</s> is victorious!' ||
In the <s>Śrī Muktā-carita</s> (4) —
'By the strength of association with whom, by me
the wondrous story of the finest pearl was propagated —
may association with that king of poets, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, in <s>Vraja</s>
be mine in every birth.' ||
Of <s>Śrī Karṇapūra Gosvāmin</s> — 'Here shines the master of <s>Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa Kuṇḍa</s>' — and so forth.
'I [bow to] the one named <s>Śrī Premī Kṛṣṇadāsa</s>, the infinite supreme <s>guru</s>,
by a mere fraction of whose grace, devotion to <s>Śrī Govinda</s> arises.' ||
'By the force of the Lord's command, by <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, the ocean of compassion,
the worship was entrusted to my <s>guru</s> named <s>Haridāsa</s>.' ||
'He by whose service the glorious <s>Govinda</s>, the son of <s>Nanda</s>, is under control —
the ocean of compassion [who] asks the devotee for [an offering of] milk.' ||

children.text:
kiṃ cāsmin kadācid vasanta-vāsarāvasare rātrau rāsa-maṇḍale bhramati sati
saṃcāriṇyāḥ śrī-vṛṣabhānu-sutāyā āścarya-rūpaṃ dṛṣṭvā tamālasya mūle
mūrcchitavān iti prasiddhiḥ |
children.translated_text: Moreover, once, on the occasion of a spring day, at night, while revolving in the <s>rāsa-maṇḍala</s>, having beheld the wondrous form of the wandering daughter of <s>Śrī Vṛṣabhānu</s>, he fainted at the foot of a <s>tamāla</s> tree — thus it is well known.
'That [<s>Haridāsa</s>] himself is the attendant-servant of that beloved [<s>Rādhā</s>],

children.text: tayoś ca dāsaḥ kila ko'pi nāmnā |
children.translated_text: and [there is] indeed someone named a servant of those two —
he makes effort for the entry of the minds of his own people
into the service of those two.' ||
'The glorious and valiant <s>Māna-siṃha</s>, the king,
devoted to the worship of the feet of <s>Govinda</s>, a devotee at the lotus feet of <s>Caitanya</s>.' ||
'<s>Pratāparudra</s>, whose mind was attached to the worship of majesty of <s>Hari</s> —
this king, whose mind was seized by longing for the worship of sweetness.' ||
'By whom the construction of the great temple was caused to be made with effort.
Even today, the kings of that dynasty are devoted to the Lord.' ||
Of <s>Śrī Raghunātha Gosvāmin Pāda</s> (in the <s>Prārthanāmṛta</s>) —
'Greedy solely for the foot-service of <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> and <s>Rati-mañjarī</s> —
may my dwelling in <s>Vraja</s> be constant, even through countless births!' ||
Furthermore, following the <s>Gaura-gaṇoddeśa</s> (enumeration of <s>Gaura</s>'s associates) stated by <s>Śrī Karṇapūra Gosvāmin</s>, the former names of some [associates] are written (180-184) —
'She who was formerly known as <s>Śrī Rūpa-mañjarī</s> in <s>Vṛndāvana</s> —
having now become the <s>Gosvāmin</s> named <s>Rūpa</s>, has attained manifestation.' ||
is now <s>Sanātana</s>, whose body is non-different from <s>Gaura</s>, worshippable by all.'
'A certain scholar called him <s>Śrī Lavaṅga-mañjarī</s>.'
'She who was <s>Anaṅga-mañjarī</s> is now <s>Gopāla Bhaṭṭaka</s>.'
'Some call <s>Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmin</s> <s>Śrī Guṇa-mañjarī</s>.' ||
'She who was formerly <s>Rati-mañjarī</s>, dearest to <s>Rūpa-mañjarī</s> —
'The <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> named <s>Raghunātha</s> was formerly <s>Rāga-mañjarī</s>.'
'[He] who made a small dwelling at <s>Śrī Rādhikā-kuṇḍa</s> — of the Lord,' ||
'<s>Dāsa Raghunātha</s>'s former [name] was <s>Rasa-mañjarī</s>.'
'Of <s>Bhūgarbha Ṭhakkura</s>, the former [name] was <s>Prema-mañjarī</s>.'
'The <s>Gosvāmin</s> named <s>Lokanātha</s> was formerly <s>Śrī Līlā-mañjarī</s>.' ||
'<s>Śivānanda Cakravartī</s> was formerly <s>Lavaṅga-mañjarī</s>.' ||
In the <s>Śrī Rādhā-Kṛṣṇa-gaṇoddeśa</s> —
'<s>Kalāvatī</s>, <s>Rasollāsā</s>, <s>Guṇatuṅgā</s>, residing in <s>Vraja</s> —
they are considered as always singing the song composed by <s>Śrī Viśākhā</s>.' ||
'<s>Govinda</s>, <s>Mādhavānanda</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, in order —'
<s>Rāga-Lekhā</s> and <s>Kalā-Keli</s> are <s>Rādhā</s>'s maidservants, formerly established.

children.text:
etāḥ khalu pūrvāparair dehair abhinnāḥ śrī-vṛṣabhānujāyāḥ priya-narma-sakhyo'pi
pāda-mardana-payodānābhisārādikaṃ paricārikā iva kurvanti yathā stavāvalyāṃ
(vraja-vilāsa-stave)-svābhilaṣita-paricaraṇa-viśeṣa-lābhāya raṅgaṇa-vallī-raṅgaṇa-
mālā-prabhṛtayaḥ | etāḥ parama-praṇayi-sakhyo'pi paricārikā iva vyavaharanti |
children.translated_text: These, though <s>priya-narma-sakhīs</s> (intimate joking companions) of the daughter of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>, who are non-different from Her in their earlier and later bodies, perform foot-massage, water-offering, tryst-arrangement, and the like, just as maidservants do. As in the <s>Stavāvalī</s> (<s>Vraja-Vilāsa-Stava</s>): '<s>Raṅgaṇa-Vallī</s>, <s>Raṅgaṇa-Mālā</s>, and others [perform these services] for the attainment of their specifically desired service.' These supremely loving companions also behave as maidservants.
In the <s>Śrī Govinda-Līlāmṛta</s> (1.86):
From the edge of the bed, picking up the bodice, <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s>,
the <s>priya-narma-sakhī</s>, secretly went out and gave it to the [other] <s>sakhīs</s>.

children.text:
yat tu śrī-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikādau dāsītvenoktam asti | tat tu svayaṃ grantha-kṛtatvād
dainyenoktiḥ smaraṇa-maṅgala-daśa-ślokī-vaiṣṇava-raṅga-bhāṣye dhṛtā | śrī-
govinda-līlāmṛte varṇanaṃ yathā (23.89-91)-
children.translated_text: The fact that she is described as a maidservant (<s>dāsī</s>) in the <s>Śrī Gaṇoddeśa-Dīpikā</s> and elsewhere — that is a statement of humility, since the author is writing about himself. [This interpretation] is upheld in the commentary on the <s>Smaraṇa-Maṅgala-Daśa-Ślokī</s>. The description in the <s>Śrī Govinda-Līlāmṛta</s> is as follows (23.89–91):
<s>Śrī Rūpa</s> and <s>Rati Mañjarī</s> performed foot-massage for the two;

children.text: cakratuś cāparā dhanyā vyajanais tāv avījayan ||
children.translated_text: and other blessed ones fanned Them with fans.
After serving Them for a moment, they went out from the love-pavilion;

children.text: sakhyas tāḥ suṣupuḥ sve sve kalpa-vṛkṣa-latālaye ||
children.translated_text: those <s>sakhīs</s> slept in their own resting-places among the wish-fulfilling trees and vines.
<s>Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī</s> and the other <s>sakhīs</s> devoted to service
slept happily on the terrace outside that pastime-pavilion.
<s>Mañjarī</s>, beginning with <s>Rūpa</s>, is an intimate companion equal to <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>'s very life;
famous is the one beginning with <s>Anaṅga</s> (i.e., <s>Anaṅga Mañjarī</s>), renowned as dearer than life to Her;
well-known is <s>Hari-Priyā</s>, who in following the lotus feet of that [<s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s>],
yearns greatly for those lotus feet — [she is] <s>Mañjarī</s> beginning with <s>Rāsa</s> (i.e., <s>Rāsa Mañjarī</s>).
Moreover —
<s>Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī</s> — her follower is <s>Anaṅga Mañjarī</s>;

children.text: haripriyāś ca tāḥ santu rāsa-mañjarikā hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: may <s>Hari-Priyā</s> and <s>Rāsa Mañjarikā</s> abide in my heart.
Now, the <s>Śrī Rūpa-Mañjarī-Aṣṭaka</s> (Eight Verses to <s>Śrī Rūpa Mañjarī</s>):
She who is unattainable to the multitude of people whose minds are imbued with the conception of <s>aiśvarya</s> (divine majesty),
the beloved expert in bestowing the jewel of the path of manifest <s>rāga</s> (spontaneous attachment);
a cage for the parrot-sport in the cowshed-gathering with the beloved and her friends —
may <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> eternally accept me. //1//
With compassionate thought toward human beings devoid of <s>bhakti</s>,
with mercy naturally manifesting from a mind always elevated,
a cascade overflowing with the nectar of the activities of the moon of the cowshed (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) —
may <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> eternally accept me. //2//
The group of <s>sakhīs</s> of <s>Vṛṣabhānu</s>'s daughter, sprinkled with the honey of good character,
a mind surging with constant, respective, favorable deeds;
auspicious in every way toward dull-witted ones like me —
may <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> eternally accept me. //3//
Having come to the forest of <s>Vṛndā</s> by the command of <s>Gauracandra</s>,
the sole life of the saintly circle of travelers on the path of <s>rāga</s>;
a wish-fulfilling vine for fulfilling the desires of devotees throughout the world —
may <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> eternally accept me. //4//
A pure mine of good qualities such as steadfastness, depth, and the like;
the heart-jewel of the son of <s>Vrajendra</s>, colored by her own <s>rāga</s> (attachment);
the eternal maidservant of <s>Rādhikā</s>, the upholder of the mountain (<s>Girīndra-dhārī</s>) —
may <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> eternally accept me. //5//
Those good souls who reside at the shelter of her lotus feet —
a mind ever anxious to bestow upon them their heart's desire;
regarded as a sister by all the beautiful cowherd women —
may <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> eternally accept me. //6//
Trembling within, agitated by the bee of mature devotional ecstasy,
yet always bashful when adopting worldly conventions;
a <s>jhallarī</s> (small drum) proclaiming <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s glories that shame clusters of <s>kunda</s> flowers —
may <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> eternally accept me. //7//
With the treasure of all secret, charming love-sports and their descriptions,
with the treasure received from the satisfied <s>sakhīs</s> and rival <s>gopīs</s>;
a dance-performance (<s>carcarī</s>) of dancing in the arena with the desired <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> together with them —
may <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s> eternally accept me. //8//
One who reads this excellent set of eight [verses], indicative of merely a fraction of <s>Rūpa Mañjarī</s>'s qualities,
understanding the essence of one's own purpose,
by the pleased <s>Rādhikā</s>'s most beloved (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>), together with His beloved —
fitness for the service of Their lotus feet is given to that person. //9//
Moreover —

children.text: matād bahiṣkṛtā ye ca śrī-rūpasya kṛpāmbudheḥ |
children.translated_text: Those who are expelled from the doctrine of <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, the ocean of mercy —

children.text: teṣu saṅgo na kartavyo rāgādhva-pathikaiḥ khalu ||
children.translated_text: association with them should indeed not be kept by travelers on the path of <s>rāga</s>.

children.text: teṣām annaṃ phalaṃ mūlam anya-dānādikaṃ ca yat |
children.translated_text: Their food, fruits, roots, and other gifts and the like

children.text: nāśitavyaṃ na pātavyaṃ prāṇaiḥ kaṇṭha-gatair api ||
children.translated_text: should be thrown away, should not be consumed, even if life reaches the throat.
Others too, because of mere absence of firm commitment in their own domain,
who have no recourse whatsoever, devoted to the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> —

children.text: rupeti nāma vada bho rasane sadā tvaṃ
children.translated_text: 'O tongue, always speak the name <s>Rūpa</s>!'
'O mind, remember <s>Rūpa</s>, the embodiment of compassion!'
'O head, bow to <s>Rūpa</s>, of gracious glance —'
'and to his peerless second body, <s>Raghunātha Dāsa</s>.'

children.text: yadi janma hy anekaṃ syāt śrī-rūpa-caraṇāśayā |
children.translated_text: Even if there be many births, may they be at the shelter of <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>'s feet;

children.text: tac ca svīkṛtam asmābhir nānyat śīghram ihāpi ca ||
children.translated_text: that is accepted by us — nothing else, swiftly, here too.
May <s>Hari-Priyā</s>, filled with the grace of <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> and <s>Anaṅga Mañjarī</s>,
always flash forth in my heart by her mercy, for I have no other refuge.

Thus concludes the <s>Sādhana-Dīpikā</s>,
uttered by <s>Rādhākṛṣṇadāsa</s>, the humble follower of the feet of <s>Śrī Haridāsa Gosvāmī</s>, the chief of the service of <s>Śrī Govinda Deva</s>.
Thus the eighth section (<s>kakṣā</s>).
//8//

(9)
Ninth Section (<s>Kakṣā</s>)
Now the principal <s>tattva</s> (reality) is ascertained. In the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> (1.2.11):

children.text: vadanti tat tattva-vidas tattvaṃ yaj jñānam advayam |
children.translated_text: The knowers of <s>tattva</s> declare that <s>tattva</s> which is non-dual knowledge,
designated as <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Paramātman</s>, and <s>Bhagavān</s>.

children.text:
atra tat-tattva-trayeṣu bhagavān eva mukhyaḥ | bhagavān svayaṃ bhagavān | sa tu
śrī-kṛṣṇo vrajendra-nandano govinda eva | tatra pramāṇam-
children.translated_text: Here, among those three aspects of <s>tattva</s>, <s>Bhagavān</s> alone is the principal. <s>Bhagavān</s> is <s>Svayaṃ Bhagavān</s> (the Lord Himself). And He is none other than <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>, the son of the king of <s>Vraja</s>, <s>Govinda</s>. The evidence for this:
The Supreme Lord (<s>Īśvara</s>) is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, whose form is existence-consciousness-bliss (<s>saccidānanda</s>);
beginningless, the origin, <s>Govinda</s> is the cause of all causes. //1//

children.text: yat tu brahma, tad asyaiva prabhā-rūpam, yathā-
children.translated_text: As for <s>Brahman</s>, it is the effulgence-form (<s>prabhā-rūpa</s>) of this very [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], as follows:
He whose effulgence (<s>prabhā</s>), of the effulgent one, in the tens of millions
of cosmic eggs, is variegated with the limitless glories of earths and the like —
I worship that <s>Brahman</s>, undivided, infinite, all-encompassing —
that <s>Govinda</s>, the primeval Person. //40//

children.text: tatra bhagavad-gītā brahmaṇo hi pratiṣṭhāham ity ādi |
children.translated_text: Therein, the <s>Bhagavad-Gītā</s> [says]: 'For I am the foundation of <s>Brahman</s>' — and so forth.

children.text: yaś ca paramātmā sa tu asya bhagavato'ṃśāṃśa-rūpaḥ, yathā dvitīye (2.2.8)-
children.translated_text: And the <s>Paramātman</s> is a partial-part form (<s>aṃśāṃśa-rūpa</s>) of this Lord, as in the Second [Canto] (2.2.8):
Some [yogis] remember, through meditation, the Person dwelling
within the heart-space of their own body, of a thumb's measure,
four-armed, bearing lotus, discus, conch,
and mace.

children.text:
kṛṣṇa-brahmaṇor aikyam (BRS 2.3.218) kiraṇārokopamājuṣoḥ ity ādeḥ | atas tat-
tattva-trayeṣu parama-tattva-rūpasya svayaṃ-bhagavato mukhyatvaṃ dṛśyate | tasmād
yoga-trayeṣu bhakti-yoga eva mukhyaḥ | sa tu anyābhilāṣitā-śūnyam ity ādua

children.translated_text: is accepted as the highest. As in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> (11.11.48):

The identity of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and <s>Brahman</s> [is established in] (<s>BRS</s> 2.3.218): 'of those related as ray and radiance' — and so forth. Therefore, among those three aspects of <s>tattva</s>, the principal status of <s>Svayaṃ Bhagavān</s>, who is the supreme <s>tattva</s> in form, is seen. Therefore, among the three <s>yogas</s>, <s>bhakti-yoga</s> alone is the principal. And that, beginning with 'devoid of desires for anything other [than devotion],'

children.text:
prāyeṇa bhakti-yogena sat-saṅgena vinoddhava |
nopāyo vidyate samyak prāyaṇaṃ hi satām aham || ity ādeḥ |
children.translated_text:
'Generally, O <s>Uddhava</s>, without <s>bhakti-yoga</s> and the association of saints,
there is no proper means — for I am indeed the goal of the saintly.' — and so forth.
In the <s>Bhakti-Rasāmṛta-Sindhu</s> 1.2.1, 5

children.text: sā bhaktiḥ sādhanaṃ bhāvaḥ premā ceti tridhoditā |
children.translated_text: That <s>bhakti</s> is said to be threefold: <s>sādhana</s> (practice), <s>bhāva</s> (ecstatic emotion), and <s>prema</s> (pure love).

children.text: vaidhī rāgānugā ceti sā dvidhā sādhanābhidhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vaidhī</s> (regulated) and <s>rāgānugā</s> (following spontaneous attachment) — thus <s>sādhana</s> is twofold.
Therein, the principality of <s>rāgānugā</s>, as follows (<s>BRS</s> 1.2.281):

children.text: rāga-bandhena kenāpi taṃ bhajanto vrajanty amī |
children.translated_text: Those who worship Him bound by some <s>rāga</s> (spontaneous attachment) — they go [to Him];
the nectar of His lotus feet — they are His dear ones, in the form of <s>prema</s>.
'The excellence [of <s>rati</s>] attains its specificity from the specificity of the recipient.' (<s>BRS</s> 2.5.1)
The definition of following one's appropriate form, [as stated] by the feet of <s>Śrīmat Prabhu</s> (<s>BRS</s> 1.2.270):
That which follows the <s>rāgātmikā</s> [devotion] that is manifest
and shining in the residents of <s>Vraja</s> and others — that is called <s>rāgānugā</s>.

children.text: iti pūrvaṃ vicāritam asti | śrībhāgavate ca (10.14.32)-
children.translated_text: This has been discussed before. And in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> (10.14.32):
Ah, what fortune, what fortune of <s>Nanda</s> the cowherd and the residents of <s>Vraja</s>!
Whose friend is the Supreme Bliss, the complete, eternal <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text:
atha rāgānugā sā dvidhā sambandhānugā kāmānugā ca | tatra kāmānugā
mukhyā | sā dvidhā sambhogecchāmayī tat-tad-bhāvecchāmayī ca |
children.translated_text: Now, that <s>rāgānugā</s> is twofold: <s>sambandhānugā</s> (following relationship) and <s>kāmānugā</s> (following desire). Therein, <s>kāmānugā</s> is the principal. It is twofold: <s>sambhogecchāmayī</s> (desire for direct enjoyment) and <s>tat-tad-bhāvecchāmayī</s> (desire for the respective mood).
That which has its purport in amorous play — that is <s>sambhogecchāmayī</s>;
that which has the nature of desiring their mood and sweetness — that is <s>tat-bhāvecchātmikā</s>. (<s>BRS</s> 1.2.299)

children.text:
tatrādhikārī-
śrī-mūrter mādhurīṃ prekṣya tat-tal-līlāṃ niśamya vā |

children.translated_text: those who desire that mood — for them, the two kinds of <s>sādhana</s> [apply].' (<s>BRS</s> 1.2.3)

Therein, the qualified aspirant:
'Seeing the sweetness of the sacred form, or hearing of His various pastimes,

children.text: matto'sya sukhaṃ bh ād iti sambhogecchāmayī | matto'nayoḥ sukhaṃ bhūyād iti tat-

children.translated_text: <s>tat-tad-bhāvecchāmayī</s> — thus is the distinction between the two. As in the <s>Śrīmad Bhāgavata</s> (10.44.14):
'May my happiness arise from Him' — this is <s>sambhogecchāmayī</s>. 'May the happiness of these two arise from me' — this is

children.text: gopyas tapaḥ kim acaran yad amuṣya rūpaṃ
children.translated_text: What austerity did the <s>gopīs</s> perform, that they [can drink in] the form of this one,
the essence of beauty, unsurpassed and unequaled, achieved by no other,
with their eyes sipping at every moment [His] ever-fresh, hard-to-attain [beauty],
the sole abode of fame, beauty, and lordship!

children.text: trailokye pṛthivī dhanyā yatra vṛndāvanaṃ purī |
children.translated_text: In the three worlds, the earth is blessed, where the city of <s>Vṛndāvana</s> is;

children.text: tatrāpi gopikāḥ pārtha tatra rādhābhidhā mama ||
children.translated_text: there, the <s>gopikās</s>, O <s>Pārtha</s> — among them, she who is called <s>Rādhā</s> is Mine.

children.text:
śrī-bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhau (2.5.38) ca-yathottaram asau ity ādi, ity uddhavādayo'py
etaṃ vāñchati bhagavat-priyāḥ | (1.2.286) iti | tad yathā (BhP 10.47.61)-
children.translated_text: And in the <s>Śrī Bhakti-Rasāmṛta-Sindhu</s> (2.5.38): 'each successive one is greater' — and so forth. 'Thus <s>Uddhava</s> and others too desire this — they who are dear to the Lord.' (1.2.286). Namely thus (<s>BhP</s> 10.47.61):
Oh, may I be any of the bushes, vines, or herbs
in <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, sprinkled by the dust of the feet of these [<s>gopīs</s>],

children.text: yā dustyajaṃ sva-janam ārya-pathaṃ ca hitvā
children.translated_text: who, abandoning their hard-to-abandon families and the path of propriety,
worshiped the path of <s>Mukunda</s>, sought by the <s>śrutis</s>.
The hymn of <s>Brahmā</s> (<s>BhP</s> 10.14.34):

children.text:
tad bhūri-bhāgyam iha janma kim apy aṭavyāṃ
yad gokule'pi katamāṅghri-rajo'bhiṣekam | ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
'What great fortune is any birth in this forest,
where [one attains] the bathing in the foot-dust of some [person or other] in <s>Gokula</s>!' — and so forth.

children.text:
ato vraja-vāsi-janādiṣu virājamānāyā rāgātmikāyā mukhyatvena rāgānugāyā
mukhyatvam | tad-anusāratvāt | asyām eva rāgānugāyāṃ gṛhasthodāsīna-
bhedenādhikāriṇo dvividhā dṛśyante | tatra udāsīnā mukhyāḥ | tad yathā śrī-
nārada-vākye (BhP 1.5.5)-
children.translated_text: Therefore, because of the principality of the <s>rāgātmikā</s> [devotion] shining forth in the residents of <s>Vraja</s> and others, the principality of <s>rāgānugā</s> [follows] — because of following that. In this very <s>rāgānugā</s>, the qualified aspirants are seen to be of two kinds, differentiated as householders and renunciants. Therein, the renunciants are the principal. Namely thus, in the words of <s>Śrī Nārada</s> (<s>BhP</s> 1.5.5):

children.text:
tat sādhu manye'sura-varya dehināṃ
sadā samudvigna-dhiyām asad-grahāt |
hitvātma-pātaṃ gṛham andha-kūpaṃ
vanaṃ gato yad dharim āśrayeta || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
'That I consider good, O best of <s>asuras</s>, for embodied beings
whose minds are always disturbed due to grasping at the unreal —
abandoning the home, a blind well leading to self-destruction,
going to the forest, where one may take refuge in <s>Hari</s>.' — and so forth.

children.text:
kiṃ vāsanaṃ te garuḍāsanāya
kiṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ kaustubha-bhūṣaṇāya |
lakṣmī-kalatrāya kim asti deyaṃ
vāgīśa kiṃ te vacanīyam āste || ity ādeḥ |
children.translated_text:
'What garment is [needed] for the one whose seat is <s>Garuḍa</s>?
What ornament for the one whose ornament is the <s>Kaustubha</s>?
What is there to give to the one whose consort is <s>Lakṣmī</s>?
O Lord of speech, what remains for you to say?' — and so forth.

children.text:
aiśvarya-mādhuryānubhavi-bhaktānāṃ divivdhatve'pi punaś caturvidhā bhaktāḥ
śrī-laghu-bhāgavatāmṛte (2.5.39)-
children.translated_text: Although the devotees who experience <s>aiśvarya</s> and <s>mādhurya</s> are twofold, the devotees are further fourfold, [as stated] in the <s>Śrī Laghu-Bhāgavatāmṛta</s> (2.5.39):
His abode is famous in the <s>Purāṇas</s> and the like as four places:

children.text: vraje madhupure dvāra-vatyāṃ goloka eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vraja</s>, <s>Madhupurī</s>, <s>Dvāravatī</s>, and <s>Goloka</s> itself.
In the same [text] (1.5.488–9):
Those who descended as partial beings of <s>Vrajeśa</s> (the king of <s>Vraja</s>) and the like, such as <s>Droṇa</s> and others —

children.text: kṛṣṇas tān eva vaikuṇṭhe prāhiṇod iti sāmpratam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> sent those very ones to <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> — such is the current [understanding].
With the residents of <s>Gokula</s>, persons dearer than the dearest —
in <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s>, <s>Hari</s> always performs His pastimes.

children.text:
bṛhad-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikāyām (125)-sarvā evākhilaṃ karma jānante ity ādeḥ | tathā
hi laghu-bhāgavatāmṛte (1.5.498)-yat tu goloka-nāma syāt tac ca gokula-vaibhavam
iti | tathāpi stava-mālāyāṃ (nandāpaharaṇam) ca-vaikuṇṭhaṃ yaḥ suṣṭhu
sandarśya ity ādi |
children.translated_text: In the <s>Bṛhad-Gaṇoddeśa-Dīpikā</s> (125): 'All of them know all activities' — and so forth. Thus in the <s>Laghu-Bhāgavatāmṛta</s> (1.5.498): 'That which is called <s>Goloka</s> is the splendor of <s>Gokula</s>.' And also in the <s>Stava-Mālā</s> (<s>Nandāpaharaṇam</s>): 'He who, having properly shown <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>' — and so forth.

children.text:
śrī-kṛṣṇa-sandarbhe (116) śrī-vṛndāvane śrī-goloka-darśanaṃ tu
tasyaivāparicchinnasya golokākhya-vṛndāvanāprakaṭa-prakāśa-viśeṣaḥ
paryavasyatīti māhātmyāvalambanena bhajatāṃ sphuratīti jñeyam | tat tu na
kevalam upāsanā-sthānam evedaṃ prāpti-sthānam idam eva |
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha</s> (116): The vision of <s>Śrī Goloka</s> in <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s> —
'That culminates in a particular unmanifest manifestation of that very unlimited [abode] called <s>Goloka</s>-<s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
and it should be understood that it becomes visible to those who worship with reliance on [its] greatness.' That [<s>Vṛndāvana</s>] is
not merely a place of worship — it is the very place of attainment.

children.text:
tatropāsakāś caturvidhāḥ-kevalaiśvaryānubhavinaḥ, mādhurya-
miśraiśvaryānubhavinaḥ, aiśvarya-miśra-mādhuryānubhavinaḥ, kevala-
mādhuryānubhavinaś ca | tatra kevalaiśvaryānubhavināṃ sthānaṃ vaikuṇṭhaṃ
mādhurya-miśraiśvaryānubhavināṃ mahā-vaikuṇṭha-para-vyoma-golokam |
aiśvarya-miśra-mādhuryānubhavināṃ pura-dvayam | kevala-mādhuryānubhavināṃ
tu śrī-vṛndāvanam (BRS 1.2.303)-
children.translated_text:
Therein, the worshipers are of four kinds: those who experience <s>aiśvarya</s> (majesty) alone, those who experience
<s>mādhurya</s> (sweetness) mixed with <s>aiśvarya</s>, those who experience <s>aiśvarya</s> mixed with <s>mādhurya</s>, and those who experience
<s>mādhurya</s> alone. Among them, the abode of those who experience <s>aiśvarya</s> alone is <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>;
of those who experience <s>mādhurya</s> mixed with <s>aiśvarya</s> — <s>Mahā-Vaikuṇṭha</s>, the supreme sky, <s>Goloka</s>.
Of those who experience <s>aiśvarya</s> mixed with <s>mādhurya</s> — the two cities [<s>Mathurā</s> and <s>Dvārakā</s>]. Of those who experience
<s>mādhurya</s> alone — <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana</s> (BRS 1.2.303)—

children.text: riraṃsāṃ suṣṭhu kurvan yo vidhi-mārgeṇa sevate |
children.translated_text: One who serves well through the path of <s>vidhi</s> (rules), fulfilling his desire for enjoyment,

children.text: kevalenaiva sa tadā mahiṣītvam iyāt pure ||
children.translated_text: he thereby attains the status of queen (<s>mahiṣī</s>) in the city [of <s>Dvārakā</s>]. ||

children.text:
kiṃ ca svakīyā-parakīyayor madhye parakīyāyām eva mukhyo raso jāyate iti
pūrvaṃ vicārito'sti | ato ratis tridhā-sādhāraṇī samañjasā samarthā ca | tatra
sādhāraṇī sambhogecchā-nidānā kubjādiṣu | samañjasā tu patnībhāvābhimāna-
mayī kvacid bhedita-sambhogecchā-sāndrā rukimṇy-ādiṣu | samarthā khalu sva-
svarūpa-jātā śrī-kṛṣṇa-sukha-svarūpā sāndratamā śrī-rādhikādiṣu | yathā (UN
14.53)-
children.translated_text:
Moreover, it has been previously discussed that among <s>svakīyā</s> (wedded) and <s>parakīyā</s> (unwedded), the principal <s>rasa</s> arises
in the <s>parakīyā</s> mood alone. Therefore, <s>rati</s> (attachment) is threefold: <s>sādhāraṇī</s> (ordinary), <s>samañjasā</s> (proper), and <s>samarthā</s> (competent). Among them,
<s>sādhāraṇī</s>, rooted in the desire for union, is found in <s>Kubjā</s> and others. <s>Samañjasā</s>, consisting of the self-identification as a wife,
sometimes intense with a differentiated desire for union, is found in <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and others. <s>Samarthā</s>, arising from one's own essential nature,
whose nature is <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s happiness itself, the most intense, is found in <s>Śrī Rādhikā</s> and others. As stated (UN 14.53)—
That which arises from one's own essential nature or from His nature, through whatever connection,
the <s>samarthā</s> [<s>rati</s>] is considered to be all-forgetting in its very fragrance, and the most intense. ||

children.text:
kiṃ ca mantra-mayī svārasikyor madhye svārasikī śreṣṭhā | svārasikī cātra śrī-
rādhā-prāṇa-bandhor ity atra māsayām api sevāyāṃ sad-bhāvāt | ataeva gītāyāṃ
(12.10)-
children.translated_text:
Moreover, between the <s>mantra-mayī</s> (mantra-based) and <s>svārasikī</s> (spontaneous), the <s>svārasikī</s> is superior. And the <s>svārasikī</s> here —
since the mood of '<s>Śrī Rādhā-prāṇa-bandhu</s>' (the life-friend of Śrī Rādhā) is present even in the month-long service. Therefore, in the <s>Gītā</s>
(12.10)—
If you are unable even in practice, become one whose supreme [concern] is My work;

children.text: madartham api karmāṇi kurvan siddhim avāpsyasi ||
children.translated_text: performing actions even for My sake, you shall attain perfection. ||
Practice (<s>abhyāsa</s>) means mental yoga; 'My work' means <s>śravaṇa</s> (hearing), <s>kīrtana</s> (chanting), and so on.
In the <s>Śrī Hari-bhakti-vilāsa</s> (20.382)—

children.text:
evam ekāntināṃ prāyaḥ kīrtanaṃ smaraṇaṃ prabhoḥ |
kurvatāṃ parama-prītyā ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
Thus, for the single-pointed devotees, the <s>kīrtana</s> and <s>smaraṇa</s> (remembrance) of the Lord,
performed with supreme love — and so forth. |
Thus, in the <s>Bhakti-sandarbha</s> [*ENDNOTE #12]—
One who always teaches true <s>dharma</s>, who directs proper conduct,
who belongs to a <s>sampradāya</s> (lineage), who is full of mercy, who is detached — he is called a <s>guru</s>. ||

children.text:
ṭīkā-virāgī viśiṣṭa-rāgavān | tasmād doṣa-dṛṣṭyā viṣaya-parityāgaḥ sutarāṃ
labhyate |
children.translated_text:
Commentary: '<s>Virāgī</s>' (detached) means one who possesses a special attachment (<s>rāga</s>). Therefore, through a fault-seeing perspective, renunciation of sense objects
is very easily obtained.
As follows—
For those whose minds are engrossed in sense objects, absorption in <s>Viṣṇu</s> is very far away;

children.text: vāruṇī-dig-gataṃ vastu vrajann aindrīṃ kim āpnuyāt ||[*ENDNOTE #13]
children.translated_text: can one who travels westward obtain a thing located in the east? || [*ENDNOTE #13]

children.text: gṛhārambho hi duḥkhāya na sukhāya kadācana | iti ca |
children.translated_text: The undertaking of household life is indeed for suffering, never for happiness. | Thus. |
And in the words of <s>Śrī Prahlāda</s> (7.5.5)—
I consider it right, O best of <s>Asuras</s>, that embodied beings,
whose minds are always agitated due to grasping the unreal,
having abandoned the self-destroying household, which is a blind well,
should go to the forest and take refuge in <s>Hari</s>. ||
In the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>, in the Lord's own words (11.7.6)—

children.text: tvaṃ tu sarvaṃ parityajya snehaṃ sva-jana-bandhuṣu |
children.translated_text: You should completely renounce all affection for your own kinsmen and relatives,

children.text: mayy āveśya manaḥ samyak sama-dṛg vicarasva gām ||
children.translated_text: and fixing your mind properly upon Me, with equal vision, wander the earth. ||

children.text:
tyaktvā sva-dharmaṃ caraṇāmbujaṃ harer
bhajann apakvo'tha patet tato yadi |
yatra kva vābhadram abhūd amuṣya kiṃ
ko vārtha āpto'bhajatāṃ sva-dharmataḥ || iti |
children.translated_text:
Even if one who has abandoned his own <s>dharma</s>, worshiping the lotus feet of <s>Hari</s>,
falls incomplete — then what misfortune befalls him?
What gain is achieved by those who observe their own <s>dharma</s> but do not worship? || Thus. |

children.text:
(gītā 18.65)-
sarva-dharmān parityajya mām ekaṃ śaraṇaṃ vraja |
children.translated_text:
(<s>Gītā</s> 18.65)—
Abandon all <s>dharmas</s> and take refuge in Me alone. |

children.text: api cet sudurācāro bhajate mām ananya-bhāk |
children.translated_text: Even if one of very wicked conduct worships Me with undivided devotion,

children.text: sādhur eva sa mantavyaḥ samyag vyavasito hi saḥ ||
children.translated_text: he is to be regarded as saintly, for he has rightly resolved. ||

children.text: ananyāś cintayanto māṃ ye janāḥ paryupāsate |
children.translated_text: Those persons who, thinking of Me with undivided attention, worship Me,
for them, who are ever devoted, I carry what they lack and preserve what they have. ||
From this and many such [statements].
Specifically, he shows the characteristics of one qualified for <s>rāgānugā</s> [<s>bhakti</s>] (BRS 1.4.7)—

children.text: na patiṃ kāmayet kañcid brahmacarya-sthitā sadā |
children.translated_text: She never desired any husband, always established in celibacy (<s>brahmacarya</s>),
meditating only on His form — <s>Candrakānti</s>, the beautiful-faced one. ||
Remembrance, glorification, playfulness, gazing, secret conversation,
desire, determination, and the consummation of action — ||

children.text:
etan-maithunam aṣṭāṅgaṃ pravadanti manīṣiṇaḥ |
viparītaṃ brahmacaryam etad evāṣṭa-lakṣaṇam || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
the wise declare these eight-limbed [activities] to constitute union (<s>maithuna</s>).
The opposite of these is <s>brahmacarya</s> (celibacy), characterized by these very eight [negations]. || And so forth. |

children.text:
ye tu bhagavat-parikarāṇāṃ viṣayā dṛśyante | te tu siddhānāṃ teṣāṃ bhava-
bandhanāya na bhavanti | nitya-siddhā mukundavat ity ādeḥ | kiṃ ca śrī-svāmi-
caraṇaiḥ gṛha-sthitasya punar āsakti-sambhavāt ity ādeḥ |
children.translated_text: Those sense-objects that are seen among the Lord's associates — they do not serve as bonds of worldly existence for those who are <s>siddhas</s> (perfected beings). As stated: 'The eternally perfected ones are like <s>Mukunda</s>' and so forth. Moreover, by the revered <s>Gosvāmī</s>'s own feet: 'Because attachment may arise again for one situated in household life' — and so forth.
In this connection, the characteristics of a disciple (<s>śiṣya-lakṣaṇa</s>) (HBV 1.59-62, in the <s>Mantra-muktāvalī</s>)—
A disciple should be of pure lineage, prosperous, humble, pleasant to behold,
truthful in speech, of meritorious conduct, of keen intellect, free from hypocrisy, ||
free from lust and anger, devoted to the <s>guru</s>'s feet,
inclined toward the deity, with body, mind, and speech, day and night, ||
free from disease, having conquered all sins, endowed with faith,
always devoted to the daily worship of the <s>brāhmaṇas</s>, the gods, and the ancestors, ||

children.text:
yuvā viniyatāśeṣa-karaṇaḥ karuṇālayaḥ |
ity ādi-lakṣaṇair yuktaḥ śiṣyo dīkṣādhikāravān || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
youthful, with all senses restrained, an abode of compassion —
endowed with these and other qualities, a disciple is qualified for <s>dīkṣā</s> (initiation). || And so forth. |

children.text: nanv anukārya-jñānaṃ vinā katham anusaraṇa-jñānam | ity ata āha-
children.translated_text: Now, [one may ask:] without knowledge of the model to be imitated, how can there be knowledge of following? To this he replies—
For the purpose of discerning <s>rāgānugā</s> [<s>bhakti</s>], first <s>rāgātmikā</s> is described. || (BRS 1.2.271)
Commentary: Now he establishes that [<s>rāgātmikā bhakti</s>] by means of both its essential definition (<s>svarūpa-lakṣaṇa</s>) and its marginal definition (<s>taṭastha-lakṣaṇa</s>).
In the desired object, the spontaneous supreme absorption —

children.text: tan-mayī yā bhaved bhaktiḥ sātra rāgātmikoditā || (BRS 1.2.272)
children.translated_text: that devotion which is pervaded by that [absorption] is declared here to be <s>rāgātmikā</s>. || (BRS 1.2.272)

children.text:
ṭīkā-iṣṭe svābhīpsita-prema-viṣaye śrī-nanda-nandane iti yāvat | svārasikī
svābhāvikī paramāviṣṭatā kāyikī vācikī mānasī ceṣṭā | sā rāgo bhavet | tan-
mayī tan-mātra-preritā yā bhaktiḥ sā rāgātimkoditeti yojanā | iṣṭe premamaya-
gāḍha-tṛṣṇeti svarūpa-lakṣaṇam | iṣṭe svārasikī paramāviṣṭateti taṭastha-
lakṣaṇam |

children.translated_text: Now he states its divisions (BRS 1.2.273)—

children.text: sā kāmarūpā sambandha-rūpā ceti bhaved dvidhā ||
children.translated_text: It is of two kinds: <s>kāma-rūpā</s> (in the form of desire) and <s>sambandha-rūpā</s> (in the form of relationship). ||

children.text:
yadyapi kāma-rūpāyām api sambandha-viśeṣo'sty eva, tathāpi pṛthag-upādānaṃ
vaiśiṣṭyāpekṣayā |
children.translated_text:
Although in the <s>kāma-rūpā</s> as well there is indeed a particular relationship, nevertheless the separate mention is
due to the consideration of its distinctive character.
Therein, he describes the <s>kāma-rūpā</s> (BRS 1.2.283)—

children.text: sā kāmarūpā sambhoga-tṛṣṇāṃ yā nayati svatām |
children.translated_text: The <s>kāma-rūpā</s> is that which brings the thirst for union into its own nature,

children.text: yad asyāṃ kṛṣṇa-saukhyārtham eva kevalam udyamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in which the effort is solely for the sake of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s happiness. ||
Now, the <s>sambandha-rūpā</s> (BRS 1.2.288)—
The <s>sambandha-rūpā</s> is the self-identification as having fatherhood and similar [relationships] toward <s>Govinda</s>;
here, by way of implication, the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> are indicated, [as well as] the cowherds. ||

children.text:
atra śuddha-sambandha-rūpāyāṃ sambandhād vṛṣṇayaḥ (7.1.20) ity atra vṛṣṇīnām
upalakṣaṇatayā ye vallavāḥ prāptās ta evātra matāḥ | na tu mahima-jñāna-yuktā
dvārakādi-nitya-siddha-bhaktā ity arthaḥ | tad vettum evopapādayati (1.2.288)-
children.translated_text: the eternally perfected devotees of <s>Dvārakā</s> and so forth — that is the meaning. To establish that, he states (1.2.288)—

Here, in the pure <s>sambandha-rūpā</s>, by the statement 'the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s> by relationship' (7.1.20), by way of implication of the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,
those cowherds who are included are the ones intended here — but not those endowed with awareness of [the Lord's] greatness,
Because of their being devoid of awareness of [the Lord's] <s>aiśvarya</s> (majesty), attachment (<s>rāga</s>) is predominant in them. ||
Now he states the divisions of the aforementioned <s>rāgānugā bhakti</s> (1.2.290)—

children.text: rāgātmikāyā dvaividhyād dvidhā rāgānugā ca sā |
children.translated_text: Due to the twofold nature of <s>rāgātmikā</s>, <s>rāgānugā</s> is also twofold:
<s>kāmānugā</s> (following desire) and <s>sambandhānugā</s> (following relationship) — so it is declared. ||
Therein, the qualification of the eligible person (1.2.291)—
Those who are exclusively devoted to <s>rāgātmikā</s> [<s>bhakti</s>], such as the residents of <s>Vraja</s> —
one who is eager to attain their moods becomes qualified herein. ||

children.text:
nanu rāgānugāyāṃ lubdhaś ced adhikāravān tarhi lobha-jñānaṃ vinā kathaṃ
pravṛttir ity ata āha lobha-svarūpam (BRS 1.2.292)-
children.translated_text:
Now [one may ask:] if the eager person is qualified for <s>rāgānugā</s>, then without knowledge of that eagerness (<s>lobha</s>), how can there be engagement?
To this he states the nature of <s>lobha</s> (BRS 1.2.292)—
When the sweetness of those various moods is heard, whatever the mind longs for —

children.text: nātra śāstraṃ na yuktiṃ ca tal-lobhotpatti-lakṣaṇaṃ ||
children.translated_text: [when] it considers neither scripture nor reasoning — that is the defining mark of the arising of <s>lobha</s> (spiritual greed). ||

children.text:
ṭīkā-tat-tad-bhāvādi-mādhurye śrute śrī-kṛṣṇa-bhakta-mukhāt śrī-
bhāgavatādiṣu śravaṇa-dvārā yat kiñcid anubhūte sati dhīr yan-mādhuryādikam
apekṣate kadā mama tad-bhāva-mādhurya-ceṣṭā mādhuryaṃ ca bhavet iti tad eva
lobhotpatter lakṣaṇaṃ svarūpam | ata āśrayiṣyamāṇe gurau tad-bhāva-mādhuryam
āyātam | yataḥ (BhP 11.2.21) tasmād guruṃ prapadyeta jijñāsuḥ śreya uttamam ity
children.translated_text: has arrived. Because (BhP 11.2.21) 'Therefore one should take shelter of a <s>guru</s>, one who is desirous of knowing the highest good' —

children.text:
ekādaśa-skandha-padya-ṭīkāyāṃ śrī-śrīdhara-svāmibhir apy uktam | anyathā
nyāyato bodha-saṃcārābhāvāt |
children.translated_text:
this has also been stated by <s>Śrī Śrīdhara Svāmī</s> in his commentary on the verse of the Eleventh Canto. Otherwise,
due to the absence of transmission of understanding through proper reasoning.

Commentary: 'When the sweetness of those various moods is heard' — when something is experienced through hearing from the mouths of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s devotees,
through the medium of hearing the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> and other texts, then whatever sweetness the mind longs for —
'When will the sweetness of those moods and the sweetness of those activities be mine?' — that itself
is the defining mark, the essential nature, of the arising of <s>lobha</s>. Therefore, in the <s>guru</s> who is to be taken shelter of, the sweetness of that mood
One who hears with faith or describes the sportive play

children.text: śraddhānvito yaḥ śṛṇuyād atha varṇayed vā |
children.translated_text: of <s>Viṣṇu</s> with the women of <s>Vraja</s>,
attaining supreme devotion to the Lord, swiftly
abandons the disease of the heart — the wise one does so without delay. || (BhP 10.33.39)

children.text:
ṭīkā--hṛd-rogaṃ kāmādikam api śīghram eva tyajati | atra sāmānyato'pi
paramatva-siddhes tatrāpi parama-śreṣṭha-śrī-rādhā-saṃvalita-līlā-maya-tad-
bhajanaṃ tu paramatamam eveti svataḥ sidhyati | kintu rahasya-līlā tu pauruṣa-
vikāravad indriyaiḥ pitṛ-putra-dāsa-bhāvaiś ca nopāsyā svīya-bhāva-virodhāt |
rahasyatvaṃ ca tasyāḥ kvacid alpāṃśena kvacit tu sarvāṃśeneti jñeyam | (Bhakti-
sandarbhe 338)
children.translated_text:
Commentary: 'The disease of the heart' — lust and such things — he abandons very quickly. Here, since supremacy is established even in a general sense,
and since within that, the worship pervaded by the pastimes accompanied by the supremely excellent <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>
is supremely the highest — this is self-evident. However, the confidential pastimes (<s>rahasya-līlā</s>) are not to be worshiped
with the senses like masculine transformations, nor through the moods of father, son, or servant, since that contradicts one's own mood.
The confidentiality thereof is to be understood as sometimes partial and sometimes total. (<s>Bhakti-sandarbha</s> 338)

children.text:
tatratya-bhakti-mārgā darśitāḥ | tathā hi-sva-puṃstva-bhāvanāyāṃ tu naiva
rāgānugāṃ gatā śrī-daśame śruty-adhyāye striya uragendra-bhoga-bhuja-daṇḍa-
viṣakta-dhiyo [BhP 10.87.23] ity ādiḥ | śruta-mātro'pi yaḥ strīṇāṃ prasahyākarṣate
manaḥ (BhP 10.90.26) | na patiṃ kāmayet kañcid brahmacarya-sthitā sadā (BRS
1.4.7) | evaṃ veda-stutau (!0.87.21)-
children.translated_text:
The paths of devotion therein have been shown. As follows — 'In the contemplation of one's own masculinity, one has indeed not
entered <s>rāgānugā</s>.' In the Tenth [Canto], in the <s>Śruti</s> chapter: 'Women, their minds fixed on the pillar-like arms
of the best of serpent-lords' [BhP 10.87.23] — and so forth. 'Even merely heard of, He forcefully attracts
the minds of women' (BhP 10.90.26). 'She never desired any husband, always established in celibacy' (BRS 1.4.7). Likewise, in the <s>Veda-stuti</s> (10.87.21)—
Those who, for the purpose of revealing the difficult-to-comprehend truth of the Self, [toiled in] the ocean of the great nectar of Your deeds,
wearied by their circling about in that [ocean of narratives] — You who have assumed a form —

children.text: na parilaṣanti kecid apavargam apīśvara te
children.translated_text: some of them do not even desire liberation, O Lord,
having abandoned their homes through association with the communities of swans at Your lotus feet. || (10.87.21)

children.text: ṭīkā-yāni kulāni śiṣyopaśiṣyatayā teṣāṃ saṅgena visṛṣṭa-gṛhāḥ |
children.translated_text: Commentary: 'Communities' means [communities formed] as disciples and sub-disciples; through their association, 'having abandoned their homes.'
Now he states the limbs of <s>rāgānugā</s> (BRS 1.2.294-5, 309, 300-2, 307)—

children.text: kṛṣṇaṃ smaran janaṃ cāsya preṣṭhaṃ nija-samīhitam |
children.translated_text: Remembering <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and also His dearest person, [in accordance with] one's own aspiration,

children.text: tat-tat-kathā-rataś cāsau kuryād vāsaṃ vraje sadā ||
children.translated_text: being devoted to the narrations of those [personalities], one should always reside in <s>Vraja</s>. ||
Service should be performed here both in the practitioner-form (<s>sādhaka-rūpa</s>) and in the perfected-form (<s>siddha-rūpa</s>),
by one who desires to attain that mood, following the people of <s>Vraja</s>. ||
Having the grace of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and His devotees as its sole cause,
this [<s>bhakti</s>] is called <s>rāgānugā</s> by some as the <s>puṣṭi-mārga</s> (path of grace). ||

children.text: purāṇe śruyate pādme puṃsam api bhaved iyam ||
children.translated_text: In the <s>Purāṇa</s>, it is heard in the <s>Padma</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>] that this can arise even in men. ||
Formerly, all the great sages dwelling in the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest,

children.text: dṛṣṭvā rāmaṃ hariṃ tatra bhoktum aicchan suvigraham ||
children.translated_text: seeing <s>Rāma</s>, <s>Hari</s>, there, desired to enjoy His beautiful form. ||

children.text: te sarve strītvam āpannāḥ samudbhūtāś ca gokule |
children.translated_text: They all attained womanhood and were born in <s>Gokula</s>,

children.text: hariṃ samprāpya kāmena tato muktā bhavārṇavāt ||
children.translated_text: and having obtained <s>Hari</s> through desire, they were liberated from the ocean of existence. ||
Likewise, it is also heard in scripture that a certain person dwelling in <s>Kurupurī</s> (Hastināpura),
worshiping the abode of <s>Nanda</s>'s son in the mood of a son,
through the instruction of <s>Nārada</s>, the old carpenter became a <s>siddha</s> (perfected being). ||

children.text:
ṭīkā-siddhi'bhūd iti bālavatsa-haraṇa-līlāyāṃ tat-pitṝṇām eva siddhir jñeyā | evaṃ
ca sati śruit-kanyā-candrakānti-prabhṛtīnāṃ nitya-siddha-parkarānugatyābhāvāt
śrī-nanda-nandanasya prakāśa-rūpasyaiva prāptir na tu tādṛśa-svarūpasya | ataeva
prāmāṇikair apy uktam dhāmno'bhede'pi parikara-bhede prakāśaḥ | yathā tāsāṃ
madhye dvayor dvayoḥ (10.77.7) iti | nitya-siddhānugatānāṃ tu śrī-nanda-
nandanasya tādṛśa-svarūpasyaiva prāptir ity ānugatyāpekṣāvaśyakīti bhūyān
viśeṣo'stīti vibhāvanīyam |
children.translated_text: The commentary [says] 'perfection occurred' — in the pastime of stealing the calves [by Brahmā], the perfection is to be understood as pertaining to their fathers only. This being the case, since <s>Śruti</s>-born maidens like <s>Candrakānti</s> and the rest lack the quality of following the eternal associates (<s>nitya-siddha-parikara</s>), they attain only the <s>prakāśa</s> (manifestation) form of Śrī <s>Nanda-nandana</s> (the son of Nanda), not that very <s>svarūpa</s> (essential form). Therefore, even the authoritative teachers have said: 'Even when the <s>dhāma</s> (abode) is non-different, when the associates differ, it is [merely] a <s>prakāśa</s> (manifestation).' As [stated]: 'Among them, two by two' (10.77.7). But for those who follow the eternal associates (<s>nitya-siddha</s>), the attainment is of that very <s>svarūpa</s> of Śrī <s>Nanda-nandana</s> — thus there is a great distinction arising from the necessity of following (<s>ānugatya</s>).

children.text:
atha candrakānti-prabhṛtiṣu rāgānugīya-guru-caraṇāvalambanasyādṛṣṭatvād
rāgānugāyām etasya kāraṇatā na sambhavati cen na | sāmānyatas tādṛśa-guru-
caraṇāvalambanasya kāraṇatāyāḥ sākṣāt paramparayā svīkārāt | yatra
sākṣātkāraṇatā na sambhavati tatra janmāntarīṇa-kāraṇa-kalpanam phala-balāt |
ataevālaṅkārikair bālaksaya kavitāyāṃ tathaiva kalpyate | ataḥ svayam eva vakṣyate
sādhanekṣāṃ vinā yasminn akasmād bhāva īkṣyate |
children.translated_text: Where, without observance of any <s>sādhana</s>, <s>bhāva</s> (spiritual emotion) is suddenly seen,
there, the excellent <s>sādhana</s> from a previous birth, obstructed by obstacles, should be inferred.

Now, if it be objected that since the taking shelter of the <s>guru's</s> feet in the mode of <s>rāgānuga</s> [<s>bhakti</s>] is not observed in the case of <s>Candrakānti</s> and others, causality [of guru-shelter] for <s>rāgānuga</s> is not possible — [we say] no. Because the causality of such shelter at the <s>guru's</s> feet is accepted in general, whether directly or through tradition (<s>paramparā</s>). Where direct causality is not possible, the hypothesis of a cause from a previous birth [is applied], on the strength of the result. Therefore, even the literary theorists (<s>ālaṅkārikas</s>) postulate the same for precocious talent in poetry. Hence, he himself will say:

children.text: ataeva gopālopāsakāḥ pūrvam aprāptābhīṣṭa-siddhayaḥ ity ādikaṃ ca |

children.translated_text: Now <s>bhāva</s> (spiritual emotion) (BRS 1.3.1):
That which is of the nature of a special [manifestation of] <s>śuddha-sattva</s> (pure goodness), which has a share equal to a ray of the sun of <s>prema</s>,
and which, through its flavors, softens the heart — that is called <s>bhāva</s>.
Therefore [the statement] 'worshippers of <s>Gopāla</s> who had not previously attained the desired perfection' and so on.
As stated in a <s>Tantra</s>:

children.text: premṇas tu prathamāvasthā bhāva ity abhidhīyate |
children.translated_text: The initial stage of <s>prema</s> is called <s>bhāva</s>;
the <s>sāttvika</s> (involuntary ecstatic) symptoms such as tears, horripilation, and the like are present here in slight measure.
Now <s>prema</s> (divine love) (BRS 1.4.1):
When <s>bhāva</s>, whose heart has become thoroughly softened, is marked by an excess of possessive attachment (<s>mamatva</s>),

children.text: bhāvaḥ sa eva sāndrātmā budhaiḥ premā nigadyate ||
children.translated_text: and has become dense in its nature — that is declared by the wise to be <s>prema</s>.
As stated in the <s>Pañcarātra</s>:
Exclusive possessive attachment to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, attachment conjoined with <s>prema</s> —
that is called <s>bhakti</s> by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s>, <s>Uddhava</s>, and <s>Nārada</s>.
First <s>śraddhā</s> (faith), then <s>sādhu-saṅga</s> (association with saints), then <s>bhajana-kriyā</s> (practice of worship),

children.text: tato'nartha-nivṛttiḥ syāt tato niṣṭhā rucis tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: then <s>anartha-nivṛtti</s> (removal of unwanted habits), then <s>niṣṭhā</s> (steadfastness), then <s>ruci</s> (taste),
then <s>āsakti</s> (attachment), then <s>bhāva</s> (spiritual emotion), then <s>prema</s> (divine love) arises —

children.text: sādhakānām ayaṃ premnaḥ prādurbhāve bhavet kramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: this is the sequence for the manifestation of <s>prema</s> in practitioners.
Now it is stated that this <s>rati</s> (love) for <s>Keśava</s>, when manifested,
attains the supreme state of <s>rasa</s> through the full nourishment of its constituent elements.
Through <s>vibhāvas</s> (stimulants), <s>anubhāvas</s> (consequents), <s>sāttvika-bhāvas</s> (involuntary ecstatic symptoms), and <s>vyabhicāri-bhāvas</s> (transitory emotions),
this <s>Kṛṣṇa-rati</s>, being relishable in the hearts of devotees, brought [to fruition] by hearing and the like,

children.text: eṣā kṛṣṇa-ratiḥ sthāyī bhāvo bhakti-raso bhavet ||
children.translated_text: when it becomes the <s>sthāyī-bhāva</s> (permanent sentiment), becomes <s>bhakti-rasa</s>.
He who has the <s>vāsanā</s> (latent impression) of genuine <s>bhakti</s>, whether from previous births or from the present life —
the relishing of <s>bhakti-rasa</s> arises in his heart alone.
When <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> and the other <s>vibhāvas</s>, etc., enter the path of experience,
[the devotee] attains the supreme culmination of mature bliss and wonder.

children.text: tathā hi śrutiḥ-raso vai saḥ | rasaṃ hy evāyaṃ labdhvānandī bhavati iti |
children.translated_text: As the <s>Śruti</s> [says]: 'He indeed is <s>rasa</s>' (<s>Raso vai saḥ</s>). 'Having obtained this <s>rasa</s>, one becomes blissful' (<s>Rasaṃ hy evāyaṃ labdhvā ānandī bhavati</s>).

children.text: upapatau parakīyāyām eva rasotkarṣaḥ | ataeva ujjvala-nīlamaṇau (1.19)
children.translated_text: The supreme excellence of <s>rasa</s> exists in <s>upapatī</s> (paramour love) alone, which is <s>parakīyā</s> (the 'belonging to another' modality). Therefore, in the <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> (1.19):
In this [paramour relationship] alone is established the supreme excellence of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment).
Commentary: 'In this alone' means in <s>upapatī</s> (paramour love). And thus, [citing] <s>Bharata</s> (UN 1.20-21):

children.text: bahu vāryate khalu yatra pracchanna-kāmukatvaṃ ca |
children.translated_text: Where there is much obstruction and concealed passion,

children.text: yā ca mitho durlabhatā sā manmathasya paramā ratiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and where there is mutual rarity — that is the supreme <s>rati</s> (love) of <s>Manmatha</s> (Cupid).

children.text: laghutvam atra yat proktaṃ tat tu prākṛta-nāyake |
children.translated_text: The disgrace that is said [to belong] here applies to a mundane hero,
not to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the <s>avatāra</s> who descends for the purpose of relishing the essence of <s>rasa</s>.

children.text:
punas tatraiva (UN 3.19)-
kanyakāś ca paroḍhāś ca parakīyā dvidhā matāḥ |
vrajeśa-vrajavāsinya etāḥ prāyeṇa viśrutāḥ |
children.translated_text:
Again, in the same [text] (UN 3.19):
The <s>parakīyā</s> (those belonging to another) are considered twofold: unmarried maidens and married women.
The women of the King of <s>Vraja</s> and the residents of <s>Vraja</s> — these are generally renowned.
And thus <s>Rudra</s> [says] (UN 3.20):

children.text: vāmatā durlabhatvaṃ ca strīṇāṃ yā ca nivāraṇā |
children.translated_text: The coyness of women, their rarity,

children.text: tad eva pañca-bāṇasya manye paramam āyudham ||
children.translated_text: and their being forbidden — that indeed I consider the supreme weapon of the five-arrowed one (Cupid).
And in the <s>Viṣṇugupta-saṃhitā</s> (UN 3.21):

children.text: yatra niṣedha-viśeṣaḥ sudurlabhatvaṃ ca yan mṛgākṣīṇām |
children.translated_text: Where there is a special prohibition and where the doe-eyed women are most rare to obtain —
there alone the hearts of connoisseurs (<s>nāgaras</s>) become intensely attached.

children.text: āḥ kiṃ vānyad yatas tasyām idam eva mahāmuniḥ
children.translated_text: Ah! What more [need be said]? For regarding this [parakīya modality], the great sage

children.text: jagau pāramahaṃsyāṃ ca saṃhitāyāṃ svayaṃ śukaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śuka</s> himself sang in the supreme <s>Paramahaṃsa-saṃhitā</s> (the Bhāgavata).
As in the Śrī [Bhāgavata], tenth [canto] (10.33.19):
Making Himself into as many [forms] as there were cowherd women (<s>gopa-yoṣitas</s>),

children.text: reme sa bhagavāṃs tābhir ātmārāmo'pi līlayā ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Bhagavān</s>, though <s>Ātmārāma</s> (self-delighting), sported with them in play.

children.text: ṭīkā-gopīnāṃ yoṣita iti tāsāṃ spaṣṭam eva parakīyatvam |
children.translated_text: Commentary: '<s>Yoṣitas</s>' (women) 'of the <s>gopas</s>' — their <s>parakīyatva</s> (belonging to another) is plainly evident.
They were forbidden by their husbands, fathers, brothers, and kinsmen. (BhP 10.33.19)
O [<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>], You who are the knower of <s>dharma</s>, have declared to be the proper <s>dharma</s> of women. (BhP 10.29.32)
The following of husbands, sons, and friends,

children.text: tad yāta mā ciraṃ goṣṭhaṃ śuśrūṣadhvaṃ patīn satīḥ |
children.translated_text: Go now to <s>Goṣṭha</s> (the cowherding settlement) without delay; serve your husbands, O virtuous women;

children.text: krandanti vatsā bālāś ca tān pāyayata duhyata || (10.29.22)
children.translated_text: the calves and children are crying — feed them and milk [the cows]. (BhP 10.29.22)

children.text: bhartuḥ śuśrūṣaṇaṃ strīṇāṃ paro dharmo hy amāyayā | (10.29.24)
children.translated_text: Service to one's husband is the supreme <s>dharma</s> of women, performed without deceit. (BhP 10.29.24)
It does not lead to heaven, it brings infamy,
it is difficult, fearsome, and everywhere loathsome — the adultery of a woman of good family. (BhP 10.29.26)
In the same [text]:
How then did He, the speaker, doer, and protector of the boundaries of <s>dharma</s>,
act contrarily, O <s>brāhmaṇa</s>, touching the wives of others? (BhP 10.33.27)

children.text:
tathā śrī-ekādaśe (11.12.13)-
mat-kāmā ramaṇaṃ jāram asvarūpa-vido'balāḥ ||
children.translated_text:
And in the Śrī Eleventh [Canto] (11.12.13):
Desiring Me, [considering Me] a paramour lover — though not knowing My true nature, those women (<s>abalāḥ</s>) —

children.text:
padma-purāṇe ca-
gopa-nārībhir aniśaṃ yatra krīḍati kaṃsahā ||
children.translated_text:
And in the <s>Padma-purāṇa</s>:
Where the slayer of <s>Kaṃsa</s> ceaselessly sports with the cowherd women —

And in the <s>Krama-dīpikā</s>:
'Surrounded by hosts of cows, cowherds, and cowherd women' — thus.

children.text:
bṛhad-gautamīya-tantre ca-
atra yā gopa-patnyaś ca nivasanti mamālaye |
śrī-gopāla-stave-
vicitrāmbara-bhūṣābhir gopa-nārībhir āvṛtam || iti |
children.translated_text:
And in the <s>Bṛhad-gautamīya-tantra</s>:
'Here the cowherd wives dwell in My abode.'
In the Śrī <s>Gopāla-stava</s>:
'Surrounded by cowherd women of varied garments and ornaments' — thus.

children.text:
bṛhad-vāmane ca-
jāra-dharmeṇa susnehaṃ sarvato'dhikam uttamam |
mayi samprāpya sarvo'pi kṛtakṛtyo bhaviṣyati || iti |
children.translated_text:
And in the <s>Bṛhad-vāmana</s> [Purāṇa]:
'Through the way of paramour love (<s>jāra-dharma</s>), with great affection, supreme and beyond all else —
having attained Me, everyone will become fulfilled.' Thus.
Now, in the Śrī <s>Rāsa-pañcādhyāyī</s> commentary, the Śrī <s>Bṛhad-vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī</s>, by the venerable Śrī <s>Sanātana Gosvāmī</s>, [commenting on] (10.22.21):

children.text: yātābalā vrajaṃ siddhā mayemā raṃsyatha kṣapāḥ |
children.translated_text: 'Go, O women, to <s>Vraja</s>; you are <s>siddhas</s> (perfected); you shall enjoy [these] nights with Me;

children.text: yad uddiśya vratam idaṃ cerur āryārcanaṃ satīḥ ||
children.translated_text: for this purpose you performed this vow, the worship of the Noble One (<s>Āryā</s>, i.e. Kātyāyanī), O virtuous women.'

children.text:
ṭīkā-bharjitāḥ kvathitā dhānāḥ prāyo bījāya phalāntarotpādanāya neśate | kintu
