svayaṃ bhogyatāpattyā sadya eva parama-sukhāya samarthā bhavantīty arthaḥ | ity
evaṃ patitvena prema-viśeṣāsiddher upapatitvenaiva tat saṃsiddher iti bhāvaḥ | tad
evāha yāteti | he abalā ity ātibālyaṃ sūcayati | ato'dhunā raty-ayogyā iti bhāvaḥ |
yad vā pūrvokta-nyāyena sarvato'dhika-śaktimatya ity arthaḥ | prakāra-viśeṣeṇa
mad-vaśīkāra-viśeṣāt | yataḥ siddhāḥ sampanna-kāmitvāt tad-atīta-phalā ity
arthaḥ | imā nikaṭa evaiṣyac charatkālīnā iti tāsāṃ vidūravartitve'pi imā iti
sannihitatayā uktiḥ sāntvanārthā | anyat samānam |
children.translated_text: Commentary: 'Grains that have been roasted and boiled are generally unable to produce fruit [sprout again], serving as seeds. But by themselves becoming objects of enjoyment, they are immediately capable of giving supreme pleasure' — this is the meaning. Thus, since the special <s>prema</s> cannot be perfected through the husband-relationship (<s>patitva</s>), it is perfected only through the paramour relationship (<s>upapatitva</s>) — this is the purport. That is what He says with 'Go' (<s>yāta</s>). 'O <s>abalāḥ</s> (women/weak ones)' — this indicates their extreme youth, hence the sense that they are presently unfit for amorous union. Alternatively, by the principle stated earlier, they are possessed of the greatest power. In a special manner, because of their special power to bring Me under control. Because '<s>siddhāḥ</s>' (perfected) — since they have attained the object of desire, they have transcended the fruit — this is the meaning. '<s>Imāḥ</s>' (these) — though [the nights] are still distant, being the autumnal [nights] that are yet to come, He says '<s>imāḥ</s>' as if they were near, for the purpose of consolation. The rest is the same.

children.text:
yad vā, hemantasyottara-māsa-sambandhinīr āgaminīḥ kṣapāḥ mayā saha ramaṇaṃ
prāpsyatha iti |
children.translated_text: Alternatively: 'You shall attain enjoyment (<s>ramaṇam</s>) with Me during the nights of the latter month of the <s>hemanta</s> (winter) season that are coming.'

children.text:
nanu asmat-saṅkalpitaṃ tvayodvahana-sukhaṃ sidhyatu, tena rāsa-krīḍādiṣu sukhaṃ
ca sampadyatām | tatrāha yad iti | yad uddiśya āryāyāś cic-chakteḥ kātyāyanyā
arcanaṃ vrataṃ cerur bhavatyaḥ, tad idaṃ mayoktam aupapatyena rāsa-krīḍādi-
sukham evety arthaḥ | vivāhena patitve rāsa-krīḍādi-sukha-viśeṣo na sampadyata
iti bhāvaḥ | satīḥ he satya iti aupapatye'pi yūyaṃ sarvathā sādhvya eva | mad-eka-
mātra-niṣṭhatvād iti bhāvaḥ | tattvato'naupapayāt vivāhitābhyo'py adhika-priyatvāt
|
children.translated_text: Objection: 'Let the happiness of marriage planned by us be fulfilled by You, and through that let the happiness of <s>rāsa</s>-play and the like be accomplished.' To that He says '<s>yat</s>': 'For which purpose (<s>yad uddiśya</s>) you performed the vow of worshipping the Noble One (<s>Āryā</s>), the <s>cit-śakti</s> (consciousness-potency) <s>Kātyāyanī</s> — that [which I have stated, namely] the happiness of <s>rāsa</s>-play and the like through the paramour relation (<s>aupapatya</s>) alone, is what I have declared.' The meaning is that through marriage, as a husband, the special happiness of <s>rāsa</s>-play and the like cannot be accomplished. '<s>Satīḥ</s>' — O truthful ones! Even in the paramour relationship, you are in every way virtuous women, because of your exclusive devotion to Me alone — this is the purport. [Moreover,] in truth, since there is no [real] paramour relationship [with God], and since [the gopīs] are even more dear than married wives —

children.text:
yad vā satīr iti kṣapā-viśeṣaṇam | uttamā rāsānandāvirbhāvikāḥ śāradāḥ
śītoṣṇādi-rahitā jyotsnāś cety arthaḥ |
children.translated_text: Alternatively, '<s>satīḥ</s>' is an adjective of '<s>kṣapāḥ</s>' (nights). The meaning is: excellent autumnal [nights] that bring forth the bliss of the <s>rāsa</s>, free from cold, heat, and the like, luminous with moonlight.

children.text:
yad vā tat krīḍā-māhātmyam evāha yad yasmāt satyo lakṣmī-dharaṇādayaḥ | idaṃ
rāsa-krīḍādi-sukham uddiśya āryārcana-vrataṃ cerur eva, na tu tat sukhaṃ prāpur
ity arthaḥ | yad ramaṇam idaṃ vratam | anyat samānam |
children.translated_text: Or He states the very greatness of that play with '<s>yat</s>': Because '<s>satyaḥ</s>' — <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Dharaṇī</s> (the Earth), and others — performed the vow of worshipping the Noble One (<s>Āryā</s>) aiming at (<s>uddiśya</s>) this very happiness of <s>rāsa</s>-play and the like, but did not attain that happiness — this is the meaning. '<s>Yat ramaṇam</s>' — this enjoyment is the vow. The rest is the same.

children.text:
śrīmaj-jīva-gosvāmi-caraṇaiḥ-atha vraje prakaṭāyāṃ ca śrī-kṛṣṇasyaupapatyaṃ
nityam | śrī-rādhikādīnāṃ ca parakīyātvaṃ nityam | tayoḥ svarūpeṇa dvaividhyaṃ
nāsti | kintu aprākṛta-dvāpare prākṛta-dvāparasya milane svayaṃ-rūpe śrī-nanda-
nandane vasudeva-nandanādiṣu prakāśeṣu militeṣu satsu līlāyāḥ prākaṭyaṃ

children.translated_text: As stated in the source (<s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> 1.5.438):

By the venerable Śrī <s>Jīva Gosvāmī</s>: Now, in the manifest (<s>prakaṭa</s>) <s>Vraja</s> as well, the <s>aupapatya</s> (paramour status) of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is eternal; and the <s>parakīyātva</s> (belonging-to-another-ness) of Śrī <s>Rādhikā</s> and others is eternal. In their essential natures (<s>svarūpa</s>), there is no duality between the two. But when the transcendent <s>Dvāpara</s> merges with the mundane <s>Dvāpara</s>, when the <s>svayaṃ-rūpa</s> (original form), Śrī <s>Nanda-nandana</s>, merges with the <s>prakāśas</s> (manifestations) such as the son of <s>Vasudeva</s> and others, the <s>līlā</s> becomes manifest (<s>prakaṭa</s>).
That <s>līlā</s> which comes within the range of the mundane world is known as 'manifest' (<s>prakaṭa</s>);

children.text: anyās tv aprakaṭā bhānti tādṛśyas tad-agocarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: the others, which are of the same nature but beyond its range, are known as 'unmanifest' (<s>aprakaṭa</s>).

children.text: kiṃ ca śrī-kṛṣṇasyaupapatyābhāve rasotkarṣābhāvaḥ syāt | yathākare (UN 1.19,21)-
children.translated_text: Moreover, without the paramour status (<s>aupapatya</s>) of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the supreme excellence of <s>rasa</s> would not exist. As in the source (UN 1.19, 21):
In this [paramour relationship] alone is the supreme excellence of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) established.

children.text: laghutvam atra yat proktaṃ tat tu prākṛta-nāyake |
children.translated_text: The disgrace that is said [to belong] here applies to a mundane hero,
not to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the <s>avatāra</s> who descends for the purpose of relishing the essence of <s>rasa</s>.
Therefore, in the Eleventh [Canto] (11.12.13):
Desiring Me as a paramour lover, not knowing My true nature, those women —

children.text: brahma māṃ paramaṃ prāpuḥ saṅgāc chata-sahasraśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: they attained Me, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, through intimate association, in hundreds of thousands.

children.text:
asya vyākhyā sva-daśa-ślokī-bhāṣye kṛtaiva | tatredaṃ bījam | yatraupapatye loka-
viruddhaṃ dharma-viruddhaṃ ca | tatraiva laghutvam | yatra tu tad-ubhayābhāvas
tatra bahu-nivāraṇādi-hetubhiḥ śṛṅgārasya paramotkarṣatā | tatra laukikaupapatye-
paradārān na gacchec ca manasāpi kadācana iti śāstra-viruddhatvena pāpa-

children.translated_text: opposed to worldly norms as well. Therefore, by Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself (BhP 10.29.26):

The explanation of this has already been given in the commentary on the <s>Sva-daśa-ślokī</s>. Herein, this is the seed [argument]: Where in paramour love there is [something] opposed to worldly norms and opposed to <s>dharma</s>, there indeed is the disgrace. But where both of those are absent, there the supreme excellence of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> [is established] through causes such as manifold obstructions and the like. In mundane paramour love: 'One should not go to another's wife even in thought' — since it is opposed to scripture, sin is possible; it is opposed to <s>dharma</s>. Therefore, because blame is possible, and because it causes shame, it is
It does not lead to heaven, it brings infamy,
it is difficult, fearsome, and everywhere loathsome — the adultery of a woman of good family.

children.text:
ity anena tasyaivāsvargyādikam uktam | śrī-vraja-devībhir api niḥsvaṃ tyajanti
gaṇikā jārā bhuktvā ratāṃ striyam (10.47.7) iti tasyaivollekhaḥ kṛtaḥ | śrī-kṛṣṇe tu
śāstra-virodhābhāvena pāpāsambhavān na dharma-viruddhatvam |
ataevānindyatvena lajjādy-asambhavān na loka-viruddhaṃ ca | pratyuta loke
suṣṭhūpādeyatvam eveti bahu-nivāraṇādi-hetubhiḥ śṛṅgārasya paramotkarṣateti
tāsāṃ parama-duḥsaha-loka-lajjānādareṇa tad-eka-prītyā pravṛtter avagamāt | tat-

children.translated_text: because that love for Him constitutes the fruit of all scriptures. There (10.33.29):

By this [verse], its heaven-lessness and the rest were stated by Him Himself. Even by the divine ladies of <s>Vraja</s>: 'Paramour lovers, like courtesans, abandon a woman devoid of wealth after having enjoyed her' (10.47.7) — thus a reference to it was made by them. But in the case of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, because there is no opposition to scripture, and because sin is not possible — it is not opposed to <s>dharma</s>. Therefore, because it is not blameworthy, and because shame and the like are not possible — it is not opposed to worldly norms either. Rather, in the world, it is entirely to be honored. Thus, through causes such as manifold obstructions, the supreme excellence of <s>śṛṅgāra</s> [is established] — this is understood from the recognition that [the gopīs] acted with utter disregard for the supremely unbearable worldly shame, motivated solely by love for Him alone. And
Transgression of <s>dharma</s> seen [in the case of] the Lords, and [their] daring,

children.text: tejīyasāṃ na doṣāya vahneḥ sarva-bhujo yathā ||
children.translated_text: does not become a fault for those of great power — just as fire [is not harmed] by consuming everything.

children.text: ity ādi | vacana-prāmāṇyāt na dharma-viruddham api, yathā-
children.translated_text: And so on. By the authority of these statements, it is not opposed to <s>dharma</s> either. As for example:

children.text:
go-cāraṇāyānucaraiś carad vane
yad gopikānāṃ kuca-kuṅkumāṅkitam
children.translated_text:
Who wanders in the forest tending cows, accompanied by His companions,
whose [body] is marked with the breast-saffron of the <s>gopīs</s> —

children.text:
ity atra yad akrūreṇa śrī-kṛṣṇasyaupapatyasyollekhaḥ kṛtaḥ | tat khalu pitṛvyatvena
dāsatvena cety ubhayathā na yujyate | kintu upādeyatvenaiva | na ca prīti-
viśeṣollekha eva kṛta iti vaktavyam | tad-vācaka-śabdayānupādānāt | yat khalu śrī-
bhāgavatādi-purāṇeṣu nānā-jātīya-muni-rāja-sabhādiṣu tad-aupapatya-
pratipādikā rāsa-līlā gīyate tat tu suṣṭhūpādeyatvenaiva, nānyathā | tāsāṃ tad-
eka-sukhārtha-pravṛttis tu yat te sujāta ity ādi-śrī-bhāgavatokteḥ | tat-prīteḥ sarva-
śāstra-phala-rūpatvaṃ yathā tatraiva kurvanti hi tvayi ratiṃ kuśalāḥ iti | kuśalāḥ
śāstra-nipuṇāḥ iti ṭīkā ca |
children.translated_text: Here, the reference made by <s>Akrūra</s> to Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> paramour status (<s>aupapatya</s>) is indeed not fitting in either way — neither as an uncle nor as a servant. Rather, it is [mentioned] only as something to be accepted (worthy). Nor can it be said that merely a reference to a special kind of affection was made, because the word denoting that [paramour status] was not employed [by Akrūra]. Indeed, the fact that in the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata</s> and other <s>Purāṇas</s>, the <s>rāsa-līlā</s> — which establishes His paramour status — is sung in assemblies of sages and kings of various classes, that is certainly only as something worthy of acceptance, not otherwise. The engagement of those [<s>gopīs</s>] solely for His pleasure is [established] from the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata</s> statement beginning 'O You of beautiful feet (<s>sujāta</s>)' and the like. That love for Him is the fruit of all scriptures, as stated there: 'The wise (<s>kuśalāḥ</s>) indeed develop <s>rati</s> (attachment) toward You.' The commentary [explains]: '<s>kuśalāḥ</s>' means 'skilled in the scriptures.'
He also illustrates the <s>parakīya</s> (paramour) nature, as stated [in the <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 3.18]:

children.text:
rāgollāsa-vilaṅghitārya-padavī-viśrāntayo'py uddhura-
śraddhā-rajyad-arundhatī-mukha-satī-vṛndena vandyehitāḥ |
āraṇyā api mādhurī-parimala-vyākṣipta-lakṣmī-śriyas
tās trailokya-vilakṣaṇā dadatu vaḥ kṛṣṇasya sakhyaḥ sukham || iti |

children.translated_text: In anticipation of the question 'Who are they?', he says (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 3.19):

children.text: kanyakāś ca paroḍhāś ca parakīyā dvidhā matāḥ |
children.translated_text: <s>Parakīyā</s> (those belonging to another) are considered of two kinds: unmarried maidens (<s>kanyakā</s>) and married women (<s>paroḍhā</s>).
He states the supreme excellence (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 3.19):
The concealed desire (<s>pracchanna-kāmatā</s>) here constitutes the supreme happiness of the Lord of <s>Gokula</s>.

children.text:
atra parakīyātva-viśeṣe iti | tasmāt śrī-kṛṣṇa-tad-dhāma-samaya-parikara-
līlādīnāṃ sarva-laukikātītatve'pi yathā lokaval līlāyāṃ sac-cid-ānanda-maya-śrī-
vigrahe mutra-purīṣotsargādikaṃ svīkriyate tathā tal-līlā-parikara-rūpābhir
manvādibhiḥ pāṇi-grahaṇe ko doṣaḥ | saṅgame tu doṣa eva, sa ca nāsti | yathā
(UN 3.32)--
children.translated_text: Here, regarding the specific <s>parakīya</s> nature: Therefore, although Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, His abode, His time-associates, pastimes, and the rest are all beyond worldly [categories], just as in His <s>līlā</s> which appears worldly, His <s>sac-cid-ānanda</s> (existence-consciousness-bliss) divine form accepts [apparent activities like] urination, defecation, and the like — similarly, what fault is there in the marriage ceremony (<s>pāṇi-grahaṇa</s>) performed by <s>Manu</s> and others who are forms of His pastime-associates? But in [actual] union [of the <s>gopīs</s> with their nominal husbands] there is indeed a fault — and that [union] does not exist. As stated (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 3.32):

children.text: na jātu vraja-devīnāṃ patibhiḥ saha saṅgamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The goddesses of <s>Vraja</s> never have union with their [nominal] husbands.
Therefore (<s>Bhāgavata Purāṇa</s> 10.33.27):

children.text: manyamānāḥ svapārśvasthān svān svān dārān vrajaukasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The residents of <s>Vraja</s> considered their own wives to be at their sides.

children.text:
iti pārśvasthān na tu saṅgamocita-śayyā-sthānāni | tathāpi yogamāyayā vivāhocitaṃ
laukika-vaidikaṃ karma kārayitvā pāṇi-grahaṇaṃ pratyāyitam |
children.translated_text: 'At their sides' — but not in the beds appropriate for union. Nevertheless, through <s>Yogamāyā</s>, having caused the performance of the worldly and Vedic rites appropriate for marriage, the marriage ceremony was made to appear [real].

children.text:
kiṃ ca gokulasya prakaṭāprakaṭa-rūpeṇa prakāśa-dvaividhya-svīkāre sati līlāyā
dvaividhyaṃ syāt | tayoḥ svarūpeṇa dvaividhyasyābhāvaḥ | ataḥ śrī-rādhikādibhiḥ
sārdhaṃ prakaṭa-vihāre'pi śrī-kṛṣṇasyādhokṣajatvāt tat parivāra-samaya-
līlādīnāṃ tat-svarūpa-śaktivilāsatvena tat-samāna-dharmatvāc ca tasya teṣāṃ ca
prapañcendriyāviṣayatvam aprākaṭyam | tataḥ svayaṃ prakāśatva-śaktyā svecchā-
prakāśayā so'bhivyaktyo bhaven netre na netra-viṣayas tv ataḥ iti nirdhāraṇāt tasya
teṣāṃ ca prapañcendriya-viṣayatvaṃ prākaṭyam | ataeva śrī-laghu-bhāgavatāmṛte
(1.5.391-2)-
children.translated_text: Furthermore, when the twofold manifestation of <s>Gokula</s> — in manifest (<s>prakaṭa</s>) and unmanifest (<s>aprakaṭa</s>) forms — is accepted, there would be a twofold division of the <s>līlā</s>. But in their essential nature (<s>svarūpa</s>), there is no such duality. Therefore, even in the manifest pastimes with Śrī <s>Rādhikā</s> and others, because Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is <s>Adhokṣaja</s> (beyond material senses), and because His entourage, time, pastimes, etc. are manifestations of His <s>svarūpa-śakti</s> (essential potency) and share the same nature as Him — He and they are not objects of mundane senses, [which constitutes] the unmanifest (<s>aprākaṭya</s>). Then, through His self-manifesting potency (<s>svayaṃ-prakāśatva-śakti</s>), by His own will, that manifestation occurs — as determined by 'He becomes visible to the eyes, but is not an object of [ordinary] eyes.' Thus, His and their becoming objects of mundane senses is the manifest [aspect]. Therefore, in the Śrī <s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> (1.5.391-2):
Even today, those dear ones who are afflicted with longing and wish to see

children.text: tāṃ tāṃ līlāṃ tataḥ kṛṣṇo darśayet tān kṛpā-nidhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: each particular <s>līlā</s> — <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, that treasury of mercy, reveals it to them.
By certain supreme devotees (<s>bhāgavatottamas</s>) who are blessed with the helplessness of <s>prema</s>,
even today <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is seen playing within <s>Vṛndāvana</s>.

children.text:
ity atraiva vṛndāvane līlāyāḥ prapañcāgocarāyāḥ sākṣād-darśanam | aprakaṭa-
vṛndāvana-sattā-pakṣe tu brhama-hrada-nītāḥ itivad atra tasya sākṣād-
darśanānupapattiḥ |
children.translated_text: Thus, the direct vision of the <s>līlā</s> that is beyond mundane perception occurs in this very <s>Vṛndāvana</s>. But if one holds the position that there is a separate unmanifest <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, then — like [the statement that the <s>gopīs</s>] 'were taken to <s>Brahma-hrada</s>' — the direct vision of Him here would be untenable.
Furthermore, regarding the existence of the unmanifest <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, [from the <s>Utkalikā-vallarī</s> 66]:
Attaining Your ownership, [this place] which is desired

children.text: mahadbhir api kāmyate kim api yatra tārṇaṃ januḥ |
children.translated_text: even by great souls endowed with pure <s>prema</s>, where even a birth as grass [is coveted],

children.text: kṛtātra kujaner api vraja-vane sthitir me yayā
children.translated_text: where even a wicked person like me has obtained a dwelling in the forest of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text: kṛpāṃ kṛpaṇa-gāminīṃ sadasi naumi tām eva vām ||
children.translated_text: I praise in this assembly that very mercy of Yours both, which flows toward the wretched.
