ādy-anupapattiḥ | evaṃ ca sati kalpa-vṛkṣādi-rūpāṇāṃ nimbādi-rūpeṇa yat pratītiḥ
| tat tu (naiṣadhīya-carite 3.94) pittena dūne rasane sitāpi tiktāyate itivat | nayana-
doṣāt śaṅkhaṃ pītam iva paśyatītivat | prakāśaika-rūpāyāḥ sūrya-kānter ulūkeṣu
tamo'bhivyañjakatā itivac ca sāparādheṣv ayogyeṣu teṣu tasya svarūpāprakāśa-
prāyikatvāc ca | anena śrī-kṛṣṇasyaupapatye śrī-rādhikādīnāṃ parakīyātve kecit
punar evam āhuḥ-yaḥ khalūpapatyādy-utkarṣo varṇitaḥ śrīmadbhir grantha-
kṛdbhiḥ sa tu parecchayaiva na tu svābhimataḥ | tan na teṣāṃ prārthanā-virodhāt
| yathā hy utkalikā-vallaryāṃ (45)-
children.translated_text: Similarly, in the Śrī <s>Gāndharva-samprārthanāṣṭaka</s> (1), 'Of the two who sport in this pleasure-grove of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>' and so forth — [the meaning of such prayers] would be untenable [if unmanifest Vṛndāvana were elsewhere]. And when this is so, the perception of wish-fulfilling trees (<s>kalpa-vṛkṣa</s>) and the like in the form of neem trees, etc. — that is like [the verse from] the <s>Naiṣadhīya-carita</s> (3.94): 'Even sugar tastes bitter to a tongue afflicted by bile'; like one who, due to a defect of the eyes, sees a conch as yellow; and like the sun's radiance, which is of the sole nature of light, manifesting darkness for owls. [This is] because, for those who are offenders and unqualified, His essential nature mostly does not manifest. By this [reasoning], regarding Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> paramour status and Śrī <s>Rādhikā</s> and others' <s>parakīya</s> nature, some again say thus: 'The excellence of paramour status and the like described by the illustrious authors was only according to the desire of others (<s>parecchā</s>), not their own conviction.' That is not so, because it would contradict their own prayers. As in the <s>Utkalikā-vallarī</s> (45):

children.text: ālībhiḥ samam abhupetya śanakair gāndharvikāyāṃ mudā
children.translated_text: Approaching together with her <s>sakhīs</s>, slowly, joyfully, as <s>Gāndharvikā</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>)
steals Your garland of flowers, O son of the lord of the cowherds,

children.text: prekṣiṣye purataḥ praviśya sahasā gūḍha-smitāsyaṃ balād
children.translated_text: when shall I see [this]: entering suddenly before [them], with a face of concealed smiles, forcefully

children.text: ācchindānam ihottarīyam urasas tvāṃ bhānumatyāḥ kadā ||
children.translated_text: snatching the upper garment from the chest of <s>Bhānumatī</s> (<s>Rādhā</s>)?

children.text: ity atra hi svakīyatvena tayā tayā tasya puṣpa-haraṇam | tena ca tat-tat-sakhyā |
uttarīyākarṣaṇaṃ na sambhavatīti | tathā kārpaṇya-pañjikāyāṃ (35) ca-
children.translated_text: the snatching of the upper garment would not be possible [if she were His wife]. And similarly, in the <s>Kārpaṇya-pañjikā</s> (35):
Here, the stealing of flowers by her and her [<s>sakhīs</s>] from Him is in the manner of <s>svakīya</s> (one's own); but by Him, the [snatching from] that particular <s>sakhī</s> —
When shall I, searching for each other within <s>Vṛndāvana</s>,
bring the two of You together and receive a delightful reward?
And also (34):
When the two of You, whose mutual sight is rare due to dependence on elders,
when shall I delight You both with the nectar-like messages to each other?

children.text:
atrāpi parasparānveṣaṇaṃ dulrabhānyo'nya-vīkṣaṇaṃ ca parakīyāyām eva
sambhavatīti | evaṃ śrīman-mahāprabhoḥ paramāntaraṅga-bhakta-śrī-raghunātha-
dāsa-gosvāmi-pādair yathā vilāpa-kusumāñjalyām (88)-
children.translated_text: Here too, the mutual searching and the rarity of mutual sight are possible only in the <s>parakīya</s> [mode]. Thus, by Śrī <s>Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī</s>, the most intimate devotee of Śrīman <s>Mahāprabhu</s>, as in the <s>Vilāpa-kusumāñjali</s> (88):

children.text: bhrātrā goyutam atra mañju-vadane snehena dattvālayaṃ
children.translated_text: When her brother (<s>Śrīdāmā</s>), having given ten-thousand cows here, O lovely-faced one, and out of affection giving [You to his] household,
and <s>Śrīdāmā</s>, having pleased the wretched <s>Jaṭilā</s> on the occasion of the full-moon festival called '<s>Rakṣā</s>',
when You are led [there], melting with torrents of joyful-sorrowful weeping,

children.text: vātsalyāj janakau vidhāsyata itaḥ kiṃ lālanāṃ me'grataḥ ||
children.translated_text: will Your parents, out of parental affection, from then on bestow their caresses upon me before [Your eyes]?

children.text:
ity ādi bahuśaḥ |
kiṃ ca vraje śrī-kṛṣṇasya nava-yauvane samṛddhimān śṛṅgāro jñeyaḥ | sa ca
mahābhāva-svabhāvena cira-pravāsaṃ vinā nikaṭa-pravāse'pi tat-sphūrtyā
sambhavati | truṭir yugāyate tvām apaśyatām ity ādi nyāyena brahma-rātra-tativad
virahe'bhūt ity ādi nyāyena śaraj-jyotsnā-rāse vidhi-rajani-rūpāpi nimiṣādi-nyāyena

children.translated_text: and so forth. Therefore, in the Śrīmad <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> (15.203), as an illustration of <s>sampanna</s> [union], a verse from the Śrī

children.text: haṃsadūtasya padyaṃ dattam | ato vidagdha-mādhave (1.36) paugaṇḍatvena
children.translated_text: <s>Haṃsadūta</s> was given. Hence, in the <s>Vidagdha-mādhava</s> (1.36), His appearance

children.text:
bhāsamānatvaṃ darśitam | yathā duddha-muhassa vacchassa dāṇiṃ ko kkhu
uvvāhā-osaro | ity ādau |
children.translated_text: as being in the <s>paugaṇḍa</s> (boyhood) stage was shown. As in the [Prakrit]: 'For a calf just weaned from milk, what occasion is there now for marriage?' and so on.

And so on, in many [such passages].
Furthermore, in <s>Vraja</s>, the <s>śṛṅgāra</s> (erotic sentiment) of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> in the prime of youth (<s>nava-yauvana</s>) should be understood as <s>samṛddhimān</s> (opulent). And that, by the nature of <s>mahābhāva</s> (supreme ecstasy), is possible even in nearby separation — without prolonged absence — through the manifestation [of the feeling of prolonged separation]. By the principle 'A <s>truṭi</s> (moment) becomes a <s>yuga</s> for those who do not see You,' and by the principle 'It became like the night of <s>Brahmā</s> in separation,' the autumn-moonlit <s>rāsa</s> [dance], though of the nature of a single night by rule, [appeared prolonged] by the principle of a blink of an eye,

children.text:
nava-yauvanasyaiva sadāsthāyitvena dhyeyatvam | yathā stava-mālāyāṃ (utkalikā-
vallarī 17) śyāmayor nava-vayaḥ-suṣamābhyām ity ādau | ataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-dugdha-
mukhatvasya sadā sphūrtyā śrī-vrajeśvaryādibhis tasya pariṇayodyamaḥ kvāpi na
kṛtaḥ | kim uta mahā-bhāva-prabhedādhirūḍha-viśeṣa-mādana-bhāva-svabhāve |
sa ca taṃ vinā sambhavatīti vaktavyam | yathā śrī-ārṣa-vacanam-
children.translated_text: The <s>nava-yauvana</s> (fresh youth) alone, being the permanent state (<s>sadāsthāyin</s>), is to be meditated upon. As in the <s>Stava-mālā</s> (<s>Utkalikā-vallarī</s> 17): 'By the charm of the fresh youth of the dark Couple' and so on. Therefore, because of the constant manifestation of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa's</s> milk-drinking face [i.e., eternal boyhood], neither <s>Vrajeśvarī</s> (<s>Yaśodā</s>) nor others ever attempted His marriage. How much more so in the case of the special <s>mādana-bhāva</s> (supreme erotic ecstasy), which is a particular variety of <s>mahābhāva</s> at the stage of <s>adhirūḍha</s>? And that [<s>mādana-bhāva</s>] arises without Him [being absent] — this must be stated. As the ancient (<s>ārṣa</s>) verse says:
I worship the supreme culmination of the <s>bhāva</s> (spiritual ecstasy) of Śrī <s>Rādhikā</s> and others,

children.text: vinā viyogaṃ sambhogaṃ yā turyam udapādayat ||
children.translated_text: from which the fourth [state] arose as union without separation.
Here, 'the culmination of <s>bhāva</s>' means the <s>mādana</s> form. The definition of <s>mādana</s> (<s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> 14.219, 226, 229):
This <s>mādana</s>, in which all <s>bhāvas</s> arise and shine, is the supreme beyond the supreme.

children.text: rājate hlādinī-sāro rādhāyām eva yaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: The essence of <s>hlādinī</s> (-<s>śakti</s>, the bliss-potency), which always resides in <s>Rādhā</s> alone,

children.text: na nirvaktuṃ bhavec chakyā tenāsau munināpy alam |||
children.translated_text: cannot be described even by the sage (<s>Vyāsa</s>).

children.text: sphuranti vraja-devīṣu parā bhāva-bhidāś ca yāḥ |
children.translated_text: The supreme varieties of <s>bhāva</s> that manifest in the goddesses of <s>Vraja</s> —

children.text: tās tarkāygocaratyā na samyag iha varṇitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: those, being beyond the reach of reasoning, have not been fully described here.

children.text:
ity ādeś ca cira-nikaṭa-pravāse cira pravāsa sphūrtyā samṛddhimān sambhogo
bhavatīti kim āścaryam |
children.translated_text: And so forth. Thus, what wonder is it that in prolonged nearby separation, through the manifestation [of the feeling] of prolonged absence, the <s>samṛddhimān</s> (opulent) union occurs?

children.text:
nanu tarhi kathaṃ śrī-gosvāmi-pādaiḥ samṛddhimān sambhogo nava-vṛndāvane
udāhṛtaḥ ? tat tu spaṣṭa-līlāyāṃ nandanandana-vasudeva-nandanayor
ektavābhimānāt | tad yathā (11.12.13) mat kāmā ramaṇaṃ jāram asvarūpa-
children.translated_text: a sense of identity. As stated (<s>Bhāgavata</s> 11.12.13): 'Those women who desired Me, their lover — not knowing [My] true nature —

children.text: vido'balāḥ | tathā (10.46.3) gacchoddhava vrajaṃ saumya pitror naḥ prītim āvahan
children.translated_text: the unwise [women].' And also (10.46.3): 'Go, <s>Uddhava</s>, to <s>Vraja</s>, O gentle one, bringing delight to Our parents' —
and so on. Therefore, in the Śrīmad <s>Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> (15.185-6):

Now then, how was the <s>samṛddhimān</s> union illustrated by the Śrī <s>Gosvāmī</s> as taking place in Nava-<s>Vṛndāvana</s>? That is because in the manifest <s>līlā</s> (<s>spaṣṭa-līlā</s>), <s>Nandanandana</s> (the son of <s>Nanda</s>) and <s>Vasudeva-nandana</s> (the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>) have
In accordance with the manifest [aspect] of <s>Hari's</s> particular <s>līlā</s>,
the state of separation of the beautiful-browed women of <s>Goṣṭha</s> (<s>Vraja</s>) has been described.
[But] by <s>Hari</s>, who always sports in <s>Vṛndāraṇya</s> (<s>Vṛndāvana</s>) with the <s>rāsa</s> dance and other delights,
there is never any separation from the goddesses of <s>Vraja</s>.

children.text:
ataeva śrī-rasāmṛta-sindhau (2.5.128) śrī-bhāgavatādi-gūḍhārthaḥ śrī-gosvāmi-
pādair darśitaḥ | yathā-
children.translated_text: Therefore, in the Śrī <s>Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</s> (2.5.128), the hidden meaning of the Śrī <s>Bhāgavata</s> and other texts was shown by the Śrī <s>Gosvāmī</s>. Namely:
This state of separation has been described in accordance with the manifest <s>līlā</s>;

children.text: kṛṣṇena viprayogaḥ syān na jātu vraja-vāsinām ||
children.translated_text: [but] there is never any separation of the residents of <s>Vraja</s> from <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
As indeed the statement from the <s>Yāmala</s> [tantra]:

children.text:
kṛṣṇo'nyo yadu-sambhūto yaḥ pūrṇaḥ so'sty ataḥ param |
vṛndāvanaṃ parityajya sa kvacit naiva gacchati || iti |
children.translated_text:
The <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> who was born among the <s>Yadus</s> is a different, complete [manifestation]; beyond that,
He never leaves <s>Vṛndāvana</s> and goes anywhere. Thus.

children.text:
spaṣṭa-lkīlā śrī-nandanandana-vasudeva-nandanayor ekātma-vyañjikāḥ | aspaṣṭa-
līlā gūḍha-līlā tayor bheda-vyañjikā | ataeva śrī-nanda-yaśodādīnāṃ parikaraiḥ
saha dvāravatyādi-gamanaṃ vrajeśāder aṃśabhūtā ye droṇādyā ity ādivat jñeyam
| śrī-lalita-mādhave (10.36) śrī-rādhā-prārthanā--
children.translated_text: The manifest <s>līlā</s> (<s>spaṣṭa-līlā</s>) reveals the identity of <s>Nandanandana</s> and <s>Vasudeva-nandana</s>. The unmanifest <s>līlā</s> (<s>aspaṣṭa-līlā</s>), the hidden <s>līlā</s> (<s>gūḍha-līlā</s>), reveals their distinction. Therefore, the going of the associates of Śrī <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Yaśodā</s>, and others to <s>Dvārakā</s> and the like should be understood as being like the [statement] 'Those who were portions [of <s>Vrajeśa</s>], such as <s>Droṇa</s> and others,' and so on. In the Śrī <s>Lalita-mādhava</s> (10.36), the prayer of Śrī <s>Rādhā</s>:
The blessed land of <s>Mathurā</s>, surrounded by forests

children.text: dhanyā kṣauṇī vilasati vṛtā māthurī mādhurībhiḥ |
children.translated_text: that exude the fragrance of the <s>rasa</s> of Your pastimes, shines with [Your] sweetness;
there, by us, whose hearts are enchanted with the <s>bhāva</s> of playful cowherd-women,
may You, with the flute gleaming on Your face, engage in sport! [verse 38]
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>: 'O beloved, so be it!'
<s>Rādhikā</s>: 'How [can that be] indeed?'

children.text:
(kṛṣṇaḥ sthagitam ivāpasavyato vilokate |)
(praviśya gārgyā sahāpaṭīkṣepeṇa ekānaṃśā |)
children.translated_text:
(<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> looks to the side as if concealing something.)
(Enter <s>Ekānaṃśā</s> together with <s>Gārgī</s>, throwing aside the curtain.)

children.text:
ekānaṃśā-sakhi rādhe ! mātra saṃśayaṃ kṛthāḥ | yato bhavatyaḥ śrīmati gokule
tatraiva vartante kintu mayaiva kāla-kṣepaṇārtham anyathā prapañcitam | tad etan
manasy uanbhūyatām | kṛṣṇo'py eṣa tatra gata eva pratīyatām |
children.translated_text: <s>Ekānaṃśā</s>: O friend <s>Rādhā</s>! Do not entertain any doubt. For you ladies are in the illustrious <s>Gokula</s>, and there indeed you remain. It is only by me that [the appearance of being elsewhere] has been contrived for the sake of passing time. Let this be understood in your mind. And let it be understood that <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> too has gone there [i.e., He never left].
<s>Gārgī</s> (aside): My father's good prediction has borne fruit!

children.text:
śrī-bhāgavate yathā śrī-nandanandana-vasudeva-nandanayor ekatva-vyañjikā
spaṣṭā | tathā śrī-lalita-mādhave vindhyādāra-prasūtā-kīrtidā-prasūtayor ekatva-
vyañjikā līlā spaṣṭā | yathā gūḍha-līlāyāṃ śrī-kṛṣṇo vasudeva-nandana-rūpeṇa
gatas tathā śrī-rādhā satyabhāmā-rūpeṇa gatā | yathā spaṣṭa-līlāyāṃ vasudeva-
nandane nanda-nandanāveśas tathā śrī-satyabhāmāyāṃ śrī-rādhāveśa iti |
children.translated_text:
Just as in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>, the indication of the oneness of <s>Śrī Nanda-nandana</s> and <s>Vasudeva-nandana</s>
is clear, similarly in the <s>Śrī Lalita-Mādhava</s> the pastime indicating the oneness of <s>Vindhyādara</s>'s daughter <s>Kīrtidā</s>'s daughter [<s>Rādhā</s>] and [<s>Satyabhāmā</s>]
is clear. Just as in the concealed pastime (<s>gūḍha-līlā</s>) <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> went in the form of <s>Vasudeva-nandana</s>,
so <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> went in the form of <s>Satyabhāmā</s>. Just as in the manifest pastime the presence of <s>Nanda-nandana</s>
is within <s>Vasudeva-nandana</s>, so is the presence of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> within <s>Śrī Satyabhāmā</s>.

children.text:
nanv aprakaṭa-līlāyāṃ pūrva-rāgo nāstīti prakaṭa-līlā-viśeṣo'pekṣyaḥ | prakaṭa-
līlāyāṃ samṛddhimān sambhogo nāstīty aprakaṭa-līlā-viśeṣo'pekṣyaḥ | ataeva
gokulasya prakaṭāprakaṭa-prakāśayoḥ svarūpeṇa dvaividhyaṃ syāt | evaṃ līlāyāś
ca ? tatrāha samṛddhimān sambhogas tatra prakaṭa-līlāyāṃ na jātaś cet, tad artham
aprakaṭa-līlā-viśeṣo'pekṣyaḥ | sa tatra jāta eva yathā dantavakra-vadhānantaraṃ
ramya-keli-sukhenātra māsa-dvayam uvāsa ha iti |
children.translated_text:
Now, [one may object:] since <s>pūrva-rāga</s> (prior attraction) does not exist in the unmanifest pastime (<s>aprakaṭa-līlā</s>), the specific features of the manifest pastime (<s>prakaṭa-līlā</s>) must be sought. Since enriched union (<s>samṛddhimān sambhoga</s>) does not exist in the manifest pastime, the specific features of the unmanifest pastime must be sought. Therefore, <s>Gokula</s>'s essential nature would be twofold in its manifest and unmanifest manifestations; likewise for the pastime.
To this he replies: if that enriched union has not arisen in the manifest pastime, then for that purpose the specific features of the unmanifest pastime must be sought. But it has indeed arisen there, as [stated]: 'After the killing of <s>Dantavakra</s>, He dwelt there for two months in the happiness of charming amorous play.' Thus.

children.text:
kiṃ ca svakīyāsu samañjasā ratiḥ, sā cānurāgāntāḥ | tatra jāti-bhedena
samṛddhimān sambhogo rasa-niryāsatvena na kathyate | parakīyāsu samarthā ratiḥ
| sā ca bhāvāntā | vaiśiṣṭyaṃ pātra-vaiśiṣṭyād ratir eṣopagacchati (BRS 2.5.1) iti
samarthā-rati-sthāyikaḥ samṛddhimān sambhogo rasa-niryāsatvena kathyate | ataeva
prakaṭa-līlāyāṃ pūrva-rāga-samṛddhimantau jātau | a prakaṭa-līlā-viśeṣa-
svīkāreṇa kiṃ prayojanam ? kiṃ ca jāta-prākaṭyāḥ pūrva-rāgādi-gatā līlā
aprakaṭā adhunā vartante tāsāṃ punaḥ prākaṭye kiṃ punaḥ pūrvarāgādi-rūpaṃ
nija-prayojanaṃ bhavati | līlāyāḥ prakaṭāyāṃ samṛddhimata āsvādanam asty eva
| tad arthaṃ prakaṭa-līlā-viśeṣa ity asaṅgatir iti | kintu rasa-śāstre sambhogasya
rātri-prādhānyatvāt | sa ca samṛddhimān rātrāv eva jāyate yathā nikaṭa-dūretyādi-
pūrvavat |
children.translated_text:
Moreover, in the wedded women (<s>svakīyā</s>), there is <s>samañjasā rati</s> (proper attachment), and that extends up to <s>anurāga</s>. Therein, due to the difference in type,
enriched union is not spoken of as the essence of <s>rasa</s>. In the unwedded women (<s>parakīyā</s>), there is <s>samarthā rati</s> (competent attachment),
and that extends up to <s>bhāva</s>. 'The distinction — attachment attains distinction due to the distinction of the vessel' (BRS 2.5.1) — thus
enriched union, whose permanent mood is <s>samarthā rati</s>, is spoken of as the essence of <s>rasa</s>. Therefore,
both <s>pūrva-rāga</s> and enriched [union] have arisen in the manifest pastime. What purpose is served by accepting a specific feature of the unmanifest pastime?
Moreover, the pastimes involving <s>pūrva-rāga</s> and so forth that had become manifest — those now exist as unmanifest;
when they become manifest again, do <s>pūrva-rāga</s> and similar features serve their own purpose again? The relishing of the enriched [union] indeed exists
in the manifest pastime; for that purpose, [to say] 'this is a specific feature of the manifest pastime' is inconsistent. However, since in the science of <s>rasa</s>,
nighttime is predominant for <s>sambhoga</s>, and that enriched [union] arises only at night — as stated previously regarding proximity, distance, and so forth.

children.text:
kecit tu dantavakra-vadhānantaraṃ prauḍha-yauvane ##[*ENDNOTE #14] prauḍha-
yauvanaṃ vicāryate | ānukramikī līlā nityā | sā ca janma karma ca me divyam ity
ādeḥ | tasyāṃ śrī-nandanandanasya vayo-gaṇanaṃ śrī-vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇyām nirṇītam
eva | tat tu pañcaviṃśaty-adhika-śata-varṣa-paryantam | tad-vyavasthā | vraje
ekādaśa-samāḥ | tatra sāvitrya-janmābhāvena dharma-śāstra-virodhād vivāho nāsti
| rāsa-krīḍā-sukha-sambhoge parakīyātvam evety arthaḥ | mathurāyāṃ
caturviṃśatiḥ varṣāḥ | tatrāpi nāsti vivāhaḥ | tataḥ sambhogād anantaraṃ
satyabhāmādīnāṃ | tataḥ ṣoḍaśa-sahasra-kanyānām | tataḥ putra-pautrādayo
bahavo jātāḥ | tato dantavakra-vadhānantaraṃ līlāvasāne vrajāgamanam | tatrāpi
keṣāṃcin mate vivāhaḥ śrī-rādhādibhiḥ sammataḥ | tad asaṅgatam | śrī-bhāgavate
kutrāpy avarṇitatvāt | bandhu-vargāer niṣedhābhāvena rasotkarṣābhāvāc ca |
ataeva gocāraṇādi-janya-virahābhāvas tato rāsa-dāna-mānādi-līlāder abhāvena
dūtī preṣaṇāder abhāvaḥ syāt | ataeva śrī-rūpa-pādair navayauvanasya
sadādheyatvena varṇitatvāt śrī-mahāprabhoḥ pārṣada-vṛndair vivāhasya kutrāpy
avarṇitatvāc ca | śrī-padma-purāṇa-mate lalita-mādhave vivāha-varṇanaṃ kalpa-
bhedena samādheyam |
children.translated_text:
Some, however, [argue that] after the killing of <s>Dantavakra</s>, in the full bloom of youth (<s>prauḍha-yauvana</s>) ##[*ENDNOTE #14] — the full bloom of youth
is to be considered. The sequential pastime (<s>ānukramikī līlā</s>) is eternal, as [stated]: 'My birth and action are divine' and so forth.
Therein, the age-calculation of <s>Śrī Nanda-nandana</s> has been determined in the <s>Śrī Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī</s>.
That extends up to one hundred and twenty-five years. Its arrangement: in <s>Vraja</s>, eleven years. There, since the <s>sāvitra</s> birth (investiture with sacred thread) has not occurred, there is no marriage due to conflict with <s>dharma-śāstra</s>.
The meaning is that in the blissful union of the <s>rāsa-krīḍā</s>, the <s>parakīyā</s> mood alone [prevails]. In <s>Mathurā</s>, twenty-four years.
There too, there is no marriage. Then, after the union with <s>Satyabhāmā</s> and others. Then, of the sixteen thousand maidens.
Then, many sons, grandsons, and so forth were born. Then, after the killing of <s>Dantavakra</s>, at the conclusion of the pastime, the return to <s>Vraja</s>.
There too, in the view of some, marriage with <s>Śrī Rādhā</s> and others is accepted. That is inconsistent,
since it is nowhere described in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>; since there is no prohibition by the kinsmen, there would be no intensification of <s>rasa</s>.
Therefore, there would be an absence of separation born of cow-herding and so forth, and hence an absence of <s>rāsa</s>, <s>dāna</s>, <s>māna</s>, and other pastimes, and an absence of sending messengers (<s>dūtī-preṣaṇa</s>) and so forth. Therefore, since <s>Śrī Rūpa Pāda</s> (Rūpa Gosvāmī) has described <s>nava-yauvana</s> (ever-fresh youth) as eternally to be meditated upon, and since by <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s>'s associate-groups marriage is nowhere described —
the description of marriage in the <s>Lalita-Mādhava</s> according to the <s>Śrī Padma Purāṇa</s> view is to be reconciled through difference of <s>kalpa</s> (cosmic cycle).

children.text:
tasmāt sarveṣāṃ mate prakaṭāprakaṭa-līlāyāṃ parakīyaiva nityatvāt | vivāhaṃ
svīkṛtya tenaiva līlāyā aparakaṭatvaṃ matvā svakīyāyā nityatvaṃ manyate | tad
asaṅgatam | pūrva-hetoḥ śrī-vrajeśvarādīnāṃ śrī-kṛṣṇasya sadā dugdha-
mukhatva-sphūrtyā sāvitra-janyābhāvena vivāhābhāvāt | nava-yauvana-saṃvalita-
pūrṇatamatvasya śrī-rūpa-gosvāmy-ādibhiḥ sadā dhyeyatvāc ca | tat tu śrī-
kṛṣṇasya mathurādi-gamanābhāvāt | sa ca kṛṣṇo'nyo yadu-sambhūtaḥ ity ādi |
mathurādi-gamane tu pūrṇataratvādipātāt | nava-yauvanasya sadā dhyeyatvaṃ yathā
stavamālāyāṃ (utkalikā-vallarī 17)-
children.translated_text:
Therefore, in the view of all, in both the manifest and unmanifest pastimes, the <s>parakīyā</s> mood alone is eternal.
Those who, having accepted marriage, consider the pastime to be non-manifest on that basis and regard the <s>svakīyā</s> mood as eternal — that
is inconsistent. Due to the aforementioned reason: since <s>Śrī Vrajeśvara</s> (Nanda) and others always perceive <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> as having a milk-drinking face (i.e., as an infant),
and since the <s>sāvitra</s> birth has not occurred, marriage is absent. And since <s>nava-yauvana</s> (ever-fresh youth) endowed with the fullest perfection (<s>pūrṇatamatva</s>)
is declared by <s>Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī</s> and others as always to be meditated upon — that is because <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> never departed to <s>Mathurā</s> and elsewhere.
'That <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is another, born among the <s>Yadus</s>' — and so forth.
If He had gone to <s>Mathurā</s> and elsewhere, there would be a fall from the fullest perfection. The eternal meditatability of <s>nava-yauvana</s>, as in the <s>Stavamālā</s> (<s>Utkalikā-vallarī</s> 17)—

children.text:
śyāmayor nava-vayaḥ-suṣamābhyāṃ
gaurayor amala-kānti-yaśobhyām |
kvāpi vām akhila-valgu-vataṃsau
mādhurī hṛdi sadā sphuratān me || ity ādeś ca |
children.translated_text:
Of the dark and golden Pair, with the beauty of ever-fresh youth,
with the splendor and glory of pure radiance —
somewhere, the sweetness that is the crest-ornament of all beauty of You both —
may it always shine forth in my heart. || And so forth. |

children.text:
asman-mate tu śrī-vasudeva-nandana-rūpeṇa mathurā-dvārakādau gatvā
dantavakra-vadhānantaraṃ punar vrajam āgatya tatra tu svayaṃ-prakāśa-rūpeṇa śrī-
vrajendra-nandanena līlāyāḥ prakaṭanaṃ kṛtam | tat tu trimāsyāḥ paratas tāsāṃ
sākṣāt kṛṣṇena saṅgatiḥ iti jātam | asya tu prakaṭāprakaṭe jātatvaṃ pūrvam eva
likhitam | tataḥ śrīmad-vrajendra-nandane pūrṇatarādi-prakāśe | na tu mathurā-
dvārakādau ca | ataḥ prakaṭāprakaṭe parakīyāyāḥ sad-bhāvena nityatvāt | tat tu
jayati jananivāsa ity āder vartamāna-prayogā bahavaḥ santi | ataḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-
caitanya-mahāprabhoḥ parivāreṣu śrīman-nityānandādvaitādibhiḥ śrī-
bhāgavatānusāreṇa prakaṭāprakaṭe vraja-līlāyāṃ śrī-kṛṣṇasyaupapatyaṃ
nityatvena svīkṛtya sva-sva-parivāre pravartitaṃ dṛśyate | teṣu ca śrī-gadādhara-
svarūpa-rūpa-sanātana-bhaṭṭa-raghunātha-dāsa-karṇapūrādibhis tat-tan-
matānusāreṇa tatra tatraiva parakīyātvaṃ sva-sva-grantha-gaṇe varṇayitvā
pravartitaṃ dṛśyate | līlā-mātrasya nityatvāt | tat tu jayati jananivāsaḥ ity ādeḥ |
children.translated_text:
In our view, however, having gone to <s>Mathurā</s>, <s>Dvārakā</s>, and other places in the form of <s>Śrī Vasudeva-nandana</s>,
after the killing of <s>Dantavakra</s>, having returned again to <s>Vraja</s>, there by <s>Śrī Vrajendra-nandana</s> in the form of His own self-manifestation (<s>svayaṃ-prakāśa</s>),
the manifestation of the pastime was accomplished. That, after three months, [the statement] 'their direct meeting with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>' was fulfilled.
That this occurs in both the manifest and unmanifest [pastimes] has been written previously. Therefore, in <s>Śrīmad Vrajendra-nandana</s>,
the manifestation of the fuller [perfection] and so forth — but not in <s>Mathurā</s>, <s>Dvārakā</s>, and elsewhere.
Therefore, since the <s>parakīyā</s> mood exists in both the manifest and unmanifest pastimes, it is eternal. As
many present-tense usages exist [beginning with] 'Victorious is the abode of all beings' and so forth. Therefore, among the associates of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya Mahāprabhu</s>,
<s>Śrīman Nityānanda</s>, <s>Advaita</s>, and others, following the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>, in both the manifest and unmanifest <s>Vraja-līlā</s>,
having accepted <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s>'s status as paramour (<s>aupapatya</s>) as eternal, they are seen to have propagated this in their respective circles.
Among them, <s>Śrī Gadādhara</s>, <s>Svarūpa</s>, <s>Rūpa</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, <s>Bhaṭṭa Raghunātha</s>, <s>Dāsa</s> [Raghunātha], <s>Karṇapūra</s>, and others,
following their respective doctrines, have described the <s>parakīyā</s> mood precisely in their respective collections of works
and propagated it. Because the pastime itself is eternal — as [stated:] 'Victorious is the abode of all beings' and so forth.

children.text:
tathā śrī-rāmānujācārya-madhvācārya-prabhṛtibhiś ca līlā-mātrasya nityatvaṃ
sthāpyate | ato līlā-mātrasya nityatvenānukramikyā līlāyā nityatve na doṣas tasmāt
prakaṭāprakaṭe parakīyāyā nityatvam |
children.translated_text:
Likewise, by <s>Śrī Rāmānujācārya</s>, <s>Madhvācārya</s>, and others, the eternity of the pastime itself
is established. Therefore, since the pastime itself is eternal, in the eternity of the sequential pastime there is no fault; hence,
the <s>parakīyā</s> mood is eternal in both the manifest and unmanifest [pastimes].

children.text:
tat tu punaḥ paripāṭyā vicāryate | svayaṃ bhagavān śrī-vrajendra-nandanaḥ śrī-
kṛṣṇa-caitanyaḥ | sa ca saptottara-caturdaśa-śata-śakābde prakaṭitaḥ | jagad-
gurutvād ācāryatvam aṅgīkṛtavān | avatāre tu mukhya-kāraṇam āha (CC 1.1.6)-
children.translated_text: universal teacher, He accepted the role of <s>ācārya</s>. The primary cause of His descent is stated (CC 1.1.6)—

Now that is examined again in order. <s>Svayaṃ Bhagavān</s> (the Lord Himself), <s>Śrī Vrajendra-nandana</s>, is <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>.
He became manifest in the <s>Śaka</s> year 1407 (1486 CE). As the

children.text:
śrī-rādhāyāḥ praṇaya-mahimā kīdṛśo vānayaivā-
svādyo yenādbhuta-madhurimā kīdṛśo vā madīyaḥ |
saukhyaṃ cāsyā mad-anubhavataḥ kīdṛśaṃ veti lobhāt
tad-bhāvāḍhyaḥ samajani śacī-garbha-sindhau harīnduḥ || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
'What is the nature of the greatness of <s>Śrī Rādhā</s>'s love?
And what is the nature of My own wonderful sweetness, relished by Her alone?
And what is the nature of the happiness She experiences through tasting Me?' —
driven by such longing, <s>Hari</s>, the moon, enriched with Her mood, was born in the ocean of <s>Śacī</s>'s womb. || And so forth. |

children.text:
gauṇa-kāraṇaṃ tu bhū-bhāra-rūpa-mahā-pāpinām asura-svabhāvaṃ dūrīkṛtya kalau
mukhya-dharma-nāma-saṅkīrtana-pravartanam | tasya pramāṇaṃ anugrahāya
bhaktānām (10.33.36) ity ādi | ataeva śrī-nityānadādvaita-gadādhara-svarūpa-rūpa-
sanātanādīn nija-pārṣadān prakaṭayya tad-dvāreṇa yuga-dharmaṃ pravartayitvā
taiḥ saha punar aṣṭa-catvāriṃśad-varṣa-paryantaṃ prakaṭa-mukhya-kāraṇaṃ
mukhya-rasāsvādanaṃ kṛtavān | āsvādanaṃ tu sarva-vedānta-sāra-śrī-bhāgavata-
saṃmatam | tat tu prakaṭāprakaṭe nityatvāt | tatra ca (10.33.19)-
children.translated_text:
The secondary cause, however, is: having removed the <s>asura</s>-nature of the great sinners who constitute the burden of the earth,
the inauguration of <s>nāma-saṅkīrtana</s> (congregational chanting of the Name), which is the primary <s>dharma</s> of <s>Kali</s>-yuga. The authority for this:
'For the blessing of the devotees' (10.33.36) and so forth. Therefore, having manifested His own associates —
<s>Śrī Nityānanda</s>, <s>Advaita</s>, <s>Gadādhara</s>, <s>Svarūpa</s>, <s>Rūpa</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, and others — and through them having inaugurated the <s>dharma</s> of the age,
together with them, for forty-eight years in the manifest [pastime], He accomplished the manifest primary purpose:
the relishing of the supreme <s>rasa</s>. That relishing is sanctioned by the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>, the essence of all <s>Vedānta</s>.
That is eternal in both the manifest and unmanifest [pastimes]. Therein also (10.33.19)—
Having made Himself as many as there were cowherd women,

children.text: reme sa bhagavāṃs tābhir ātmārāmo 'pi līlayā ||
children.translated_text: that Lord, though self-delighted (<s>ātmārāma</s>), sported with them as a pastime. ||

children.text:
ity ādi bahuśaḥ | tasmād vrajendra-nandanasya gopa-strīṣūpapatitvaṃ tāsāṃ tu
tasmin parakīyātvaṃ krama-līlāvasāne prakaṭaṃ nityam eva | yataḥ śrīman-
mahāprabhuḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanyaḥ sarva-bhaktān tad evāsvādanaṃ kārayitvā
svayam evāsvādanaṃ kṛtavān | tatra svayam āsvādanaṃ yathā śrī-caitanya-
caritāmṛte (2.1.11)-
children.translated_text:
And so forth, in many places. Therefore, the paramour-status (<s>upapatitva</s>) of <s>Vrajendra-nandana</s> with the cowherd women,
and their <s>parakīyā</s> mood toward Him — at the conclusion of the sequential pastime, this is manifestly eternal. Because <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s>,
<s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s>, having made all the devotees relish that very thing, Himself also relished it.
Therein, His own relishing, as in the <s>Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s> (2.1.11)—

children.text:
caṇḍī-dāsa vidyāpati rāyera nāṭaka gīti
karṇāmṛta śrī gīta govinda
mahāprabhu rātri dine svarūpa-rāmānandera sane
nāce gāya parama ānanda
children.translated_text:
The songs of <s>Caṇḍīdāsa</s>, <s>Vidyāpati</s>, the dramas of <s>Rāya</s>,
the <s>Karṇāmṛta</s>, the <s>Śrī Gīta-govinda</s> —
<s>Mahāprabhu</s>, day and night, with <s>Svarūpa</s> and <s>Rāmānanda</s>,
dances and sings in supreme bliss.

children.text:
etad-abhāve hṛdi yasya preraṇayā pravartito'haṃ varāka-rūpo'pi iti vacanāt | śrī-
mahāprabhunā nija-prākaṭyasya prayojanasya śrīmad-rūpa-gosvāmi-kṛta-śrīmad-
ujjvala-nīlamaṇy-ādibhiḥ sampāditatvāt | prākaṭya-mukhya-prayojanasya hānyā
śrī-mahāprabhoḥ prākaṭyam aprayojakam | tasmāt śrī-mahāprabhoḥ
kṛtāsvādanasya parama-vijña-sevyatvam | yathā tatra śrī-dāsa-gosvāmi-kṛta-
stavāvalyāṃ (śrī-caitanyāṣṭake 4)
children.translated_text:
From the statement: 'In the absence of this, by whose inspiration in the heart I, though lowly in form, have been set in motion.' Because
the purpose of <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s>'s own manifestation was accomplished through <s>Śrīmad Rūpa Gosvāmī</s>'s compositions such as the <s>Śrīmad Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s> and others.
If the primary purpose of the manifestation were lost, <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s>'s manifestation would be purposeless. Therefore,
the relishing accomplished by <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s> is to be served by the supremely wise. As stated therein, in the <s>Stavāvalī</s> composed by <s>Śrī Dāsa Gosvāmī</s> (<s>Śrī Caitanyāṣṭaka</s> 4)—
That creeper of devotion, not revealed previously even by hosts of sages skilled in <s>bhakti</s>,
concealed within the <s>Śruti</s>, bearing the fruit of the radiant <s>rasa</s> of <s>prema</s> —

children.text: kṛpālus tāṃ gauḍe prabhu atikṛpābhiḥ prakaṭayan
children.translated_text: the compassionate Lord, manifesting it in <s>Gauḍa-deśa</s> with His supreme grace —

children.text: śacī-sūnuḥ kiṃ me nayana-saraṇīṃ yāsyati padam ||
children.translated_text: will that son of <s>Śacī</s> ever come within the path of my eyes? ||

children.text:
ataeva śrī-mahāprabhoḥ śakti-rūpaiḥ śrī-rūpa-gosvāmi-caraṇaiḥ śrīmad-ujjvala-
nīlamaṇi-śrī-vidagdha-mādhava-dāna-keli-kaumudy-ādi-granthānāṃ samarthā-
rati-vilāsa-rūpāṇāṃ sūtra-rūpe śrī-smaraṇa-maṅgale pratijñātam-śrī-rādhā-prāṇa-

children.translated_text: <s>bandhu</s>' (the life-companion of Śrī Rādhā). Likewise, in the <s>Laghu-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> (1.5.448, 451)—

Therefore, by <s>Śrī Rūpa Gosvāmī</s>'s feet, who are the potency-form of <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s>, in the works
such as the <s>Śrīmad Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s>, <s>Śrī Vidagdha-Mādhava</s>, <s>Dāna-keli-kaumudī</s>, and others,
whose form is the play of <s>samarthā rati</s> — in the <s>Śrī Smaraṇa-maṅgala</s>, in the form of a sūtra, it is pledged: '<s>Śrī Rādhā-prāṇa-</s>

children.text: prapañcāgocaratvena sā līlā prakaṭā matā || iti |
children.translated_text: Since it is beyond the reach of the material world, that pastime is considered manifest. || Thus. |
Now, when <s>Vrajendra</s>'s ordained festival has attained manifestation,

children.text: tatra prakaṭayaty eṣa līlā bālyādikā kramāt |
children.translated_text: therein He manifests childhood and other pastimes in sequence,
which He performs in His manifest forms and also in millions of unmanifest ones. ||

children.text:
evaṃ stava-mālā-stavāvalī-gaṇoddeśa-dīpikādiṣu prakaṭāprakaṭe vartamānāḥ
parakīyā līlāḥ prārthanīyā vartante | evaṃ śrī-mahāprabhu-pārṣada-vargaiḥ
kṛteṣu saṃskṛta-prākṛta-maya-grantha-nicayeṣu bahu-vidhāni pramāṇāni vartante|
tatra śrī-mahāprabhu-parama-guru-śrī-mādhavendra-purī-gosvāmi-pādiaḥ śrī-
śrī-bhagavat-prāpti-kāle prārthitavān-
children.translated_text:
Thus, in the <s>Stava-mālā</s>, <s>Stavāvalī</s>, <s>Gaṇoddeśa-dīpikā</s>, and other works, the <s>parakīyā</s> pastimes that exist
in both the manifest and unmanifest [modes] are the object of prayer. Thus, in the collections of works
composed in Sanskrit and Prakrit by the associate-groups of <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s>, there exist many kinds of evidence.
Therein, by <s>Śrī Mādhavendra Purī Gosvāmī</s>, the supreme <s>guru</s> of <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s>, at the time of attaining the Lord —
he prayed:

children.text:
ayi dīnadayārdra nātha he,
mathurānātha kadāvalokyase |
hṛdayaṃ tvad-aloka-kātaraṃ
dayita bhrāmyati kiṃ karomy aham || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
O Lord, whose heart melts with compassion for the wretched,
O Lord of <s>Mathurā</s>, when shall I behold You?
My heart, distressed by not seeing You,
O Beloved, wanders about — what shall I do? || And so forth. |

children.text:
tat tu pārṣadāḥ śrī-kṛṣṇa-caitanyasya prakaṭāprakaṭe sabhāsu svayam
āsvāditavantas teṣāṃ śiṣya-praśiṣyādayas tad-grantha-dvāreṇedānīm apy
āsvādayanti - jayati jananivāsa ity ādi-vartamāna-prayogair līlā-mātrasya nityatvāt
| tatra pramāṇāni yathā śrī-rāmānanda-rāya-gosvāmi-pādānāṃ jagannātha-
vallabhākhyaṃ nāṭakam, śrī-svarūpa-gosvāmi-pādānāṃ karacā, śrī-gadādhara-
paṇḍita-gosvāmi-pādānāṃ premāmṛta-stotrādi, śrī-narahari-ṭhakkura-pādānāṃ
śrī-kṛṣṇa-bhajanāmṛtādi, śrī-vāsudeva-ghoṣa-pādānāṃ padāvaly-ādi, śrī-
rāghava-paṇḍita-gosvāmi-pādānāṃ śrī-bhaktiratna-prakāśādi, śrī-viṣṇu-purī-
gosvāmi-pādānāṃ bhakti-ratnāvaly-ādi, śrī-sārvabhauma-bhaṭṭācārya-pādānāṃ
śrīman-mahāprabhoḥ śata-nāma-stotrādi, śrī-prabodhānanda-sarasvatī-pādānāṃ
pādānāṃ śrī-vṛndāvana-śatakādi, śrī-sanātana-gosvāmi-pādānāṃ śrī-vaiṣṇava-
toṣaṇy-ādi, śrī-rūpa-gosvāmi-pādānāṃ śrī-bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhuḥ, śrī-ujjvala-
nīlamaṇiḥ, śrī-vidagdha-mādhavādi, śrī-gopāla-bhaṭṭa-gosvāmi-pādānāṃ śrī-
bhāgavata-sandarbha-śrī-kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta-ṭīkādiḥ, śrī-raghunātha-bhaṭṭa-
gosvāmi-pādānāṃ tat-śiṣya-dvāreṇa śrībhāgavatādi-bhakti-śāstra-paṭhana-
pāṭhanādikam, śrī-raghunātha-dāsa-gosvāmi-pādānāṃ muktā-carita-stava-mālādi,
śrī-karṇapūra-gosvāmi-pādānāṃ śrī-ānanda-vṛndāvana-campū-śrī-kṛṣṇāhnika-
kaumudī-śrī-gaura-gaṇoddeśa-śrī-caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭakādi, śrī-
bhāgavatācārya-pādānāṃ śrī-kṛṣṇa-prema-taraṅginī, tatra śrīmad-anantācārya-
pāda-śrī-nayanānanda-pādādīnāṃ padāvaly-ādi |
children.translated_text: Now, the associates (<s>pārṣadas</s>) of <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa Caitanya</s> personally tasted [these truths] in both the manifest and unmanifest assemblies; their disciples and sub-disciples even now taste them through their writings — by the use of present tense in 'Jayati Jananivāsa' and similar [expressions], since the pastimes alone are eternal. The evidence therein is as follows: of the venerable <s>Rāmānanda Rāya Gosvāmī</s>, the drama called <s>Jagannātha-vallabha</s>; of the venerable <s>Svarūpa Gosvāmī</s>, his <s>Karacā</s> (notebook); of the venerable <s>Gadādhara Paṇḍita Gosvāmī</s>, the <s>Premāmṛta-stotra</s> and other works; of the venerable <s>Narahari Ṭhakkura</s>, the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-bhajanāmṛta</s> and others; of the venerable <s>Vāsudeva Ghoṣa</s>, the <s>Padāvalī</s> and others; of the venerable <s>Rāghava Paṇḍita Gosvāmī</s>, the <s>Bhaktiratna-prakāśa</s> and others; of the venerable <s>Viṣṇu Purī Gosvāmī</s>, the <s>Bhakti-ratnāvalī</s> and others; of the venerable <s>Sārvabhauma Bhaṭṭācārya</s>, the <s>Śata-nāma-stotra</s> of <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s> and others; of the venerable <s>Prabodhānanda Sarasvatī</s>, the <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana-śataka</s> and others; of the venerable <s>Sanātana Gosvāmī</s>, the <s>Śrī Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī</s> and others; of the venerable <s>Rūpa Gosvāmī</s>, the <s>Śrī Bhakti-rasāmṛta-sindhu</s>, the <s>Śrī Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s>, the <s>Śrī Vidagdha-mādhava</s> and others; of the venerable <s>Gopāla Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī</s>, the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata-sandarbha</s>, the commentary on <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta</s> and others; of the venerable <s>Raghunātha Bhaṭṭa Gosvāmī</s>, through his disciples, the reading and teaching of the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> and other devotional scriptures; of the venerable <s>Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī</s>, the <s>Muktā-carita</s>, the <s>Stava-mālā</s> and others; of the venerable <s>Karṇapūra Gosvāmī</s>, the <s>Śrī Ānanda-vṛndāvana-campū</s>, the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇāhnika-kaumudī</s>, the <s>Śrī Gaura-gaṇoddeśa</s>, the <s>Śrī Caitanya-candrodaya-nāṭaka</s> and others; of the venerable <s>Bhāgavatācārya</s>, the <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-prema-taraṅgiṇī</s>; and therein, of the venerable <s>Anantācārya</s>, the venerable <s>Nayanānanda</s> and others, the <s>Padāvalī</s> and other works.

children.text:
evaṃ ca śrī-mahāprabhos tāmbūla-carvita-janma-śrī-nityānanda-prabhu-sevaka-śrī-
nārāyaṇī-putra-śrī-vṛndāvana-ṭhakkura-varṇita-śrī-caitanya-bhāgavatādi | tat tu
śrī-nityānanda-prabhunā sākṣāt preraṇayā likhitaṃ bhavati | tathā hi śrī-caitanya-
caritāmṛte (1.8.) caitanya-līlāra vyāsa vṛndāvana dāsa ity ādi |
children.translated_text: And thus the <s>Śrī Caitanya Bhāgavata</s> and other works composed by <s>Śrī Vṛndāvana Ṭhakkura</s>, the son of <s>Śrī Nārāyaṇī</s>, the servant of <s>Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu</s>, who was born from <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s>'s chewed betel. And that was written by the direct inspiration of <s>Śrī Nityānanda Prabhu</s>. As stated in the <s>Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s> (1.8): 'The <s>Vyāsa</s> of <s>Caitanya</s>'s pastimes is <s>Vṛndāvana Dāsa</s>' and so forth.

children.text:
evaṃ śrī-mahāprabhor mata-virodhinaḥ śrīmad-acyutānandādi vinā śrīmad-
advaita-prabhu-putrāḥ śrīmad-advaitācārya-pādais tyaktāḥ | tat tu śrī-caitanya-
caritāmṛtādau prasiddham | evam upamahatsu śrī-locana-dāsa-ṭhakkura-kṛta-śrī-
caitanya-maṅgala-durlabha-sārādi, śrī-kṛṣṇadāsa-kavirāja-mahānubhāva-kṛta-śrī-
govinda-līlāmṛta-śrī-caitanya-caritāmṛta-śrī-kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta-ṭīkādi |
śrīnivāsācārya-kṛta-catuḥ-ślokī-ṭīkādi, śrī-narottama-dāsa-ṭhakkura-śrī-
govinda-kavirāja-kṛta-padāvaly-ādayaḥ sarvatra prasiddhāḥ | evam utkala-nivāsi-
śrī-śyāmānandādīnāṃ padāvalī prasiddhā |
children.translated_text: Thus, except for the venerable <s>Acyutānanda</s> and others who opposed <s>Śrī Mahāprabhu</s>'s doctrine, the sons of <s>Śrīmad Advaita Prabhu</s> were rejected by <s>Śrīmad Advaitācārya</s> himself. This is well known in the <s>Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s> and other works. Likewise, among the secondary authorities: the <s>Śrī Caitanya-maṅgala</s> and <s>Durlabha-sāra</s> composed by <s>Śrī Locana Dāsa Ṭhakkura</s>; the <s>Śrī Govinda-līlāmṛta</s>, <s>Śrī Caitanya-caritāmṛta</s>, and commentary on <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa-karṇāmṛta</s> composed by the great soul <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja</s>; the commentary on the <s>Catuḥ-ślokī</s> and other works by <s>Śrīnivāsācārya</s>; the <s>Padāvalī</s> and other works by <s>Śrī Narottama Dāsa Ṭhakkura</s> and <s>Śrī Govinda Kavirāja</s> — all are well-known everywhere. Likewise, the <s>Padāvalī</s> of <s>Śrī Śyāmānanda</s> and others residing in <s>Utkala</s> (Orissa) is well-known.

children.text: kiṃ ca śrīman-mahāprabhor mantra-sevakaḥ sākṣāt ko'pi śrī-rūpa-sanātanādīnāṃ
ca | tatra śakti-sañcāra-kṛta-sevakatve pramāṇaṃ manaḥ-śikṣāyāṃ (7,12) yadīccher
children.translated_text: Therein, the evidence for initiation accomplished through the transmission of power (<s>śakti-sañcāra</s>) is in the <s>Manaḥ-śikṣā</s> (7, 12): 'If you desire

children.text: āvāsaṃ vraja-bhuvi sa-rāgaṃ pratijanuḥ ity atraiva, sa-yūtha-śrī-rūpānuga iha
children.translated_text: a dwelling in the land of <s>Vraja</s>, with passion (<s>sa-rāgam</s>), in every birth' — in that very [verse], 'in this [<s>Vraja</s>], O you who follow <s>Śrī Rūpa</s> with her group,
in the forest of <s>Gokula</s>' and so forth. In the first part of <s>Śrī Bṛhad-bhāgavatāmṛta</s> (1.1.1)—
Moreover, who indeed was the direct <s>mantra</s>-initiator of <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s>, and of <s>Śrī Rūpa</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, and others?

children.text:
namaś caitanya-devāya sva-nāmāmṛta-sevine |
yad rūpāśrayaṇād yasya ity ādi |
atha śrī-jīva-gosvāmi-pādaḥ śrīmad-rūpa-pādasya bhrātuṣputras tasmāt taṃ
mantra-sevakaṃ kṛtavān | tasya tu śrīman-mahāprabhor darśanaṃ nāsti śrīmad-
rūpādīnām aprakaṭe parakīyātvaṃ svakīyātvaṃ ca mataṃ sva-granthe likhitaṃ tena
| tatra svakīyātvaṃ śrīmad-raghunātha-dāsa-prabhṛtayaḥ śrī-caitanya-pārṣadāḥ
śrī-rūpādi-saṅgino'naṅgī-kṛtavantaḥ | śrī-jīva-pādasya tat tu svecchā-likhanaṃ na
bhavati | kintu parecchā-likhanam | tat-pāṇḍitya-balāt likhana-paripāṭī-darśanena
paṇḍita-janās tat svīkurvanti | ye ca labdha-śrī-mahāprabhu-kṛpā labdha-śrī-
rūpādi-kṛpās te tu sarvathā nāṅgīkurvanti | etan-mata-pravartanaṃ tu kāla-kṛtam
eva | tat tu sarvaṃ kāla-kṛtam manye ity ādi | śreyāṃsi bahu-vighnāni ity ādi ca |
atas tu kecid evaṃ vadanti śrī-jīva-pādas tu bhrātuṣputra eva śiṣyaś ca | tan-mataṃ
svakīyātvam eva | tasmāt brūyuḥ snigdhasya śiṣyasya guravo guhyam apy uta (1.1.8)
children.translated_text: is <s>svakīyātva</s> (the wedded-love doctrine) alone. Therefore, according to the maxim 'Preceptors reveal even secrets to an affectionate disciple' (1.1.8),

children.text:
ity-ādi-nyāyena śrīmad-rūpa-pāda-mataṃ svakīyātvam eva | evaṃ cet śrīman-
mahāprabhoḥ pārṣadeṣu viruddhaṃ jātam | śrīman-mahāprabhuṇā tu śrīmad-
rūpa-sanātanau prati svakīyātvam upadiṣṭam | anyeṣu tu parakīyātvam
upadiṣṭam iti gurutaraṃ viruddhaṃ syāt | śrīmad-rūpa-gosvāmi-pādānāṃ śakti-
sañcāropadiṣṭa-śrīmaj-jīva-pādādi-śiṣyāṇāṃ sarveṣāṃ parakīyaiva | kevalaṃ śrī-
jīva-gosvāmi-pāda-gaṇa-madhye kvacit kvacid guru-viruddham āścaryaṃ dṛśyate
| yato'dyāpi teṣu santāneṣu evaṃ śiṣyeṣu sva-sva-grantheṣu prakaṭe'prakaṭe ca
parakīyātvaṃ dṛśyate | tasmāt śrīman-mahāprabhos tat-pārṣadādīnāṃ ca
parakīyātvam eva matam | śrīmaj-jīva-pādena tu yat svakīyātvaṃ likhitam tat
parecchayaiva | ataeva śrī-kṛṣṇa-sandarbhe svakīyā-siddhāntānantaraṃ tad-doṣaḥ
prārthanayā svayam eva kṣamāpitaḥ | tathā hi-
children.translated_text: the view of the venerable <s>Rūpa</s> must also be <s>svakīyātva</s> alone. If that were so, a contradiction would arise among <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s>'s associates. [For it would mean that] <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s> taught <s>svakīyātva</s> to <s>Śrīmad Rūpa</s> and <s>Sanātana</s>, but <s>parakīyātva</s> to others — which would be an even greater contradiction. Among all the disciples of the venerable <s>Rūpa Gosvāmī</s> — those initiated through the transmission of power, including the venerable <s>Jīva</s> — [the view is] <s>parakīyā</s> alone. Only in some places within the lineage of the venerable <s>Jīva Gosvāmī</s> is something astonishingly contrary to the <s>guru</s> seen. Since even now, in those lineages and among those disciples, <s>parakīyātva</s> is found in their own works, both publicly and privately. Therefore, the view of <s>Śrīman Mahāprabhu</s> and His associates is <s>parakīyātva</s> alone. What the venerable <s>Jīva</s> wrote regarding <s>svakīyātva</s> was indeed at the desire of another. And therefore, in the <s>Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha</s>, immediately after the <s>svakīyā</s> conclusion, the fault thereof was apologized for by himself through a prayer. As follows—
Therefore, some say thus: The venerable <s>Jīva</s> was indeed [<s>Rūpa</s>'s] nephew and also his disciple; his view

children.text: yad etat tu mayā kṣudratareṇa taralāyitaṃ |
children.translated_text: Whatever agitation has been made here by me, the most insignificant one —
may the glorious <s>Gokula-vallabha</s> (Lord of <s>Gokula</s>), who is of a forgiving nature, forgive that. ||

children.text:
tatra śiṣya-paramparā-śravaṇam āha-gopāla-dāsa-nāmā ko'pi vaiśyaḥ śrī-jīva-
gosvāmi-pādānāṃ priya-śiṣyaḥ | tat-prārthanā-paravaśena tena svakīyātvaṃ
siddhāntitam | ataeva śrīmad-rūpa-sanātana-pādādīnāṃ grantheṣu kutra kutrāpi
chedanādikaṃ kṛtam | kṛtvāpi tatra tatrāpi sva-doṣa-kṣamāpaṇaṃ kṛtam | yathā
śrī-kṛṣṇa-sandarbhe yad etat tu mayā kṣudratameṇa taralāyitam | śrī-laghu-
vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇyāṃ ca (sarvāntime)-
children.translated_text: Therein, the tradition of hearing through the disciple-succession states — a certain <s>Vaiśya</s> named <s>Gopāla Dāsa</s> was the beloved disciple of the venerable <s>Jīva Gosvāmī</s>. Compelled by his entreaties, [<s>Jīva</s>] established the <s>svakīyātva</s> doctrine. And therefore, in the works of <s>Śrīmad Rūpa</s>, <s>Sanātana</s>, and others, excisions and such were made here and there. Even having made them, apologies for his own fault were offered in various places. As in the <s>Kṛṣṇa-sandarbha</s>: 'Whatever agitation has been made here by me, the most insignificant one.' And in the <s>Śrī Laghu-vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī</s> (at the very end)—
This <s>Līlā-stava</s> and commentary, the <s>Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī</s>,
was abridged by me, the most insignificant one, at his command. ||

children.text: abuddhyā buddhyā vā yad iha mayakālekhi sahasā
children.translated_text: Whatever was hastily written here by me, whether through ignorance or through deliberation,

children.text: tathī̀a yad vācchedi dvayam api saheran param api |
children.translated_text: and whatever was cut — may both be endured by the great ones!

children.text: aho kiṃ vā yad yan manasi mama visphoritam abhūd
children.translated_text: Ah, or whatever flashed forth in my mind —

children.text: ambhobhis tan mātraṃ yadi balam alaṃ śaṅkita-kulaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: if that alone [causes agitation] like waters [troubling] families overcome with doubt, [may it be forgiven]. ||

children.text: harināmāmṛte tan-nāma spaṣṭam evoṭṭaṅkitam | tad yathā-
children.translated_text: In the <s>Harināmāmṛta</s>, that name is clearly engraved. That is as follows—
The work whose purpose is known by the name <s>Harināmāmṛta</s> — this I have published.

children.text: ubhayatra mama mitraṃ sa bhavatu gopāla-dāsākhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: May he who is called <s>Gopāla Dāsa</s> be my friend in both [worlds]. ||
And in the invocation of the <s>Śrī Gopāla-campū</s> (GCP 1.5)—
For the delight of the followers of <s>Śrī Gopāla</s>, for the cowherds —

children.text: bhavatu samantād eṣā nāmnā gopāla-campūr yā ||
children.translated_text: may this, which is called <s>Gopāla-campū</s> by name, be [beneficial] in every way. ||
And in the commentary on the <s>Śrīmad Ujjvala-nīlamaṇi</s>—

children.text: svecchayā likhitaṃ kiñcit kiñcid atra parecchayā |
children.translated_text: Some things here were written by my own will, some at the will of another;

children.text: yat pūrvāpara-sambandhaṃ tat pūrvam aparaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: that which has proper connection with what precedes and follows is the former; the other is the latter. ||
And in the <s>Śrī Bhāgavata-sandarbha</s>—
In order to please those two saints, the glorious <s>Rūpa</s> and <s>Sanātana</s>,
by the southern <s>Bhaṭṭa</s> (<s>Gopāla Bhaṭṭa</s>), this was again examined. ||
His original manuscript-writing, having been traversed [and found] exceeded and broken [in parts],
was reconsidered, rearranged, and then rewritten by <s>Jīvaka</s> (<s>Jīva</s>). ||
And so forth.

children.text:
śrī-kṛṣṇa-dāsa-nāmā brāhmaṇo gauḍīyaḥ śrīmaj-jīva-vidyādhyayane śiṣyaḥ, na
tu mantra-śiṣyaḥ | teṣāṃ śiṣyākaraṇāt | śiṣya-karaṇe pravṛttiś cet tarhi śrīnivāsa-
narottamādīnāṃ śiṣyatvaṃ śrī-jīvena katham atyāji | tasmāt teṣv aprakaṭeṣu
svādhikārecchayā tan-mantra-śiṣyatva-prakaṭanaṃ kṛṣṇa-dāsena svenaiva kṛtam
| teṣāṃ grantheṣu chedanādi kutra kṛtaṃ, kutrāpi pallavitam |
children.translated_text: A <s>Brāhmaṇa</s> named <s>Kṛṣṇa Dāsa</s>, a <s>Gauḍīya</s>, was a student of the venerable <s>Jīva</s> in learning, but not a <s>mantra</s>-disciple, since [<s>Jīva</s>] did not make disciples. If there were a practice of making disciples, then why would <s>Śrī Jīva</s> have relinquished the discipleship of <s>Śrīnivāsa</s>, <s>Narottama</s>, and others? Therefore, after their [the Gosvāmīs'] disappearance from the manifest world, the declaration of <s>mantra</s>-discipleship to them was made by <s>Kṛṣṇa Dāsa</s> himself, by his own desire for authority. In their works, excisions were made in some places, and elaborations were added in others.

children.text:
ataeva śrī-vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇy-ādiṣu kutra kutrāpi saṃśayāspadatvena na sarva-
saṃmatam | tasmād ekasyāprāmāṇyenāny asyāprāmāṇyam iti nyāyāt svakīyātva-
siddhānte sarveṣāṃ śrī-caitanya-pārṣadānām asaṃmatatvena śrīmaj-jīva-pādena
tu parāpekṣā-kṛtena ca parakīyātvaṃ sarva-saṃmataṃ matam iti saṅgatam |
iti śrīmad-rādhā-govinda-deva-sevādhipati-śrī-haridāsa-gosvāmī-caraṇānujīvi-
śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-dāsodīritā bhakti-sādhana-dīpikā-navama-kakṣā
||9||
children.translated_text:
Therefore, in the <s>Śrī Vaiṣṇava-toṣaṇī</s> and other works, some passages are suspect in places and hence not universally accepted. Therefore, by the maxim 'the unreliability of one [entails] the unreliability of another,' the <s>svakīyā</s> doctrine is not accepted by any of <s>Śrī Caitanya</s>'s associates; and since the venerable <s>Jīva</s> wrote it at the desire of another, <s>parakīyātva</s> (the paramour-love doctrine) is the universally accepted view — this is consistent.
Thus ends the ninth <s>kakṣā</s> (division) of the <s>Bhakti-sādhana-dīpikā</s>, composed by <s>Śrī Rādhā-kṛṣṇa Dāsa</s>, who lives in service at the feet of <s>Śrī Haridāsa Gosvāmī</s>, the superintendent of the worship of <s>Śrī Rādhā-Govinda Deva</s>.
||9||

(10)
Tenth <s>Kakṣā</s> (Division)

children.text: tatrādau suṣṭhu vaiśiṣṭyam asyāḥ kathayituṃ sphuṭam |
children.translated_text: In order to clearly state first the great excellence

children.text: lakṣaṇaṃ kriyate bhakter uttamāyāḥ satāṃ matam ||
children.translated_text: of this [<s>bhakti</s>], the definition of <s>uttamā bhakti</s> (supreme devotion) according to the view of the saintly is given. ||
That is as follows—
Devoid of all other desires, uncovered by <s>jñāna</s> (speculative knowledge), <s>karma</s> (ritualistic action), and so forth,
the continuous cultivation of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> [consciousness] with favorable intent — that is <s>uttamā bhakti</s> (supreme devotion). ||
As stated in the <s>Śrī Nārada Pañcarātra</s>—
Freed from all designations, purified by exclusive devotion to Him,
the service of <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s> (the Lord of the senses) with the senses — that is called <s>bhakti</s> (devotion). ||
And in the Third Canto of <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> (3.29.11-13)—
The characteristic of <s>bhakti-yoga</s> that is beyond the <s>guṇas</s> (modes of nature) has been declared:
causeless and uninterrupted — such devotion toward <s>Puruṣottama</s> (the Supreme Person). ||
<s>Sālokya</s> (same world), <s>sārṣṭi</s> (equal opulence), <s>sāmīpya</s> (proximity), <s>sārūpya</s> (same form), and even <s>ekatva</s> (oneness) —

children.text: dīyamānaṃ na gṛhṇanti vinā mat-sevanaṃ janāḥ ||
children.translated_text: even when offered, people do not accept them without service to Me. ||
That itself, called <s>bhakti-yoga</s>, is declared to be ultimate,
by which, transcending the three <s>guṇas</s>, one attains My nature. ||
The description of the excellence of the devotee found in the verse beginning with '<s>sālokya</s>' and so forth
culminates in the definition [of <s>bhakti</s>] through the expression of the purity of devotion. ||
[<s>Bhakti</s>] destroys afflictions (<s>kleśa</s>), bestows auspiciousness (<s>śubha</s>), trivializes liberation (<s>mokṣa</s>), is extremely rare to attain,
is the essence of the most intense bliss (<s>sāndrānanda</s>), and attracts <s>Śrī Kṛṣṇa</s> Himself — such is she. ||
Of the threefold <s>bhakti</s> to be described hereafter, in sequence,

children.text: dviśaḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ padair etan māhātyaṃ parikīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: this greatness has been proclaimed in six verses, two for each [kind]. ||
Moreover—
Even a slight taste (<s>ruci</s>) alone can reveal the truth of <s>bhakti</s>;

children.text: yuktis tu kevalā naiva yad asyā apratiṣṭhatā ||
children.translated_text: mere reasoning alone cannot, for it has no firm foundation. ||
Therein, it has been said even by the ancients—
A meaning established with great effort by skilled reasoners
is demonstrated otherwise by others who are even more expert. ||

children.text:
(BRS 1.2.1-2)
sā bhaktiḥ sādhanaṃ bhāvaḥ premā ceti tridhoditā ||
children.translated_text:
(BRS 1.2.1-2)
That <s>bhakti</s> is declared to be threefold: <s>sādhana</s> (practice), <s>bhāva</s> (ecstatic emotion), and <s>prema</s> (pure love). ||
Therein, <s>sādhana-bhakti</s> (devotion in practice)—
That which is to be accomplished through endeavor, having the state-to-be-achieved (<s>sādhya-bhāva</s>) as its goal — that is called <s>sādhana</s> (practice). |
The manifestation of the eternally perfected <s>bhāva</s> (devotional ecstasy) in the heart is what is to be attained. ||

children.text:
(BRS 1.2.5-7)-
vaidhī rāgānugā ceti sā dvidhā sādhanābhidhā ||
children.translated_text:
(BRS 1.2.5-7)—
That <s>sādhanā</s> (practice) is twofold: <s>vaidhī</s> (injunction-based) and <s>rāgānugā</s> (following spontaneous attachment). ||
Therein, <s>vaidhī</s> —
Where engagement arises due to the non-attainment of <s>rāga</s> (spontaneous attachment),

children.text: śāsanenaiva śāstrasya sā vaidhī bhaktir ucyate ||
children.translated_text: solely through the injunction of scripture — that is called <s>vaidhī bhakti</s> (devotion based on scriptural rules). ||
As stated in the Second [Canto] (2.1.6)—

children.text: tasmād bhārata sarvātmā bhagavān īśvaro hariḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, O <s>Bhārata</s>, the all-pervading Lord, <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Supreme Controller <s>Hari</s>,
should be heard about, glorified, and remembered by one who desires freedom from fear. ||
Therein, the eligible person (BRS 1.2.15-16)—
Whoever, by some great fortune, has developed faith in the service of Him,

children.text: nātisakto na vairāgya-bhāg asyām adhikāry asau ||
children.translated_text: who is neither overly attached [to material things] nor possessed of [dry] renunciation — such a person is qualified for this [<s>vaidhī bhakti</s>]. ||
As stated in the Eleventh [Canto] (11.20.28)—
A person in whom faith in hearing about Me and such [devotional practices] has arisen by providence,
who is neither disgusted [with the world] nor overly attached — for him <s>bhakti-yoga</s> bestows perfection. ||
Now, <s>rāgānugā</s> (BRS 1.2.270)—
That which follows the <s>rāgātmikā</s> [devotion] that shines forth fully manifest
in the residents of <s>Vraja</s> and others — that is called <s>rāgānugā</s>. ||

children.text:
ṭīkā-abhivyaktaṃ suvyaktaṃ yathā syāt tathā vraja-vāsi-janādiṣu virājantīṃ
rāgātmikāṃ bhaktim anusṛtā yā bhaktiḥ | yā rāgānugā ucyate iti yojanā | vraja-
vāsi-janādiṣv ity atra jana-padena manuṣya-mātraṃ bodhitam | ādi-padena paśu-
pakṣy-ādayo gṛhyante | ataevoktaṃ-
children.translated_text: Commentary: 'Fully manifest' means very clearly — that <s>rāgātmikā bhakti</s> which shines forth in the residents of <s>Vraja</s> and others — the devotion that follows it is what is called <s>rāgānugā</s>: this is the construction. In 'the residents of <s>Vraja</s> and others,' by the word 'people' (<s>jana</s>), human beings in general are indicated; by the word 'and others' (<s>ādi</s>), animals, birds, and such are included. Therefore it is stated—

children.text:
trailokya-saubhagam idaṃ ca nirīkṣya rūpaṃ
yat go-dvija-druma-mṛgāḥ pulakāny abibhran | iti |
children.translated_text: 'This beauty which is the good fortune of the three worlds — seeing which, the cows, the twice-born [birds], the trees, and the deer bore goosebumps.' || Thus.

children.text:
virājantīm iti viśeṣeṇa rājamānām, na tu dhāmāntara-parivāra-bhaktivad aiśvarya-
jñānādinābhibhūtām | anusṛtety atrānusaraṇaṃ nitya-siddha-vraja-vāsi-jana-bhāva-
ceṣṭānugamanātmakānukaraṇam | tac ca śrī-kṛṣṇa-preṣṭhānugata-niṣṭhaṃ tad
evānugatyam iti phalitārthaḥ | tac ca tad-anugatatve sati tādṛśa-kāya-vāṅ-
mānasīya-sevā-kartṛtvaṃ ceti |
children.translated_text: 'Shining forth' means especially resplendent — not like the devotion of the associates in other abodes, which is overwhelmed by awareness of [the Lord's] majesty (<s>aiśvarya-jñāna</s>) and such. 'Following' here means imitation in the form of following the moods and activities of the eternally perfected residents of <s>Vraja</s>. And that is established in allegiance to Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s most beloved — that very allegiance is the resultant meaning. And that means: while being subordinate to them, having the agency of service through body, speech, and mind of that nature.
The dependence on Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s most beloved, as [stated] in the Eleventh [Canto] (11.3.21)—

children.text: tasmād guruṃ prapadyeta jijñāsuḥ śreya uttamam |
children.translated_text: Therefore, one who is desirous of knowing the highest good should surrender to a <s>guru</s>

children.text: śābde pare ca niṣṇātaṃ brahmaṇy upaśamāśrayam ||
children.translated_text: who is well-versed in the Vedic scriptures (<s>śabda-brahman</s>) and in the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, and who is a shelter of tranquility. ||

children.text:
ṭīkā ca-uttamaṃ śreyo jijñāsuḥ | śābde brahmaṇi vedākhye niṣṇātaṃ, anyathā
saṃśaya-nirāsakatvāyogyatvād dhetoḥ | pare brahmaṇi aparokṣānubhave ca
niṣṇātam | anyathā yato bodha-saṃcārābhāvāt | pare brahmaṇi niṣṇātatve
dyotakam āha upaśamāśrayam iti |
children.translated_text: Commentary: 'Desirous of knowing the highest good.' 'Well-versed in the Vedic <s>Brahman</s>' means in the <s>Vedas</s> — because otherwise he would be incapable of removing doubts. 'Well-versed in the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>' means in direct experience of [the Supreme] — because otherwise there would be no transmission of realization. To indicate his being well-versed in the Supreme <s>Brahman</s>, he says 'a shelter of tranquility.'
In the same [Canto], Śrī <s>Bhagavān</s> [speaks] to Śrīmad <s>Uddhava</s> (11.10.12)—
The <s>ācārya</s> is the lower fire-churning stick (<s>araṇi</s>), and the student is the upper <s>araṇi</s>;
their conjunction is the teaching (<s>pravacana</s>); knowledge is the friction-point that brings happiness. ||

children.text:
ṭīkā-ādyo'dharaḥ | tat-sandhānaṃ ca tayor madhyamaṃ manthana-kāṣṭhāṃ
pravacanam upadeśaḥ | vidyā śāstrotthaṃ jñātam | tatra sandhau bhavo'gnir iva |
tathā ca śrutiḥ-ācāryaṃ pūrva-rūpaḥ antevāsy uttara-rūpaḥ ity ādi | ataeva tad-
vijñānārthaṃ sa gurum evābhigacchet iti | ācāryavān puruṣo veda iti | naiṣā tarkeṇa
matir āpaneyā ity ādi ca |
children.translated_text: Commentary: 'The first' means the lower [stick]. 'Their conjunction' — the middle churning-stick between the two — is the teaching, the instruction. 'Knowledge' is what is known through scripture. The fire, as it were, arises at the junction therein. And thus the <s>Śruti</s> [states]: 'The <s>ācārya</s> is the prior form, the student is the latter form,' and so forth. Therefore, 'For the sake of that knowledge, one should approach the <s>guru</s> alone.' 'A person who has an <s>ācārya</s> knows.' 'This understanding is not to be attained by reasoning,' and so forth.
this is the purport. Therefore, in <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s> (11.17.27)—
Thus, the arising of that mood occurs only through association with the <s>guru</s> who is most dear to Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> — not otherwise:
One should know the <s>ācārya</s> as Myself and never disrespect him;
one should not find fault through mortal judgment — the <s>guru</s> is the embodiment of all the gods. ||

children.text:
nitya-siddhasya bhāvasya prākaṭyaṃ hṛdi sādhyatā (BRS 1.2.2) iti nitya-siddhasya
bhāvasya sādhaka-bhaktānāṃ hṛdi svayaṃ prakaṭanaṃ sādhyatā | tat-tad-bhāvādi-
mādhurye śrute dhīr yad apekṣate (BRS 1.2.292) ity āśrayiṣyamāṇe gurau tad-
bhāva-mādhuryaṃ sutarāṃ dṛśyate | etādṛśe śrī-kṛṣṇa-rūpa-gurau dṛṣṭe sati

children.translated_text: <s>lobha</s> (spiritual greed) arises spontaneously. As stated (BRS 1.2.241)—

'The manifestation of the eternally perfected <s>bhāva</s> in the heart is what is to be attained' (BRS 1.2.2) — the self-manifestation of the eternally perfected <s>bhāva</s> in the hearts of practitioner-devotees is what is to be attained. 'When the sweetness of those various moods is heard, whatever the mind longs for' (BRS 1.2.292) — in the <s>guru</s> who is to be taken shelter of, the sweetness of that mood is seen all the more clearly. When such a <s>guru</s>, who is Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s own form, is beheld,
Washed by the tears from his eyes, his body adorned with a covering of goosebumps,

children.text: skhalann antaḥ-phullo dadhad atipṛthuṃ vepathum api |
children.translated_text: faltering, blossoming within, bearing an exceedingly great trembling —

children.text: dṛśoḥ kakṣāṃ yāvan mama sa puruṣaḥ ko'py upayayau
children.translated_text: when a certain Person entered the range of my vision,

children.text: na jāte kiṃ tāvan matir iha gṛhe nābhiramate ||
children.translated_text: did not my mind then cease to find pleasure in household life? ||

children.text:
atha śravaṇa-guru-bhajana-śikṣā-gurvoḥ prāyikam ekatvam iti | yathā tathaivāha
śrī-bhakti-sandarbhe (206)-
children.translated_text: Now, the <s>guru</s> from whom one hears (<s>śravaṇa-guru</s>) and the <s>guru</s> who teaches worship (<s>bhajana-śikṣā-guru</s>) are generally one and the same. As stated in the <s>Bhakti-sandarbha</s> (206)—

children.text: amāyayānuvṛttyā yais tuṣyed ātmātma-do hariḥ || (BhP 11.2.21) iti |
children.translated_text: by sincere and guileless service, by which <s>Hari</s>, the Self who gives Himself, is pleased. || (BhP 11.2.21) Thus.
One should learn the religious duties pertaining to <s>Bhagavān</s>, regarding the <s>guru</s> as one's very self and deity,
In the same [passage], <s>Bhagavān</s>, the Lord [states]:
He states the necessity of the <s>śikṣā-guru</s> (instructing spiritual master) as well, in the Tenth [Canto] (10.87.33)—
Those who, having conquered the senses and the vital air, [attempt to control] the untamed horse of the mind

children.text: ya iha yatanti yantum ati-lolam upāya-khidaḥ |
children.translated_text: which is exceedingly restless — they who strive here to restrain it are afflicted by [the failure of their] methods;
beset by hundreds of calamities, having abandoned the feet of the <s>guru</s>,
they are like merchants, O Unborn One, without a helmsman on the ocean. ||

children.text:
ṭīkā-ye guroś caraṇaṃ samavahāān āśrityātilola-madāntam adamitaṃ mana eva
turagaṃ durgama-sāmyād vijitair indriyaiḥ prāṇaiś ca yantuṃ bhagavad-
antarmukhīkartuṃ prayatante | te upāya-khidas teṣu teṣūpāyeṣu khidyante | ato
vyasana-śatānvitā bhavanti | ataeva iha saṃsāra-samudre santi tiṣṭhanti duḥkham
eva prāpnuvantīty arthaḥ | jaladhau akṛta-karṇadharā asvīkṛta-nāvikā vaṇijo yathā
tadvat |
children.translated_text: Commentary: Those who, having abandoned the feet of the <s>guru</s> — not having taken shelter [of them] — strive to restrain with conquered senses and vital airs the very untamed, unrestricted mind, [which is] like an [unbroken] horse due to the similarity of being difficult to control — they become afflicted by those various methods. Thus they become beset by hundreds of calamities. Therefore, they remain in this ocean of <s>saṃsāra</s>, meaning they attain only suffering. Like merchants without a helmsman on the ocean — so it is.

children.text:
śrī-guru-pradarśita-bhagavad-bhakti-bhajana-prakāreṇa bhagavad-dharma-jī̀iāne
sati tat-kṛpayā vyasanānabhibhūtau ca satyāṃ śīghram eva mano niścalaṃ bhavatīti
bhāvaḥ |
children.translated_text: Through the method of devotional worship shown by Śrī <s>Guru</s>, when there is knowledge of the Lord's dharma, and when, by his grace, one is not overwhelmed by calamities — then the mind very quickly becomes steady: this is the purport.
Now, in the <s>Brahma-vaivarta</s> [<s>Purāṇa</s>]—

children.text: guru-bhaktyā sa milati smaraṇāt sevyate budhaiḥ |
children.translated_text: Through devotion to the <s>guru</s>, He is met; through remembrance, He is served by the wise;
even when met, He is not obtained by souls who are absorbed in egoism. ||
Therefore, in the <s>Nārada-pañcarātra</s>, the necessity of worshiping [the <s>guru</s>] is stated, as follows—

children.text: vaiṣṇavaṃ jñāna-vaktāraṃ yo vidyād viṣṇuvad gurum |
children.translated_text: One who knows a <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> teacher of knowledge as a <s>guru</s> equal to <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: pūjayed vāṅ-manaḥ-kāyaiḥ sa śāstrajñaḥ sa vaiṣṇavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and worships him with speech, mind, and body — he is a knower of scripture, he is a [true] <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>. ||

children.text:
śloka-pādasya vaktāpi yaḥ pūjyaḥ sa sadaiva hi |
kiṃ punar bhagavad-viṣṇoḥ svarūpaṃ vitanoti yaḥ || ity ādi |
children.translated_text: Even one who speaks a single quarter of a verse is always worthy of worship. How much more so one who reveals the essential nature of Lord <s>Viṣṇu</s>! || And so forth.

children.text:
tasmāt śrī-guror āvaśyakatvam | tac-caraṇāvalambanaṃ vinā premotpattir na
bhavatīti niṣkarṣārthaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, the necessity of Śrī <s>Guru</s> [is established]. Without taking shelter of his feet, the arising of <s>prema</s> (divine love) does not occur — this is the conclusive meaning.
In the <s>Manaḥ-śikṣā</s> composed by Śrī <s>Raghunātha Dāsa Gosvāmī</s>, as follows—

children.text:
śacī-sūnuṃ nandīśvara-pati-sutatve guru-varaṃ
mukunda-preṣṭhatve smara ity ādi |
children.translated_text: 'Remember the son of <s>Śacī</s> as the son of the lord of <s>Nandīśvara</s>, and the best of <s>gurus</s> as the most beloved of <s>Mukunda</s>' — and so forth.
In the <s>Kālikā Purāṇa</s>, in the <s>Śyāmā-rahasya</s>—

children.text: madhu-lobhād yathā bhṛṅgaḥ puṣpāt puṣpāntaraṃ vrajet |
children.translated_text: Just as a bee, out of greed for honey, goes from flower to flower,

children.text: jñāna-lobhāt tathā śiṣyo guror gurv-antaraṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: so a disciple, out of greed for knowledge, should go from <s>guru</s> to <s>guru</s>. ||
And in the <s>Stavāvalī</s> (<s>Manaḥ-śikṣā</s> 3, 12)—
If you desire a dwelling in the land of <s>Vraja</s> with passionate attachment, life after life,

children.text: yuva-dvandvaṃ tac cet paricartium ārād abhilaṣeḥ |
children.translated_text: and if you wish to serve the Youthful Couple from nearby—

children.text: svarūpaṃ śrī-rūpaṃ sa-gaṇam iha tasyāgrajam api
children.translated_text: <s>Svarūpa</s>, Śrī <s>Rūpa</s> with his associates, and also his elder brother [<s>Sanātana</s>]:

children.text: sphuṭaṃ premṇā nityaṃ smara nama tadā tvaṃ śṛṇu manaḥ ||
children.translated_text: clearly, with love, always remember and bow to them — O mind, hear this! ||

children.text:
sa-yūthaḥ śrī-rūpānuga iha bhavan gokula-vane
jano rādhā-kṛṣṇātula-bhajana-ratnaṃ sa labhate ||
children.translated_text: One who is a follower of Śrī <s>Rūpa</s>, together with his group, here in the forest of <s>Gokula</s> — such a person obtains the jewel of the incomparable worship of <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>. ||
(<s>Vilāpa-kusumāñjali</s>, 14)—

children.text:
yad-avadhi mama kācin mañjarī rūpa-pūrvā
vraja-bhuvi bata netra-dvandva-dīptiṃ cakāra |
tad-avadhi tava vṛndāraṇya-rājñi prakāmaṃ
caraṇa-kamala-lākṣā-sandidṛkṣā mamābhūt || iti |
children.translated_text: From the moment a certain <s>mañjarī</s> named <s>Rūpa</s> cast the radiance of her two eyes upon me in the land of <s>Vraja</s>, from that very moment, O Queen of <s>Vṛndāvana</s>, a longing to behold the lac-dye on Your lotus feet arose in me most intensely. || Thus.

children.text:
ata etādṛśānugatyaṃ vinā śrī-nandanandanasya tathāvidha-svarūpa-prāptir na
bhavati tatrāpi śrī-rūpānugatyaṃ vinā śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇātula-bhajana-ratnaṃ na
labhata iti niṣkarṣārthaḥ |
children.translated_text: Therefore, without such allegiance, the attainment of the true essential form of Śrī <s>Nandanandana</s> (<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>) does not occur; and moreover, without allegiance to Śrī <s>Rūpa</s>, the jewel of the incomparable worship of Śrī <s>Rādhā</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is not obtained — this is the conclusive meaning.
Incidentally, the defining characteristics of an <s>ācārya</s>, as stated in the <s>Vāyu Purāṇa</s>—

children.text: ācinoti yaḥ śāstrārthān svācāraiḥ sthāpayaty api |
children.translated_text: One who gathers the meanings of the scriptures and establishes them through his own conduct,

children.text: svayam ācarate yasmāt tasmād ācārya ucyate ||
children.translated_text: and who himself practices [what he teaches] — therefore he is called an <s>ācārya</s>. ||
As stated in the <s>Viṣṇu-smṛti</s> (HBV 1.45-46)—
A <s>guru</s> is not one who desires service, fame, or gain from disciples;
[rather, he is] an ocean of mercy, completely fulfilled, and a benefactor of all beings. ||
Desireless, perfected in all respects, expert in all branches of knowledge,
a dispeller of all doubts, and never idle — such a one is called a <s>guru</s>. ||

children.text:
gautamīye-
na japo nārcanaṃ naiva dhyānaṃ nāpi vidhi-kramaḥ |
kevalaṃ satataṃ kṛṣṇa-caraṇāmbhoja-bhāvinām || iti |
children.translated_text:
In the <s>Gautamīya</s> [<s>Tantra</s>]—
Neither <s>japa</s>, nor worship, nor meditation, nor the sequence of ritual injunctions — but solely the constant contemplation of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>'s lotus feet. || Thus.

children.text:
kiṃ ca-
nāyikānāṃ ca sarvāsāṃ madhyā śreṣṭhatamā matā |
prāyaḥ sarva-rasotkarṣo madhyāyām eva yujyate || ity ādi |
children.translated_text:
Furthermore—
Among all the heroines (<s>nāyikās</s>), the <s>madhyā</s> (moderate) type is considered the most excellent; the pre-eminence of all <s>rasas</s> is generally found in the <s>madhyā</s> alone. || And so forth.

children.text:
darśitam eva | kiṃ ca-tvadīyatā-madīyatā-madhyayor madhye madīyatā śreṣṭhā
|
children.translated_text: This has already been shown. Furthermore — between 'yours' (<s>tvadīyatā</s>) and 'mine' (<s>madīyatā</s>), 'mine' (<s>madīyatā</s>) is superior.
And this <s>līlā</s> (divine play) of Śrī <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> is the most excellent, bestowing everything;

children.text: na dātavyā na prakāśyā jane tv anadhikāriṇi ||
children.translated_text: it should not be given or revealed to an unqualified person. ||

children.text:
tathā hi (pādme)-
māṃ ca gopaya yena syāt sṛṣṭir eṣottarottarā | iti |
children.translated_text:
As stated (in the <s>Padma Purāṇa</s>)—
'And conceal Me, by which this creation shall be ever-ascending.' || Thus.

children.text:
śrī-bhāgavate prathama-skandhe (1.1.8) brūyuḥ snigdhasya śiṣyasya guravo guhyam
apy uta iti bṛhad-gautamīye ca |
iti śrīmad-rādhā-govinda-deva-sevādhipati-śrī-haridāsa-gosvāmī-caraṇānujīvi-
śrī-rādhā-kṛṣṇa-dāsodīritā bhakti-sādhana-dīpikā-daśama-kakṣā sampūrṇa |
children.translated_text:
In <s>Śrī Bhāgavata</s>, First Canto (1.1.8): '<s>Gurus</s> speak even the confidential [truths] to an affectionate disciple.'
And in the <s>Bṛhad-gautamīya</s>.
Thus ends the Tenth Section of the <s>Bhakti-sādhana-dīpikā</s>, composed by Śrī <s>Rādhā Kṛṣṇa Dāsa</s>, a follower at the feet of Śrī <s>Haridāsa Gosvāmī</s>, the superintendent of the worship of Śrī <s>Rādhā-Govinda Deva</s>.

The Śrī <s>Sādhana-dīpikā</s> is complete.
Let it be offered at the feet of Śrī Śrīmad <s>Gurudeva</s>.
